title: Biomarkers in Patients With Acute Ischaemic Stroke Undergoing Thrombectomy Compared With Controls: A Pilot Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Detection of cerebral ischaemia is challenging in patients who are anaesthetised, sedated or have reduced levels of consciousness, as neurological examination is difficult or even impossible to assess. Furthermore, as some patients cannot be transported for radiology, for example during surgery, a reliable blood biomarker for detecting acute cerebral events would be of considerable clinical value. We aimed to compare levels of brain injury biomarkers glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP), neurofilament light chain (NfL), and total tau (tau) in patients with acute ischaemic stroke (AIS) undergoing endovascular thrombectomy under general anaesthesia or sedation to controls undergoing non-cerebral surgery under general anaesthesia. These biomarkers were chosen because previous studies have demonstrated their potential as blood biomarkers of acute cerebral injury and ischaemic stroke. METHODS: In this prospective, observational pilot study, conducted at the Sahlgrenska University Hospital, Gothenburg, Sweden, between 2021 and 2024, GFAP, NfL, and tau were analysed using the Simoa Neurology 4-plex assay, before thrombectomy or surgery and at 2- and 24 h thereafter. RESULTS: Blood samples from 21 patients with AIS and 19 controls were analysed. GFAP concentrations in patients with AIS increased significantly from baseline to 24 h (median 301.0 → 1443.0 pg/mL; p = 0.001) and were higher than in controls at all time points (p < 0.01). In the controls there was no significant increase in GFAP from baseline to 24 h (p = 0.449). NfL and tau increased significantly in patients with AIS (p = 0.001 and 0.002) but also in the controls (p = 0.001 and 0.047). CONCLUSION: GFAP and NfL concentrations were higher in patients with acute ischaemic stroke than in surgical controls at all sampling time points, whereas tau differed only after 24 h. Unlike NfL and tau, GFAP did not increase significantly in controls, suggesting that it may be less influenced by anaesthesia and surgery. These findings support further evaluation of GFAP as a potential biomarker of acute cerebral injury in perioperative and critical care settings. EDITORIAL COMMENT: A biomarker of ischaemic cerebral injury could be attractive to support treatments to protect brain health during anaesthesia and surgery. In a pilot study, glial fibrillary acidic protein emerged as a potential candidate as it was increased in patients undergoing endovascular thrombectomy for large-vessel ischaemic stroke compared to anaesthetised patients undergoing non-cerebral surgery. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT03919370.

title: Epidemiology of 376,383 arteriovenous fistula creations for hemodialysis over 9 years within the Brazilian Unified Public Health System and the Private Healthcare Sector.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Chronic kidney disease represents a growing public health challenge worldwide, particularly in low- and middleincome countries. In Brazil, where most patients with end-stage renal disease depend on the public healthcare system for dialysis and transplantation, ensuring adequate vascular access - with arteriovenous fistula (AVF) being one of the available options - is critical to sustaining treatment. Despite its clinical relevance, comprehensive national data on vascular access patterns across both sectors have historically been limited. OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to examine trends in AVF creation for hemodialysis across Brazil from 2015 to 2023, assessing differences in frequency, geographic distribution, and sectoral disparities between the public and private healthcare sectors. METHODS: A retrospective population-based analysis was conducted using anonymized data from national administrative databases: DATASUS (public sector) and D-TISS (private sector). The majority of AVF creation procedures were included. Statistical analyses considered regional adjustments and were performed using SPSS v.20, with significance set at p < 0.001. RESULTS: Over the nine- year period, 376,383 AVF procedures were recorded, with 90.57% occurring in the public sector. While the absolute number of AVF creations increased, the ratio of AVFs per 1,000 dialysis patients showed a declining trend. Regional disparities were evident, with the Southeast and South regions presenting higher procedure rates compared to other areas. The private sector consistently reported lower creation rates. CONCLUSION: Although, separately, dialysis and AVF rates have risen steadily in Brazil, the relative rate between them has shown a decreasing trend over the years. The predominance of AVF procedures in the public system is more pronounced.

Despite its clinical relevance, comprehensive national data on vascular access patterns across both sectors have historically been limited.

title: Postoperative Outcomes Following Autologous Breast Reconstruction in Patients Receiving Selective Estrogen Receptor Modulators and Aromatase Inhibitors: A Multicenter Propensity Score-Matched Cohort Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The perioperative management of endocrine therapy remains controversial in patients undergoing autologous breast reconstruction. Because selective estrogen receptor modulators (SERMs) and aromatase inhibitors (AIs) differ in their mechanisms of action and adverse-effect profiles, we evaluated their associations with postoperative outcomes separately in a large multicenter propensity score-matched cohort. METHODS: This retrospective TriNetX study included patients undergoing autologous breast reconstruction. Preoperative exposure was defined as a documented SERM or AI prescription within 3 months of reconstruction. Exposure cohorts were mutually exclusive, and controls excluded both endocrine therapy classes. Separate 1:1 propensity score matching incorporated demographic, comorbidity, oncologic, treatment, venous thromboembolism, and antithrombotic covariates. Outcomes were assessed within 90 days. RESULTS: After matching, 1993 SERM-exposed patients were compared with 1993 controls and 3167 AI-exposed patients with 3167 controls. SERM exposure was not significantly associated with evaluable 90-day outcomes, including coded postoperative debridement (3.01% vs. 2.56%; RR, 1.18; 95% CI, 0.81-1.73; p = 0.39). AI exposure was associated with increased coded postoperative debridement (4.45% vs. 3.38%; RR, 1.33; 95% CI, 1.03-1.72; p = 0.028), while other evaluable outcomes were not significantly different. AI exposure was also associated with greater debridement hazard (HR, 1.44; 95% CI, 1.12-1.87; p = 0.0049). CONCLUSIONS: Documented SERM exposure was not significantly associated with evaluable postoperative outcomes, whereas AI exposure was associated with increased coded postoperative debridement. Because debridement codes lack anatomical specificity, this finding is exploratory and does not establish flap-specific compromise. These separate analyses do not establish differences between endocrine therapy classes or support recommendations regarding perioperative continuation or discontinuation.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: The perioperative management of endocrine therapy remains controversial in patients undergoing autologous breast reconstruction. Because selective estrogen receptor modulators (SERMs) and aromatase inhibitors (AIs) differ in their mechanisms of action and adverse-effect profiles, we evaluated their associations with postoperative outcomes separately in a large multicenter propensity score-matched cohort. METHODS: This retrospective TriNetX study included patients undergoing autologous breast reconstruction.

title: Factors Associated With the Autonomy of Patients Treated by Haemodialysis in Community Centres. A Cross-Sectional Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: In France, haemodialysis is delivered in different settings depending on patients' health status and autonomy. Community centres include self-care and satellite units, which vary in organisation and patient involvement. OBJECTIVES: To describe the characteristics of patients treated in haemodialysis community centres and to identify factors associated with autonomy in self-care units. DESIGN: Cross-sectional study. PARTICIPANTS: All patients receiving haemodialysis in community centres in a French region on December 31, 2021. MEASUREMENTS: Patient characteristics and multiple dimensions of patient autonomy were recorded. Multivariate analyses assessed associations between patient factors and technical autonomy. RESULTS: Among 507 patients, 304 were treated in self-care units and 203 in satellite haemodialysis units. Patients in satellite haemodialysis units had a median age of 69 years (IQR 59-78; range 24-90), compared with 66 years (IQR 54-75; range 22-91) in self-care haemodialysis units. They also had more comorbidities. Younger age was associated with greater autonomy in arteriovenous fistula puncture-site dressing (PR 0.97, 95% CI 0.96-0.98), setting the haemodialysis machine (PR 0.97, 95% CI 0.96-0.98), and programming it (PR 0.97, 95% CI 0.95-0.98). Autonomy differed significantly between centres, with centre affiliation significantly associated (p < .001) with autonomy for the arteriovenous fistula puncture-site dressing and machine-related tasks. CONCLUSIONS: Patient characteristics in self-care haemodialysis units did not fully explain autonomy for haemodialysis tasks. Considerable variability between centres was observed, suggesting that centre-related factors may contribute to differences in patient autonomy.

title: Spectral Photon-Counting Detector CT for Comprehensive Evaluation of Carotid Plaque and Stenosis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Conventional energy-integrating detector (EID) CT is limited in differentiating soft-plaque components due to overlapping attenuation values and is frequently affected by calcification-related blooming artifacts that obscure the vessel lumen and may overestimate stenosis. Photon-counting detector CT (PCD-CT) can provide enhanced spatial resolution and spectral discrimination compared with conventional EID-CT, potentially improving carotid plaque characterization and mitigating artifact-related limitations. This study systematically evaluated image quality, plaque component attenuation, and stenosis visualization across spectral PCD-CT reconstructions. METHODS: We retrospectively included patients who underwent PCD-CT for carotid stenosis assessment. Four monoenergetic (ME 40, 55, 70, and 85 keV), PureLumen (PL), and virtual noncontrast (VNC) reconstructions were analyzed. Signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR), edge sharpness, plaque area, degree of NASCET stenosis, and attenuation of plaque components (intraplaque hemorrhage, lipid-rich necrotic core, fibrotic tissue, calcification) were compared using repeated-measures ANOVA with Bonferroni correction. RESULTS: Our study included 27 patients (16 men, age: 74.5±9.1 y) with 50 plaques. CNR, SNR, and noise decreased with increasing ME levels ( P <0.001). PL yielded CNR and sharpness comparable to ME55, whereas VNC exhibited a near-zero lumen signal. Stenosis remained consistent across ME reconstructions (44% to 45%, P =1.00), but significantly reduced for PL (38%, P <0.001). Lower-energy reconstructions (ME40/ME55) improved the separation of attenuation values between the lumen and the various plaque components. CONCLUSION: Low-energy PCD-CT reconstructions enhance CNR and sharpness while maintaining consistent plaque and stenosis measurements. The PL algorithm may improve the assessment of calcified plaques, where conventional reconstructions may overestimate stenosis. PCD-CT shows promise for advanced plaque composition evaluation, but further validation against MRI and histology is warranted.

Photon-counting detector CT (PCD-CT) can provide enhanced spatial resolution and spectral discrimination compared with conventional EID-CT, potentially improving carotid plaque characterization and mitigating artifact-related limitations. This study systematically evaluated image quality, plaque component attenuation, and stenosis visualization across spectral PCD-CT reconstructions.

title: 2025 National Guidelines on the Mediterranean Diet: Executive Summary of a Joint Report by Italian Scientific Societies and the National Institute of Health Task Force on Clinical Practice Guidelines.
abstract: CONTEXT: Chronic non-communicable diseases (NCDs) are the leading global causes of morbidity, mortality, and escalating health care costs, driven largely by unhealthy lifestyles in an aging population. OBJECTIVE: The Mediterranean Diet (MD), traditionally associated with healthy longevity, is increasingly recognized for its preventative and therapeutic benefits across many NCDs. DATA SOURCES: Using the NUTRIGRADE methodology, a multidisciplinary panel of clinical, methodological, and public health experts conducted a comprehensive systematic review across 9 health domains and one economic domain. DATA EXTRACTION: Data were extracted from multiple databases without date restrictions, assessing outcomes such as disease incidence and prevalence, mortality rates of nutrition-related NCDs, quality of life indicators, and relevant biochemical markers. Evidence was critically appraised and synthesized to formulate evidence-based recommendations. DATA ANALYSIS: A total of 84 evidence-based recommendations were developed. The MD was found to significantly reduce all-cause mortality in the general population and cardiovascular morbidity and mortality, particularly in high-risk individuals. High-quality evidence supports the protective role of the MD against myocardial infarction, stroke, atrial fibrillation, and peripheral arterial disease. In oncological evidence, MD adherence has been found to be linked to a lower incidence of several cancer types and improved survival outcomes. Additional benefits include reduced incidence and progression of cognitive decline, type 2 diabetes, metabolic syndrome, and obesity, and improved pregnancy outcomes. The strength of recommendations varied by outcome and target population, with many supported by robust evidence. CONCLUSIONS: The MD is a scientifically supported dietary intervention with broad preventive and therapeutic benefits. Its integration into clinical practice, public health strategies, and policy initiatives is strongly recommended to promote health and reduce the global health care burden.

title: Prevention of Venous Thromboembolism after Total Hip or Knee Replacement.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Studies comparing aspirin with anticoagulants for venous thromboembolism (VTE) prophylaxis after total hip or knee arthroplasty have had conflicting results. METHODS: In a comparative-effectiveness noninferiority trial, we randomly assigned patients undergoing elective hip or knee arthroplasty to receive aspirin (81 mg twice daily), warfarin (to a target international normalized ratio of 2.0), or rivaroxaban (10 mg daily) for 30 days. The composite primary effectiveness outcome (death from any cause or symptomatic VTE) and primary safety outcome (bleeding, reoperation for wound problems, or myocardial infarction) were evaluated through 6 months in a blinded fashion. The noninferiority margin for the risk difference was 0.69 percentage points. RESULTS: Among 18,883 participants who had undergone randomization, 15,317 (7214 with hip arthroplasty and 8103 with knee arthroplasty) were included in the primary per-protocol analysis. A primary effectiveness outcome event occurred in 77 of 6090 participants (1.26%) in the aspirin group, in 52 of 4231 (1.23%) in the warfarin group, and in 47 of 4996 (0.94%) in the rivaroxaban group; a primary safety outcome event occurred in 177 (2.91%), 142 (3.36%), and 174 (3.48%), respectively. In pairwise comparisons, 6-month risks of a primary effectiveness outcome event were 1.24% and 0.94% for aspirin versus rivaroxaban (difference, 0.30 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -0.20 to 0.81); 1.24% and 1.01% for aspirin versus warfarin (difference, 0.23 percentage points; 95% CI, -0.34 to 0.81); and 1.13% and 1.10% for warfarin versus rivaroxaban (difference, 0.03 percentage points; 95% CI, -0.57 to 0.63). Risks of a primary safety outcome event were 3.70% and 3.02% for rivaroxaban versus aspirin (difference, 0.68 percentage points; 95% CI, -0.04 to 1.41); 3.65% and 2.88% for warfarin versus aspirin (difference, 0.77 percentage points; 95% CI, -0.04 to 1.58); and 3.59% and 3.61% for rivaroxaban versus warfarin (difference, -0.02 percentage points; 95% CI, -0.89 to 0.85). Intention-to-treat analyses yielded similar results. CONCLUSIONS: Aspirin prophylaxis after total hip or knee arthroplasty was not noninferior to rivaroxaban or warfarin with respect to death or symptomatic VTE. Warfarin and rivaroxaban were not noninferior to aspirin for safety. (Funded by the Patient-Centered Outcomes Research Institute; PEPPER ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT02810704.).

title: Cilengitide limits syndromic and sporadic thoracic aortic aneurysm by targeting specific αV integrin.
abstract: Thoracic aortic aneurysm (TAA) is one of the major causes of morbidity and mortality worldwide, still lacking an etiologic therapy. Aberrant activation of TGF-β and dysregulation of mechanotransduction signalling in vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs) play a key role in the pathology. However, a precise picture of molecular mechanisms in the disease is still unclear. Integrins containing the αV subunit are central in pro-fibrotic pathways mediated by TGF-β and mechanotransduction signalling pathways, but their role as a potential therapeutic target in syndromic and sporadic TAAs still needs investigation. We showed higher expression levels of αV integrin in both types of human TAAs and that the αV integrin inhibitor Cilengitide limits pro-fibrotic events in patient-derived VSMCs. In vivo results defined Cilengitide as the most effective and promising drug for the treatment of TAAs in humans.

title: Feasibility, safety, and efficacy of the amber peripheral liquid embolic system: results from stage I of the first-in-human OPAL study.
abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate the early safety and technical feasibility of Amber 20 for peripheral vascular embolization in a prospective, multicenter, first-in-human stage I study. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This was a prospective, single-arm, multicenter, open-label first-in-human stage I trial conducted across 11 centers in Spain. Fifteen patients requiring peripheral embolization for various indications (including hemorrhage, aneurysm/pseudoaneurysm, endoleak, portal vein embolization, and hypervascular tumors) were enrolled. The primary endpoint was the rate of device-related serious adverse events (SAEs) within 24 h. Secondary endpoints included overall adverse events (AEs) and technical success, defined as complete vascular occlusion or devascularization on final angiography. RESULTS: Fifteen patients (60% female; median age 56 years) underwent embolization using Amber 20. Technical success was achieved in 100% of cases (15/15). No device-related SAEs or AEs were reported within 24 h. Five patient (33%) experienced a mild adverse event (postembolization syndrome) related to the procedure. All adverse events resolved without sequelae. No device deficiencies were observed. CONCLUSION: In this first-in-human, multicenter study, Amber 20 demonstrated a favorable safety profile and high technical success rate for peripheral vascular embolization. These preliminary findings support its potential as an effective liquid embolic agent, warranting further evaluation in larger studies with longer follow-up (stage II).

title: National incidence and predictors of in-hospital venous thromboembolism after inpatient lumbar fusion, 2016-2022.
abstract: PURPOSE: To estimate the national incidence of in-hospital VTE recorded during the index lumbar fusion admission and identify independent comorbidity predictors. METHODS: Adult (≥ 18 years) inpatient admissions undergoing lumbar fusion were identified in the National Inpatient Sample (NIS) from 2016 to 2022 using ICD-10-PCS procedure codes. The primary outcome was in-hospital VTE during the index admission. Characteristics were compared between VTE and non-VTE admissions, and multivariable survey-weighted logistic regression evaluated independent predictors. Significance was set at the P < 0.05 level. RESULTS: Across 631,165 weighted inpatient lumbar fusion admissions, in-hospital VTE incidence was 0.6%. VTE admissions were older (age distribution, P < 0.001), more frequently male (P = 0.003), and more often involved multilevel fusion (78.5% vs. 74.2%, P = 0.007). On multivariable analysis, the largest adjusted associations were observed for other neurologic disorders (OR 3.76, 95% CI 2.93-4.83, P < 0.001), coagulopathy (OR 3.70, 95% CI 2.89-4.75, P < 0.001), weight loss (OR 3.57, 95% CI 2.35-5.42, P < 0.001), pulmonary circulation disorders (OR 2.78, 95% CI 1.82-4.23, P < 0.001), and paralysis (OR 2.78, 95% CI 2.09-3.71, P < 0.001). Additional predictors included solid tumor without metastasis (OR 1.97, P = 0.022), cerebrovascular disease (OR 1.90, P = 0.003), peripheral vascular disease (OR 1.58, P = 0.002), obesity (OR 1.75, P < 0.001), seizure disorders (OR 1.74, P = 0.016), congestive heart failure (OR 1.71, P < 0.001), and deficiency anemia (OR 1.64, P < 0.001). CONCLUSIONS: In-hospital VTE recorded during the index lumbar fusion admission was uncommon but concentrated among patients with distinct high-risk comorbidity profiles. These findings support risk-stratified inpatient surveillance and prevention strategies during hospitalization.
englishSummary: PURPOSE: To estimate the national incidence of in-hospital VTE recorded during the index lumbar fusion admission and identify independent comorbidity predictors. METHODS: Adult (≥ 18 years) inpatient admissions undergoing lumbar fusion were identified in the National Inpatient Sample (NIS) from 2016 to 2022 using ICD-10-PCS procedure codes. The primary outcome was in-hospital VTE during the index admission.

title: Robotic mini-thoracotomy approach to aortic valve and ascending aorta replacement.
abstract: Fully endoscopic robotic-assisted aortic valve replacement has emerged as a safe, reproducible and effective minimally invasive approach with favourable clinical outcomes. In patients undergoing aortic valve surgery, concomitant ascending aortic aneurysms should be addressed whenever indicated, as failure to do so may lead to serious long-term aortic complications. Currently these patients must undergo some form of sternotomy to address both pathologies. The use of a totally robotic minithoracotomy approach for concomitant aortic valve and ascending aortic replacement has not, to our knowledge, been previously reported. This video tutorial highlights a robotic approach for combined aortic valve and ascending aortic replacement, representing a pioneering step in the evolution of complex robotically assisted aortic surgery. Our vision is to develop a robotic aortic surgery programme that maintains the safety, efficacy and durability of conventional techniques while significantly expediting postoperative recovery for selected patients.

title: Two-year patency rates of drug-coated balloon angioplasty for radiocephalic arteriovenous fistula juxta-anastomotic stenosis: A single-center study.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: The study aims to assess primary and secondary patency rates and the need for reintervention after drug-coated balloon (DCB) angioplasty performed for juxta-anastomotic AVF stenoses. METHODS: This retrospective observational study included patients who underwent DCB angioplasty for AVF stenosis between May 2019 and December 2023. Information on reinterventions was obtained from medical records, while AVF functional patency was assessed through Duplex Ultrasound Scanning. The primary outcomes measured were patency rates at 6, 12, and 24 months. RESULTS: The study included 69 patients. The average age was 61.4 ± 12.7 years, with 45 (65.2%) being male. Primary patency rates were 72.5% (50/69), 46.4% (32/69), and 30.4% (21/69) at 6, 12, 24 months, respectively. Secondary patency rates were 85.5% (59/69), 59.4% (41/69), and 46.4% (32/69). DISCUSSION: DCB angioplasty shows acceptable mid-term primary patency and sustained longer-term secondary patency for treating juxta-anastomotic stenosis in primary RC AVFs. Notably, the secondary patency rates indicate that re-interventions can help preserve the access circuit.

title: Severity-Based Triage for Direct Transportation to Nearest Comprehensive Stroke Center: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: The efficacy of endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) for acute ischemic stroke due to large vessel occlusion (LVO) is time dependent. Patients initially transported to a primary stroke center (PSC) may require secondary transfer, potentially delaying EVT. For severely affected patients, bypassing the PSC for direct transport to a comprehensive stroke center may expedite EVT but risks delaying IV thrombolysis. Effects of prehospital bypass strategies on functional outcomes are thus uncertain. METHODS: For this systematic review and meta-analysis, PubMed and Web of Science were searched until December 2025. Randomized and nonrandomized studies comparing transport to the nearest stroke center with transport to a more distant comprehensive stroke center in patients with suspected stroke were included. Two investigators independently screened records, selected eligible studies, extracted summary data, and assessed risk of bias. Random-effects meta-analysis was used to quantify associations between prehospital bypass, endovascular therapy, and functional outcomes. RESULTS: Literature search identified 1,991 distinct reports. Of 18 eligible studies, 2 were randomized controlled trials (RCTs, n = 1,540 patients), 11 before-after studies (n = 11,837), and 5 cross-sectional studies (n = 1,139), comprising a total of 14,516 patients (52% men/48% women). Risk of bias was high in nonrandomized studies. Patients undergoing prehospital bypass and control patients had similar likelihoods of receiving EVT (odds ratio [OR] 1.52, 95% CI 0.98-2.35) or thrombolysis (OR 1.12, 0.92-1.35). Prehospital bypass was associated with earlier groin puncture (median difference -63.9 minutes, 95% CI -84.1 to -43.7). Time to needle in bypass patients was longer than in control patients in RCTs (median delay 34 minutes, 23.1-44.9 minutes), but similar in nonrandomized studies. Functional independence (modified Rankin Scale 0-2) at 90 days was more frequent in bypass patients (OR 1.23, 1.04-1.45). In patients with intracerebral hemorrhage, bypass was associated with increased mortality (risk ratio 1.30, 1.02-1.64). DISCUSSION: For patients with LVO stroke, benefits of expedited thrombectomy may outweigh possible risks associated with longer prehospital transport times. However, evidence is insufficient to recommend the routine implementation of prehospital bypass protocols. Further research is needed to determine circumstances under which direct access to comprehensive stroke centers should be prioritized for patients with severe stroke symptoms.

Patients initially transported to a primary stroke center (PSC) may require secondary transfer, potentially delaying EVT. For severely affected patients, bypassing the PSC for direct transport to a comprehensive stroke center may expedite EVT but risks delaying IV thrombolysis.

title: Association of Prethrombectomy Hemorrhagic Infarction on MRI With Further Transformation and Functional Outcomes: A Multicenter Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Mechanical thrombectomy (MT) is the standard of care for acute ischemic stroke from large vessel occlusion (LVO). Although postprocedural parenchymal hematoma (PH) predicts poor outcomes, pretreatment hemorrhagic infarction (HI), defined as petechial bleeding within infarcted tissue, is traditionally viewed as a benign radiologic finding. Its significance on sensitive preintervention MRI remains underexplored. We evaluated whether pretreatment MRI HI is associated with 90-day functional dependence, post-MT PH, and symptomatic intracerebral hemorrhage (SICH). METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included consecutive patients with anterior circulation LVO undergoing MT at 2 stroke centers (2015-2022). Patients required pre-MT T2*-weighted MRI. HI was graded (types I/II) per European Cooperative Acute Stroke Study III criteria in blinded fashion. The primary outcome was 90-day functional dependence (modified Rankin Scale 3-6). Secondary outcomes were post-MT ipsilateral PH and SICH. We used multivariable Bayesian and frequentist logistic regression to adjust for age, sex, NIH Stroke Scale, baseline disability, comorbidities, infarct volume, and procedural factors. RESULTS: p p p Among 479 patients (median age 72 years; 46% female; 50% received IV thrombolysis), pretreatment HI was identified in 25 (5.2%), with excellent inter-rater agreement (Cohen κ = 0.9). Functional dependence at 90 days occurred in 47% of the total cohort, ipsilateral PH in 9.4%, and SICH in 3.1%. In multivariable analysis, pre-MT HI was independently associated with 90-day functional dependence (Bayesian adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 6.66, 95% credible interval [CrI] 2.15-24.28, Pr[OR > 1] = 1.00; frequentist aOR 5.95, 95% CI 1.91-18.52,= 0.002). Pre-MT HI also demonstrated a high posterior probability of association with post-MT ipsilateral PH (Bayesian aOR 2.76, 95% CrI 0.73-9.26, Pr[OR > 1] = 0.94; frequentist aOR 2.84, 95% CI 0.84-9.58,= 0.091) and SICH (Bayesian aOR 5.59, 95% CrI 0.63-34.92, Pr[OR > 1] = 0.95; frequentist aOR 6.02, 95% CI 1.00-36.11,= 0.049). DISCUSSION: HI detected on pretreatment MRI is an independent predictor of poor long-term functional outcomes and correlates with post-MT PH/SICH. Pre-MT HI may reflect significant blood-brain barrier disruption and microvascular fragility, serving as a marker of reperfusion vulnerability. Limitations include the retrospective design and the relatively low frequency of HI, PH, and SICH, which were addressed using Bayesian modeling to quantify uncertainty. Although not a contraindication to MT, identifying HI may aid in periprocedural risk stratification and serve as a candidate marker for future neuroprotective trials.

Although postprocedural parenchymal hematoma (PH) predicts poor outcomes, pretreatment hemorrhagic infarction (HI), defined as petechial bleeding within infarcted tissue, is traditionally viewed as a benign radiologic finding. Its significance on sensitive preintervention MRI remains underexplored.

title: Early-onset Pulmonary Embolism After Prolonged Combined Cosmetic Breast Surgery: 2 Case Reports and a Literature Review.
abstract: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) after aesthetic breast surgery is considered rare, and patients are often perceived as low risk. However, prolonged operative time and combined procedures may increase pulmonary embolism (PE) risk, and adjunctive liposuction may be a marker of procedural complexity and longer duration rather than an independent cause. We describe 2 women with intermediate Caprini scores who developed early-onset PE after prolonged combined cosmetic breast surgery (including adjunctive liposuction) and summarize relevant reports of thromboembolic events after aesthetic breast procedures. Procedures lasted 225 and 370 minutes, respectively. Dyspnea, chest discomfort, or palpitations occurred within 48 hours postoperatively. D-dimer was elevated, and computed tomography pulmonary angiography confirmed acute PE, including a saddle embolus in 1 patient. Therapeutic low-molecular-weight heparin followed by rivaroxaban led to clinical improvement without observed recurrence at the short-term follow-up. A focused literature review identified additional thromboembolic events after aesthetic breast surgery, most within the first postoperative week. Early-onset PE can complicate prolonged, combined cosmetic breast surgery even in patients classified as intermediate risk. Pharmacologic venous thromboembolism prophylaxis before symptom onset could not be reliably ascertained from available records. These cases support a protocolized, Caprini-informed pathway that specifies routine mechanical measures and clear indications, agent/dose, and timing for chemoprophylaxis, with explicit documentation and vigilance for early postoperative cardiopulmonary symptoms.

However, prolonged operative time and combined procedures may increase pulmonary embolism (PE) risk, and adjunctive liposuction may be a marker of procedural complexity and longer duration rather than an independent cause. We describe 2 women with intermediate Caprini scores who developed early-onset PE after prolonged combined cosmetic breast surgery (including adjunctive liposuction) and summarize relevant reports of thromboembolic events after aesthetic breast procedures.

title: Segmental arterial mediolysis: An underrecognized rare vascular disease requiring an interprofessional diagnostic and therapeutic pathway.
abstract: Segmental arterial mediolysis (SAM) is a rare, non-inflammatory, non-atherosclerotic arteriopathy that predominantly affects the visceral circulation and may cause dissection, aneurysm, hemorrhage, or ischemia. Its diagnosis is challenging because imaging findings overlap with fibromuscular dysplasia, vasculitis, connective tissue disorders, atherosclerosis, and mycotic aneurysm. This narrative review synthesizes the available evidence into an interprofessional diagnostic and therapeutic pathway. The proposed framework links radiological suspicion with structured exclusion of major mimics, multidisciplinary vascular assessment, treatment selection, management of hemodynamic instability, and longitudinal imaging surveillance. Conservative management is appropriate for stable patients without active hemorrhage, whereas endovascular treatment is generally preferred when intervention is required and anatomically feasible, with surgery reserved for failed stabilization or uncontrolled bleeding. Because current evidence is largely observational and case-based, the pathway should be regarded as a literature-based framework requiring prospective validation rather than a validated clinical guideline.

title: CCL19 emerges as a regional signal in human abdominal aortic aneurysm through targeted proteomic and transcriptomic profiling of the aneurysmal wall and neck.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIM: The molecular mechanisms underlying abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) progression remain incompletely understood and may vary across anatomically distinct regions of the diseased aorta. We hypothesised that the aneurysmal wall and aneurysm neck exhibit distinct molecular profiles, reflecting regional heterogeneity in AAA tissue. To this end, we characterized and compared targeted proteomic and transcriptomic profiles of these two anatomically distinct regions to identify molecular alterations associated with AAA pathology. METHODS: Paired aneurysmal wall and aneurysm neck tissues were obtained from 18 patients with AAA. Inflammatory proteins were quantified using the Olink Target 48 cytokine panel, with 45 proteins retained for analysis after quality-control filtering. Directional RNA sequencing was subsequently performed on matched tissue samples to characterize the expression of genes corresponding to the proteins included in the proteomic analysis and to assess concordance between transcriptomic and proteomic differences. RESULTS: Proteomic analysis identified three differentially expressed proteins (IL6, IL15, CCL19) between aneurysmal wall and neck. Transcriptomic analysis of the corresponding genes identified three differentially expressed transcripts (CCL19, CCL11, LTA). CCL19 was consistently elevated at both the protein and transcript levels in aneurysmal wall, whereas the remaining molecular alterations were specific to either the proteomic or transcriptomic analysis. CONCLUSIONS: Aneurysm wall and neck tissues showed largely similar inflammatory molecular profiles, with only a limited number of regional differences identified either on the protein or transcript level. CCL19 being the only concordant signal in both proteomic and transcriptomic analysis.

title: Evolving management of upper extremity pseudoaneurysms: Role of observation and nonsurgical management.
abstract: BACKGROUND: While the natural history and treatment algorithm of femoral pseudoaneurysms has been well established, the management of Upper Extremity Pseudoaneurysm (UEPSA) is not clearly defined. We sought to evaluate our 30-year experience and management strategies of this pathology. METHODS: We reviewed 93 patients that were identified utilizing ICD9/10 codes from an initial 384 patients with the diagnosis of aneurysm of the upper extremity from 1992 to 2023. Patients with UEPSA secondary to iatrogenic arterial interrogation were analyzed by duplex based follow-up until successful thrombosis or subsequent intervention was performed. Dialysis access pseudoaneurysms or trauma related UEPSAs were excluded for analysis. RESULTS: A total of 93 patients were identified with a UEPSA (39 brachial, 43 radial, 6 axillary, 5 ulnar arteries); 12 additional patients were identified who had only a patent neck at the time of formal vascular laboratory imaging and were excluded from treatment strategy analysis (11 radial, 1 brachial). The mean time between iatrogenic event and vascular surgery evaluation was 22 days. Fifty-nine (63.4%) underwent surgical repair, 27 (29.0%) received conservative management, and 7 (7.5%) underwent thrombin injection. Of the 93 treatment group patients that were analyzed, separated into sizes, patients with pseudoaneurysms less than 2cm there were a total of 21/93 (22.5%) patients managed conservatively, and 16/93 (17.2%) patients managed surgically; in contrast for those with greater than 2cm UEPSAs, 6/93 (6.5%) patients were managed conservatively, 43/93 (46.2%) were managed surgically, and 7/93 (7.5%) with thrombin injection. Comparing the first 15 years of the study period there were 27 iatrogenic UEPSAs noted with only 3/27 (11.1%) managed conservatively, while after 2010 there were 66 iatrogenic pseudoaneurysms with 24/66 (36.4%) managed conservatively. Of the UEPSAs managed conservatively, only 3/24 (12.5%) failed conservative management and were recommended to pursue intervention. CONCLUSIONS: Upper extremity pseudoaneurysms with significant symptomatic hematomas, suspected infection, and/or nerve related symptoms should undergo surgical exploration and repair. A consideration for conservative management of small pseudoaneurysms <2cm without the above presentation, observation and surveillance may be considered with more than 90% achieving successful spontaneous thrombosis.

We sought to evaluate our 30-year experience and management strategies of this pathology. METHODS: We reviewed 93 patients that were identified utilizing ICD9/10 codes from an initial 384 patients with the diagnosis of aneurysm of the upper extremity from 1992 to 2023.

title: Systematic Review of Clinical Outcomes With the E-tegra™ Stent Graft System for Endovascular Aneurysm Repair: Endoleaks, Limb Patency, Reinterventions, Aneurysm Sac Behaviour, and Mid-Term Follow-Up.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To systematically synthesize the published clinical evidence regarding endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR) using the E-tegra™ stent graft system, evaluating technical success, endoleaks, limb patency, reinterventions, aneurysm sac behavior, and mid-term follow-up outcomes. METHODS: Conducted according to the PRISMA 2020 framework, systematic searches were performed across PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, and the Cochrane databases. Observational studies and registry reports reporting clinical outcomes of adults undergoing EVAR with the E-tegra system were included. Because of cohort overlap and heterogeneous endpoint definitions, data were synthesized narratively and descriptively without formal quantitative pooling. RESULTS: Three eligible publications were identified, representing 209 unique patients across two underlying cohorts: the multicenter TIGRE registry (147 patients) and an independent single-center series (62 patients). Primary technical success was high, reaching 99.3% in the registry and 100% in the single-center cohort, with zero perioperative mortality across both. At mid-term follow-up (ranging from 18 months to 2 years), type II endoleak and iliac limb occlusion emerged as the primary complications. The TIGRE update reported 16 total complications (10.88%), including 8 type II endoleaks and 6 iliac limb occlusions, with a 2-year reintervention rate of 4.76%. In the single-center series, 1 type IIIa endoleak (1.6%) and 3 clinically significant type II endoleaks requiring embolization were observed. Favorable mid-term sac behavior was noted in the registry, with 72.11% of patients demonstrating >10-mm aneurysm sac shrinkage. Predefined anatomical hostility did not demonstrate a statistically significant association with adverse outcomes or reinterventions in the registry data. CONCLUSIONS: Early and mid-term evidence for the E-tegra stent graft demonstrates high procedural success and acceptable clinical outcomes with competitive mid-term complication and reintervention rates. However, the current literature is strictly limited to single-arm observational data with short-to-medium horizons (18-24 months). Long-term durability and structural performance relative to well-established companion platforms remain unestablished, highlighting the critical need for continued prospective surveillance and comparative, long-term multicenter trials.
englishSummary: OBJECTIVE: To systematically synthesize the published clinical evidence regarding endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR) using the E-tegra™ stent graft system, evaluating technical success, endoleaks, limb patency, reinterventions, aneurysm sac behavior, and mid-term follow-up outcomes. METHODS: Conducted according to the PRISMA 2020 framework, systematic searches were performed across PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, and the Cochrane databases. Observational studies and registry reports reporting clinical outcomes of adults undergoing EVAR with the E-tegra system were included.

title: The IMA-PLUS Score for Predicting Type 2 Endoleak After Endovascular Repair: Development and External Validation in European and Japanese Cohorts.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Prophylactic embolisation of infrarenal branch vessels has been investigated to prevent type 2 endoleak (EL2) following endovascular repair (EVAR) of abdominal aortic aneurysms (AAA), but patient selection is poorly defined. In this study, a computed tomography angiography (CTA) based risk score was developed and validated to predict EL2 after EVAR. METHODS: This multicentre, retrospective diagnostic study used prospectively collected data from the Zenith alpha for aneurysm Repair Registry (ZEPHYR) as the development cohort. Eligible patients underwent standard EVAR with pre-operative arterial phase CTA and at least one post-operative delayed phase CTA. The model was converted into a numerical score ("IMA-PLUS Score") and validated in two retrospective cohorts. Discrimination, calibration, and risk group thresholds were assessed. In validation cohorts, freedom from AAA expansion and EL2 associated reinterventions up to 5 years were analysed. RESULTS: Data from 245 patients of the ZEPHYR registry were included. EL2 occurred in 96 patients (39.2%). The IMA-PLUS Score includes inferior mesenteric artery diameter, number of infrarenal renal pole arteries, number of patent lumbar arteries, and median sacral artery patency, achieving a crossvalidated area under the curve (AUC) of 0.78. Using prespecified thresholds (low < 128, medium 128 - 200, high > 200), observed EL2 incidences in ZEPHYR were 19%, 59%, and 74%. In the Heidelberg cohort (n = 134; EL2 44%), AUC was 0.77 (95% confidence intervals [CI] 0.69 - 0.85) with EL2 incidences of 24%, 60%, and 89% across risk groups with good calibration; interobserver agreement for total score was high (intraclass correlation coefficient of 0.95). In the Tokyo cohort (n = 123; EL2 52.8%) AUC was 0.75 (95% CI 0.67 - 0.84); EL2 incidences were 36%, 76%, and 80%, with higher observed incidence than predicted. In validation cohorts, the IMA-PLUS Score was associated with AAA expansion and reduced freedom from EL2 associated reinterventions. CONCLUSION: The IMA-PLUS Score may support selection of patients for future studies on preventive management strategies.

In this study, a computed tomography angiography (CTA) based risk score was developed and validated to predict EL2 after EVAR. METHODS: This multicentre, retrospective diagnostic study used prospectively collected data from the Zenith alpha for aneurysm Repair Registry (ZEPHYR) as the development cohort.

title: Fenestrated-Branched Endovascular versus Open Surgical Repair for Elective Thoracoabdominal Aortic Aneurysms: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: This study compared outcomes between patients undergoing elective open surgical repair (OSR) and fenestrated branched endovascular aortic repair (FBEVAR) for thoraco-abdominal aortic aneurysms (TAAAs) through a systematic review and meta-analysis. DATA SOURCES: PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane. REVIEW METHODS: A total of 5 980 articles were screened following the PRISMA protocol. Primary endpoints were thirty day or in hospital major adverse events (MAEs) and mortality, and late all cause mortality. Secondary endpoints were thirty day or in hospital permanent paraplegia, stroke, bowel ischaemia, and new onset dialysis, as well as late re-interventions. A DerSimonian-Laird random effects model was employed to calculate risk ratios (RRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for binary endpoints. Significance was defined as a p value of . Risk of bias was assessed with ROBINS-I and evidence certainty with GRADE. RESULTS: 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 A total of 1 567 patients from five retrospective observational comparative studies were included. FBEVAR was used to treat TAAA in 824 patients (52.6%). Thirty day MAEs (RR 0.51, 95% CI 0.34 - 0.78; p = .002; I= 77.0%), mortality (RR 0.60, 95% CI 0.37 - 0.97; p = .040; I= 29.0%), and dialysis (RR 0.18, 95% CI 0.06 - 0.54; p = .002; I= 80.0%) were significantly less frequent among patients undergoing FBEVAR. Conversely, late aortic related re-interventions were significantly more common in the elective FBEVAR cohort (RR 1.80, 95% CI 1.04 - 3.13; p = .040; I= 18.0%). No statistically significant differences were observed between groups in thirty day or in hospital permanent paraplegia (RR 0.98, 95% CI 0.51 - 1.91; p = .96; I= 39.0%), bowel ischaemia (RR 0.46, 95% CI 0.09 - 2.33; p = .35; I= 81.0%), and stroke (RR 0.88, 95% CI 0.37 - 2.06; p = .76; I= 0.0%), or late mortality (RR 1.29, 95% CI 0.87 - 1.92; p = .20; I= 57.0%). According to GRADE, certainty of evidence was low to very low across outcomes. CONCLUSION: Elective FBEVAR was associated with a significantly lower incidence of thirty day MAEs, mortality, and acute kidney injury requiring dialysis compared with OSR. In contrast, elective OSR was associated with a significantly lower incidence of late aortic related re-interventions, whereas overall re-intervention rates were similar between groups.
englishSummary: OBJECTIVE: This study compared outcomes between patients undergoing elective open surgical repair (OSR) and fenestrated branched endovascular aortic repair (FBEVAR) for thoraco-abdominal aortic aneurysms (TAAAs) through a systematic review and meta-analysis. DATA SOURCES: PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane. REVIEW METHODS: A total of 5 980 articles were screened following the PRISMA protocol.

title: Endothelial Contributions to Venous Thrombus Resolution.
abstract: Deep vein thrombosis (DVT) is an obstructive vascular condition with an incidence of ~1 in 1000 adults per year. Complications of DVT include post-thrombotic syndrome, which is debilitating and painful, and pulmonary embolism, which is life-threatening. Current treatments for DVT are associated with increased risks of bleeding, infection, or re-thrombosis, and fail to accelerate natural venous thrombus resolution. Venous thrombus resolution occurs through a process of organization that involves thrombus retraction away from the vein, fibrinolysis of the thrombus, and the formation of vascular channels within and around the thrombus. Endothelial cell (EC)-lined vascular channels are present in rodent and human resolving thrombi. Rodent models of DVT show that thrombus neovascularization occurs as early as 3-4 days after thrombus induction and increases progressively thereafter throughout thrombus resolution. The extent to which thrombus neovascularization contributes to its resolution, as well as the source of the ECs that vascularize the resolving thrombus, are unclear. Circumstantial evidence suggests that neovascularization is driven by resident ECs that ingress into the resolving thrombus, while circulating endothelial progenitor cells (EPCs) promote neovascularization in a paracrine manner. Resident ECs and EPCs also contribute to thrombus fibrinolysis. The aim of this review is to describe the role of ECs and EPCs in DVT resolution, and the potential of promoting thrombus endothelialization and vascularization for the treatment of DVT. We will also outline knowledge gaps in the understanding of EC/EPC-mediated contributions to DVT resolution. The promotion of EC-mediated thrombus resolution represents a novel therapeutic strategy for DVT.

title: Pantothenate metabolic alterations in PROS1 mutation carriers and the antithrombotic effects of pantethine.
abstract: Background Patients carrying PROS1 mutations are at increased risk of venous thromboembolism (VTE). However, metabolic alterations linked to PROS1 mutations and their thrombotic contribution remain unclear. Objectives This study aimed to identify metabolic changes in PROS1‑mutation patients through integrated multi‑omics analyses, and to investigate the role of pantothenate derivatives in thrombosis using in vivo and in vitro models. Methods Serum metabolomics, siRNA‑mediated PROS1 knockdown in THLE‑2 cells, murine thrombosis models, and endothelial cell functional assays were employed. Results Patients with PROS1 mutations exhibited significantly reduced serum levels of pantothenate derivatives, particularly pantetheine. siRNA‑mediated PROS1 knockdown in THLE‑2 cells recapitulated this metabolic disturbance. In vivo, pantethine supplementation attenuated thrombus formation and platelet activation in murine models, accompanied by reduced serum levels of vWF and ICAM‑1, and increased TFPI. In vitro, pantethine pretreatment suppressed NF‑κB phosphorylation and reduced endothelial reactive oxygen species, counteracting IL‑1β‑induced procoagulant phenotype, leading to downregulation of vWF and ICAM‑1 and upregulation of TFPI and THBD. Furthermore, pantethine‑conditioned endothelial cells reduced responsiveness of co‑incubated platelets, including attenuated spreading, aggregation, and activation. These findings associate PROS1 mutation‑driven metabolic alterations with thrombotic risk, and suggest a metabolic‑endothelial‑platelet mode of interaction. Conclusions This study demonstrates that patients with PROS1 mutations exhibit reduced circulating pantothenate derivatives, and that pantethine attenuates murine thrombosis and modulates endothelial and platelet function in vitro. These findings identify a metabolic‑endothelial‑platelet association in Protein S deficiency. Whether PROS1 mutations directly cause pantothenate metabolic disturbance, and whether this disturbance mediates thrombosis, require testing in PROS1‑deficient in vivo models.

title: Incidence and predictors of suboptimal functional outcomes despite successful reperfusion in paediatric stroke: a cohort study from the Save ChildS Pro registry.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Successful vessel reperfusion with persistent clinical deficit occurs in 40-60% of adults undergoing mechanical thrombectomy but has never been characterised in childhood stroke. We aimed to determine the incidence and predictors of so-called futile recanalisation, in which the occluded artery is reopened but the patient does not recover good function, in paediatric mechanical thrombectomy for acute ischaemic stroke. METHODS: We retrospectively analysed prospectively collected data from the Save ChildS Pro registry, an international, multicentre, observational registry that included children aged 28 days to 18 years presenting with acute ischaemic stroke across 45 centres in 12 countries between Jan 1, 2020, and Aug 31, 2023. Patients who underwent endovascular thrombectomy and had successful recanalisation (expanded Treatment in Cerebral Infarction [eTICI] grade ≥2b) were included. The primary outcome was suboptimal functional outcome despite successful recanalisation, defined as a modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score greater than 2 at 90 days, on a scale from 0 (no symptoms) to 6 (death) on which 0-2 denotes functional independence; three additional thresholds (mRS score >1, Pediatric Stroke Outcome Measure [PSOM] >1·0, and PSOM >0·5) were analysed as sensitivity analyses. Adjusted associations between candidate predictors (age, baseline Pediatric National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale [PedNIHSS] score, baseline Alberta Stroke Program Early CT Score [ASPECTS], and final eTICI grade) and each outcome were estimated using Firth-penalised multivariable logistic regression. Save ChildS Pro is registered with the German Clinical Trials Registry (DRKS00018960). FINDINGS: 101 patients (54 [53%] males and 47 [47%] females; median age 11·0 years [IQR 6·0-15·0]) had successful recanalisation with 90-day follow-up and comprised the analytical cohort. A suboptimal outcome (mRS score >2) occurred in 18 (18%) of 101 patients. On Firth-adjusted multivariable analysis, lower final eTICI grade was significantly associated with suboptimal outcome (adjusted OR 0·44 [95% CI 0·23-0·84], p=0·012), and younger age was associated in the same direction (0·87 [0·78-0·97] per year, p=0·0098); baseline PedNIHSS score and baseline ASPECTS were not independently associated with a suboptimal outcome. Findings were directionally consistent across the three sensitivity thresholds. INTERPRETATION: In this analysis, 18% of children with successful recanalisation had a suboptimal functional outcome at 90 days, markedly lower than the proportion reported in adults (40-60%). Lower recanalisation quality and younger age were independently associated with suboptimal outcome, whereas baseline PedNIHSS score and ASPECTS had limited prognostic value. These findings highlight the need for longer-term studies and challenge the direct translation of adult prognostic frameworks to paediatric stroke, supporting age-specific approaches. Given the limited event count, these findings should be considered exploratory and require external validation. FUNDING: None.

title: Intravascular Lithotripsy in the Treatment of Heavily Calcified Femoropopliteal Arterial Occlusive Disease.
abstract: ABSTRACT: Severely calcified lesions of the femoropopliteal segment have always presented very complex conditions for endovascular therapy of peripheral arterial disease (PAD). In particular, the rigidity and instability of the heavily calcified vessel wall result in a limited initial lumen gain after angioplasty, frequent recoil, early restenosis, and an increased rate of reinterventions. In this context, intravascular lithotripsy (IVL) is increasingly becoming the focus of interest. By using low-energy shock waves, both superficial and deep intimal and medial calcifications are selectively micro-fractured. This leads to improved vessel compliance and enables effective angioplasty. At low inflation pressures of 4-6 atm, the barotrauma acting on the vessel wall during IVL is overall reduced. Randomized clinical studies demonstrate a higher technical success rate of IVL compared to PTA plus DCB-PTA, with a lower complication rate and significantly better 1- and 2-year patency. IVL can be used both as a stand-alone therapy and for vessel preparation in combination with DCBPTA, and also presents an alternative therapy to atherectomy, cutting, scoring, and high-pressure balloon angioplasty. This review focuses on the methodological description of the IVL with the Shockwave system in the femoropopliteal segment, considering both technical and clinical success data. KEY POINTS: · IVL enables effective vessel preparation in severe calcified femoropopliteal lesions.. · IVL works with low inflation pressures thereby reducing barotrauma, dissections, and bail-out stenting.. · Patency rates of IVL plus DCB are superior to conventional angioplasty plus DCB.. CITATION FORMAT: · Hölting MS, Bekker I, Stehr A et al. Intravascular Lithotripsy in the Treatment of Heavily Calcified Femoropopliteal Arterial Occlusive Disease. Rofo 2026; DOI 10.1055/a-2907-7766.

title: Image quality assessment of 40-keV virtual monoenergetic reconstruction in low-contrast lower-extremity spectral CT angiography.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Lower-extremity CT angiography (CTA) is widely used for the assessment of peripheral arterial disease. Reducing iodinated contrast medium is desirable, particularly in patients with impaired renal function. This study evaluated the impact of 40-keV virtual monoenergetic images (VMI) on image quality in low-contrast lower-extremity spectral CTA. METHODS: In this retrospective single-center study, 60 patients who underwent lower-extremity spectral CTA with 40 mL of iodinated contrast medium were included. Conventional reconstructions and 40-keV VMI were compared regarding vascular attenuation, signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR), iodine concentration, and subjective image quality across predefined arterial segments. Qualitative image quality was independently assessed by two readers using a 5-point Likert scale. RESULTS: Compared with conventional reconstructions, 40-keV VMI significantly increased vascular attenuation, SNR, and CNR across all arterial segments (all p < 0.001). Subjective ratings for vessel contrast, vessel sharpness, overall image quality, and diagnostic confidence were significantly higher with VMI for both readers across all evaluated arterial segments (all p < 0.05). Iodine concentration decreased progressively from proximal to distal arterial segments, whereas the CNR advantage of VMI remained preserved throughout the arterial tree. CONCLUSION: Forty-keV virtual monoenergetic reconstruction significantly improves quantitative and qualitative image-quality parameters in low-contrast lower-extremity spectral CTA compared with conventional reconstructions. These findings suggest that low-keV VMI may improve image-quality characteristics in reduced-contrast CTA protocols, particularly in distal arterial segments. IMPLICATIONS FOR PRACTICE: Low-keV virtual monoenergetic reconstruction may support reduced-contrast lower-extremity CTA protocols by improving image quality without increasing contrast medium volume. This approach may be particularly valuable for patients in whom minimizing iodinated contrast medium exposure is desirable.

Reducing iodinated contrast medium is desirable, particularly in patients with impaired renal function. This study evaluated the impact of 40-keV virtual monoenergetic images (VMI) on image quality in low-contrast lower-extremity spectral CTA.

title: Evaluating the Quality and Accessibility of Integrated Vascular Surgery Residency Program Websites for Prospective Applicants.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The COVID-19 pandemic prompted a shift to virtual residency interviews, although approximately half of integrated vascular surgery residency (VSR) programs have since returned to an in-person format. Amidst this evolving landscape, program websites have remained an invaluable resource for candidates to learn about VSR programs. In this study, we examined whether VSR program websites provide adequate and current information for residency candidates. METHODS: A list of all active VSR programs was obtained from the Association of American Medical Colleges (AAMC) Electronic Residency Application Service (ERAS) website. Each program's website was reviewed in November 2025, and data were collected regarding program structure, faculty and current resident rosters, application requirements, and publicly available formal policies. RESULTS: Of the 81 active programs, 80 (98.8%) had a formal residency program website. Information on residency program structure was reported in the majority of websites, including mission statement (91.4%), rotation and curriculum data (65.4%), rotating sites (61.7%), educational conferences (64.2%), and resident research experience (56.8%). Only ten programs (12.3%) reported resident operative volumes. Information regarding the residency program director (PD; 91.4%), program coordinator (PC; 92.6%), teaching faculty (92.6%), and current residents (81.5%) was available in most websites. However, with the exception of the PC (91.4%), contact information for the PD (40.7%), faculty (29.6%), and residents (13.6%) was not easily accessible. The majority of websites had a "how to apply" section (86.4%), but relatively few reported their interview dates (30.9%). Resident experience videos were available in less than half of websites (39.5%). Data on salary (53.1%), resident benefits (53.1%), vacation policies (27.2%), and academic conference policies (28.4%) were also inconsistently reported. CONCLUSIONS: Residency program websites remain a central resource for applicants, particularly in the current era of virtual and hybrid interview formats. In this study, we found substantial variability in the information presented across VSR program websites, with a notable lack of accessible contact information for program leadership, faculty, and residents. Enhancing website content and transparency may better support applicants as they evaluate programs and prepare for the residency application process.

In this study, we examined whether VSR program websites provide adequate and current information for residency candidates.

title: Feasibility of robotic-assisted surgery for nutcracker syndrome: a systematic review and single-arm meta-analysis.
abstract: Nutcracker syndrome (NCS) results from compression of the left renal vein, and refractory symptoms require surgical reconstruction. Robotic platforms provide magnified three-dimensional vision and articulated instruments that are theoretically advantageous for vascular dissection and anastomosis within the confined retroperitoneal space. However, the available evidence consists almost entirely of small single-arm case series, and whether robotic-assisted surgery represents a feasible treatment option for NCS has not been established quantitatively; previous systematic reviews were descriptive only, without quantitative pooling of proportional outcomes or stratification by reconstructive technique and age. To evaluate the feasibility of robotic-assisted surgery for NCS in terms of technical completion, conversion to open surgery, perioperative safety, postoperative recovery and symptom relief, and to explore whether heterogeneity was explained by reconstructive technique, age or sample size. Four electronic databases-PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, CENTRAL (Cochrane Library) and the Web of Science Core Collection-were searched from inception to 1 October 2026, and the reference lists of the retrieved articles and of earlier reviews on this topic were screened by hand. Eligible reports were original studies of robot-assisted NCS surgery from which quantitative data could be obtained, provided the series comprised at least three patients; studies of non-robotic procedures, non-NCS cohorts, asymptomatic nutcracker phenomenon, stent implantation by the endovascular route alone, narrative reviews, conference proceedings, single-patient reports and duplicate cohorts were not considered. Screening and data collection were carried out independently by two investigators, and study quality was appraised with the JBI checklist designed for case series. Stata 17.0 was used for the single-arm proportional meta-analyses: individual proportions underwent Freeman-Tukey double arcsine transformation before being combined under a DerSimonian-Laird random-effects model, with the summary estimates then expressed on the original scale, while continuous variables were harmonised to mean ± SD following Wan et al. and Shi et al. Cochran's Q test and the I-squared statistic were used to quantify heterogeneity. Subgroup comparisons were restricted to outcomes with substantial heterogeneity and were interpreted as exploratory analyses of study-level variation rather than as tests of independent effects. Ten studies comprising 140 patients were included (China, 4; USA, 4; France, 2; 9 retrospective and 1 prospective). Reconstructive techniques were left renal vein (LRV) transposition (5 studies, 45 patients), extravascular renal vein stent placement (3 studies, 29 patients) and renal autotransplantation (2 studies, 66 patients). Completion and conversion status could be ascertained in 111 patients from eight studies: 110 (99.1%) completed the planned reconstruction robotically and 1 (0.9%) was converted to open surgery; status was not reported for 29 patients in two studies and these patients were not counted as zero events. The pooled symptom improvement rate was 96% (95% CI 85%-100%; I-squared = 46.66%; 6 studies, 87 patients) and the complete symptom resolution rate 69% (95% CI 34%-96%; I-squared = 77.83%; 4 studies, 35 patients). The pooled incidence of Clavien-Dindo < 3 complications was 17% (95% CI 5%-33%; I-squared = 60.86%) and that of Clavien-Dindo >= 3 complications was 5.5% (95% CI 2.3%-9.8%; I-squared = 0%; 8 studies, 6 events); lymphorrhea/chylous ascites occurred in 15% (95% CI 0%-43%; I-squared = 79.16%) and postoperative reintervention in 3% (95% CI 0%-10%; I-squared = 0%). Pooled operating time was 204.52 min (95% CI 157.47-251.57 min; I-squared = 99.1%), estimated blood loss 54.21 mL (95% CI 37.56-70.86 mL; I-squared = 96.2%) and postoperative length of stay 2.72 days (95% CI 1.60-3.85 days; I-squared = 96.2%). Exploratory technique-stratified analyses suggested lower estimated blood loss, shorter operating time and shorter length of stay after extravascular stent placement than after LRV transposition or renal autotransplantation; however, several strata contained only one or two studies and these differences are descriptive rather than evidence of comparative superiority. Robotic-assisted surgery for NCS was associated with a high rate of technical completion among patients with ascertainable status, favourable symptom improvement and a low frequency of major complications. The apparent ordering of perioperative burden across techniques is consistent with differences in procedural invasiveness but may also reflect confounding by indication, centre effects and case selection. Owing to the single-arm design, short and inconsistent follow-up, absent patency data and very low certainty, these findings should be regarded as a pooled feasibility benchmark rather than as evidence of comparative effectiveness.

title: Interleukin-6, soluble interleukin-6 receptor, and outcomes after transcatheter aortic valve implantation: an exploratory biomarker substudy of a prospective multicenter cohort.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Severe aortic stenosis can be treated with transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI). Identifying clinical and laboratory factors that predict clinical outcomes after TAVI may facilitate more informed decision-making. We aimed to assess the incidence of major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events (MACCE) within 12 months after TAVI and long-term survival according to baseline interleukin-6 (IL-6) and soluble interleukin-6 receptor (sIL-6R) levels. METHODS AND RESULTS: In this biomarker substudy of a prospective multicenter cohort, we evaluated clinical outcomes after TAVI according to baseline IL-6 signal and sIL-6R concentration. We included only patients with an available baseline stored plasma sample. Patients were stratified into high and low IL-6 and sIL-6R groups. Two primary end points were analyzed: (i) 12-month MACCE, and (ii) long-term overall survival. Secondary end points included the individual components of MACCE. Stored baseline plasma was available for measurements in 62 patients who underwent TAVI between December 2018 and September 2021 across three clinical sites. Patients with high IL-6 had a higher 12-month MACCE risk in age- and sex-adjusted Firth penalized Cox regression analysis (HR 3.31; 95%CI 1.02-11.04, P = 0.0458) but not in unadjusted analysis (log-rank P = 0.07). The association was not robust to alternative cutoffs and the age- and sex-adjusted continuous analysis of IL-6 also did not show a statistically significant association (hazard ratio per 1-SD increase, 1.52, 95% CI, 0.86 to 2.46, P = 0.13). No significant associations were observed in the primary models between IL-6 and long-term overall survival or between sIL-6R and either primary end point. CONCLUSIONS: High IL-6 signal at baseline may be associated with increased 12-month MACCE risk after TAVI, although this finding was sensitive to IL-6 categorization and was not statistically significant in continuous analysis. Baseline sIL-6R concentration was not significantly associated with the analyzed clinical outcomes. These findings should be considered exploratory and hypothesis-generating.

title: Outcomes with Catheter-Directed Thrombolysis versus Mechanical Thrombectomy for Patients with Intermediate/High Risk Pulmonary Embolism: A Meta-Analysis of 24,090 Patients.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Randomized trials comparing the outcomes with catheter-directed medical thrombolysis (CDT) versus mechanical thrombectomy (MT) for patients with intermediate/high risk pulmonary embolism (PE) are limited. This meta-analysis aimed to assess the clinical outcomes after CDT versus MT for patients with intermediate/high risk PE. METHODS: Eligible studies compared CDT and MT for patients with intermediate/high risk PE underwent catheter-based therapies were retrieved from a comprehensive literature search for PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, and Cochrane CENTRAL through June 2026. Outcomes included all-cause mortality, major bleeding, and the length of intensive care unit (ICU) stay. Summary estimates were analyzed using a random effects model. RESULTS: A total of 18 studies (24,090 intermediate/high risk patients) were eligible for the analysis. CDT was associated with longer length of intensive care unit (ICU) stay (mean difference: 1.01 days, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.87-1.15) compared with MT. While there was no statistical difference between the two groups regarding the risk of all-cause mortality (risk ratio [RR] 0.88, 95% CI 0.76-1.01, p = 0.068) and major bleeding (RR 1.07, 95% CI 0.74-1.55, p = 0.705). Similarly, the incidence of other clinical outcomes; all-cause readmission, PE-related readmission, blood transfusion rates, length of hospital stay, cardiac arrest, and stroke, were similar between the two groups. CONCLUSION: Among patients with intermediate/high risk PE treated with catheter-based therapies, there was no difference regarding the clinical outcomes between CDT and MT, but CDT was associated with a longer ICU stay. Larger, well designed randomized trials are needed to confirm these findings.

This meta-analysis aimed to assess the clinical outcomes after CDT versus MT for patients with intermediate/high risk PE. METHODS: Eligible studies compared CDT and MT for patients with intermediate/high risk PE underwent catheter-based therapies were retrieved from a comprehensive literature search for PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, and Cochrane CENTRAL through June 2026.

title: GLP-1 receptor agonists for people with type 2 diabetes and peripheral artery disease: reducing uncertainty in clinical practice.
abstract: Peripheral artery disease (PAD) may be the most frequent first manifestation of cardiovascular disease (CVD) in type 2 diabetes (T2D). Management of PAD in T2D aims to improve symptoms and lower the high risk of major adverse cardiovascular (MACE) and limb (MALE) events. Drugs commonly used are lipid-lowering and antihypertensive medicines, antithrombotic and antihyperglycemic agents. The ADA recommends both GLP-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) and sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT-2i) as the first-line therapy to reduce the cardio-renal risk in people with T2D, including those with PAD. Meta-analyses of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) show that semaglutide is better than placebo in reducing by 30% PAD events in people with T2D (with or without PAD at baseline), although no RCT was designed to investigate PAD-related hard outcomes as a primary endpoint; however, both liraglutide and semaglutide may increase walking distance by approximately 25-30 m at six months in people with T2D and PAD. Cohort studies also confirm that GLP-1RA use is better than non-use in reducing by 28% the risk of MALE in individuals with T2D and PAD, although their retrospective design might introduce residual confounding and under-ascertainment of outcomes. Dedicated RCTs will obtain more direct evidence for the promising lower limb benefits of GLP-1RAs, but the scientific outlook of specific RCTs on hard limb events is empty. In the meantime, clinicians should choose a GLP-1RA of proven efficacy in subjects with T2D and PAD to improve their cardio-nephro-metabolic outlook, as well as their walking capacity, limited at present to liraglutide and semaglutide.

title: Risk of Venous Thromboembolism After Lumbar Spine Interbody Fusion: A Propensity-Matched Cohort Study.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is a feared complication after spine surgery, with limited data comparing approach-specific risk factors after lumbar interbody fusion. This study compared the rate of VTE complications after transforaminal lumbar interbody fusion (TLIF) and anterior lumbar interbody fusion (ALIF). METHODS: A multi-institutional electronic medical record database was queried for patients aged older than 18 years undergoing single-level or multilevel TLIF and ALIF between 2004 and 2024. Patients were evenly divided into single-level (n = 9,618) and multilevel (n = 1,774) TLIF and ALIF cohorts. Propensity score matching (1:1) was conducted using demographics, comorbidities, and anticoagulation use. Odds ratios (95% confidence intervals) of VTE and postoperative bleeding complications were calculated at 30, 60, and 90 days. RESULTS: Compared with single-level TLIF, single-level ALIF was associated with higher odds of VTE events at 30 days (OR: 2.0, 95% CI, 1.4 to 2.9; P < 0.001), 60 days (OR: 1.8, 95% CI, 1.3 to 2.5; P < 0.001), and 90 days (OR: 1.7, 95% CI, 1.3 to 2.4; P < 0.001). Multilevel ALIF was also associated with higher odds of VTE events at 30 days (OR: 2.7, 95% CI: 1.2 to 5.1; P = 0.015), 60 days (OR: 2.0, 95% CI, 1.2 to 3.4; P = 0.010), and 90 days (OR: 1.9, 95% CI, 1.1 to 3.2; P = 0.015) when compared with multilevel TLIF. No significant differences were observed in postoperative bleeding complications between single-level and multilevel TLIF and ALIF cohorts at all study intervals (P > 0.05). DISCUSSION: ALIF was associated with increased VTE complications, with no differences in postoperative bleeding complications when compared with TLIF. These findings suggest that surgical approach should be considered in perioperative VTE risk stratification and patient counseling after lumbar interbody fusion surgery, highlighting the need for future prospective studies evaluating approach-specific VTE prevention strategies.

This study compared the rate of VTE complications after transforaminal lumbar interbody fusion (TLIF) and anterior lumbar interbody fusion (ALIF). METHODS: A multi-institutional electronic medical record database was queried for patients aged older than 18 years undergoing single-level or multilevel TLIF and ALIF between 2004 and 2024.

title: Endovascular Treatment for Ruptured Internal Carotid Artery Pseudoaneurysms Secondary to Radiotherapy for Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma: A Retrospective Analysis.
abstract: AIMS: We aimed to evaluate the safety and efficacy of endovascular intervention in treating ruptured internal carotid artery (ICA) pseudoaneurysms secondary to radiotherapy for nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC). METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed consecutive patients with NPC and angiographically confirmed ruptured ICA pseudoaneurysms who underwent endovascular treatment at Nanjing First Hospital, Nanjing Medical University, between September 2016 and September 2023. After CTA or emergency DSA, the bleeding site and collateral circulation were assessed. Balloon test occlusion (BTO) was performed selectively when parent artery occlusion (PAO) was considered feasible. Treatment was individualized using covered stent implantation, coil embolization combined with a liquid embolic agent, or PAO. Outcomes included final angiographic hemostasis, recurrent bleeding, complications (analyzed as events when patients had more than one event), and the modified Rankin Scale (mRS) at last follow-up. RESULTS: Thirty-two patients were analyzed: 15 underwent coil embolization combined with a liquid embolic agent, 12 covered stent implantation, and 5 PAO. BTO was performed in 8 patients (25.0%): 5 tolerated BTO and underwent PAO, whereas 3 had inadequate collateral reserve and received reconstructive treatment. Final angiographic hemostasis was achieved in all 32 patients (100%; 95% exact CI 89.1-100%). At last follow-up, 28 patients (87.5%; 95% CI 71.0%-96.5%) had mRS 0-1. Six complication events were recorded across 32 procedures (18.8 events per 100 procedures): 4 recurrent bleeding events and 2 transient limb weakness events, graded as Medical Research Council muscle-power grade 3. One patient contributed both recurrent bleeding and transient weakness; therefore event rates should not be interpreted as unique-patient incidence. No severe complications were observed. CONCLUSION: Endovascular treatment achieved immediate hemostasis in this small, retrospective series of ruptured radiation-related ICA pseudoaneurysms. Treatment should be individualized according to collateral reserve, vascular anatomy, and the feasibility of BTO. Covered stents and coil-based reconstruction can preserve the parent artery but require close surveillance for endoleak, residual pseudoaneurysm, and new lesions. PAO may be considered only when collateral circulation is adequate; the zero-event estimate in five patients has a wide confidence interval. These exploratory findings require confirmation in larger prospective studies.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed consecutive patients with NPC and angiographically confirmed ruptured ICA pseudoaneurysms who underwent endovascular treatment at Nanjing First Hospital, Nanjing Medical University, between September 2016 and September 2023. After CTA or emergency DSA, the bleeding site and collateral circulation were assessed.
