title: Predicting prosthetic use and survival following transfemoral amputation for peripheral arterial disease: a retrospective cohort study.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: To examine associations between BLARt, CFS, prosthetic use and 24-month survival after unilateral transfemoral amputation for peripheral arterial disease. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 168 adults aged ≥65 years who underwent unilateral transfemoral amputation between 2019 and 2023. BLARt was analysed as a continuous score and CFS as an ordinal measure grouped as ≤4, 5 and ≥6. Prosthetic-use analyses excluded participants who had died by the relevant time point. Logistic regression, exact tests, ROC analysis, and Kaplan-Meier analysis were used. RESULTS: At discharge, 23 of 132 survivors (17.4%) were using a prosthesis; at 24 months, 17 of 80 survivors (21.3%) were using one. Higher BLARt scores were associated with lower odds of prosthetic use at discharge (OR 0.44, 95% CI 0.33-0.60) and 24 months (OR 0.51, 95% CI 0.37-0.69; both p<.001). Prosthetic use differed across CFS groups at both time points (p<.001), with no prosthetic users among participants with CFS ≥6. By 24 months, 88 participants (52.4%) had died. Compared with CFS ≤4, adjusted odds of death were higher for CFS 5 (OR 4.12, 95% CI 1.12-15.20) and CFS ≥6 (OR 8.40, 95% CI 1.97-35.80). CFS and the combined mortality model each had an AUC of approximately 0.71. CONCLUSIONS: BLARt was associated with prosthetic use among survivors, while increasing frailty was strongly associated with both lower prosthetic use and higher 24-month mortality. These measures may support multidisciplinary prognostic discussion but should not be used as rigid thresholds for prosthetic rehabilitation.

title: Medical Complications of Catatonia and Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome: A Systematic Review.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Catatonia and neuroleptic malignant syndrome (NMS) are related neuropsychiatric conditions linked to diverse and potentially life-threatening medical complications; however, no large-scale review of existing literature has described the types and rates of such complications. OBJECTIVE: We aimed to systematically examine documented medical complications associated with catatonia/NMS, delineate their clinical implications, and inform strategies for monitoring and improving patient outcomes. METHODS: Systematic searches of PubMed and Web of Science were conducted up to February 8, 2025 for articles including patients with catatonia or NMS who experienced medical complications. Reviewers independently performed screening and data extraction. Quality assessment was completed via the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. Case data were analyzed using descriptive statistics. RESULTS: 281 articles (11 observational studies and 270 case reports/series) met inclusion criteria. Eleven observational studies examined medical complications in 2,008 patients with catatonia/NMS; study quality was low in 1, moderate in 6, and high in 4. Across studies, pneumonia occurred in 0-64% of patients, rhabdomyolysis in 0-30%, and deep vein thrombosis/pulmonary embolus (DVT/PE) in 0-25%, with these complications reported in both malignant and non-malignant presentations. Comparative studies identified catatonia as a significant risk factor for specific complications including DVT and rhabdomyolysis. Case reports/series (364 patients; mean age 45.7 years) demonstrated widespread complications including rhabdomyolysis (n=178), renal dysfunction (n=105), respiratory dysfunction (n=78), respiratory infections (n=47), aspiration (n=36), pulmonary emboli and infarcts (n=43), cardiac dysfunction (n=37), and malnutrition (n=63). Overall 23.9% (n=87) of case-reported patients experiencing medical complications from catatonia/NMS died. Within this case-report sample, mortality rates appeared lower among those receiving benzodiazepines (n=26, 16.9% vs n=61, 29.1%) and electroconvulsive therapy (n=6, 7.3% vs. n=81, 28.7) compared to those not receiving such interventions. CONCLUSIONS: Catatonia/NMS carries high risks for multisystem complications and mortality, including in non-malignant cases and younger patients. Rhabdomyolysis, renal injury, respiratory compromise, and thromboembolism were particularly common. Among case reported patients, numerically lower mortality rates were seen in those who received benzodiazepines or electroconvulsive therapy. Clinicians should recognize strategies that may reduce risk for certain medical complications.

title: Amrecibart and cenvacibart for the prevention of catheter-related thrombosis (ROXI-CATH): a double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled, phase 2 trial.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Peripherally inserted central catheters (PICCs) are often complicated by venous thromboembolism, yet no thromboprophylaxis is approved. Factor XI (FXI) inhibition might prevent catheter-associated venous thromboembolism without increasing bleeding. We evaluated the safety and efficacy of amrecibart and cenvacibart for preventing venous thromboembolism after PICC placement. METHODS: ROXI-CATH is a double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled, phase 2 trial conducted across 12 hospital centres in Bulgaria, Canada, Israel, Romania, the UK, and the USA. Eligible participants aged 18 years or older undergoing PICC insertion, with the PICC expected to remain for at least 14 days, and an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 2 or less were randomly assigned (1:1:1) using a permuted block design and stratified by site and diagnosis of active cancer to receive a single intravenous infusion of amrecibart (300 mg; anti-FXI A2 domain monoclonal antibody), cenvacibart (250 mg; anti-FXI catalytic domain monoclonal antibody), or placebo. Participants, principal investigators, and study site staff were masked to treatment assignment. The primary efficacy outcome was adjudicated venous thromboembolism (symptomatic or asymptomatic PICC-associated deep vein thrombosis or superficial vein thrombosis, or pulmonary embolism, including pulmonary embolism-related death) up to day 14. Ultrasounds were performed on days 7 and 14. The key secondary efficacy outcome was adjudicated thrombosis detected by ultrasound in the upper extremity with the PICC up to day 14. The primary safety outcome was site-reported treatment-emergent adverse events up to the end of the study. The key secondary safety outcomes were adjudicated major and clinically relevant non-major (CRNM) bleeding up to day 14. Efficacy analyses were performed in the full analysis set, which consisted of all randomly assigned participants who received any study drug and with any evaluable post-baseline ultrasound or a confirmed episode of venous thromboembolism. Safety analyses were performed in the safety analysis set, which included all randomly assigned participants who received any study drug (as treated). This trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT06299111 (completed; these analyses were performed after database lock on May 6, 2026). FINDINGS: Between Sept 20, 2024, and Dec 19, 2025, 240 participants were screened, and 195 were randomly assigned to amrecibart (n=65), cenvacibart (n=66), or placebo (n=64). One participant in the placebo group who did not receive study treatment and had no evaluable ultrasound was excluded from the full analysis set. The median follow-up time was 100 days (IQR 100-103). The median age was 60 years (49-69), and 89 (46%) of 194 participants were female, 105 (54%) were male, and 192 (99%) were White. Adjudicated venous thromboembolism up to day 14 occured in 13 (20%) of 65 participants in the amrecibart group (odds ratio [OR] 0·37 [90% credible interval 0·18-0·65]), 13 (20%) of 66 participants in the cenvacibart group (0·36 [0·17-0·64]) compared with 27 (43%) of 63 participants in the placebo group. Adjudicated PICC-associated venous thromboembolism up to day 14 occurred in 12 (18%) participants in the amrecibart group (OR 0·30 [95% CI 0·14-0·67]), 13 (20%) participants in the cenvacibart group (0·32 [0·14-0·69]), compared with 27 (43%) participants in the placebo group. Site-reported treatment-emergent adverse events up to day 100 occurred in 45 (69%) participants in the amrecibart group, 42 (64%) participants in the cenvacibart group, and 48 (76%) participants in the placebo group. No participants had major bleeding up to day 14. CRNM bleeding up to day 14 occurred in two (3%) participants in the amrecibart group, two (3%) in the cenvacibart group, and two (3%) in the placebo group. Serious adverse events occurred in nine (14%) participants in the ambrecibart group, six (9%) in the cenvacibart group, and ten (16%) in the placebo group. One (2%) participant in the amrecibart group, four (6%) participants in the cenvacibart group, and two (3%) participants in the placebo group died; these deaths were assessed as not related to treatment by the respective investigators. INTERPRETATION: A single infusion of amrecibart or cenvacibart reduced the incidence of venous thromboembolism following PICC insertion, suggesting FXI inhibition at the A2 or catalytic domain as a promising prophylactic strategy for contact-mediated thrombosis. We evaluated the safety and efficacy of amrecibart and cenvacibart for preventing venous thromboembolism after PICC placement.

title: Global trends and intellectual structure in war surgery and combat casualty care: A bibliometric and science-mapping analysis (2000-2026).
abstract: BACKGROUND: War surgery and combat casualty care (CCC) research has expanded rapidly, yet its growth dynamics, collaboration structure, thematic evolution and citation-based intellectual architecture remain incompletely characterised. This study mapped war surgery and CCC literature to identify dominant, emerging and declining themes and influential actors. METHODS: A bibliometric and science-mapping analysis used Web of Science Core Collection records retrieved on 15 February 2026. Articles published between 2000 and 2026 were identified through a topic search combining war/CCC terms with conflict-setting anchors and refined to English-language journal publications in relevant clinical categories. Performance indicators and network analyses were implemented in bibliometrix/Biblioshiny, VOSviewer and CiteSpace. The corpus was partitioned into three time slices to assess thematic evolution and temporal keyword dynamics. RESULTS: The final corpus comprised 413 WoSCC records indexed as Article. Production rose markedly after 2009 and remained sustained, while mean citations per article declined in recent cohorts, consistent with shorter citation windows. Thematic mapping showed a stable core around trauma/CCC and haemorrhage, alongside diversification towards capability-oriented themes. Burst detection and frequency-ratio analyses identified prolonged field care, readiness, and endovascular and transfusion-related innovations as accelerating topics, while earlier intervention-specific terms declined. The collaboration network was hub-dominated, indicating a concentrated knowledge-production structure organised around limited high-intensity bilateral links. CONCLUSIONS: War surgery and CCC research is organised around a durable clinical core but is increasingly oriented towards system resilience under evacuation delays and resource constraints. Strengthening multi-country collaboration and sustaining inter-conflict research capacity are key levers for preparedness and civilian-military knowledge transfer.

METHODS: A bibliometric and science-mapping analysis used Web of Science Core Collection records retrieved on 15 February 2026.

title: The pathological role of chemokines and chemokine receptors in diabetic vascular disease.
abstract: Diabetic vascular diseases, which include microvascular and macrovascular diseases, are a common complication of diabetes mellitus. Both chemokines and their receptors are involved in the pathophysiological process of diabetic vascular diseases, given their diverse functions. Crucially, when evaluating these chemokine networks, it is essential to distinguish descriptive clinical and bioinformatic biomarker observations from functional causal mechanisms established through in vitro and in vivo interventional studies, as observational concentration changes alone do not inherently demonstrate a direct pathogenic role or identify a therapeutic target. In this review, we examine recent studies and provide an overview of the mechanisms underlying chemokine-mediated signaling in diabetic microvascular and macrovascular diseases. We conclude that while circulating chemokines primarily serve as diagnostic or prognostic biomarkers, specific functional chemokine axes represent viable therapeutic targets for diabetic vascular complications.

title: Pediatric spontaneous vertebro-venous fistula coil occlusion with vertebral artery preservation and distal vertebral artery flow restoration.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Vertebro-venous fistula (VVF) is a rare high-flow arteriovenous shunt between the vertebral artery and the surrounding venous plexus. Spontaneous VVF in the pediatric population is exceptionally uncommon. Prior pediatric reports have demonstrated successful endovascular fistula occlusion with preservation of vertebral artery patency, although the reported experience remains limited. OBSERVATIONS: A 9-year-old boy presented with an 8-month history of progressive cervical and upper thoracic pain without neurological deficit. MRI demonstrated a left suboccipital vascular lesion with bilateral vertebral artery enlargement and diminution of the distal left vertebral artery. Digital subtraction angiography confirmed a high-flow direct arteriovenous fistula at the V3 segment with a large venous pouch and absence of V4 visualization. Endovascular coil embolization achieved marked reduction in fistula flow with immediate restoration of V4 segment visualization. Follow-up angiography confirmed complete obliteration without residual shunting. LESSONS: Spontaneous pediatric VVF can be successfully treated by precise fistula-point coil occlusion with vertebral artery preservation. Timely and complete endovascular fistula obliteration can restore distal vertebral artery visualization while preserving the parent artery. This illustrates the potential reversibility of flow-related angiographic abnormalities in high-flow VVF.

title: Endovascular treatment of hepatic artery bleeding and pseudoaneurysms using stent-grafts: a retrospective single-centre analysis.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: To evaluate technical and clinical success rates and complications of stent-grafting for hepatic artery bleeding or pseudoaneurysms. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This single-centre retrospective study consecutively included 58 patients who underwent attempted stent-grafting for hepatic artery bleeding (n = 40) or pseudoaneurysm (n = 18) between January 2010 and June 2021. RESULTS: Technical success was achieved in 97% (56/58) of cases. Insufficient haemostasis after technical success was present in five cases (88% primary clinical success), decreasing to three cases after reintervention. In 3/5 cases, it was due to undersizing of the stent-graft, which occurred frequently, especially in vessel sizes ≥ 6 mm (n = 19, compared to the non-acute vessel diameter; n = 11, compared to the acute one). Median occlusion-free survival was 763 days. Patency rates were 81 ± 6% at 30 days and 56 ± 10% at two years. Early occlusion (≤ 30 days) was associated with significantly smaller stent-graft diameters (4.7 ± 0.7 mm vs 5.4 ± 0.7 mm; p = 0.014). In multivariate Cox regression analysis, a small diameter (4 mm) was confirmed as a risk factor for stent-graft occlusion (HR = 8.59, p = 0.006). Liver necrosis or liver failure due to insufficient collateralization occurred only in early occlusions. Median overall survival was 714 days. In 6/29 documented deaths, mortality was procedure-related (four because of insufficient haemostasis, with two after technical failure and two after technical success, and two because of fatal liver failure after stent-graft occlusion). CONCLUSION: Stent-grafting is effective for managing hepatic artery bleeding, but precise sizing is crucial, as undersizing and small diameters increase the risk of inadequate haemostasis and occlusion. KEY POINTS: Question What are the technical and clinical outcomes of stent-graft treatment for hepatic artery bleeding or pseudoaneurysm, and which factors influence these outcomes? Findings Stent-graft treatment achieved high technical and clinical success rates. Stent-graft undersizing and smaller stent-graft diameters were associated with inadequate haemostasis and occlusion. Clinical relevance Stent-graft treatment is an effective option for managing hepatic artery bleeding or pseudoaneurysm in critically ill patients. Accurate stent-graft sizing is a key determinant of clinical success.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: This single-centre retrospective study consecutively included 58 patients who underwent attempted stent-grafting for hepatic artery bleeding (n = 40) or pseudoaneurysm (n = 18) between January 2010 and June 2021. title: [Image-guided procedures for treatment of erectile dysfunction].
abstract: Erectile dysfunction (ED) is defined as the chronic inability to achieve and maintain erection sufficient for sexual intercourse. It is a common condition, affecting an estimated 30-50 % of men above the age of 40, and can significantly impair quality of life and interpersonal relationships. The most common vascular etiology includes arterial obstruction of the pelvic arteries and venous leakage. The goal of image-guided endovascular treatments is to restore adequate erectile function. Arterial blood flow to the penis can be achieved through endovascular revascularization and venous leakage can be treated by embolization. The studies published to date show that these minimally invasive procedures are effective and safe in carefully selected patients and treatment outcomes remain stable over the long term in most patients.

title: Saphenofemoral junction reconstruction and recurrence after the treatment of superficial venous reflux disease with endovenous ablation methods.
abstract: 2 p BackgroundRecurrence of varicosities and reflux-related symptoms after endovenous ablation of the great saphenous vein (GSV) remains common. Standard ablation is delivered 1.5-2 cm distal to the saphenofemoral junction (SFJ), leaving the junctional tributaries and dilated proximal junction untreated, unlike conventional high ligation and stripping. We compared standard endovenous ablation with a technique combining open SFJ reconstruction and endovenous ablation.MethodsWe retrospectively reviewed patients treated for symptomatic primary GSV reflux. Group 1 underwent standard endovenous ablation (at our institution or referred from elsewhere). Group 2 underwent open SFJ reconstruction - ligation of the junctional tributaries, division of the saphenous vein, and reduction of the dilated common femoral vein - plus endovenous ablation of the GSV trunk. The protocol was introduced during the study period and applied selectively and non-randomly; patients with a body mass index ≥30 kg/m, those aged ≥70 years and those with groin skin infection received standard ablation. Beyond a 3-month review, duplex follow-up was not standardised and was performed mainly when symptoms recurred. Symptomatic recurrence, recurrent visible varicosities, duplex recurrence patterns, reintervention and complications were reported separately.ResultsGroup 1 included 115 patients (70 treated at our institution and 45 referred after treatment elsewhere) and Group 2 included 203. Mean age was 54.3 ± 10.9 and 48.7 ± 14.8 years, and 62.6% and 71.9% were female, respectively. Group 1 had a higher body mass index and more diabetes, hypertension and smoking (all P ≤ .003). During follow-up, 18 patients in Group 1 (15.7%) returned with symptomatic recurrence, compared with 7 (3.4%) in Group 2 (< .001; adjusted OR 0.14, 95% CI 0.05-0.40). No Group 2 patient showed a patent refluxing GSV trunk. In Group 2, six patients (3.0%) had groin wound complications, four managed with wound care and two requiring surgical revision, and one had a minor groin hematoma; one Group 1 patient developed deep vein thrombosis. There was no pulmonary embolism and no mortality.ConclusionsIn this selected, non-randomised cohort, adding open SFJ reconstruction to endovenous GSV ablation was associated with an acceptable complication rate, at the cost of reintroducing groin wound morbidity, and with lower symptomatic recurrence than standard ablation. Given the baseline imbalance, potential referral bias and non-standardised follow-up, these findings show an association rather than a preventive effect. Whether patients at particularly high risk of SFJ/anterior accessory saphenous vein-related recurrence benefit from this approach should be tested prospectively.

title: MEX3B leads to aberrant expression of VCAN, aggravating the thoracic aortic dissection by contributing to the phenotype transformation of VSMCs.
abstract: In vitro Thoracic aortic dissection (TAD) is a lethal condition due to the risk of aortic rupture and malperfusion of arterial branches. Currently, effective treatments are unavailable due to the unclear pathogenic mechanisms; therefore, it is essential to explore the underlying mechanisms of TAD to find novel therapeutic targets. The present study aimed to explore the effects of Mex3 RNA‑binding family member B (MEX3B) on TAD pathogenesis. A murine model of TAD was established with β‑aminopropionitrile monofumarate and angiotensin II. Hematoxylin and eosin and elastic Van Gieson staining were performed to assess the TAD formation and fragmentation of elastic fibers. Echocardiography was applied to measure the diameter of thoracic aorta. RT‑qPCR, western blot, and immunohistochemistry were employed to detect the expression of phenotypic transformation markers of vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs). mRNA sequencing was performed to further explore the downstream factors of MEX3B. MEX3B was upregulated following TAD induction. Knockdown of MEX3B alleviated TAD formation, as evidenced by decreased diameter and hematomas of thoracic aorta, as well as the enhanced integrity of the aortic structure and decreased thrombi in the false lumens. Loss of MEX3B mitigated the TAD‑induced depletion and fragmentation of elastic fibers., small interfering RNA pool‑mediated MEX3B downregulation triggered VSMC switching from a synthetic towards a contractile phenotype. High‑throughput transcriptomics demonstrated that the MEX3B knockdown reduced the expression of versican (VCAN). MEX3B potentiated VCAN mRNA stability by binding to its 3'untranslated region. VCAN downregulation induced a contractile phenotype of VSMCs. In conclusion, the loss of MEX3B protected against TAD, potentially via its contribution to VSMC phenotype switching, which may be associated with the downregulation of VCAN. The present study preliminarily demonstrated the function and mechanism of MEX3B in TAD. These findings provide a theoretical basis for understanding TAD pathogenesis.

Currently, effective treatments are unavailable due to the unclear pathogenic mechanisms; therefore, it is essential to explore the underlying mechanisms of TAD to find novel therapeutic targets. The present study aimed to explore the effects of Mex3 RNA‑binding family member B (MEX3B) on TAD pathogenesis.

title: Case Report: Suspected Lower Limb Congestive Injury Associated with Decreased Compliance of the External Iliac Vein After Laparoscopic Myomectomy.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The incidence of lower extremity deep vein thrombosis following gynecologic laparoscopy is 4.0%, whereas postoperative well-leg compartment syndrome (WLCS) is much rarer, with a reported incidence of only 0.03%-0.20%. Both conditions can present with postoperative lower limb swelling and pain. We report a case of postoperative lower limb swelling and pain that suspected to be caused by venous congestion injury secondary to decreased compliance of the external iliac vein, a condition that has not been previously reported in the literature. CASE PRESENTATION: A 44-year-old woman underwent an 8-hour gynecologic laparoscopic procedure in the Lloyd-Davies position. Thirty minutes after surgery, she developed acute swelling, pain, and numbness of the right lower limb. Deep vein thrombosis was initially suspected, but treatment was ineffective. Unilateral well-leg compartment syndrome (WLCS) was subsequently considered, and her symptoms were relieved following supportive treatment, including dehydration therapy and elevation of the affected limb. Repeated review of the surgical video suggested lower limb congestive injury potentially associated with decreased compliance of the external iliac vein. The patient also experienced persistent postoperative symptoms resembling venous intermittent claudication, consistent with the clinical manifestations of impaired external iliac venous outflow. CONCLUSION: This case highlights the need for increased attention to the condition of the external iliac vascular sheath during gynecologic laparoscopic surgery. Swelling and thickening of the vascular sheath, resulting in decreased compliance of the venous wall, may lead to severe venous congestion injury of the lower limb and may require timely intraoperative intervention when necessary. This case may provide a reference for the clinical diagnosis and management of postoperative lower limb swelling and pain following gynecologic laparoscopic surgery.

title: Perioperative venous thromboembolism prophylaxis during penile prosthesis surgery without routine drain placement: a retrospective cohort study.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Patients undergoing penile prosthesis surgery are at elevated risk for venous thromboembolism (VTE), yet perioperative thromboprophylaxis is not addressed in current urologic guidelines and the safety of subcutaneous heparin (SqH) without drain placement remains unclear. We aim to evaluate the safety and efficacy of perioperative SqH for VTE prevention in penile prosthesis surgery performed without surgical drains. METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed all penile prosthesis surgeries performed at a single institution from January 2019 to January 2025 in which no drain was placed. Demographics, comorbidities, Caprini risk scores, VTE risk factors, hematoma incidence, and 90-day postoperative complications were compared between patients who did and did not receive perioperative SqH. RESULTS: The primary outcome of our study was postoperative VTE, with secondary outcomes including hematoma formation and 90-day complications. Of 524 patients, 85% were classified as high risk for VTE (Caprini ≥ 5). A total of 246 (47%) received perioperative SqH. VTE occurred in 0.7% (2/278) of patients who did not receive SqH, while no VTE was observed in the SqH group. Hematoma rates were similar between groups (SqH 2.0% vs non-SqH 2.2%; P = .920). Caprini scores and most comorbidities were comparable, though smoking (P = .043) and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) (P = .025) were more common in the non-SqH cohort. DISCUSSION: Implementation of VTE prophylaxis with SqH in penile prosthesis patients may reduce the risk of VTE in a high-risk population and is relatively cost effective and simple to implement. The main strength of this study is that it is the largest cohort of penile prosthesis patients receiving SqH to be analyzed. In addition, our patient population is unique in the lack of drain placement postoperatively. The study is limited by its retrospective nature and potential bias in reporting complications. The cohort of patients receiving SqH prophylaxis did not develop a VTE and adverse event rates were similar between groups suggesting a possible protective benefit without increasing postoperative complications.

title: Intra-arterial tenecteplase during thrombectomy for acute ischemic stroke: the BRETIS-TNK2 trial.
abstract: Intra-arterial tenecteplase during endovascular treatment (EVT) may increase first-pass recanalization and dissolve microcirculatory thrombi, but its efficacy and safety are uncertain. We hypothesised that this strategy would improve functional outcomes versus EVT alone. This phase 3, randomised, adaptive-enrichment, open-label, blinded-endpoint multicentre study aims to evaluate whether intra‑arterial tenecteplase improves clinical outcomes for patients with acute ischemic stroke. Patients with large‑vessel occlusion eligible for EVT within 24 hours of symptom onset were randomly assigned (1:1) to the tenecteplase group receiving intra‑arterial tenecteplase during EVT or the control group receiving EVT alone. The primary endpoint was favorable functional outcome. Of 380 randomised patients (192 in the tenecteplase group and 188 in the control group), primary outcome data were available for 190 and 186 patients, respectively. Favorable 90-day functional outcomes (modified Rankin Scale 0-2) occurred in 40.0% of the tenecteplase group versus 46.8% of the control group (unadjusted odds ratio 0.76, [95% CI 0.50-1.14], P = 0.19). This work suggests intra-arterial tenecteplase during thrombectomy did not improve 90-day functional outcomes in this population. (Funded by National Science and Technology Major Project and hospital-initiated grants; ClinicalTrials.gov registration: NCT05657444).
englishSummary: Intra-arterial tenecteplase during endovascular treatment (EVT) may increase first-pass recanalization and dissolve microcirculatory thrombi, but its efficacy and safety are uncertain. We hypothesised that this strategy would improve functional outcomes versus EVT alone. This phase 3, randomised, adaptive-enrichment, open-label, blinded-endpoint multicentre study aims to evaluate whether intra‑arterial tenecteplase improves clinical outcomes for patients with acute ischemic stroke.

title: [Right aortic arch with a true bicarotid trunk and aberrant left subclavian artery in an adult: Value of CT angiography].
abstract: We report a rare right aortic arch variant detected during neurovascular assessment in a 48-year-old woman. Arch-to-vertex computed tomography angiography showed three consecutive branches: a true bicarotid trunk dividing into both common carotid arteries, a separate right subclavian artery, and an aberrant left subclavian artery with a retroesophageal course. Neither a Kommerell diverticulum nor aortic dissection was identified. Focused questioning disclosed chronic dysphagia, without definitive evidence of vascular esophageal compression. No causal relationship with the presenting stroke could be established. This case underscores the value of multiplanar and three-dimensional imaging in distinguishing a true bicarotid trunk from a common brachiocephalic-carotid origin, identifying aberrant subclavian anatomy, and informing cardiovascular and neuroendovascular procedural planning.

Neither a Kommerell diverticulum nor aortic dissection was identified.

title: Concurrent Selective Serotonin Reuptake Inhibitor and Factor Xa Inhibitor Use Is Associated With Increased Transfusion and Periprosthetic Joint Infection After Primary Total Hip Arthroplasty Despite Tranexamic Acid.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs) impair platelet function, and concurrent SSRI and oral anticoagulant use has been associated with major bleeding in medical populations. We evaluated whether preoperative concurrent SSRI and factor Xa (FXa) inhibitor use was associated with higher transfusion and complication rates compared with use of either medication alone after primary total hip arthroplasty (THA) when tranexamic acid (TXA) use was standard. METHODS: Adult patients who underwent primary THA and received TXA on the day of surgery were identified in a large electronic health records database. The SSRI-only, FXa-only, and concurrent-use cohorts were independently 1:1 propensity-score matched to controls who did not have either exposure. The concurrent-use cohort was also matched directly to the SSRI-only and FXa-only cohorts. The primary outcome was allogeneic red blood cell transfusion. The secondary outcomes were surgical site infection (SSI), venous thromboembolism (VTE), periprosthetic joint infection (PJI), and revision THA at 30, 90, and 365 days. RESULTS: Compared with matched controls, SSRI-only patients had significantly higher transfusion, PJI, and revision THA rates at all timepoints (30-day transfusion risk ratio [RR] 1.44; 1-year PJI, RR 1.48; 1-year revision, RR 1.84; all P < 0.001). The FXa-only patients did not have higher transfusion or complication rates. Compared with SSRI-only patients, concurrent use was not associated with significantly different rates of any outcome at any timepoint. Compared with FXa-only use, concurrent use was associated with higher transfusion rates at all timepoints and higher PJI and revision rates at 90 days and one year (RR 1.54 to 2.12; all P ≤ 0.026). CONCLUSION: Preoperative SSRI use was associated with higher transfusion, PJI, and revision THA rates. Concurrent use exceeded FXa-only rates, but not SSRI-only rates, suggesting that SSRI use may be the more important perioperative risk marker. The use of SSRIs should be recognized during preoperative bleeding-risk assessment.

We evaluated whether preoperative concurrent SSRI and factor Xa (FXa) inhibitor use was associated with higher transfusion and complication rates compared with use of either medication alone after primary total hip arthroplasty (THA) when tranexamic acid (TXA) use was standard. METHODS: Adult patients who underwent primary THA and received TXA on the day of surgery were identified in a large electronic health records database.

title: VOLUME ADJUSTED CALCIUM ANALYSIS OF AORTOILIAC ATHEROSCLEROSIS AS A PREDICTOR OF AMPUTATION FREE SURVIVAL.
abstract: INTRODUCTION/OBJECTIVES: Pre-operative cross-sectional imaging guides surgical planning in vascular surgery. Despite the relationship between atherosclerotic burden and surgical success, no studies have adjusted atherosclerotic burden according to lumen volume. Given variability in vessel diameter and significance of aortoiliac disease, we developed a volume-adjusted calcium score (VACS) and evaluated its association with patient outcomes. METHODS: This single-institution retrospective study included 187 patients over nine years who underwent peripheral vascular intervention. Using TeraRecon, calcium and patent lumen volumes were quantified along a contiguous aorto-iliac segment totaling 10 cm generating a VACS. An intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) assessed inter-rater reliability. Patients were stratified into two groups. Primary outcomes were death at one year and amputation-free survival. Secondary outcomes were re-interventions and number of arteries treated. RESULTS: Intervention type did not differ between the two groups. Patients with higher VACS were more likely older, have CHF, COPD, or hypertension. Patient in the higher VACS group had greater number of arteries treated, subsequent vascular interventions, and one-year all-cause mortality. A Cox-regression model demonstrated a VACSgreater than 0.33 was independently associated with decreased amputation-free survival at one year (HR 2.24, p=0.019). CONCLUSION: In patients undergoing intervention for aortoiliac occlusive disease, higher VACS was independently associated with worse one-year amputation free survival. Incorporating patent lumen volume into VACS appears to capture a systemic atherosclerotic burden not fully reflected by traditional lesion-specific assessments.
englishSummary: INTRODUCTION/OBJECTIVES: Pre-operative cross-sectional imaging guides surgical planning in vascular surgery. Despite the relationship between atherosclerotic burden and surgical success, no studies have adjusted atherosclerotic burden according to lumen volume. Given variability in vessel diameter and significance of aortoiliac disease, we developed a volume-adjusted calcium score (VACS) and evaluated its association with patient outcomes.

title: Prevalence of concomitant aneurysms in patients with thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysms who underwent Fenestrated/Branched Endovascular Aortic Repair (F-BEVAR).
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To determine the prevalence of synchronous ascending aortic and peripheral arterial aneurysms in patients with Crawford extent I-IV thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysms (TAAA) undergoing fenestrated/branched endovascular aneurysm repair (F/BEVAR). METHODS: We performed a single-center retrospective review of prospectively collected data from patients with Crawford extent I-IV TAAA treated with F/BEVAR under a physician-sponsored investigational device exemption. The preoperative CTA obtained for device planning was used to measure the ascending aorta and bilateral common iliac (CIA), hypogastric (HA), and common femoral (CFA) arteries using centerline reconstruction. Bilateral popliteal artery (PA) diameters were obtained from preoperative arterial duplex imaging. An aneurysm was defined as a vessel diameter >50% greater than the expected normal diameter for that arterial bed, using references available from literature. Multivariable logistic regression included sex, obesity, race/ethnicity, TAAA diameter ≥7 cm, and prior aortic dissection. A sensitivity analysis was performed after excluding patients with prior aortic dissection. RESULTS: Among 249 patients (mean age, 70.8±8.6 years; 40.2% women), 177 (71.1%) had at least one concomitant aneurysm. Race/ethnicity was 75.1% NH-White, 21.7% NH-Black, 0.8% Hispanic, and 2.4% Other. Among evaluable patients, aneurysm prevalence was 12.0% in the ascending aorta (29/242), 62.8% in the CIA (140/223), 42.1% in the HA (98/233), 22.2% in the PA (51/230), and 9.6% in the CFA (22/228). On multivariable analysis, CIA aneurysm was associated with obesity, non-White race/ethnicity, and TAAA diameter ≥7 cm; HA aneurysm with male sex, obesity, and prior dissection; CFA aneurysm with male sex; PA aneurysm with male sex and prior dissection; and ascending aortic aneurysm with TAAA diameter ≥7 cm and prior dissection. After exclusion of 46 patients with prior dissection, concomitant aneurysms remained a common occurrence. CONCLUSIONS: Concomitant aneurysms are common in patients undergoing F/BEVAR for Crawford extent I-IV TAAA. Several associations remained significant after multivariable adjustment. These findings should be interpreted in the context of a single-center referral population, variable arterial-bed denominators, possible diffuse arteriomegaly, and residual confounding. The prevalence of PA aneurysm supports further evaluation of selective popliteal assessment; however, this study does not support a universal screening recommendation or establish an effect on management, outcomes, or cost.

The preoperative CTA obtained for device planning was used to measure the ascending aorta and bilateral common iliac (CIA), hypogastric (HA), and common femoral (CFA) arteries using centerline reconstruction.

title: Repair durability following fenestrated versus chimney endovascular repair for elective juxtarenal abdominal aortic aneurysms: a multicenter cohort study.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To compare repair durability following elective fenestrated endovascular aneurysm repair (FEVAR) and chimney endovascular aneurysm repair (ChEVAR) for juxtarenal abdominal aortic aneurysms using complementary procedural, imaging, and clinical outcome measures. METHODS: 2 A retrospective multicenter cohort study was performed across five high-volume aortic referral centers. Consecutive patients undergoing elective FEVAR or ChEVAR for juxtarenal abdominal aortic aneurysms were included. Baseline characteristics, technical success, endoleaks, secondary aortic intervention, aneurysm sac remodeling, and target vessel patency were compared. Repair durability was assessed by integrating proximal seal integrity, longitudinal aneurysm sac remodeling, and freedom from secondary aortic intervention. Continuous variables were compared using Student's t test or the Mann-Whitney U test, and categorical variables using χor Fisher's exact tests. Statistical significance was defined as P < .05. RESULTS: A total of 130 patients underwent elective repair, including 77 treated with FEVAR and 53 with ChEVAR. Baseline demographic characteristics, aneurysm diameter, and duration of follow-up were similar between groups. Technical success was comparable (98.7% vs 98.1%; P = .76), and target vessel patency exceeded 95% in both cohorts (P = .38). Type Ia endoleak occurred less frequently following FEVAR than ChEVAR (1.3% vs 22.6%; P < .001), with a lower incidence of all Type I endoleaks (Types Ia, Ib, and Ic) (7.8% vs 26.4%; P = .006). Secondary aortic intervention was also less common following FEVAR (10.4% vs 30.2%; P = .006). Progressive aneurysm sac regression was observed following FEVAR, with a mean reduction of 11 mm at 24 months, whereas ChEVAR demonstrated limited early regression followed by late sac re-expansion, resulting in an overall 2-mm reduction. Mean aneurysm sac diameter was significantly smaller following FEVAR compared with ChEVAR at both 12 months (55 vs 59 mm; P = .01) and 24 months (51 vs 63 mm; P < .001). CONCLUSIONS: Elective FEVAR and ChEVAR achieved similarly high technical success and target vessel patency for juxtarenal abdominal aortic aneurysms. During mid-term follow-up, FEVAR was associated with lower rates of proximal attachment-site failure, greater aneurysm sac regression, and fewer secondary aortic interventions. These concordant procedural, imaging, and clinical outcomes suggest that integrated longitudinal assessment provides a more comprehensive evaluation of repair durability following complex endovascular aneurysm repair than technical success alone.

METHODS: 2 A retrospective multicenter cohort study was performed across five high-volume aortic referral centers. Consecutive patients undergoing elective FEVAR or ChEVAR for juxtarenal abdominal aortic aneurysms were included.

title: Risk Prediction With a Type Ia-Oriented Proximal Neck Anatomic Severity Grading Score After EVAR.
abstract: BACKGROUND: We developed an exploratory Type Ia-oriented proximal neck Anatomic Severity Grading Score (Type Ia-ASGS) and assessed its association with postoperative type Ia endoleak after endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR). METHODS: We analyzed 304 elective standard EVAR patients treated during 2016-April 2024 with an Ankura endograft (Lifetech). Neck measurements were proximal diameter (A), distal diameter (B), and centerline length (C). The score assigned 1 point each for C ≤15 mm, max(A, B) >28 mm, and B - A ≥3 mm, and 2 points each for angulation >60° and calcification. The theoretical range was 0-7; weights reflected observed univariable associations. RESULTS: Mean clinical and imaging follow-up was 27.6 ± 3.2 months, with final follow-up in June 2026. Type Ia endoleak occurred in 14/304 patients (4.6%). Observed event proportions were 1.2%, 2.8%, and 28.1% in exploratory low (0-1), intermediate (2-3), and high (≥4) score categories (p < 0.001). Each point was associated with greater odds of type Ia endoleak (odds ratio, 2.78; 95% confidence interval, 1.80-4.29). Apparent area under the curve was 0.859 (bootstrap 95% confidence interval, 0.750-0.943). Individual event and censoring dates were unavailable for time-to-event analysis. CONCLUSIONS: The Type Ia-ASGS was associated with postoperative type Ia endoleak in this derivation cohort. Its heuristic weights and exploratory categories require independent validation before clinical use.

title: Managing Abnormal Uterine Bleeding During Anticoagulant Therapy in Clinical Practice.
abstract: Anticoagulant therapies, including heparins, vitamin K antagonists, and direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) such as rivaroxaban, apixaban and dabigatran, are crucial for the treatment and the prevention of venous thromboembolism (VTE). While DOACs offer improved safety profiles, their use, espe-cially in women of reproductive age, increases the risk of abnormal uterine bleeding (AUB), partic-ularly heavy menstrual bleeding (HMB). HMB, defined as blood loss exceeding 80 mL per cycle or causing significant life disruption, is associated with reduced quality of life and substantial economic costs. Women on anticoagulants report higher incidences of HMB, often requiring adjustments in therapy or additional interventions. Management strategies include the referral for a gynecological consultation, the adjustment of hormonal therapy and anticoagulant treatment, the administration of tranexamic acid, and the treatment of iron deficiency. The review underscores the importance of a comprehensive, personalized approach to managing AUB in women on anticoagulants to optimize both anticoagulation effectiveness and patient quality of life.

title: Temporal trend and geographic variation in anticoagulation of patients hospitalized with acute pulmonary embolism: the RIETE registry 2013-2024.
abstract: BACKGROUND: A recent U.S. study of initial anticoagulation in adults with acute pulmonary embolism (PE) requiring hospitalization found intravenous unfractionated heparin (UFH) use exceeded 50%. Guidelines, however, recommend low molecular weight heparin (LMWH) over UFH for most patients requiring parenteral anticoagulation. Use patterns in other geographic regions are unclear. METHODS: We analyzed data from RIETE, a prospective multinational registry of consecutive patients with venous thromboembolism. We included adults hospitalized for acute PE from 2013 through 2024 in 273 hospitals across 31 countries. We assessed temporal trend and regional variation in initial anticoagulation. Using multivariable regression, we identified variables independently associated with UFH. RESULTS: Among 36,210 adults, 83.2% received subcutaneous LMWH, 7.1% UFH, and 6.8% direct oral anticoagulants. LMWH use decreased slightly from 2013 to 2024 (85.8% to 79.2%; unadjusted), while UFH increased (8.9% to 10.4%). Wide geographic variation was observed in overall use of LMWH (37%--95%) and UFH (2%--39%). When adjusted for demographic and clinical covariates, increased weight, recent surgery, recent major bleeding, severe anemia, thrombocytopenia, severe renal dysfunction, abnormal vital signs, and early reperfusion therapy were positively associated, whereas age >80 years, active cancer, chronic lung disease, prior ischemic stroke, and year were negatively associated with UFH. Compared with Spanish hospitals, hospitals in other European countries, the United States, and Asia were independently associated with UFH use. CONCLUSIONS: Results highlight opportunities for some geographic regions to align anticoagulation practices more closely with evidence-based guidelines recommending LMWH as the preferred parenteral agent in most patients with PE requiring hospitalization.

title: Association between nasogastric tube placement and self-reported anxiety/depression symptoms in patients receiving endovascular thrombectomy for large vessel occlusion: A post-hoc analysis of the ENCHANTED2/MT trial.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Post-stroke anxiety and depression are common after endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) for large vessel occlusion (LVO) and impair long-term recovery. Nasogastric tube (NGT) placement marks severe dysphagia and illness, but its association with anxiety or depression remains unclear. We aimed to evaluate whether NGT placement is associated with the presence and severity of 90-day self-reported anxiety/depression symptoms after successful EVT. METHODS: We performed a post-hoc analysis of the ENCHANTED2/MT multicentre randomized controlled trial, including patients with anterior-circulation LVO who achieved successful reperfusion and had complete 90-day EQ-5D-3 L data. Participants were stratified by in-hospital NGT placement (No-NGT group vs. NGT group). The primary outcome was self-reported anxiety/depression assessed by the EQ-5D-3 L dimension (no, moderate, or extreme symptoms). We explored the association between NGT placement and the proportion and severity of self-reported anxiety/depression using propensity score matching (PSM) and logistic regression, and performed exploratory subgroup analyses. RESULTS: Of 575 patients, 280(48.7%) received an NGT. Before matching, the proportion reporting self-reported anxiety/depression symptoms was 38.6% in the NGT group versus 15.6% in the no-NGT group (unadjusted OR3.40, 95%CI 2.30-5.09). After adjustment for measured clinical covariates, the association remained significant (adjusted OR2.97, 95%CI 1.93-4.63; ordinal OR3.06, 95%CI 1.99-4.77). After PSM, 175 patients were matched in each group; NGT placement remained associated with higher odds of self-reported anxiety/depression symptoms (37.7% vs 21.1%; OR2.26, 95%CI 1.41-3.65; ordinal OR2.25, 95%CI 1.41-3.63). In exploratory subgroup analyses, the association appeared more pronounced in patients with admission NIHSS ≤ 15 (OR3.83, 95% CI1.82-8.07; P for interaction = 0.049). CONCLUSION: In this post-hoc analysis, NGT placement was associated with higher odds of self-reported anxiety/depression symptoms.NGT requirement may identify patients who deserve closer psychological assessment.

Nasogastric tube (NGT) placement marks severe dysphagia and illness, but its association with anxiety or depression remains unclear. title: Predictors of longer recognition time in acute aortic dissection: a retrospective observational study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Acute aortic dissection (AAD) carries a high mortality risk closely tied to diagnostic timeliness. Delays remain prevalent, driven by atypical presentations-particularly in patients without a chief complaint of pain. This study identified predictors of a longer recognition time, as indicated by prolonged door-to-CT times, and developed a cumulative prediction model for patients presenting without pain complaints. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective study of 197 adult patients diagnosed with AAD at a tertiary emergency department (ED) from 2016 to 2023. Patients were classified as having a shorter (< 74 min) or longer (≥ 74 min; cohort median) door-to-CT completion time. Predictors were identified by least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO)-penalized logistic regression and decision tree analysis. A subgroup analysis characterized pain-complaint-free patients using a stepwise identification algorithm. RESULTS: A longer door-to-CT time was associated with female sex, older age, and physiological instability. The strongest multivariable predictors were absence of abrupt pain (odds ratio [OR] 2.81, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.47-5.46) and non-severe triage classification (OR 4.70, 95% CI 1.71-15.29). Dyspnea (OR 2.14) and elevated diastolic blood pressure (OR 1.02/mmHg) also independently predicted a longer door-to-CT time. Among pain-complaint-free patients (n = 46), a stepwise combination of mediastinal widening on chest radiography, Charlson Comorbidity Index ≥ 3, and Shock Index > 1.0 was present in all identified cases (cumulative case coverage 46/46; 95% CI 92.3%-100%). CONCLUSION: This study identifies a high-risk profile for a longer recognition time of AAD, particularly in older female patients and those presenting without sudden pain. For patients unable to report pain, chest radiography, shock index, and comorbidity burden may be considered to help identify atypical presentations warranting urgent evaluation.

title: Real-world safety of intrasaccular flow disruption for unruptured cerebral aneurysms: a multicenter analysis of on-label versus off-label aneurysm location treatment in the NeuroVascular Quality Initiative-Quality Outcomes Database registry.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Intrasaccular flow disruption (IFD) has been shown to be safe and efficacious in the treatment of unruptured cerebral aneurysms. However, previous studies were typically performed at large-volume centers, were carefully curated, and devices were used in on-label locations. The purpose of this study was to examine IFD safety using real-world data, in both on-label and off-label aneurysm locations. METHODS: The NeuroVascular Quality Initiative-Quality Outcomes Database registry was analyzed for all unruptured aneurysms treated with IFD. On-label versus off-label treatment locations were compared. The primary outcome was the modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score at discharge. Secondary outcomes included intraoperative complications, mRS score at last follow-up, and aneurysm occlusion status. Direct comparisons between groups were performed first, and results were confirmed with propensity score matching. RESULTS: There were 329 (82%) on-label aneurysm location treatments and 72 (18%) off-label treatments. The mean patient age was 64.6 years (range 27-86 years). On-label aneurysms were slightly larger than off-label aneurysms, with a mean maximum dimension of 6.9 mm versus 6.2 mm (p = 0.041). Otherwise, there were no significant differences in group characteristics. The mean follow-up was 512 days. There was no significant difference for the primary outcome of mRS score at discharge (mRS score ≤ 2: 94.1% on-label vs 97.5% off-label, p = 0.615). There were no significant differences for secondary outcomes including any intraoperative complication (3.6% vs 2.8%, p > 0.999), mRS score at last follow-up, and aneurysm occlusion status at discharge (Raymond-Roy class 1: 54.1% vs 56%, p = 0.929). There were significant missing data for occlusion status at the last follow-up, precluding analysis. Propensity score matching yielded 68 patients in each group and confirmed no significant differences for primary and secondary outcomes. CONCLUSIONS: This largest-to-date prospective registry study supports the overall safety of IFD treatment for unruptured cerebral aneurysms in both on-label and off-label aneurysm locations. Questions remain regarding long-term efficacy due to current follow-up data limitations in the registry.

title: Pediatric cerebral arteriovenous malformation: an institutional experience from 25 years of treatment.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: In pediatric cerebral arteriovenous malformation (AVM), the long-term outcome data are scarce. The aim of this study was to analyze the clinical and radiological long-term outcomes from an institutional experience of children and adolescents treated for AVM over 25 years. METHODS: The authors reviewed clinical and radiological data from a consecutive series of patients (age ≤ 18 years) treated for AVM at a single institution from 2000 to 2024, with at least 1 year of follow-up. RESULTS: Overall, 96 patients were treated for AVM (48 males and 48 females, mean age 12.8 ± 4.8 years). Spetzler-Martin grades were I in 18 patients (19.4%), II in 33 (35.5%), and III in 30 (32.3%), and 14.6% of patients had an infratentorial location. Overall, 8.3% of patients were asymptomatic and 54.2% presented with hemorrhage. Moreover, 11.5% of patients experienced new or repeated hemorrhage during the initial observation or ongoing treatment. The stand-alone treatment was microsurgery in 38.5% of patients, radiosurgery in 28.1%, and embolization in 2.1%, while 9.4% of patients were treated conservatively. The treatment was multimodal in 21.9% and repeated in 49.4% of patients. The obliteration rate in patients with completed treatment (n = 75) was 80% (higher in those presenting with hemorrhage: 91.1% vs 63.3%, p = 0.003). The obliteration rate was 88.6% after microsurgery and 57.9% after radiosurgery (higher in the hemorrhagic group: 87.5% vs 36.4%, p = 0.026). Recurrence occurred in 8.3% of patients at a median of 60 months (range 36-68 months), and following microsurgery in all cases. A favorable clinical outcome (modified Rankin Scale scores 0-2) was achieved in 83.2% of patients, nonsignificantly less in those with hemorrhagic presentation (76.5% vs 90.9%, p = 0.061). The overall mortality rate was 5.3%, without a significant difference between the hemorrhagic and nonhemorrhagic groups. Hydrocephalus, hemorrhage volume, nidus size, infratentorial location, and Spetzler-Martin, supplementary, and combined grades were negative predictors of a good outcome in the univariate analysis, with the combined grade being the strongest predictor. Hemorrhage was a strong predictor of obliteration in the multivariate model, whereas radiosurgery and the number of treatments were predictors of nonobliteration. CONCLUSIONS: Although more than half of children and adolescents with AVM presented with hemorrhage, most patients had a favorable clinical outcome. In our experience, microsurgery and radiosurgery resulted in the highest obliteration rates, particularly in hemorrhagic cases, while the role of endovascular treatment was only supplementary.

The aim of this study was to analyze the clinical and radiological long-term outcomes from an institutional experience of children and adolescents treated for AVM over 25 years. METHODS: The authors reviewed clinical and radiological data from a consecutive series of patients (age ≤ 18 years) treated for AVM at a single institution from 2000 to 2024, with at least 1 year of follow-up.

title: Association Between Intradialytic Foot Temperature Gradients and Severe Peripheral Artery Disease in Patients Undergoing Hemodialysis: Prospective Cohort Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Peripheral artery disease (PAD) is prevalent in hemodialysis (HD) patients but remains difficult to diagnose due to unreliable ankle-brachial index (ABI) measurements caused by vascular calcification. We hypothesized that monitoring foot temperatures and their changes during HD, provoked by hemodynamic shifts, could serve as a novel diagnostic tool for detecting severe PAD. OBJECTIVE: This study aims to evaluate the diagnostic utility of intradialytic foot temperature monitoring using wearable mobile health (mHealth) sensors for detecting severe PAD in patients undergoing HD. METHODS: In this prospective observational study, we recruited 109 patients undergoing chronic maintenance HD. Skin temperatures were monitored continuously at the instep and sole during HD sessions using wearable sensors (Temp Pal, iWEECARE Co, Ltd), which are wireless, nanochip-based mHealth thermometers with ±0.05 °C accuracy. The diagnostic performance of temperature parameters, specifically the temperature difference between the wrist and foot at the end of HD, was evaluated against vascular duplex ultrasound (DUS). Severe PAD was defined as abnormal (monophasic or absent) flow in the distal posterior tibial artery (PTA) or anterior tibial artery (ATA). RESULTS: Patients with abnormal tibial flow on DUS exhibited significantly different temperature gradients between the wrist and foot at the end of dialysis compared to those with normal flow. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis demonstrated that the wrist-foot temperature difference at the sole effectively discriminated abnormal ATA flow (area under the curve [AUC] 64.5%, 95% CI 57.8%-70.9%) and abnormal PTA flow (AUC 62.0%, 95% CI 55.2%-68.5%). Notably, an instep wrist-foot temperature difference cutoff of -2.2 °C or less yielded a specificity of 97.6% (95% CI 94.0%-99.3%) for detecting abnormal PTA flow. CONCLUSIONS: Intradialytic foot temperature monitoring, particularly the temperature gradient between the wrist and foot, significantly correlates with severe tibial artery flow abnormalities. This method offers an accessible, noninvasive screening adjunct to the ABI for detecting severe PAD in the HD population. These findings indicate an association rather than a standalone diagnostic test; given the modest discriminative ability, external validation is warranted.

title: Evaluating the Performance of Large Language Models in Vascular Surgery Cases: Cross-Sectional Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Large language models (LLMs) such as ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude are increasingly used by clinicians, yet their accuracy, safety, and consistency in clinical cases remain poorly defined. Most studies assess LLMs using multiple-choice questions rather than free-response reasoning. OBJECTIVE: The primary objective of this study was to evaluate the performance and safety of 3 widely used LLMs in realistic vascular surgery scenarios in key domains such as diagnosis, investigation, and multidisciplinary and multimodal management. The secondary objective of this study was to evaluate the safety of the models' outputs. METHODS: t A total of 42 fictitious vascular cases across 5 major pathologies (acute limb ischemia [ALI], aortopathy, chronic limb ischemia, diabetic foot infection, and extracranial cerebrovascular disease) were independently entered into GPT-5, Gemini 2.5, and Claude Sonnet 4.5 using standardized prompts. Each model answered structured questions covering diagnosis, investigation, and management (both operative and nonoperative). Responses were scored out of 20 by a panel using a predefined rubric. Each plan's overall safety was separately assessed. Comparative analyses used 2-tailedtests, ANOVA, and multivariable logistic regression. RESULTS: P P P P Mean composite scores by model were 86.5% for ChatGPT, 83.5% for Gemini, and 88.0% for Claude, whereas scores by disease were 82.7% for ALI, 83.8% for aortopathy, 85.9% for chronic limb ischemia, 86.1% for diabetic foot infection, and 80.7% for extracranial cerebrovascular disease (>.05 in each case). Unsafe plans were generated in 11.9%, 23.8%, and 7.1% of cases by ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude, respectively. On multivariable analysis, independent predictors of unsafe outputs were lower composite score (odds ratio [OR] 0.471, 95% CI 0.306-0.722;=.001), higher word count (OR 1.003, 95% CI 1.001-1.005;=.001), and ALI (OR 20.9, 95% CI 3.79-61.8;<.001). CONCLUSIONS: Our findings demonstrate LLMs' promise in managing routine vascular surgery cases. However, their inconsistent safety profiles and ethical limitations preclude unsupervised clinical use. Rigorous specialty-specific validation is essential before they may be integrated into routine practice.

title: Effects of angiotensin receptor blockers on aortic growth and clinical events in Marfan syndrome: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
abstract: Thoracic aortic aneurysm (TAA) is a major cause of aortic dissection and premature mortality in Marfan syndrome. Angiotensin receptor blockers (ARBs) may slow aortic enlargement, but their effects on clinical and imaging outcomes remain uncertain. The aim of the study is to evaluate the effects of ARBs on clinical events and aortic growth in patients with Marfan syndrome. We searched the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, Ovid MEDLINE, PubMed, and Web of Science through February 1, 2025. Acute aortic dissection and all-cause mortality were the primary outcomes. Binary outcomes were analyzed using both Mantel-Haenszel common-effect (MH-CE) and inverse-variance random-effects (IV-RE) models. For outcomes with an event incidence below 10% in every contributing study, the MH-CE estimate was emphasized and the IV-RE estimate was treated as a sensitivity analysis. Continuous outcomes were analyzed using IV-RE models. All analyses were conducted with the meta package in R (v4.3.2). Seven randomized controlled trials involving 1522 patients with Marfan syndrome were included in the main analysis. For acute aortic dissection, the MH-CE estimate was RR 0·62 (95% CI 0·24-1·59) and the IV-RE estimate was RR 0·62 (95% CI 0·20-1·92). For all-cause mortality, the corresponding estimates were RR 0·53 (95% CI 0·17-1·64) and RR 0·58 (95% CI 0·16-2·07). Confidence intervals were wide and crossed unity. ARBs were associated with less aortic-root growth measured by MRI (MD - 0·48 mm/year, 95% CI - 0·89 to - 0·08) and by echocardiography over 3 years (MD - 0·51 mm/3 years, 95% CI - 0·85 to - 0·17), whereas annual echocardiographic measurement showed no significant difference (MD - 0·06 mm/year, 95% CI - 0·22 to 0·10). No significant effect was observed on ascending-aortic diameter, aortic Z-score at 3 years, aortic surgery, or serious adverse events. No statistically significant effect modification was detected in exploratory subgroup analyses. In patients with Marfan syndrome, ARB therapy was associated with small reductions in aortic-root growth in selected imaging analyses but did not significantly reduce acute aortic dissection or all-cause mortality. Sparse events, wide confidence intervals, and limited follow-up preclude firm conclusions regarding clinical benefit. Adequately powered, long-term trials with standardized imaging and clinical outcomes are required.

Angiotensin receptor blockers (ARBs) may slow aortic enlargement, but their effects on clinical and imaging outcomes remain uncertain. The aim of the study is to evaluate the effects of ARBs on clinical events and aortic growth in patients with Marfan syndrome.

title: Percutaneous Transmural Arterial Bypass for Recurrent Superficial Femoral Artery Chronic Total Occlusion.
abstract: IMAGE: Fluoroscopic angiography and duplex ultrasound. CASE SUMMARY: A 73-year-old man with Rutherford class IV chronic limb-threatening ischemia had a recurrent, heavily calcified superficial femoral artery chronic total occlusion despite multiple prior endovascular interventions. After declining surgical bypass, he underwent percutaneous transmural arterial bypass using covered stent grafts routed through the femoral venous pathway. Inline flow was restored without immediate complications. At 3 months, duplex ultrasound demonstrated bypass patency, and rest pain had resolved. TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Percutaneous transmural arterial bypass may offer an alternative for carefully selected patients with complex femoropopliteal disease when conventional endovascular treatment has failed, and surgical bypass is declined.

title: Micrococcus luteus Streptococcus mitis Successful Management of Infective Native Infrarenal Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Associated Withandin a 77-year-Old Man.
abstract: Micrococcus luteus Streptococcus mitis BackgroundInfected native abdominal aortic aneurysm (INAAA) is a rare but life-threatening condition characterized by rapid progression and high mortality.Case SummaryWe report a 77-year-old male with a history of arterial hypertension, ischemic heart disease, and stage IVB hormone-sensitive prostate adenocarcinoma, presenting with lumbar pain and mild inflammatory activation, including leukocytes 8.8 ×10³/µL and C-reactive protein 3.6 mg/dL (normal <0.50 mg/dL). Computed tomography angiography (CTA) demonstrated a 50-mm infrarenal aneurysm, with periaortic inflammatory changes and a periaortic hematoma. A multidisciplinary decision, made 3 hours after admission, favored urgent open surgical repair with resection and in situ reconstruction. Midline laparotomy with debridement and resection of the affected aorta was performed; in situ reconstruction was carried out using a rifampicin soaked bifurcated Dacron graft covered with bovine pericardium with anastomoses to healthy aortic and iliac segments. Intraoperative cultures identifiedand, rare pathogens in this context. Targeted therapy included intravenous ceftriaxone during hospitalization, followed by oral amoxicillin-clavulanate and doxycycline for seven weeks. Histopathology confirmed chronic granulomatous abscessed inflammation. The postoperative course was uneventful, and the patient was discharged home on postoperative day 17. At six months, follow-up imaging demonstrated a patent reconstruction without signs of persistent infection.ConclusionThese findings highlight the importance of early recognition, aggressive debridement, and coordinated multidisciplinary management in achieving optimal outcomes in INAAA, particularly when atypical microorganisms complicate diagnosis and therapeutic decision-making.

title: Untargeted Plasma Metabolomics Reveals Molecular Subtypes Associated with Reintervention Risk in Peripheral Artery Disease after Revascularization.
abstract: Peripheral artery disease (PAD) shows substantial outcome heterogeneity after revascularization that is incompletely explained by conventional severity indicators. We performed untargeted plasma LC-MS metabolomics in 175 PAD patients undergoing revascularization and applied variability-based feature selection, unsupervised clustering, pathway and chemical-class analyses, survival modeling, and metabolite prioritization. Three metabolically defined molecular subtypes were identified: redox protective (n = 93), metabolic burden (n = 72), and renal dysfunction (n = 10). Compared to the redox-protective subtype, the metabolic-burden subtype showed higher risks of composite adverse outcomes, reintervention, and major adverse cardiovascular events, accompanied by acylcarnitine accumulation, fatty-acyl enrichment, and COX-prostaglandin-related inflammatory signaling. Secondary clustering of high-risk patients identified a subgroup with increased reintervention risk, despite no corresponding increase in Rutherford classification or ankle-brachial index severity, characterized by sphingomyelin, diglyceride, and thromboxane/leukotriene-related lipid mediator signatures. A five-metabolite score was associated with reintervention risk and showed numerically higher apparent discrimination than the original and expanded clinical models. These findings establish an untargeted metabolomics framework for molecular subtyping of PAD after revascularization and nominate metabolic phenotypes for future validation.

title: Saddle pulmonary embolism and heparin-induced thrombocytopenia in acute pancreatitis: a case report.
abstract: Acute pancreatitis causes severe inflammation, predisposing patients to thromboembolism, which can be further complicated by heparin-induced thrombocytopenia and thrombosis (HITT). A 47-year-old diabetic male patient with severe acute pancreatitis developed a massive saddle pulmonary embolism. Low-molecular-weight heparin (LMWH) treatment triggered a deep vein thrombosis, and a severe platelet drop (28 × 109/l), confirming HITT. Due to a refractory response to fondaparinux, the patient was successfully switched to direct oral anticoagulation with dabigatran etexilate (150 mg twice daily). This led to rapid platelet normalization and clinical stability. When standard parenteral treatments fail in HITT, direct oral anticoagulants like dabigatran offer an effective alternative strategy.

title: Personalized anticoagulation and drug monitoring for pregnancy-associated venous thromboembolism in hereditary type IIa antithrombin deficiency.
abstract: Pregnant women with hereditary type IIa antithrombin deficiency (ATD) are at significantly increased thrombotic risk. We present the case of a woman with four consecutive pregnancy losses due to venous thromboembolism (VTE), subsequently diagnosed with type IIa hereditary ATD. Type IIa ATD is exceptionally rare. The principal therapeutic challenge lies in the absence of established guidelines regarding optimal anticoagulant selection, dosing strategies, and monitoring approaches for such patients, contributing to treatment failure in her first four pregnancies. The patient was referred to our institution before her fifth conception. Preconception intervention began, and we instituted low-molecular-weight heparin (LMWH) therapy, with dose titration guided by thrombin-antithrombin complex (TAT) and anti-Xa activity levels. This regimen demonstrated safety and efficacy, achieving a maximum nadroparin dose of 10 250 IU twice daily. Under close pharmacotherapeutic monitoring by a clinical pharmacist using this individualized protocol, the patient achieved a successful term delivery and was discharged.

We present the case of a woman with four consecutive pregnancy losses due to venous thromboembolism (VTE), subsequently diagnosed with type IIa hereditary ATD. Type IIa ATD is exceptionally rare.

title: Perioperative combined intravenous and intra-articular tranexamic acid does not increase venous thromboembolism risk after total knee arthroplasty in plateau areas: a randomized controlled trial.
abstract: After total knee arthroplasty (TKA), rivaroxaban is often used to prevent venous thromboembolism (VTE), while tranexamic acid (TXA) is used to reduce perioperative bleeding. However, plateau hypoxia may affect coagulation. We assessed whether combined intravenous and intra-articular TXA increases VTE risk in plateau TKA patients. This single-center, prospective, randomized, double-blind, pilot controlled trial was conducted at altitude greater than 3500 m. Fifty unilateral TKA patients were randomized to experimental (intravenous + intra-articular TXA) or control (intravenous TXA alone). All received rivaroxaban for 14 days. Primary outcome was new-onset DVT (deep vein thrombosis) or PE (Pulmonary Embolism) at day 3; secondary outcomes included thromboelastography (TEG) and coagulation parameters at 6 h, 1, 2, and 3 days. No VTE occurred in either group. Nonthrombotic ultrasound findings (intermuscular vein dilation with blood stasis) were observed in 9/25 (36%) of the experimental group and 13/25 (52%) of the control group, with no between-group difference (P = 0.254). TEG parameters showed no significant differences, except for a transiently lower D-dimer in the experimental group on day 1 (P < 0.001), though clinical relevance is unclear. Hb and Hct declined less in the experimental group at all time points (P < 0.05), suggesting reduced blood loss. In plateau TKA patients, adding intra-articular TXA to intravenous TXA did not increase short-term VTE risk. These preliminary findings suggest combined TXA with rivaroxaban may be well tolerated in this population.

title: The effect of renal denervation on blood pressure in patients with chronic kidney disease (RDN-CKD Study): Results of a multicentre, prospective, randomized, sham-controlled and blinded investigator-initiated trial.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Endovascular ultrasound renal denervation (uRDN) offers the opportunity to modulate sympathetic nervous system activity, thereby lowering blood pressure (BP) and potentially improving or stabilizing renal outcomes. OBJECTIVE: We hypothesized that in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) stage 3 and uncontrolled hypertension, endovascular ultrasound-based RDN will lower BP after 6 months. METHODS: This multicenter, prospective, randomized, sham-controlled, blinded, clinical trial, investigated the effects of uRDN or sham in patients with CKD stage 3 and uncontrolled hypertension. The primary and secondary endpoints were changes in ambulatory BP (ABP) and office BP at 6 months. The study was prematurely stopped due to slow enrollment. RESULTS: Twenty subjects (uRDN: N  = 10, sham: N  = 10) completed the 6-month visit. At 6 months, the sham-corrected change from baseline in 24 h systolic ABP was -5.60 mmHg (95% CI -10.7, -0.54 mmHg; P  = 0.170). The sham corrected change from baseline in 24-h diastolic ABP was -5.90 mmHg (95% CI -9.25, -2.55; P  = 0.035) and from baseline daytime ABP -6.85 mmHg (95% CI -10.6, -3.08; P  = 0.030). Sensitivity analysis restricting the analysis to those patients who were fully adherent to medication ( N  = 7 in each group) found a sham-corrected change from baseline 24-h diastolic ABP of -5.71 mmHg (95% CI -9.40, -2.03; P  = 0.053) at 6 months. Based on the composite endpoint of 24 h ABP and office BP for systolic/diastolic BP, a win ratio of 1.71 (95% 1.26-2.34; P  = 0.014) was found for systolic BP and a win ratio of 4.59 (95% CI 2.94-7.16, P  < 0.001) was found for diastolic BP, indicating significant changes in BP following RDN. Estimated glomerular filtration rate remained stable over 6 months, with no difference between the groups. There were no safety signals associated with uRDN. CONCLUSIONS: This prospective randomized, sham controlled, blinded trial in patients with uncontrolled hypertension and CKD was prematurely stopped, resulted in small number of patients and we did not find a statistically significant effect on systolic BP, whereas a consistent reduction in diastolic BP following uRDN was observed. These data should guide the design of a larger confirmatory trial in patients with CKD.

title: Pulmonary hypertension and right ventricular dysfunction in hemodialysis: an overlooked cardiorenal interface and a target for dialysis prescription.
abstract: Pulmonary hypertension is an under-recognized cardiovascular complication of advanced chronic kidney disease, especially in maintenance hemodialysis. It links kidney failure, chronic volume stress, left-heart disease, pulmonary vascular remodeling, arteriovenous access flow, and right-ventricular dysfunction. This review frames pulmonary hypertension as central to the cardiorenal interface in hemodialysis and summarizes epidemiology, prognosis, mechanisms, diagnosis, and phenotyping. Echocardiography is the main screening tool, but pressure estimates should be interpreted according to dialysis timing and volume status. Right-heart catheterization remains essential to define phenotype and guide management. Treatment should target modifiable drivers: euvolemia without excessive ultrafiltration, optimized left-heart disease care, assessment of high-flow vascular access, and treatment of respiratory or hematologic contributors. Empirical pulmonary arterial hypertension-specific therapy should be avoided without hemodynamic confirmation. Pulmonary-artery denervation is promising in heart-failure pulmonary hypertension with mild to moderate CKD, but its role in hemodialysis remains unknown.
