title: Propensity Score Matched Analysis of Outcomes of Conservative and Invasive Management of Patients with Chronic Limb Threatening Ischaemia: The PROCLION Study.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Current guidelines recommend revascularisation for patients with chronic limb threatening ischaemia (CLTI). However, revascularisation may be burdensome in these frail patients. The objective of this study was to compare the clinical and patient reported outcomes in patients with CLTI treated with conservative best supportive care versus primary invasive endovascular and/or surgical revascularisation. METHODS: This was a multicentre prospective cohort study in the Netherlands. Propensity score matching was used to create similar groups based on known factors influencing the odds of undergoing revascularisation. Twelve month amputation free survival (AFS), major amputation rates, mortality, and patient reported outcomes after primary conservative treatment were compared with primary invasive treatment (intention to treat; ITT). Outcomes after invasive treatment at any time were compared with definitive conservative treatment (per protocol; PP). RESULTS: A total of 365 patients with CLTI were included in 18 centres. In the ITT analysis, patients were matched 1 : 1, resulting in two groups of 121 patients. Twelve month AFS was 73.0% for patients after conservative treatment and 72.1% after invasive treatment (risk difference [RD] -0.9%, 95% confidence interval [CI] -10.2 - 8.4%). There were no significant differences in amputation and mortality rates. In the PP analysis, patients were matched 1 : 2, with 51 in the conservative group and 102 in the invasive group. Again, no significant differences were found for AFS, amputation rate, and mortality. Patient reported outcomes improved after 1 year in both groups (VascuQoL: ITT conservative group from 14 to 16.2, and invasive group from 13.8 to 16.5), but no significant differences were found in ITT or PP comparisons. CONCLUSION: The current study suggests that the 12 month clinical outcomes of primary conservative and invasive treatment for CLTI are similar. Conservative management may therefore be a viable first choice treatment option in selected patients with CLTI.

However, revascularisation may be burdensome in these frail patients. The objective of this study was to compare the clinical and patient reported outcomes in patients with CLTI treated with conservative best supportive care versus primary invasive endovascular and/or surgical revascularisation.

title: Prediction models for venous thromboembolism in pediatric patients: A protocol for systematic review and critical appraisal.
abstract: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) in children is a severe disease with high mortality rates. It is also gradually recognized as a major source of morbidity in hospitalized children, leading to increased length of hospital stay, higher mortality, and increased costs. The majority of pediatric subjects with VTE present inherited or acquired risk factors,such as the use of a central venous catheter (CVC), which accounts for more than more than 90% of neonatal VTE and 50% of pediatric VTE. Clinical studies on predictive models for VTE in children have shown inconsistent results. This systematic review aims to evaluate published prediction models for pediatric VTE, analyzing their characteristics, predictors, efficacy, and the methodological quality and applicability. The protocol has been prepared using the Preferred Items for Systematic Review and Meta-analysis Protocols (PRISMA-P) guidelines. The systematic review protocol for VTE prediction in pediatric patients has been registered on PROSPERO (PROSPERO 2025CRD420251231316. Available from https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/vi-ew/CRD420251231316.) A comprehensive search across five major databases (PubMed, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, CNKI, and Wanfang) will be conducted for studies on prediction models of VTE among pediatric patients. Two researchers will independently screen literature, extract data, and evaluate the bias risk and applicability of included studies using prediction modelling study tools. This systematic review will provide critical insights into the efficacy and quality of reporting of the VTE model in pediatric patients. This will guide clinical physicians in selecting the most appropriate VTE prediction model and inform future research endeavors in pediatric VTE prediction.

title: SEQuential tUnneled Catheters and Infective Events in haemodiaLysis: A Five-Year Retrospective Cohort Study (SEQUEL Study).
abstract: BACKGROUND: Tunnelled-cuffed catheters (TCCs) are widely used for haemodialysis access when permanent vascular access is unavailable. Internal jugular vein (IJV) placement is guideline-preferred, but femoral vein (FV) catheters are frequently used when upper venous access is limited. Whether femoral access confers a higher infection risk than catheter sequence number remains unclear. This study evaluated these two competing determinants of catheter-related bloodstream infection (CRBSI). METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included all TCC insertions at a tertiary nephrology unit between January 2016 and December 2021. The primary analysis examined CRBSI incidence per 1000 catheter-days stratified by catheter sequence number (first, second, third+ insertion per patient). Secondary analyses compared femoral versus internal jugular TCCs overall and within sequence strata. A registry-index cohort (patients with no documented prior TCC before January 2016, n = 135) was used to reduce, though not eliminate, sequence-related confounding in the site comparison; given only 24 CRBSI events, this analysis is exploratory and a clinically meaningful site difference cannot be excluded. Kaplan-Meier methods with log-rank testing were used for time-to-event outcomes. A cluster-robust marginal Cox model was used to account for repeated catheter insertions within patients, adjusting for sequence number, insertion site, age, sex, insertion setting, and exchange from a non-tunnelled catheter. RESULTS: Among 626 TCC insertions in 339 patients (389 FV, 237 IJV), contributing 98,727 catheter-days, CRBSI incidence escalated with catheter sequence: 1.17 per 1000 catheter-days for first insertions, rising to 1.98 for second and 2.49 for third-or-more insertions. Notably, by the second insertion, CRBSI rates were similar between FV and IJV access (31.7% each). In the index cohort (n = 135; FV = 95, IJV = 40), CRBSI-free survival did not differ significantly between sites (log-rank p = 0.340), nor did catheter survival (p = 0.950) or patient survival (p = 0.487). In the all-TCC cohort, after adjustment for catheter sequence number, age, sex, insertion setting, and exchange from a non-tunnelled catheter using a cluster-robust marginal Cox model, femoral access remained associated with a higher, though attenuated, CRBSI hazard after adjustment for the measured covariates (HR 1.43, 95% CI 1.02-2.01; p = 0.039), indicating a modest residual site hazard beyond the sequence effect. CONCLUSIONS: Repeated catheterization was independently associated with increasing CRBSI risk, and catheter sequence number was the strongest predictor in the fully adjusted model. The femoral site effect was substantially attenuated after adjustment for sequence and was not statistically significant in the registry-index cohort analysis, though the wide confidence intervals preclude an equivalence interpretation. IJV access remains preferred; when IJV is unavailable, femoral TCC placement may be an acceptable alternative from an infection-risk perspective, but this must be weighed against thrombotic and limb complications, including deep vein thrombosis, which were not systematically ascertained in this study. Residual confounding cannot be excluded in this single-center retrospective study.

Internal jugular vein (IJV) placement is guideline-preferred, but femoral vein (FV) catheters are frequently used when upper venous access is limited. Whether femoral access confers a higher infection risk than catheter sequence number remains unclear.

title: Middle meningeal artery embolization in chronic subdural hematoma: A real-world multicenter italian experience.
abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate technical feasibility, short-term radiological outcomes, subsequent surgical intervention, and complications of middle meningeal artery (MMA) embolization for chronic subdural hematoma (CSDH), distinguishing primary embolization from embolization after surgery. METHODS: This retrospective study included 228 consecutive patients undergoing attempted MMA embolization at three Italian referral centers between January 2019 and November 2024. Technical success was the primary outcome. Secondary outcomes included radiological success, defined as residual hematoma thickness ≤ 6 mm on CT at 60-90 days, subsequent surgical evacuation, and procedure-related complications. Subgroup comparisons were exploratory and used available-case data. RESULTS: Primary embolization was performed in 115 patients and embolization after surgery in 113. Technical success was achieved in 223/228 patients (97.8%). Follow-up CT was available in 188/228 patients (82.5%). Median residual hematoma thickness was 4 mm (interquartile range, 0-8), without a significant difference between groups (p = 0.372). Radiological success occurred in 132/188 patients (70.2%): 57/88 (64.8%) after primary embolization and 75/100 (75.0%) after surgery (p = 0.151). Complications occurred in 7/228 patients (3.1%), including one major ischemic stroke, without a significant between-group difference (p = 0.720). Subsequent surgical evacuation was required in 7/188 patients (3.7%): 5/88 (5.7%) versus 2/100 (2.0%), respectively (p = 0.255). CONCLUSION: MMA embolization demonstrated high technical success, favorable short-term radiological outcomes, and a low rate of subsequent surgical intervention. These findings support its feasibility and potential clinical value in selected patients with CSDH, both as primary treatment and after surgical evacuation. Prospective comparative studies are needed to confirm these observations.

METHODS: This retrospective study included 228 consecutive patients undergoing attempted MMA embolization at three Italian referral centers between January 2019 and November 2024. Technical success was the primary outcome.

title: The Coagulation-Immune Axis in Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma: Mechanisms, Prognostic Significance, and Therapeutic Opportunities.
abstract: Oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) develops in a microbe-rich, injury-prone mucosa in which coagulation, inflammation, and tissue repair are closely coupled. Tumor and host cells can activate tissue factor-thrombin signaling, platelets, fibrin turnover, extracellular vesicles, and neutrophil extracellular traps, thereby reshaping myeloid-cell recruitment, cytotoxic immunity, angiogenesis, and invasion. However, local procoagulant biology does not necessarily predict systemic venous thromboembolism. We therefore organize the evidence using a compartmentalized immunothrombosis model that distinguishes intratumoral coagulation-immune remodeling, systemic thrombosis, and treatment-dependent perioperative events. Direct OSCC studies support several components of this network, but much of the evidence linking coagulation to immune escape and treatment response remains preclinical or extrapolated from other tumors. Circulating D-dimer, fibrinogen, platelet indices, and inflammatory ratios show prognostic associations, yet their incremental value beyond established clinicopathologic factors has not been established. Anticoagulant, antiplatelet, protease-activated receptor, podoplanin-CLEC-2, fibrinolytic, and NET-directed strategies are biologically plausible but should not be used as OSCC treatment without a standard indication or clinical trial. Future studies should pair longitudinal blood measurements with spatial tumor profiling and match interventions to a verified mechanism, anatomical compartment, and safe treatment window.

title: Case report: Severe consequence of unnecessary retention of a TIVAD, phlegmasia cerulea dolens-A case for better stewardship.
abstract: Totally implanted venous access devices (TIVADs) have been used for decades in cancer management. Traditionally placed in the chest wall, they can also be inserted in the upper arm using peripherally inserted central catheter methodologies (PICC-Ports), which are recognized as a safe and comfortable alternative. However, as with all vascular access devices, their safety profile depends on appropriate management, including timely removal. We report a case of Phlegmasia Cerulea Dolens (PCD)-critical venous ischemia-occurring a year after treatment completion due to a retained device. A 59-year-old breast cancer patient presented with arm edema ipsilateral to a PICC-Port, 1 year after chemotherapy had ended. Despite an initial "normal" duplex ultrasound (DUS), her condition worsened into full-blown PCD with cyanosis and loss of pulses. CT angiography revealed massive thrombosis, and standard anticoagulation failed, necessitating interventional radiology for subclavian stenting. While TIVADs are established as a safe method of chemotherapy administration, their safety remains contingent upon adherence to insertion protocols, timely removal, and knowledge of international guidelines. Leaving an inactive device for 12 months post-treatment represents a significant risk. Furthermore, a false-negative initial ultrasound led to a critical diagnostic delay, underscoring that strong clinical suspicion should sometimes override early negative imaging to prevent progression from deep vein thrombosis to PCD. Ultimately, "lost to follow-up" patients with retained TIVADs and non-compliance with international guidelines represent a major iatrogenic risk in cancer management.

However, as with all vascular access devices, their safety profile depends on appropriate management, including timely removal.

title: Hemodialysis access dysfunction caused by heavily calcified subclavian artery chronic total occlusion: Two cases treated with balloon-expandable covered stents.
abstract: Proximal arterial inflow lesions are an underrecognized cause of hemodialysis access dysfunction, particularly in patients with advanced arterial calcification. We report two hemodialysis patients with access dysfunction associated with heavily calcified left subclavian artery chronic total occlusion. Both patients lacked upper-limb claudication or neurological symptoms. Endovascular recanalization was achieved using balloon-expandable covered stents (Viabahn VBX) while preserving the vertebral artery origin. In the first patient, brachial artery flow increased from 55 to 731 mL/min. In the second, flow increased from 275 to 339 mL/min after subclavian revascularization and to 1090 mL/min after subsequent angioplasty of residual fistula stenosis. No procedure-related adverse events occurred, and both accesses remained functional during follow-up. Subclavian artery occlusion should be considered in otherwise unexplained access dysfunction. Balloon-expandable covered stents may provide a useful reconstruction option for heavily calcified proximal inflow lesions.

We report two hemodialysis patients with access dysfunction associated with heavily calcified left subclavian artery chronic total occlusion. Both patients lacked upper-limb claudication or neurological symptoms.

title: Two chromosome-scale genomes of wild Aedes aegypti aegypti mosquitoes from North America and South-East Asia.
abstract: The yellow fever mosquito (Aedes aegypti) is the primary vector for diseases such as chikungunya, dengue fever, yellow fever, and Zika fever. These mosquitoes have been designated as two subspecies: Ae. aegypti formosus (Aaf) and Ae. aegypti aegypti (Aaa)-the former being a darker form limited to sub-Saharan Africa and the latter referring to lighter colored individuals found circumglobally in the tropics and sub-tropics. In addition to morphology and distribution, these two sub-species differ in their behavior and ecology-Aaf females generally feed on nonhuman mammals and live in rural and sylvatic areas, whereas Aaa females preferentially feed on humans and are found in human dwellings in urban areas. These characteristics and differences make them species of great medical importance, and the development of resources for understanding their biology has high priority. We recently published a chromosome-scale wild Aaf genome assembly and here we add to this body of resources by presenting two de novo chromosome-scale genome assemblies of wild-caught Aaa from North America and Southeast Asia. Using the Pacific Biosciences HiFi sequencing platform combined with HiC sequencing, we achieved high continuity (N50: >400 Mb; L50: 2) and completeness (BUSCO single-copy: ~97%; diptera set). These assemblies will contribute to further elucidate the global genetic diversity of this major disease vector and uncover the genetic basis of phenotypic differences between the sub-species.

title: Perioperative Management of the Orthopedic Patient Taking Antipsychotics: A Narrative Review.
abstract: PURPOSE: Antipsychotic prescribing continues to rise among older adults, the group most likely to present for orthopedic surgery, and orthopedic surgeons now operate regularly on patients taking these agents. Guidance for managing them around an operation sits largely in the psychiatric, anesthesiology and pharmacologic literature rather than the surgical one. This narrative review gathers the orthopedic-specific evidence and organizes it by whether a finding reflects the medication or the psychiatric illness for which it was prescribed. FINDINGS: Antipsychotic exposure is associated with higher all-cause revision and periprosthetic fracture after total knee arthroplasty, and second-generation exposure raises all-cause and aseptic revision after shoulder arthroplasty independent of psychiatric diagnosis. Venous thromboembolism roughly doubles after primary total knee arthroplasty. Among geriatric hip fracture patients antipsychotics are the only medication class independently linked to in-hospital falls, and preoperative use independently predicts postoperative delirium that prophylaxis does not prevent. Spine, sports medicine and trauma surgery all show worse outcomes in patients carrying a psychiatric diagnosis, yet none of those literatures disentangles the drug from the disorder. Thromboembolism and the shoulder revision signal are the clearest drug-attributable exceptions. Hyperprolactinemia-mediated hypogonadism, metabolic derangement and impaired fracture healing remain plausible but unproven. Nearly all available evidence is retrospective. CONCLUSION: Antipsychotic therapy should continue through the perioperative period unless a specific reason exists to stop it. Abrupt discontinuation risks psychiatric relapse, which is harder to manage than the perioperative risks the drugs themselves carry. Low bone mineral density, poor glycemic control and thromboembolic risk are all worth addressing before surgery, drawing on psychiatry and internal medicine. Antipsychotics are not recommended for delirium prophylaxis. Whether altering therapy improves orthopedic outcomes has not been studied prospectively.

title: Long-term functional and orthopaedic outcomes in patients with severe pelvic ring injury requiring REBOA: A two-center matched cohort study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Resuscitative endovascular balloon occlusion of the aorta (REBOA) is used for life-threatening hemorrhage, but evidence has largely focused on acute outcomes. Long-term functional and orthopaedic outcomes among survivors treated with REBOA remain poorly characterized. METHODS: This retrospective two-center matched cohort included 98 adults with severe, hemodynamically unstable pelvic ring injuries who survived at least 24 h; hospital survivors required at least 12 months of follow-up. Forty-nine REBOA-treated patients were matched 1:1 to 49 non-REBOA patients by major Young-Burgess category, Injury Severity Score, and age. The primary outcome was functional status among hospital survivors, categorized as good/fair/poor. Deep surgical site infection (SSI) after definitive pelvic fixation was the key secondary outcome, and nonunion was exploratory. Main models used a propensity-score linear predictor based on age, Injury Severity Score, initial systolic blood pressure, and lactate. RESULTS: Seventy-five patients survived hospitalization (30 REBOA; 45 non-REBOA); median follow-up was 19 months. Good/fair/poor outcomes were 16.7%/46.7%/36.7% in REBOA survivors and 51.1%/37.8%/11.1% in non-REBOA survivors. REBOA exposure was associated with worse functional status after adjustment (common odds ratio [cOR], 3.14; 95% CI, 1.11-8.92; P = 0.032). Among 68 definitive-fixation survivors, deep SSI occurred in 44.0% versus 9.3% (adjusted OR, 7.01; 95% CI, 1.88-31.07; P = 0.003); all observed events occurred within 60 days. Nonunion occurred in 26.7% versus 6.7% (adjusted OR, 9.09; 95% CI, 2.00-53.71; P = 0.004). Sensitivity analyses for deep SSI were directionally consistent. CONCLUSIONS: Among hospital survivors, REBOA exposure was associated with poorer long-term functional recovery and a higher burden of deep SSI. Nonunion was more frequent but remained exploratory. These findings characterize a high-risk orthopaedic survivor phenotype but do not establish a direct causal effect of REBOA.

title: Dysphagia as the Initial Manifestation of Anti-HMGCR Antibody-Positive Immune-Mediated Necrotizing Myopathy Complicated by Pulmonary Embolism.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Anti-3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl-coenzyme A reductase (anti-HMGCR) antibody-positive immune-mediated necrotizing myopathy (IMNM) is a rare autoimmune myopathy characterized by progressive proximal muscle weakness and markedly elevated creatine kinase levels. Although commonly associated with prior statin exposure, statin-naïve cases and atypical presentations are well described. Patients with idiopathic inflammatory myopathies are also at increased risk for venous thromboembolism (VTE), though data specific to IMNM remain limited. CASE PRESENTATION: An 83-year-old man with brief, remote statin exposure presented with progressive proximal muscle weakness and a three-year history of oropharyngeal dysphagia preceding limb involvement. Laboratory evaluation revealed markedly elevated creatine kinase and transaminases. Anti-HMGCR antibodies were positive, and muscle biopsy confirmed necrotizing myopathy. During evaluation for occult malignancy, bilateral pulmonary emboli were incidentally identified. The patient required high-dose corticosteroids, mycophenolate mofetil, and intravenous immunoglobulin for refractory disease. With aggressive immunosuppressive therapy and rehabilitation, he demonstrated substantial clinical recovery at 6 months. CONCLUSION: This case highlights oropharyngeal dysphagia as an early and, for a prolonged period, isolated manifestation of anti-HMGCR antibody-positive IMNM; here, it preceded the onset of limb weakness by approximately 3 years. It underscores the importance of comprehensive diagnostic evaluation in patients with unexplained oropharyngeal dysfunction, in whom an inflammatory myopathy may otherwise be overlooked for years. Clinicians should maintain awareness of thrombotic risk in inflammatory myopathies, particularly during active disease. Early recognition and prompt immunosuppressive therapy remain critical to optimize outcomes and prevent irreversible muscle damage.

title: Bare-Metal vs Covered Balloon-Expandable Stents for Transplant Renal Artery Stenosis: A Retrospective Comparative Study.
abstract: PURPOSE: To compare short- and long-term outcomes of bare-metal (BMS) vs covered (CS) balloon-expandable stents in transplant renal artery stenosis (TRAS). MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective study evaluated patients who underwent elective stent placement for TRAS between 2016 and 2023. Short-term efficacy was assessed by clinical improvement (resolution of resistant hypertension/hypervolemia) and reduction in serum creatinine (sCr) within 14 days post-procedure. Long-term outcomes included Doppler ultrasound parameters - peak systolic velocity (PSV), acceleration time (AT) and resistive index (RI) - and restenosis/occlusion rates requiring or not intervention. Graft survival at the latest follow-up was recorded. RESULTS: P P P P P A total of 40 patients (mean age 58 ± 13 years, 68% male) were treated with BMS (n = 31) or CS (n = 9). Clinical improvement was observed in 71% of BMS and 83% of CS patients ( = 1.00). Median sCr decreased by 26% and 33% in BMS and CS patients, respectively ( = .30). At a median follow-up of 29 months, there were no statistically significant differences between groups in median PSV reduction (47% BMS vs 47% CS; = .44), AT improvement (36% BMS vs 25% CS; = .38) or RI increase (15% BMS vs 33% CS; = .12). In the BMS group, 2 cases of in-stent restenosis occurred (6.5%). In the CS group, 1 stent occlusion occurred (11%), resulting in graft loss. At final follow-up, overall graft survival was 85%. CONCLUSION: In this pilot study, BMS and CS showed no significant differences in TRAS outcomes. Further studies are warranted to better guide stent selection.Clinical ImpactIn transplant renal artery stenosis, balloon-expandable covered stents achieved clinical, biochemical and Doppler outcomes comparable to bare-metal stents, despite being used in more complex, atherosclerotic and longer lesions. This first direct comparison suggests that covered stents may be a reasonable option when heavy calcification, a friable wall or mural thrombus raise concern for embolisation or rupture, while bare-metal stents remain appropriate for most lesions. The single late covered-stent occlusion with graft loss highlights the need for careful platform selection and antiplatelet management. These pilot data should inform adequately powered multicentre registries rather than directly change practice.

title: The Lost Kidney: Ultrasound Diagnosis of Adult Bochdalek Hernia With Renal Herniation and Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm.
abstract: Adult Bochdalek hernia (BH) with left renal herniation is clinically rare and has an insidious onset, rendering it prone to misdiagnosis. We report a case of a 77-year-old male patient who presented with an abdominal pulsatile mass in the absence of respiratory symptoms. Ultrasonography revealed a giant abdominal aortic aneurysm and additionally identified renal echogenicity on the left side of the heart, with a normally positioned spleen. Contrast-enhanced CT demonstrated herniation of the left kidney and a portion of the bowel into the thoracic cavity, along with a giant abdominal aortic aneurysm and multiple atherosclerotic ulcers of the iliac arteries. Ultrasonography is valuable for initial screening, while contrast-enhanced CT defines diaphragmatic defect, ectopic-kidney rotational malformation, and elongated renal pedicle, providing critical evidence for definitive diagnosis.

title: A multi-guideline clinical agent for vascular surgery: architecture, implementation, and benchmark evaluation.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The clinical practice guidelines (CPGs) published by the European Society for Vascular Surgery (ESVS) span approximately 1100 pages whose simultaneous cross-referencing is impractical at the point of care. Unguarded large language models (LLMs) carry hallucination risk, motivating a guideline-locked design. METHODS: We describe the architecture and development of a context-aware clinical agent encompassing the full ESVS corpus of 14 CPGs. The system extends a validated single-guideline GraphRAG prototype with an LLM-driven Guideline Router, an embedded Context Gate that withholds retrieval when decision-critical parameters are absent, dual-channel retrieval, and GPT-5 synthesis under a mandatory citation template. An automated benchmark assessed the final system on 55 vignettes, scored by 2 blinded LLM judges over 3 runs (330 judgments), with clinician adjudication of every flagged claim. RESULTS: The system stayed within its locked corpus, declined all out-of-scope queries, and achieved 98.4% guideline-routing recall. The Context Gate showed 91.9% specificity and 78.6% sensitivity for underspecified queries, and all 259 cited recommendations were verifiable within the locked corpus. Automated judges flagged an unsupported claim in 18.2% of items under a sensitive screening definition; on adjudication by 2 vascular surgeons, 7.3% of items contained a clinically consequential error, none graded capable of causing harm. Clinical acceptability of complete answers was not scored and is reserved for prospective expert evaluation. CONCLUSION: These results support the feasibility of a multi-guideline context-aware clinical agent for vascular surgery; citation traceability and locked-corpus provenance facilitate future auditability.

title: Ruptured INfrarenal abdominal AneurySm: aortiC repair using the ENduranT Endograft. The R.IN.AS.C.ENT.E. Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm (rAAA) represents a vascular surgical emergency with high mortality. Endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR) using the bifurcated Endurant stent graft system is widely employed; however, data specifically addressing its performance in infrarenal rAAA remain limited. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective, multicenter study including 121 patients with confirmed infrarenal rAAA treated exclusively with bifurcated Endurant II or IIs (Medtronic Inc., Minneapolis, Minnesota) devices across 5 Italian tertiary vascular centers from January 2014 to October 2024. Primary endpoints were technical success and 30-day all-cause mortality. Secondary outcomes included long-term survival, incidence of endoleaks, and reintervention rates. Patients receiving alternative stent grafts or hybrid procedures were excluded to ensure cohort homogeneity. RESULTS: P P A total of 121 patients were enrolled during the study period. The cohort had a mean age of 75.3 ± 8.2 years, with 91.7% male predominance. Technical success was achieved in 96.7%. The 30-day mortality rate was 15.7%. Multivariate logistic regression identified abdominal compartment syndrome (ACS) (odds ratio [OR], 29.8; 95% confidence interval [CI], 2.8-317.7; = .005) and use of an aortic occlusion balloon (AOB) (OR, 16.4; 95% CI, 2.5-106.2; = .003) as independent predictors of early mortality. At a median follow-up of 33.6 months (interquartile range, 4.9-72.3), 5-year survival was 65.4%, freedom from any endoleak was 92.6%, and freedom from reintervention was 91.6%. Late type Ia endoleaks occurred in 2.5% of patients. CONCLUSIONS: In this large, strictly defined infrarenal rAAA cohort, bifurcated Endurant stent grafts demonstrated high technical success and favorable early and mid-term clinical outcomes, including in patients with hostile neck anatomy. Early identification and management of ACS and judicious use of AOBs may improve survival. These findings reinforce current EVAR-first guidelines and emphasize the importance of device-specific outcome assessment in emergent rAAA repair.Clinical ImpactThis multicenter study provides one of the largest device-specific evaluations of bifurcated Endurant stent grafts for infrarenal ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysms in a rigorously defined Italian cohort, demonstrating high technical success (96.7%) and low 30-day mortality (15.7%) despite a high prevalence of hostile neck anatomy (54.5%). Abdominal compartment syndrome and the use of an aortic occlusion balloon emerged as independent predictors of early mortality, highlighting the critical role of perioperative management. Mid-term outcomes were favorable, with a 5-year survival rate of 65.4%, a low incidence of type Ia endoleak (2.5%), and high freedom from reintervention (91.6%). Overall, these findings support the use of Endurant devices in emergent settings for anatomically suitable patients and reinforce EVAR-first strategies in the management of ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysms.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective, multicenter study including 121 patients with confirmed infrarenal rAAA treated exclusively with bifurcated Endurant II or IIs (Medtronic Inc., Minneapolis, Minnesota) devices across 5 Italian tertiary vascular centers from January 2014 to October 2024.

title: Outcomes of AngioJet™ Rheolytic Thrombectomy for Occluded Lower-Extremity Bypass Grafts: A Single-Center Retrospective Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Lower-extremity bypass graft occlusion is associated with recurrent ischemia and potential limb loss. This study evaluated the technical and clinical outcomes of AngioJet™ rheolytic thrombectomy for occluded bypass grafts in a single-center retrospective cohort. METHODS: Consecutive patients undergoing AngioJet™ thrombectomy as the primary strategy for occluded bypass grafts (2014-2024) were reviewed. Technical success was defined as <30% residual stenosis. Outcomes included Rutherford category improvement, complications, 30-day mortality, major amputation, target lesion revascularization, and primary patency. Follow-up was available for 38/40 (95.0%) 30-day survivors. RESULTS: Forty-one procedures were analyzed. Technical success was achieved in 38/41 (92.7%; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 80.1%-98.5%). Periprocedural complications occurred in 4 patients (9.8%; 95% CI: 2.7%-23.1%). Thirty-day mortality was 2.4% (1/41; 95% CI: 0.1%-12.9%) and major amputation was 4.9% (2/41; 95% CI: 0.6%-16.5%). Rutherford category improvement at 30 days was 43.9% (18/41; 95% CI: 28.5%-60.3%). Primary patency at final follow-up was 63.4% (26/41; 95% CI: 46.9%-77.9%) in the overall cohort (intent-to-treat) and 68.4% (26/38; 95% CI: 51.3%-82.5%) among technically successful cases. CONCLUSION: AngioJet™ thrombectomy is a technically feasible endovascular option for occluded bypass grafts with low 30-day mortality (2.4%) and amputation rates (4.9%). Prospective comparative studies are needed to define its role relative to surgical and alternative endovascular approaches.Clinical ImpactOccluded lower-extremity bypass grafts often cause limb-threatening ischemia in patients at high surgical risk. In this single-center cohort, AngioJet rheolytic thrombectomy achieved technical success in 92.7% of procedures, with 30-day mortality of 2.4% and major amputation of 4.9%. These findings support AngioJet-assisted thrombectomy as a minimally invasive option for carefully selected patients with crossable grafts and treatable inflow or outflow disease. Clinicians should anticipate adjunctive interventions, monitor for compartment syndrome, and provide structured surveillance because reintervention remains common. Prospective comparative studies are needed before routine first-line use.

title: Examining Racial Disparities in Lower Extremity Amputation Outcomes Among Patients with Diabetic Foot Ulcers in North America: A Multicohort Study.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Racial and ethnic disparities in diabetic foot ulcer (DFU) outcomes are well described. We examined whether differences in major and minor lower extremity amputation (LEA) persist after matching for comorbidities, and whether the level of amputation identifies opportunities for earlier limb-preservation intervention. APPROACH: In this retrospective, propensity-matched cohort study using the TriNetX network (2002-2019), reported in accordance with Strengthening the Reporting of Observational Studies in Epidemiology, adults with DFU were identified by diagnostic codes and stratified by race/ethnicity. Minor and major LEA risks were compared with a matched White (non-Hispanic) reference, reporting both relative and absolute risks. We also calculated the high-to-low (Hi-Lo) ratio (major:minor). RESULTS: Among 388,371 adults with DFU and after matching, Hispanic and African American patients had higher minor, major, and overall LEA risk than White patients (major-LEA absolute risk 3.0-4.7% vs. ∼2.7%; relative risks up to 1.89). Asian patients had the lowest risk. Native American patients had the highest Hi-Lo (major-to-minor amputation) ratio despite no significant increase in major-LEA risk, suggesting potential differences in disease presentation or access to limb-preservation care that warrant further study. Disparities persisted after adjustment for diabetes-related comorbidities and peripheral arterial disease. INNOVATION: Applied to a multiethnic DFU cohort, the Hi-Lo ratio gave a descriptive view of major- versus minor-amputation burden, most notably in Native American patients. CONCLUSION: The Hi-Lo amputation ratio may identify populations experiencing disproportionate major limb loss and help prioritize earlier vascular assessment, multidisciplinary limb-preservation referral, and posthealing surveillance. Persistent racial and ethnic differences after matching warrant further study of disease severity, access, and care delivery.[Figure: see text].

title: The law of surprise: temporal variation and seasonality of acute aortic syndromes: a single-centre epidemiologic cohort analysis spanning 20 years.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Acute aortic syndromes (AAS) represent life-threatening cardiovascular emergencies characterized by high mortality rates despite rapid intervention. Global epidemiological data indicate substantial variance in incidence. Longitudinal single-centre data over extended periods are limited but crucial for understanding diagnostic, demographic, and systemic factors influencing admission trends.(1). This study aimed to analyze annual and seasonal variation trends of AAS over a 20-year period in a single maximal care centre and explore potential chronological and environmental contributors to this variation. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study evaluated 403 patients admitted with a confirmed diagnosis of AAS between 2005 and 2025 at the University Hospital Erlangen, Germany. All diagnoses were established via computed tomography angiography (CTA) and confirmed intraoperatively. Annual, quarterly, and monthly surgical volumes were calculated, and temporal trends were analyzed using Poisson and negative binomial regression models. Admission rates during public holidays and school vacations were also evaluated. RESULTS: Over the 20-year observation period, a steady increasing trend in the annual number of AAS cases was observed, peaking in 2017. Analysis of quarterly distributions revealed a statistically significant dominance of cases in the fourth quarter (Q4: October-December; p < 0.05) compared to the second (Q2) and third (Q3) quarters. Monthly analysis demonstrated a prominent peak in October (incidence rate ratio [IRR] = 1.85 vs. June, p < 0.05). Conversely, fixed public holidays and school vacations were associated with statistically significant reductions in daily admission counts (p < 0.05), with the lowest relative case counts observed during the Christmas vacation period (IRR: 0.40-0.50). CONCLUSION: The case counts of acute aortic syndromes exhibits significant temporal and seasonal variation, characterized by a distinct late-autumn and early-winter peak, alongside significant declines during institutional vacation periods. These findings suggest that acute cardiovascular events are heavily modulated by cyclical environmental and socio-systemic factors.

title: Association Between Cardiovascular Disease and Cataracts: Protocol for a Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: There is emerging evidence suggesting shared pathophysiological mechanisms between cataracts and cardiovascular disease (CVD), indicating a potential link between these 2 prevalent noncommunicable diseases. Oxidative stress, resulting from an imbalance between reactive oxygen species production and the body's antioxidant defenses, contributes to lens protein aggregation in cataracts and lipid oxidation in atherosclerosis, a key feature of several CVD subtypes. This shared pathophysiology implies that systemic vascular health may influence cataractogenesis. However, the epidemiological evidence supporting this relationship remains inconclusive. OBJECTIVE: The main objective of this systematic review is to synthesize existing evidence on the odds or risk of developing cataracts in adults with underlying CVD. METHODS: I 2 This systematic review will adhere to the PRISMA-P (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Protocols). Using the population, exposure, comparator, and outcome framework, this review will identify the association between established CVD and the risk of cataract development or needing cataract surgery. Systematic literature searches will be conducted in PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Embase using MeSH terms from database inception to December 31, 2024. Original research articles involving adults (aged ≥18 years) that assess the statistical relationship between CVD and cataracts will be included. Two independent reviewers will screen studies, extract data, and appraise the studies' quality using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. If deemed feasible, meta-analyses will be conducted using random-effects models to calculate pooled effect estimates, with heterogeneity assessed using thestatistic. RESULTS: This study did not receive any external funding. The literature search, study screening, and data extraction will be conducted in 2026, and data analysis will be performed accordingly. The findings are anticipated to be published in 2027. CONCLUSIONS: This systematic review will provide a consolidated and up-to-date evaluation of the relationship between CVD and cataracts. The findings will highlight the potential importance of integrating cardiovascular risk assessment into routine ophthalmologic care. Continued refinement of study methodologies and standardization of outcome measures may be needed to address observed heterogeneity and strengthen future evidence, ultimately supporting more holistic management of patients with coexisting cardiovascular and ocular conditions.

title: Immunothrombosis Biomarkers and Multi-Omics Profiles After Successful Recanalization in Patients Receiving Ischemic Postconditioning: An Exploratory Analysis of the INSPIRE Trial.
abstract: Successful recanalization after endovascular thrombectomy does not always restore microvascular perfusion, highlighting the need for adjunctive strategies. Ischemic postconditioning (IPostC) involves brief, controlled​ cycles of flow interruption and restoration at the onset of reperfusion to attenuate ischemia-reperfusion injury. In the parent INSPIRE trial, IPostC, delivered in situ as four cycles of 2-minute balloon inflation followed by 2-minute deflation at the previously occluded arterial segment immediately after successful recanalization, reduced infarct growth from baseline to 48 h. This exploratory secondary analysis included all 60 randomized patients. We investigated whether IPostC was associated with early changes in immunothrombosis, coagulation, and microvascular transit and explored associated plasma proteomic and metabolomic profiles. Arterial blood obtained approximately 15 min after successful recanalization was analyzed using flow cytometry and thromboelastography. Quantitative digital subtraction angiography-derived microcirculation time was analyzed in 55 patients, and plasma proteomic and metabolomic profiling was performed in 29 patients. Compared with controls, patients receiving IPostC had lower neutrophil CD11b expression (median, 52.15 versus 64.27 mean fluorescence intensity ×10²; P = 0.011), a lower thromboelastography α-angle (65.15° versus 67.95°; P = 0.037), and shorter microcirculation time (2.11 versus 3.03 s; P = 0.020). Longer microcirculation time was associated with greater infarct growth (r = 0.533; P < 0.001). Proteomic and metabolomic analyses identified signals involving blood-brain barrier and extracellular-matrix organization and mitochondrial bioenergetics. Biomarker comparisons were not adjusted for multiple comparisons; in the omics analyses, no protein and 17 metabolites remained significant after false discovery rate correction. In summary, IPostC was associated with lower neutrophil activation, slower clot propagation, and faster microvascular transit after recanalization, and multi-omics profiling pointed to blood-brain barrier integrity and mitochondrial bioenergetics as candidate pathways. These findings are hypothesis-generating and require validation in larger studies. Trial registration: NCT06545734, registered 9 August 2024.

In the parent INSPIRE trial, IPostC, delivered in situ as four cycles of 2-minute balloon inflation followed by 2-minute deflation at the previously occluded arterial segment immediately after successful recanalization, reduced infarct growth from baseline to 48 h.

title: Radiomics performance to identify high-risk carotid artery plaques: a systematic review.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Stroke is a leading cause of mortality worldwide, with 15-20% of ischemic strokes caused by extracranial carotid atherosclerotic disease. Risk stratification has traditionally relied on luminal stenosis severity, which inadequately reflects plaque vulnerability. Radiomics offers an emerging solution by extracting high-dimensional quantitative data from standard medical images. This systematic review evaluated the performance of radiomics-based models for identifying high-risk carotid plaques. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A systematic search was conducted across multiple databases. Studies were included if they developed or validated radiomics-based models for carotid plaque assessment and reported performance metrics, specifically the area under the curve (AUC). Data were extracted on study design, imaging modalities, segmentation methods, and modeling techniques. RESULTS: Twenty-eight studies involving 6,108 patients (72.4% male) were included. Computed tomography angiography was the most commonly used imaging modality (n = 16), and manual region-of-interest segmentation was performed in 27 of 28 studies. Radiomics models showed strong predictive performance. Internal validation AUCs were as high as 0.984, whereas combined models incorporating radiomics with clinical and/or conventional radiological features achieved the best predictive accuracy, often exceeding 0.90. However, only four studies included external validation cohorts. CONCLUSION: Radiomics is a powerful, non-invasive tool for identifying high-risk carotid plaques, offering superior discriminative power over conventional stenosis-based assessments. Despite these promising results, the field faces significant hurdles, and future research must prioritize prospective multicenter trials, the development of automated segmentation workflows, and the correlation of radiomic features with histopathological findings to ensure clinical reproducibility and transition into routine stroke prevention. KEY POINTS: Question Standard carotid atherosclerotic disease assessments fail to capture biological plaque complexity and vulnerability, necessitating objective, reproducible, and non-invasive methods to improve stroke prevention. Findings Radiomics and combined models demonstrate superior capability in identifying high-risk carotid plaques compared to traditional assessments. With four external validations, the field remains exploratory. Relevance statement Radiomics offers a non-invasive tool for personalized stroke prevention. However, technical barriers currently prevent its transition to routine clinical use, including reliance on manual segmentation and low compliance with international standardization guidelines.

Risk stratification has traditionally relied on luminal stenosis severity, which inadequately reflects plaque vulnerability. Radiomics offers an emerging solution by extracting high-dimensional quantitative data from standard medical images.

title: "Fatal venous thromboembolism and divergent phenotypes in DOCK8 deficiency: a three-sibling case series".
abstract: Dedicator of Cytokinesis 8 (DOCK8) deficiency is a rare autosomal recessive combined immunodeficiency characterized by early-onset eczema, recurrent bacterial, viral, and fungal infections, and an increased risk of malignancy. The disease arises from impaired actin cytoskeletal regulation, leading to defective immune cell migration and T-cell activation, together with the development of a Th2-skewed immune response. In this case report, we present three siblings with genetically confirmed DOCK8 deficiency and multisystem involvement. All patients presented with early-onset atopic dermatitis, recurrent respiratory tract infections, and failure to thrive. Bronchiectasis and severe viral infections were observed in all three patients. Ocular involvement developed in two patients: one experienced Cytomegalovirus (CMV) retinitis resulting in persistent visual impairment, while the other developed corneal perforation secondary to herpesvirus infection. One patient developed iatrogenic Cushing syndrome due to prolonged topical corticosteroid use. In the same patient, catheter-related superficial thrombophlebitis progressed to deep vein thrombosis and cerebral venous sinus thrombosis, with a fatal outcome complicated by probable pulmonary thromboembolism. This case series highlights the severe multisystem involvement and risk of irreversible organ damage associated with DOCK8 deficiency, and underscores the critical importance of early diagnosis and timely planning of hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HSCT) as the only curative therapeutic approach.

title: Shockwave Lithotripsy for Severe Calcified Extracranial Vertebral and Carotid Disease Treated With Percutaneous Stenting.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Patients harboring heavily calcified concentric or eccentric type lesions in the carotid or vertebral artery pose a challenge in placing a stent to reduce the lesion. These lesions yield suboptimal results due to poor stent expansion. Shockwave lithotripsy offers a potential solution for achieving luminal gain. METHODS: We present a retrospective study of all patients at our institution who were treated with lithotripsy for extracranial carotid or vertebral artery stenosis associated with heavily calcified lesions from July 2022 to February 2026. Data were maintained in our procedural database and retrospectively analyzed for patients treated with lithotripsy. All consecutive patients were analyzed for demographic information, procedural data, perioperative complications, and 6-month midterm follow-up imaging for restenosis. RESULTS: A total of 41 patients (8 vertebral artery lesions and 33 carotid lesions) were treated with intravascular lithotripsy at our institution between July 2022 and February 2026. The mean age for the cohort was 70.7 ± 8.7. The mean lesion pretreatment for the carotid stenosis was 77 ± 13% and for the vertebral artery treated patients 81 ± 11%. All patients were successfully treated with stenting and lithotripsy, and the mean stenosis posttreatment was 15 ± 14% for the carotid stenosis and 8 ± 5% for the vertebral artery lesions. There were 2 groin complications (5%) with femoral artery pseudoaneurysms treated with thrombin injection and 1 perioperative stroke (3%) secondary to a dissection in the carotid stent cohort. CONCLUSIONS: The current study demonstrates the feasibility of lithotripsy for heavily calcified lesions treated with transfemoral stenting. Future prospective core laboratory adjudicated studies are warranted to determine the efficacy of this technique.

These lesions yield suboptimal results due to poor stent expansion. Shockwave lithotripsy offers a potential solution for achieving luminal gain.

title: Association Between Hypoperfusion Intensity Ratio and Outcomes After Endovascular Thrombectomy in Posterior Circulation Stroke: A Retrospective Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The prognostic utility of the hypoperfusion intensity ratio (HIR) in posterior circulation stroke is undefined. We investigated the association between pretreatment HIR and outcomes after mechanical thrombectomy for acute posterior circulation large vessel occlusion. METHODS: This post hoc analysis of the ATTENTION (Endovascular Treatment for Acute Basilar Artery Occlusion)/ATTENTION-IA (Intra-Arterial Tenecteplase After Successful Endovascular Recanalisation in Patients With Acute Posterior Circulation Arterial Occlusion) trials included patients with posterior circulation occlusion who underwent mechanical thrombectomy and had baseline computed tomography perfusion. HIR (Tmax>10 s/ Tmax>6 s volume) was analyzed. Functional independence (modified Rankin Scale score, 0-2) at 90 days was the primary outcome. RESULTS: P P Among 139 patients, higher HIR (per 0.1 increment) was independently associated with lower odds of 90-day modified Rankin Scale score of 0 to 2 (adjusted odds ratio, 0.643 [95% CI, 0.422-0.979];=0.039). However, its discriminative ability was the modest (area under the curve, 0.617 [95% CI, 0.521-0.712]). The established anterior circulation cutoff (HIR<0.4) did not predict outcomes (=0.115). CONCLUSIONS: Elevated HIR is independently associated with worse 90-day outcomes after posterior circulation mechanical thrombectomy, but its overall prognostic utility is limited, and the anterior circulation threshold (0.4) could not be validated in this underpowered analysis, highlighting circulation-specific pathophysiological differences.

title: Distal Anastomotic New Entries After Acute Type A Aortic Dissection Surgery: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Distal anastomotic new entry (DANE) after acute type A aortic dissection repair may contribute to adverse downstream aortic remodelling. This study evaluated the incidence of postoperative DANE and its association with distal aortic growth, reintervention, and clinical outcomes. DESIGN: All consecutive patients undergoing type A aortic dissection repair with residual downstream dissection (DeBakey I) between 2011 and 2024 were retrospectively analyzed. Computed tomography angiography was systematically reviewed for DANE using 2-plane distal anastomosis alignment. Longitudinal descending thoracic aortic maximum diameters were analyzed using linear mixed-effects models. Univariable logistic regression, Kaplan-Meier estimates, and Cox proportional hazards analyses were performed. RESULTS: A total of 164 patients were included, of whom 77 (47.0%) had postoperative DANE. Patients with DANE demonstrated larger distal aortic diameters over time compared with patients without DANE, while baseline diameters were similar (37.6 vs 37.3, P = .77). At 3-5 years, estimated maximum descending thoracic aortic diameter was 51.6 vs 42.7 mm, respectively (P < .001). DANE was associated with ≥10-mm downstream aortic growth, ≥55-mm maximum diameter, and reintervention during 5-year follow-up (combined odds ratio 5.60 [2.48-12.65], P < .001). Overall survival did not differ between groups (hazard ratio 2.04 [0.80-5.18], P = .13). Cox regression demonstrated higher hazard ratios with DANE for reintervention (2.01 [1.01-3.97], P = .04) and reaching ≥55 mm aortic diameter (5.59 [2.33-13.42], P < .001). CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: DANE occurred frequently after type A aortic dissection repair and was strongly associated with accelerated downstream aortic growth and reintervention. Routine postoperative assessment and strategies aimed at preventing or treating DANE may improve long-term aortic outcomes.

This study evaluated the incidence of postoperative DANE and its association with distal aortic growth, reintervention, and clinical outcomes. DESIGN: All consecutive patients undergoing type A aortic dissection repair with residual downstream dissection (DeBakey I) between 2011 and 2024 were retrospectively analyzed.

title: Surveillance After Thoracic Aortic Surgery Yields to Low Number of Reinterventions: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
abstract: AIM: Postoperative imaging surveillance after thoracic aortic surgery is widely recommended, but its clinical yield, efficiency, and optimal targeting remain poorly defined. We aimed to quantify imaging intensity, determine the procedural yield of surveillance imaging, and assess whether follow-up strategies could be better individualized. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective single-centre cohort study of patients undergoing thoracic aortic surgery between 2010 and 2024. Postoperative imaging examinations were reviewed and linked with subsequent treatment decisions. Imaging findings, reinterventions, timing of events, detection context, and follow-up patterns were analysed. RESULTS: The cohort included 380 patients with 1757 postoperative imaging examinations, of which 1074 were classified as surveillance aortic imaging performed ≥30 days after surgery. Overall, 42 examinations led to reintervention in 29 patients (7.6%), including 13 examinations leading to aortic reoperation in 12 patients. Among surveillance aortic examinations, 41 (3.8%) led to reintervention and 16 (1.5%) met treatment thresholds without immediate intervention, yielding a combined directly or potentially actionable finding rate of 5.3%. This corresponded to 26.2 surveillance examinations per reintervention and 82.6 per aortic reoperation. Cumulative incidences of first reintervention were 2.8% at 1 year, 5.9% at 3 years, and 8.3% at 5 years. Most reinterventions were identified during elective surveillance imaging (71.4%). Despite more frequent imaging among emergency patients, reintervention risk and imaging yield were similar to those of non-emergency patients. CONCLUSIONS: Postoperative imaging surveillance after thoracic aortic surgery was associated with substantial imaging burden but low immediate procedural yield, with clinically relevant findings concentrated in a minority of patients. These findings support the need to better define patient-specific risk and imaging efficiency but do not establish that less intensive surveillance would be safe without prospective validation.

We aimed to quantify imaging intensity, determine the procedural yield of surveillance imaging, and assess whether follow-up strategies could be better individualized. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective single-centre cohort study of patients undergoing thoracic aortic surgery between 2010 and 2024.

title: Angiosarcoma in the Setting of Vascular Procedures: A Systematic Review and Our Experiences.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Angiosarcoma is a rare, aggressive endothelial malignancy with a poor prognosis; diagnosis is often delayed by vague symptoms, nonspecific imaging, and challenging histopathology. Case reports have suggested an association with prior vascular procedures, with or without prosthetic material, but no causal link is established. We reviewed angiosarcoma across the full spectrum of vascular reconstruction. METHODS: We systematically reviewed English-language human studies in PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library for histologically confirmed angiosarcomas diagnosed after and anatomically related to vascular procedures. The review was registered on PROSPERO (CRD42024602643). RESULTS: We describe 3 patients with metastatic angiosarcoma contiguous with vascular prostheses: a 75-year-old male with left inguinal angiosarcoma 7 years after PTFE bypass grafting; a 69-year-old male with angiosarcoma within the aneurysm sac 7 years after endovascular aortic aneurysm repair (EVAR); and an 80-year-old male with intraluminal angiosarcoma within an EVAR limb presenting as distal embolization. Systematic review identified 44 studies comprising 46 additional cases. Including these, 49 patients were analysed: 27 associated with endovascular prostheses, 14 with open prosthetic or mixed grafts, and 8 with autologous-vein bypass. Mean diagnostic latency was 7 years (range 5 months to 18 years); mean age was 70.5 years; 12.2% were female. CONCLUSIONS: Angiosarcoma is difficult to diagnose given its nonspecific presentation but should be considered in atypical or refractory post-procedural presentations. This is the largest synthesis to date and the first to describe intraluminal EVAR-limb angiosarcoma with distal embolization. Inclusion of autologous-vein reconstructions argues against a purely prosthetic-material explanation; further investigation is needed to clarify causality.

Case reports have suggested an association with prior vascular procedures, with or without prosthetic material, but no causal link is established. We reviewed angiosarcoma across the full spectrum of vascular reconstruction.

title: Association Between Blood Pressure Variability and Acute Kidney Injury Following Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement: A Study Based on the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care-IV Database.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Acute kidney injury (AKI) following transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) is a prevalent complication that impacts patient prognosis. While blood pressure variability (BPV) has been implicated in AKI among patients undergoing other surgical procedures, its association with AKI following TAVR remains uncharted. This study aimed to investigate the association between BPV and post-TAVR AKI. METHODS: Based on the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care database, logistic regression models were employed to investigate the associations of average real variability of systolic blood pressure (ARV-SBP) and average real variability of diastolic blood pressure (ARV-DBP) with AKI following TAVR. Multiple sensitivity analyses evaluated the robustness of the results. The marginal standardization analysis estimated the odds of AKI after ARV-SBP adjustment. RESULTS: A total of 340 patients undergoing TAVR were enrolled, among whom 107 (31.5%) developed AKI. Logistic regression analysis demonstrated a positive correlation between ARV-SBP and the odds of post-TAVR AKI (odds ratio [OR] = 1.34, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.03-1.74, P = .029) in the fully adjusted model. In contrast, no significant correlation was observed between ARV-DBP and AKI (P = .559). In covariate and blood pressure measurement sensitivity analyses, the direction of the ARV-SBP effect was generally consistent with that in the primary analysis. Marginal standardization analysis demonstrated that higher ARV-SBP levels were associated with elevated odds of AKI. CONCLUSIONS: Elevated ARV-SBP was associated with increased odds of post-TAVR AKI. Average real variability of systolic blood pressure may serve as an auxiliary indicator for early risk identification of post-TAVR AKI, yet its clinical value remains to be validated in prospective studies.

While blood pressure variability (BPV) has been implicated in AKI among patients undergoing other surgical procedures, its association with AKI following TAVR remains uncharted. This study aimed to investigate the association between BPV and post-TAVR AKI.

title: Role of Microcatheter Tip Position and Microguidewire Stiffness in Safe Neuroendovascular Navigation of Distal Vessels.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Advancements in neuroendovascular devices have enabled greater access to distal, tortuous vasculature. However, this expanded capability also increases the risk of serious hemorrhagic complications during device navigation. The aim of the study is to quantify how microcatheter position and microguidewire stiffness affect tip contact force at a distal MCA segment. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A moderate-tortuosity silicone model of the MCA was used to evaluate three 0.014-inch Synchro SELECT microguidewires (Soft, Standard, and Support) with a TrevoTrak microcatheter positioned proximally in the M1 or distally in the M2 segment. Tip contact forces at the distal end of the M2 segment were recorded with a digital force gauge serving as a standardized surrogate for the distal vessel wall during motorized controlled wire advancement. From the force-distance curves, tip contact force slopes (mN/mm) and maximum tip contact forces (mN) were calculated and statistically compared across wire types and catheter positions. RESULTS: P P With distal microcatheter support, the average tip contact force slopes were 10.64 mN/mm (Soft), 10.85 mN/mm (Standard), and 15.28 mN/mm (Support) (< .0001). With proximal support, the average slopes were significantly lower: 1.61 mN/mm (Soft), 3.15 mN/mm (Standard), and 3.87 mN/mm (Support) (< .01). Distal microcatheter positioning consistently produced approximately 3- to 6-fold higher tip contact force slopes and higher maximum tip contact forces than proximal positioning. CONCLUSIONS: Microcatheter tip position and microguidewire stiffness were the primary determinants of the tip contact force transmitted to distal vessel segments during neuroendovascular navigation in this model. Stiffer microguidewires exert significantly greater tip contact force, particularly when the microcatheter is positioned near the distal segment. Maintaining the microcatheter tip proximally attenuates these forces and offers a simple strategy to reduce mechanic loading of fragile distal branches during distal access procedures.

title: Histologically Validated Ex Vivo Characterization of Intraplaque Hemorrhage and Lipid Components Using Quantitative Susceptibility Mapping.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Accurate characterization of carotid plaque components is essential for stroke risk assessment. Intraplaque hemorrhage (IPH) is a well-established marker of plaque vulnerability, whereas lipid-rich necrotic cores (LRNCs) often show overlapping signal characteristics with IPH on conventional MRI. The purpose of this study was to compare quantitative susceptibility mapping (QSM) with conventional MRI in differentiating IPH and lipid components in carotid plaques using ex vivo histologic validation. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Twenty-four carotid plaque specimens obtained by en bloc excision during carotid endarterectomy between October 2017 and August 2021 were examined. All specimens underwent ex vivo MRI at 3T, including T1WI, T2WI, and TOF-equivalent FLASH, as well as QSM reconstructed from multiecho FLASH phase data. After MRI, specimens were serially sectioned and stained using H&E and immunohistochemical techniques. ROIs corresponding to histologically confirmed IPH and lipid components were delineated on MRI by consensus of 2 radiologists. On conventional MRI, signal intensities were measured in corresponding histologic regions, and contrast-to-noise ratios (CNRs) were calculated relative to surrounding agarose gel. On QSM, absolute magnetic susceptibility values were measured in the same regions. The difference between plaque tissue and the surrounding agarose gel was defined as the relative susceptibility value (rSV), which was used for statistical analysis. CNRs and rSVs among plaque components were compared using the Kruskal-Wallis test, followed by the Steel-Dwass test for pair-wise comparisons. RESULTS: P P P Seventy-nine matched cross-sectional slices were analyzed, yielding 24 IPH, 61 LRNCs, and 13 foam-cell aggregates (FAs). No significant difference in CNR was observed between IPH and LRNC on T1WI or FLASH. Histopathologic analysis demonstrated that many LRNCs exhibited erythrocyte-derived remnants consistent with prior hemorrhagic events. FAs showed lower CNRs than IPH on T1WI and FLASH (< .05). On T2WI, IPH showed lower CNRs than LRNCs or FAs (< .05). On QSM, IPH demonstrated higher rSVs than LRNCs or FAs (< .01). CONCLUSIONS: Histologic validation demonstrates that many LRNCs contain erythrocyte remnants, which may contribute to their overlapping signal characteristics with IPH on conventional MRI. QSM captures erythrocyte-derived susceptibility effects within plaques and provides complementary susceptibility-based information not available from conventional MRI.

The purpose of this study was to compare quantitative susceptibility mapping (QSM) with conventional MRI in differentiating IPH and lipid components in carotid plaques using ex vivo histologic validation.

title: Characterization of Perfusion Scotoma in Acute Ischemic Stroke after Endovascular Treatment.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: CTP may underestimate the size of the ischemic core, a phenomenon known as perfusion scotoma. We aimed to investigate the prevalence of perfusion scotoma, characterize its baseline predictors, and explore its association with functional outcomes in a real-world population of patients with stroke treated with endovascular treatment (EVT). MATERIALS AND METHODS: P Data were obtained from a prospective EVT registry, selecting patients with successful recanaliztion (final modified TICI ≥2b), a good-quality baseline CTP, and an available 24-hour noncontrast CT. Ischemic core underestimated volume (ICuV) was calculated as the difference between follow-up infarct volume and CTP-estimated ischemic core. The primary outcome was the presence of perfusion scotoma, defined as ICuV ≥10 mL. Baseline characteristics withvalue <.20 in univariable comparisons were entered in a backward stepwise, multivariable logistic regression analysis to identify factors independently associated with perfusion scotoma. RESULTS: P P P P A total of 464 patients of 672 (69%) were included in the analysis. The median age was 74 years (interquartile range = 68-83), 215 (46.3%) were men, and 116 (25%) had a perfusion scotoma. Perfusion scotoma was independently associated with male sex (adjusted OR 1.62 [95% CI, 1.01-2.51];= .04), more distal site of occlusion (adjusted OR 1.60 [95% CI, 1.10-2.34];= .01; per each 1-point increase: terminal ICA to M1 to M2), lower ASPECTS at admission (adjusted OR 0.64 [95% CI, 0.54-0.76];< .001; per each 1-point increase), and longer onset-to-CT time (adjusted OR 1.05, [95% CI, 1.01-1.10];= .03; per each 1-hour increase). The optimal onset-to-CT time cutoff to distinguish between patients without and with perfusion scotoma was 420 minutes. Perfusion scotoma was associated with 90-day ordinal mRS (adjusted common OR 3.16 [95% CI, 2.12-4.76]). CONCLUSIONS: Perfusion scotoma occurred in 1 of every 4 patients. Baseline predictors included male sex, lower ASPECTS, more distal vessel occlusion, and longer onset-to-CT time. Perfusion scotoma was associated with poorer functional outcomes.

title: The Latest Progress in the Application of Tofacitinib in Rheumatic Diseases--A Narrative Review.
abstract: Tofacitinib is an oral Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitor that modulates cytokine-dependent JAK/STAT signaling and has been extensively investigated in rheumatic diseases. This narrative review provides an updated synthesis of the pharmacological characteristics, mechanisms of action, clinical efficacy, safety, drug-drug interactions and dosing considerations of tofacitinib in special populations. The relevant literature published from January 2013 through December 2025 was identified through searches of MEDLINE, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and Google Scholar, supplemented by manual screening of reference lists. After screening and eligibility assessment, 89 clinical publications were included in the disease-specific evidence synthesis, and the strength of clinical evidence across disease indications was evaluated qualitatively. The most robust evidence is available for rheumatoid arthritis, with randomized trials, long-term extension studies, and real-world investigations demonstrating improvements in disease activity and physical function and inhibition of radiographic progression. Clinical evidence also supports therapeutic benefit in psoriatic arthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, and juvenile idiopathic arthritis, whereas evidence for Takayasu arteritis, polymyalgia rheumatica, systemic lupus erythematosus, and anti-MDA5-positive dermatomyositis-associated interstitial lung disease remains limited or exploratory. Long-term integrated safety analyses in RA have reported incidence rates of serious adverse events of approximately 9.0-9.4 per 100 patient-years and serious infections of approximately 2.5-2.7 per 100 patient-years, while herpes zoster, major adverse cardiovascular events, venous thromboembolism, and malignancy remain clinically important safety considerations. Potential drug-drug interactions and dose adjustment in patients with renal or hepatic impairment and other special populations further require individualized assessment. Overall, tofacitinib has a well-established role in RA treatment and potential therapeutic value in several other rheumatic diseases; however, its use should be guided by disease-specific evidence, previous treatment exposure, comorbidities, concomitant medications, and individual safety risks. Further prospective and long-term studies are needed to better define its role in less well-established indications and special populations.
englishSummary: Tofacitinib is an oral Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitor that modulates cytokine-dependent JAK/STAT signaling and has been extensively investigated in rheumatic diseases. This narrative review provides an updated synthesis of the pharmacological characteristics, mechanisms of action, clinical efficacy, safety, drug-drug interactions and dosing considerations of tofacitinib in special populations. The relevant literature published from January 2013 through December 2025 was identified through searches of MEDLINE, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and Google Scholar, supplemented by manual screening of reference lists.

title: Sex-associated territory-specific vascular phenotypes in genetically confirmed vascular Ehlers-Danlos syndrome.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: COL3A1 To characterise territory-specific sex-associated vascular phenotypes in genetically confirmed vascular Ehlers-Danlos syndrome and assess whether associations persisted after accounting formolecular mechanism. METHODS: In this retrospective multicentre cohort, clinical-genomics review identified 95 eligible patients from 110 source records. 18 prespecified vascular outcomes were evaluated using Firth bias-reduced logistic regression adjusted for completed age per 10-year increment. Sensitivity analyses among 75 patients with classifiable dominant-negative or haploinsufficient mechanisms additionally adjusted for molecular mechanism. RESULTS: The cohort included 34 male and 61 female patients. Male sex was associated with ascending aortic dilation or aneurysm (adjusted OR 4.88, 95% CI 1.68 to 15.41), iliac/femoral aneurysm (4.61, 95% CI 1.79 to 12.52), extra-aortic dissection (3.93, 95% CI 1.61 to 10.24), renal dissection (10.08, 95% CI 3.08 to 42.11) and splanchnic dissection (5.84, 95% CI 2.27 to 15.90). Aortic dissection and cervical aneurysm or dissection were not associated with male sex. In the imaging-restricted unadjusted comparison, head and neck tortuosity, ectasia or dilation was present in 23/44 (52.3%) female and 7/29 (24.1%) male patients (p=0.028). In genotype sensitivity analyses, associations remained for iliac/femoral, renal and splanchnic aneurysms and for extra-aortic, renal, splanchnic and iliac dissections, whereas several broader aneurysm and intervention estimates became less precise. CONCLUSIONS: Male sex was associated with a territory-specific vascular phenotype, with the most consistent genotype-adjusted associations involving renal, splanchnic, iliac/femoral and broader extra-aortic dissection territories. Surveillance should remain comprehensive rather than sex restricted.

title: Clinical and economic burden of major lower-limb amputations attributable to peripheral artery disease in Italy: A nationwide analysis.
abstract: Peripheral artery disease (PAD) represents a major cause of non-traumatic lower-limb amputation and is associated with substantial morbidity, mortality, and healthcare costs. Despite advances in medical and revascularization therapies, major amputations remain frequent, and comprehensive nationwide estimates of their clinical and hospital-related economic burden within the Italian National Health Service (SSN) are limited. The objectives of this study were to estimate the hospital-related economic burden of major lower-limb amputations attributable to PAD in Italy and to assess revascularization patterns and in-hospital mortality within the SSN. We conducted a nationwide observational study using the Italian National Hospital Discharge Database. Acute hospital discharges between 2015 and 2021 with a major lower-limb amputation and Diagnosis Related Group 113 were identified. Inpatient volumes, length of stay, and costs were estimated by amputation level. A longitudinal cohort of patients amputated between 2015 and 2017 was followed for two years before and after the index hospitalization to assess prior revascularization and in-hospital mortality using age- and sex-adjusted Cox models. A total of 26,417 PAD-attributable major amputations were identified, 75.6% of which were above-knee procedures. Cumulative inpatient expenditure reached €294 million, corresponding to over 511,000 hospital days. Only 46.0% of patients underwent revascularization before amputation. In-hospital mortality increased steeply within the first six months post-amputation and remained higher after above-knee procedures and among patients with diabetes, reaching 16-25% at 180 days and 23-34% at two years. Major lower-limb amputation remains a severe and costly outcome of PAD in Italy. Improved implementation of guideline-recommended PAD management is needed to reduce avoidable amputations and their economic burden on the SSN.

title: Orthoplastic Limb Salvage Using Transtibial Transport and Free-Flap Reconstruction in Patients With Diabetes-Related Chronic Limb-Threatening Ischemia.
abstract: Early revascularization-through endovascular or open surgery-is the cornerstone of treatment for chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI). However, some patients are deemed "no-option" because of diffuse infrapopliteal disease, poor distal runoff, or failed previous interventions, leaving limited limb-salvage strategies. We report an orthoplastic limb-salvage case in a 56-year-old man with poorly controlled diabetes, severe peripheral arterial disease, and a chronic foot ulcer complicated by toe gangrene after unsuccessful revascularization. After urgent radical débridement, ray amputation, culture-directed antibiotics, and negative-pressure wound therapy, transtibial transport (TTT) was done to improve microcirculation. After infection control and wound stabilization, definitive reconstruction was achieved using a large anterolateral thigh perforator free flap with a flow-through microsurgical technique to provide durable coverage while preserving distal perfusion. At 12-month follow-up, the flap remained viable with complete epithelialization, no ulcer recurrence, preserved foot architecture, and independent ambulation with protective footwear, indicating meaningful functional recovery. This case highlights the potential role of combining TTT with microsurgical reconstruction in orthoplastic management of "no-option" CLTI. Enhancing microcirculation alongside robust soft-tissue coverage may expand limb-salvage possibilities when traditional revascularization is not feasible.
