title: Functional outcomes and quality of life after endovascular thrombectomy in large and extensive infarcts (ASPECTS 0-5): a multicentre registry study.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) is established for large infarcts, but remains cautiously applied in extensive infarcts with an Alberta Stroke Program Early CT Score (ASPECTS) of 0-2. Real-life outcome data remain limited. PATIENTS AND METHODS: Retrospective analysis of the German Stroke Registry-Endovascular Treatment comparing extensive (ASPECTS 0-2) and large infarcts (ASPECTS 3-5) in patients with anterior-circulation occlusion and EVT. The primary outcome was the ordinal 90-day mRS distribution; secondary outcomes were mRS 0-3, survival, quality of life (3-level European Quality of Life-5 Dimensions) and living condition. RESULTS: Of 18,069 screened patients, 889 were analysed (ASPECTS 1-2, n = 89; ASPECTS 3-5, n = 800); none had ASPECTS 0. With ASPECTS 1-2, 20.2% achieved mRS 0-3 and 55.1% died within 90 days. In the model including successful reperfusion, no statistically significant association was detected between infarct group and the 90-day mRS distribution (common odds ratio [cOR] 0.80; 95% CI, 0.53-1.23) or mRS 0-3 (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 0.89; 95% CI, 0.64-1.25), whereas successful reperfusion was associated with both (cOR 3.68; 95% CI, 2.31-5.85 and aOR 4.10; 95% CI, 2.45-6.86). Among survivors, median European Quality of Life-5 Dimensions utility index was 0.445 vs 0.541 (n = 27/324), and 51.5% vs 50.9% lived at home (n = 33/411). DISCUSSION: An extensive infarct carried a challenging prognosis, yet acceptable outcome and non-institutional living remained achievable in a relevant minority. An independent association of infarct group with outcome was not detected. CONCLUSION: An acceptable outcome remained attainable in selected patients with extensive infarction, particularly after successful reperfusion. Lacking a medically managed comparator, these data describe prognosis rather than treatment effect.

title: Trends and Disparities in Peripheral Artery Disease and Dementia-Related Mortality in the United States, 1999-2024.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular risk factors are common among individuals with both peripheral artery disease (PAD) and dementia, and these co-existing conditions are a major public health problem. Our goal is to assess nationwide mortality trends and disparities associated with concomitant PAD and dementia in the United States between 1999 and 2024. METHODS: This is a population-based analysis using the CDC WONDER Multiple Cause of Death database to assess adults aged 65 years and older. Death certificates that mentioned both PAD and dementia were included. Age-adjusted mortality rates (AAMRs) and annual percent changes (APCs) were calculated to study the national trends by demographic and geographic subgroups. RESULTS: There were 317,390 deaths among patients who had both PAD and dementia. The overall AAMR was fairly stable over the study period, rising marginally from 23.97 in 1999 to 24.22 in 2024. AAMRs were higher in non-Hispanic African Americans across racial and ethnic groups and peaked in non-metropolitan regions. The sensitivity analyses showed that mortality rates that were driven by PAD significantly declined (AAPC: -4.77) and rates driven by dementia (AAPC: 3.77) increased significantly over the 25-year period. CONCLUSIONS: Overall, the age-standardized mortality for concomitant PAD and dementia was largely stable, but there are still important geographical and demographic differences. The mortality curves when divided by underlying cause of death show that deaths due to PAD have decreased, while deaths due to dementia have risen in the United States among older adults over the study period.

title: Knowledge, Attitudes and Self-Reported Practices of Emergency and Intensive Care Nurses in Managing Traumatic Brain Injury.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) is a leading cause of mortality and disability worldwide, with a growing burden in low- and middle-income countries. Nurses in emergency and intensive care units (ICUs) play a critical role in TBI management, yet little is known about their competencies in Palestine. AIMS: This study aimed to assess the knowledge, attitudes and self-reported practices of emergency and intensive care unit nurses regarding traumatic brain injury management and to identify factors associated with these outcomes. STUDY DESIGN: A descriptive cross-sectional survey using stratified random sampling was conducted in governmental and private hospitals in the northern West Bank, Palestine. Data were collected in January 2025 using a validated Arabic questionnaire. Descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation coefficients and multiple linear regression analyses were performed, with statistical significance set at p < 0.05. RESULTS: A total of 151 nurses participated, yielding a response rate of 61.4% (151/246). Nurses demonstrated generally good foundational knowledge, particularly in Glasgow Coma Scale interpretation and recognition of neurological responses, although gaps remained in advanced monitoring. Attitudes were predominantly positive, with strong support for specialised training. Self-reported practices included maintaining adequate blood pressure and initiating deep vein thrombosis (DVT) prophylaxis. Knowledge correlated significantly with attitude and self-reported practice, and attitude correlated strongly with self-reported practice. Previous TBI training, higher educational level and longer clinical experience were associated with better outcomes. CONCLUSIONS: Emergency and intensive care unit nurses demonstrated adequate foundational knowledge and positive attitudes towards traumatic brain injury management, although gaps remained in advanced monitoring and selected self-reported practices. Structured continuing professional development, standardised protocols and organisational support are needed to strengthen neurotrauma nursing care. RELEVANCE TO CLINICAL PRACTICE: The findings support context-sensitive continuing education, simulation, standardised protocols and organisational measures that enable nurses to translate knowledge into consistent neurotrauma care in resource-constrained settings.

title: Mortality, Morbidity, and Treatment-Related Outcomes Following Pathological Hip Fractures: An 8-Year Single-Center Experience.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: This study aimed to evaluate the clinical characteristics, type of treatment, and factors associated with mortality and morbidity, including the length of hospital stay, among patients with pathological hip fractures in a tertiary center in Saudi Arabia. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A retrospective study was conducted, which included all adult patients diagnosed with pathological hip fractures from 2016 to 2024. Demographics, fracture type, type of treatment, complications, and outcomes data were evaluated. A univariate analysis was performed to identify associations between clinical variables and patient outcomes. RESULTS: A total of 47 patients were included, with a mean age of 60.6 ± 17.12 years. Most patients were female (61.7%) and had femoral neck fractures (63.8%). Surgical treatment was performed in 78.7% of cases. The overall mortality rate was 6.4%, and 17.0% of patients experienced complications, including gait disturbances, bleeding, and deep vein thrombosis. Mortality was significantly associated with conservative treatment (P = 0.007). All deaths occurred in the conservatively treated group. Longer hospital stays were linked to pre-operative anticoagulant use (P = 0.011) and osteoporosis (P = 0.03). CONCLUSION: Surgical management of pathological hip fractures was associated with improved survival and should be prioritized when clinically feasible. Awareness of pre-operative anticoagulant use and osteoporosis is essential for perioperative planning and may help reduce prolonged hospitalization in this high-risk population.

title: Limb Salvage in Limb-Threatening Necrotizing Fasciitis of the Diabetic Foot: A Case Report.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Necrotizing fasciitis (NF) is a rapidly progressive soft tissue infection with high morbidity and mortality, especially in patients with diabetes mellitus. Early diagnosis is challenging because initial clinical signs may be subtle, yet timely intervention is critical to prevent limb loss and death. CASE REPORT: We report a 68-year-old male with long-standing type 2 diabetes mellitus and multiple comorbidities who presented with a 1-week history of rapidly progressive left foot pain and swelling extending to the mid-calf. Laboratory investigations revealed marked inflammation, and imaging indicated fascial involvement. The patient underwent multiple surgical debridements, broad-spectrum intravenous antibiotics, strict glycemic control, limb off-loading, tibial angioplasty to optimize perfusion, and advanced wound care including negative pressure wound therapy and reconstructive procedures. Progressive healing was achieved without major amputation. CONCLUSION: Limb salvage remains feasible in selected diabetic patients with limb-threatening NF when early recognition, aggressive surgical management, vascular optimization, metabolic control, and coordinated multidisciplinary care are implemented.

title: [Successful Hybrid Treatment of Crawford Type IV Thoracoabdominal Aortic Aneurysm:Report of a Case].
abstract: Thoracolaparotomy remains the first-line surgical approach for thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysms. However, there is still room for improvement with regard to mortality and the incidence of postoperative complications, including paraplegia. In this context, hybrid treatment strategies that allow preservation of organ blood flow have gained increasing attention. We report a case of a Crawford type IV thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysm that was successfully treated using a hybrid approach. The patient was an 87-year-old man. Computed tomography (CT) at admission revealed a thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysm. Given the patient's advanced age and severe frailty, thoracolaparotomy was considered high risk. As the primary surgery, abdominal total debranching with thoracic endovascular aortic repair was performed. Bypasses from the right external iliac artery to visceral arteries were made, and stent graft was deployed in the thoracic artery. Anastomosis to the left renal artery was technically impossible. On postoperative day two, endovascular abdominal aortic stent graft was implanted. The patient was extubated on postoperative day 4, and was transferred to a rehabilitation hospital on postoperative day 29.

title: [Non-anatomic Bypass for Severe Brachiocephalic Artery Stenosis due to Dissecting Aneurysm After Total Arch Aortic Replacement for Stanford Type A Acute Aortic Dissection:Report of a Case].
abstract: Dissecting brachiocephalic artery aneurysm after total arch aortic replacement poses a risk of postoperative cerebral infarction, yet no consensus exists regarding optimal management. Treatment decisions rely on the patient's condition, degree of true lumen stenosis, and lesion characteristics. We report a case of a dissecting brachiocephalic aneurysm with severe true lumen stenosis following surgery for Stanford type A acute aortic dissection. A 70-year-old man was transferred to our hospital with acute aortic dissection and multiple right-hemispheric cerebral infarctions and underwent emergency total arch replacement. On postoperative day nine, contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) revealed progressive false lumen expansion with significant true lumen compression. To prevent further cerebral ischemia, a left axillary-right common carotid artery non-anatomic bypass was performed. The patient gradually recovered left upper limb function and was transferred for rehabilitation on postoperative day 27.

title: [Aortic Root Replacement for a Left Sinus of Valsalva Aneurysm Complicated by Ascending Aortic Dissection:Report of a Case].
abstract: We report a case of a left sinus of Valsalva aneurysm (SVA) complicated by ascending aortic dissection (AAD). A 37-year-old man presented to our hospital with worsening leg edema and was diagnosed with heart failure due to severe aortic regurgitation (AR). Contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) and transesophageal echocardiography revealed the presence of an AAD and a left SVA. After medical treatment for heart failure, the patient underwent aortic root replacement. The postoperative course was favorable. The combination of SVA and AAD in a young patient is extremely rare and may lead to delayed diagnosis. Therefore, thorough investigation of the underlying cause is essential, particularly in young patients presenting with heart failure or AR.

title: Nomogram for Postoperative Permanent Neurologic Dysfunction Following Acute Type A Aortic Dissection Surgery: A Multicentral Retrospective Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Permanent neurologic dysfunction (PND) often complicates following surgery for acute type A aortic dissection (ATAAD) and is strongly correlated with unfavorable outcomes. Consequently, developing an effective diagnostic method to identify high-risk patients is of considerable importance. METHODS: This retrospective study, covering 2022 to 2024 across two centers, ultimately included 117 ATAAD patients with Supra-Aortic Branch Vessel (SABV) dissection from our center (2022-2023) as the training set and 52 ATAAD patients with SABV dissection from a secondary center (2024) as the validation set. We used logistic regression to identify predictors and developed a nomogram, which was assessed using the area under the ROC curve, calibration and decision curve analysis. External validation was conducted using the validation set. RESULTS: In this study, 169 cases were finally collected (117 in the training set and 52 in the validation set), of whom 64 patients developed postoperative PND. Four risk factors were identified: brachiocephalic trunk dissection at the bifurcation plane, chronic kidney disease, age over 50, and cross-clamp duration over 168 min. The AUC was 0.809 for the training set and 0.736 for the validation set. The nomogram model demonstrated acceptable predictive performance, and decision curve analysis potential clinical utility for predicting postoperative PND risk for thresholds of 1%-90% in the training set and 3%-75% in the validation set. CONCLUSIONS: This study developed and validated a predictive model for assessing the risk of postoperative PND in patients undergoing ATAAD surgery, which may assist clinicians in individualized risk assessment.

Consequently, developing an effective diagnostic method to identify high-risk patients is of considerable importance. METHODS: This retrospective study, covering 2022 to 2024 across two centers, ultimately included 117 ATAAD patients with Supra-Aortic Branch Vessel (SABV) dissection from our center (2022-2023) as the training set and 52 ATAAD patients with SABV dissection from a secondary center (2024) as the validation set.

title: Ethnic Differences in Clinical Manifestations of Behçet's Disease: A Retrospective Cohort Study of Turkic and Non-Turkic Patients.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Behçet's disease (BD) is a multisystem inflammatory vasculitis with clinical heterogeneity that may vary across ethnic groups within the same country. This study aimed to evaluate the influence of ethnicity on the clinical manifestations, immunogenic laboratory findings and disease course of BD by comparing Turkic and non-Turkic patients in a large Iranian referral cohort. METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study, 2697 patients with BD followed at the BD clinic of Shariati Hospital in Tehran, Iran, from 2007 to 2019 were included. RESULTS: Patients were stratified by ethnicity into Turkic (N = 1037; 38.5%) and non-Turkic (N = 1660; 61.5% [with Persian/Fars, N = 980 subgrouping]) groups, and demographic, clinical manifestations, and immunogenic laboratory findings were extracted from medical records. Mean age at BD onset was 25.72 ± 10.02 years in Turkic patients and 24.69 ± 10.23 years in non-Turkic patients, and males comprised 61.3% and 57.1% of the two groups, respectively. Human leukocyte antigen (HLA)-B5 positivity was 55.1% in Turkic versus 53.1% in non-Turkic patients, and HLA-B51 positivity was 48.7% versus 46.5%, respectively. Most clinical manifestations showed similar prevalence across groups, including oral aphthous ulcers (98.7% vs. 99.0%), genital aphthous ulcers (60.5% vs. 62.0%), uveitis (50.1% vs. 53.2%), and deep vein thrombosis (5.3% vs. 5.1%). Superficial phlebitis was more frequent in Turkic patients (p = 0.02), and oral aphthous ulcers occurred earlier in Turkic patients (p = 0.023). A three-class latent class model demonstrated the best fit (BIC = 14,986.58). In multinomial logistic regression analysis, Turkic patients had slightly higher odds ratio of the ocular-predominant phenotype (OR = 1.10, 95% CI: 0.91-1.33; p = 0.320) and slightly lower odds ratio of the multisystem phenotype (OR = 0.94, 95% CI: 0.68-1.30; p = 0.692); however, neither association was statistically significant. Female gender was associated with higher odds ratio of the ocular-predominant phenotype than the mucocutaneous-predominant phenotype (OR = 1.38, 95% CI: 1.14-1.67; p = 0.001). CONCLUSION: In this large Iranian BD cohort, Turkic and non-Turkic patients exhibited broadly similar disease phenotypes and comparable HLA-B51 frequencies, with small but potentially relevant ethnic differences in the timing of oral ulcers and the frequency of superficial phlebitis. These findings suggest that ethnicity may influence BD phenotype through mechanisms beyond HLA-B51, possibly involving other immune-related genetic variants such as tumor necrosis factor (TNF)-α, endoplasmic reticulum aminopeptidase 1(ERAP1), Interleukin (IL)-10. Of note, the significant differences observed in Turkic versus non-Turkic comparisons were not present in the Turkic versus Persian (Fars) comparison, indicating that the findings are not driven by a single ethnic subgroup.

This study aimed to evaluate the influence of ethnicity on the clinical manifestations, immunogenic laboratory findings and disease course of BD by comparing Turkic and non-Turkic patients in a large Iranian referral cohort. METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study, 2697 patients with BD followed at the BD clinic of Shariati Hospital in Tehran, Iran, from 2007 to 2019 were included.

title: Wound blush as a predictor for limb salvage among people with non-healing diabetic foot ulcers.
abstract: Background and objectives Wound blush represents angiographic visualisation of tissue-level perfusion around a diabetic foot ulcer. While wound blush after endovascular revascularisation (EVR) predicts improved outcomes, its' prognostic value on diagnostic digital subtraction angiography (DSA) has not been studied, particularly in India. This study compared the role of wound blush after DSA and after EVR in predicting wound healing and limb salvage in non-healing diabetic foot ulcers. Methods A total of 428 individuals with diabetic foot ulcers underwent diagnostic DSA. Wound blush was assessed on DSA and, where applicable, after EVR. Participants were followed for wound healing and amputation outcomes. The wound blush positive and wound blush negative groups on DSA, among participants managed without EVR, and according to wound blush status following EVR were compared. Results On diagnostic DSA, 137(31.6%) participants were wound blush positive and 291(68.4%) were wound blush negative. Wound blush positive participants demonstrated higher rates of complete wound healing (90.5% vs. 79%; P=0.002), and lower amputation rates (7.6 vs. 22.2%; P<0.001) compared to wound blush negative participants. Among participants managed without EVR, limb salvage was significantly higher in wound blush positive than wound blush negative participants (92.4% vs.77.8%; P=0.002). Following EVR, limb salvage was achieved in 89% of participants who demonstrated wound blush compared to 77% (P=0.062) of those who remained wound blush negative. Baseline wound blush positivity predicted favourable outcomes irrespective of EVR. Interpretation and conclusions Wound blush on diagnostic angiography and after EVR is a strong predictor of wound healing and limb salvage in non-healing diabetic foot ulcers. Wound blush on initial DSA helps identifying participants in whom revascularisation may be deferred, reducing endovascular interventions without adverse limb outcomes.

title: Development of Aortic Stents from Open Surgery to Endovascular Therapy: A Brazilian Contribution to the Treatment of Aortic Diseases.
abstract: The treatment of aortic diseases has undergone profound transformation over the last decades, with the progressive incorporation of endovascular techniques either replacing or complementing conventional open surgical repair. The development of aortic stents represents one of the most significant milestones in this transition. This article reviews the historical, experimental, and clinical evolution of aortic stents, with emphasis on pioneering Brazilian contributions, including the experimental phase in animal models, the first clinical applications in aortic dissection, and the role of the national industry in the development and dissemination of these technologies. The impact of these innovations on contemporary cardiovascular surgical practice and future perspectives are also discussed.

title: State of Art of Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation for the Treatment of Aortic Stenosis in Low-Risk Patients: A Perspective on Brazilian Contributions and Implementation Challenges.
abstract: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) has profoundly changed the management of severe aortic stenosis (AS), evolving from a treatment reserved for inoperable and high-risk patients to an established therapeutic option across a wide surgical risk spectrum. Although the expansion of TAVI indications has been largely supported by randomized clinical trials conducted in high-income countries, real-world experience and technological contributions from distinct healthcare systems are increasingly relevant. Brazil has played a significant role in the early adoption, structured implementation, and clinical evaluation of TAVI in Latin America. Since the first procedures performed in 2008, Brazilian centers have developed Heart Team models, contributed to national and regional registries, and generated real-world evidence demonstrating procedural safety and effectiveness comparable to international benchmarks, despite the presence of resource limitations and a higher prevalence of complex clinical and anatomical scenarios. The incorporation of TAVI into the Brazilian public health system in 2022 marked a major milestone in expanding access to minimally invasive therapy for patients with severe AS. In parallel, Brazilian scientific societies have adapted international guideline recommendations to local practice, supporting evidence-based patient selection across different surgical risk categories. Notably, Brazil has also emerged as a developer of locally engineered transcatheter valve technologies, highlighting its transition from a technology consumer to an active contributor in the field of structural heart disease. This review summarizes the historical evolution, national experience, clinical outcomes, guideline integration, technological innovation, and health economic considerations of TAVI in Brazil.

title: Snare-Assisted Traction Technique for Renal Artery Reconstruction in Endovascular Repair of Complex Thoracoabdominal Aortic Aneurysms.
abstract: Renal artery (RA) reconstruction during complex endovascular aortic repair often fails in hostile anatomy because of inadequate guidewire support. We describe snare-assisted traction (SAT), a novel endovascular bailout technique using conventional off-the-shelf devices. By combining distal snare traction with a long femoral sheath, SAT shifts target vessel reconstruction from simple wire guidance to sheath-based structural support. This provides robust stability for wire exchange and stent delivery without requiring specialized, unavailable tools or high-morbidity open conversion. Among 12 patients with severe RA angulation, ostial stenosis, or sac origin, SAT achieved 100% technical success without procedural complications. At median 6-month follow-up, all reconstructed RAs remained patent with stable renal function. SAT offers a safe, reproducible, and universally accessible solution for hostile target vessel access, significantly enhancing the feasibility and clinical safety of complex endovascular repair.

title: An anatomy-aware spatio-temporal generative extrapolation network for distal ascending aorta restoration in standard echocardiographic views.
abstract: BACKGROUND: In two-dimensional transthoracic echocardiography (TTE), the standard parasternal long-axis (PLAX) view enables reliable evaluation of the aortic valve and aortic root. Owing to the limited field of view of the ultrasound probe and rib-window occlusion, the distal ascending aorta (AA) is frequently truncated, compromising the diagnosis of aortic aneurysm and dilation. PURPOSE: We aim to address the incomplete visualization of the distal AA in standard PLAX views. By aggregating fragmented anatomical features intermittently visible in adjacent frames, we enhance the clarity of vessel wall edges and generate the distal AA structure, thereby completing the missing AA imagery in standard PLAX views. MATERIALS AND METHODS: ± Δ = 0.2 cm We retrospectively collected 1160 TTE videos from Nanjing Drum Tower Hospital (August 2022 - December 2024), all showing complete AA anatomy. After de-identification, 1059 cases were randomly split into training/validation/test sets (6:2:2), and 101 cases were reserved for observer agreement experiments. An additional 152 videos from three different device models (EPIQ CVX, GE Voluson E10, Resona A20T) formed an external validation set. Two training data types were constructed: (i) dual-view synchronous data - a standard PLAX sequence and an AO-PLAX sequence acquired after a cranial probe shift, phase-matched at end diastole (ED); and (ii) locally masked data - the distal AA region was masked, forcing the model to infer missing anatomy from left-side context. Input sequences of five frames (ED2) were extracted. The proposed Spatio-Temporal Ascending-Aorta generative adversarial network (STAA-GAN) first aligns adjacent frames using an Edge Boosted Feature Alignment (EBFA) module with multi-stage modulated deformable convolutions. A channel-wise fusion strategy then aggregates temporally aligned features. The fused representation is fed into a Swin-UNet generator enhanced with a Strip based Cross window Prediction (SCP) module to capture long-range structural dependencies. Training employs a composite loss including pixel reconstruction, feature reconstruction, texture consistency, relativistic average least-squares GAN (RaLSGAN), temporal coherence, and structure-aware terms, with data-dependent weighting. Statistical analyzes included Bland-Altman, Passing-Bablok regression, paired t-tests with Cohen's d, Bonferroni correction for multiple comparisons, and two one-sided tests (TOST,). RESULTS: α 1 = 0.00417 ≤ 0.01 ± 0.13 Δ = 0.2 p < 0.001 0.913 0.045 ± p < 0.001 d < 0.2 STAA-GAN achieved the best image-quality values among the compared methods, with peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) = 22.51 dB, structural similarity index (SSIM) = 0.7574, multi-scale structural similarity index (MS-SSIM) = 0.8598, and learned perceptual image patch similarity (LPIPS) = 0.1758. All 12 pairwise comparisons (SRN, IOH, and U-Transformer versus STAA-GAN, designated as the reference group) remained statistically significant after Bonferroni correction (), with absolute effect sizes ranging from 0.255 to 3.439. The per-frame inference time was 203 ms. In clinical consistency validation, the mean difference between measurements on generated and original images was cm with 95% limits of agreement within cm; TOST with cm confirmed clinical equivalence for all comparisons (). The segmentation Dice coefficient on generated images averagedacross five cross-validation folds. External validation on three different ultrasound devices (Philips, GE, Mindray) maintained consistent equivalence (TOST, Cohen's). These results demonstrate that STAA-GAN produces clinically interchangeable distal ascending aorta images with high fidelity and real-time feasibility. CONCLUSIONS: STAA-GAN enables extrapolation of the missing distal ascending aorta in standard PLAX views, achieving improved image quality and clinically equivalent diameter measurements on both internal and external validation datasets. These findings support its potential for assisting distal ascending aorta assessment in routine echocardiography.

title: Angiographic Signatures of Brain Collateralization.
abstract: The severity of ischemic strokes, the likelihood of successful endovascular treatment, and subsequent clinical patient outcomes are all strongly influenced by the degree of collateralization of the brain arterial network. Although several scoring systems based on different imaging modalities have been developed to assess brain collateralization, they are subjective and quite coarse and do not capture many nuances of the underlying collateral vessel distribution. This article introduces a methodology for quantitatively and objectively assessing the degree of collateralization of the brain. The strategy is based on a regional analysis of time-density curves extracted from dynamic angiographic image sequences. To investigate the dependence of the extracted metrics on the underlying collateralization in a controlled manner, a computational study is carried out by generating virtual patients with prescribed collateralization characteristics and conducting blood flow and transport simulations to create virtual angiographic sequences. The virtual angiograms of patients with large vessel occlusions and different collateral vessel distributions are used to generate "angiographic signatures" reflective of the underlying collateralization. The results show that angiographic signatures created from virtual angiograms exhibit consistent characteristics with angiographic signatures of actual stroke patients with different levels of collateralization. These findings indicate that these angiographic signatures can be used to assess the underlying collateralization of the brain and identify patients and conditions associated with adverse treatment outcomes.

title: A Case of Asymptomatic Carotid Artery Stenosis With Thumb-Sized Calcification Detected on Panoramic Radiograph.
abstract: A 73-year-old male with dyslipidemia and chronic kidney disease exhibited carotid calcification on a dental panoramic radiograph. Ultrasonography confirmed 30% asymptomatic carotid stenosis. This case highlights intimal calcification's link to kidney disease and atherosclerosis. Prompt medical-dental collaboration and diagnostic imaging remain crucial to prevent cerebrovascular events, extending healthy life expectancy.

title: Emergent Re-Do Open Aortic Valvular Repair and Foreign Body Retrieval During TAVR: A Case Report.
abstract: A 73-year-old man presented for a transcatheter aortic valve replacement after prosthetic aortic valve dysfunction. During the case, the transvenous pacer lost capture, causing the new prosthetic valve to embolize to the ascending aorta. This case details the intraoperative management throughout the valve deployment, attempted retrieval, and subsequent emergent redo open aortic valve repair with foreign body removal. Complications and considerations of a redo open chest, vasoplegia, cardiopulmonary bypass, aortic dissection, right ventricular failure, heart block, and prosthetic valve embolization are discussed.

title: [Efficacy of percutaneous mechanical thrombectomy combined with transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt for acute non-cirrhotic portal vein thrombosis].
abstract: Objective: Methods: Results: Conclusions: M t t CI CI HR CI P HR CI P HR CI P P vs. t P To evaluate the efficacy of percutaneous mechanical thrombectomy combined with transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (PMT-TIPS) in patients with acute non-cirrhotic portal vein thrombosis (NCPVT).This is a retrospective case series study. The clinical data of 61 patients with acute NCPVT who underwent PMT combined with TIPS at Department of Endovascular Surgery, the First Affiliated Hospital of Zhengzhou University between June 2017 and June 2023 were retrospectively analyzed. There were 39 males and 22 females, with an age ((IQR)) of 49.0 (24.5)years (range:21 to 73 years). Paired sample-test or Wilcoxon signed-rank test were used to compare liver volume and biochemical parameters before treatment and at 1 year after treatment. Independent sample-test was used to compare changes in liver volume between patients with different stent patency statuses. Kaplan-Meier analysis was used to estimate stent patency and symptom recurrence. Univariate and multivariate Cox proportional hazards regression models were used to analyze the factors associated with stent occlusion.Among the 61 patients, 7 (11.5%) died during hospitalization and 5 (8.2%) died within 30 days after discharge, most commonly due to bowel necrosis. The remaining 49 patients were followed up for 43 (34) months (range:4 to 94 months). During follow-up, stent occlusion occurred in 35 patients (71.4%), with a median primary patency of 13.0 months (95%: 7.3 to 18.7 months). Among the 35 patients with primary stent occlusion, 21 developed symptom recurrence, whereas symptom recurrence occurred in 4 of the 14 patients with sustained patency. Ten patients with stent occlusion underwent stent recanalization, with a median secondary patency of 21.0 months (95%: 16.8 to 25.2 months). Univariate Cox regression analysis showed that myeloproliferative neoplasms (=3.08, 95%: 1.48 to 6.42,=0.003) and dual-stent implantation (=2.26, 95%: 1.09 to 4.70,=0.036) were associated with an increased risk of stent occlusion; multivariate Cox regression further revealed that only myeloproliferative neoplasms (=2.75, 95%: 1.31 to 5.78,=0.008) was an independent risk factor. At one year post-procedure, inflammatory and coagulation markers improved, total liver volume decreased compared with baseline (=0.005), and the reduction in liver volume was greater in patients with patent stents than in those with stent occlusion ((-215.6±205.5)cm³(-3.5±236.5) cm³,=-3.505,=0.001).In patients with acute NCPVT, the PMT-TIPS technique is feasible, but long-term stent patency is limited. This technique can be used as a rescue strategy rather than a definitive treatment.

title: [Dominant false lumen flow and abnormally high shear stress: a hemodynamic analysis of multichanneled aortic dissection].
abstract: Objective: Methods: Results: Conclusions: To explore the hemodynamic characteristics of multichanneled aortic dissection (MCAD).This is a retrospective cohort study. Patients with acute uncomplicated Stanford-type B aortic dissection who presented at Zhongshan Hospital, Fudan University between January 2019 and December 2023 were enrolled. Patients were diagnosed as having either double-channeled aortic dissection (DCAD) or MCAD based on preoperative standardized computed-tomography angiography (CTA). Centered on 4 MCAD cases with preprocedural death, 4 non-preprocedural-death MCAD patients and 4 non-preprocedural-death DCAD patients with balanced baseline characteristics, complete preoperative CTA datasets and well-defined outcomes were matched, yielding a total of 12 male patients. The ages of patients in preprocedural-death MCAD group, non-preprocedural-death MCAD group and non-preprocedural- death DCAD group were (62.0±5.7) years (range:54 to 66 years), (61.5±5.8) years (range:54 to 67 years) and (61.3±8.1) years (range:52 to 71 years), respectively. Using computational fluid dynamics (CFD) and patient-specific aortic models, preoperative hemodynamic indices were quantitatively analyzed, including blood flow velocity, pressure distribution, flow distribution, wall shear stress (WSS) and time-averaged wall shear stress (TAWSS).Hemodynamic analyses revealed a stepwise decreasing trend of false lumen (FL) flow rate across the three groups. The preoperative death MCAD group exhibited a significantly higher FL flow ((62.81±7.59)ml/s (range: 56.29 to 73.78 ml/s)) than the non-preoperative death MCAD group ((24.84±9.25)ml/s (range: 17.23 to 36.84 ml/s)) and the non-preoperative death DCAD group ((11.86±5.62)ml/s (range: 6.72 to 19.84 ml/s)). The intergroup variation patterns of FL flow ratio and maximum FL TAWSS were highly consistent. The preoperative death MCAD group yielded values of 0.77±0.16 (range: 0.56 to 0.93) and (34.44±6.50)Pa (range: 27.54 to 41.38 Pa),which were elevated compared with the non-preoperative death MCAD group (0.44±0.17(range: 0.33 to 0.70), (15.46±7.75)Pa (range: 6.69 to 25.01 Pa)) and the non-preoperative death DCAD group (0.22±0.11(range: 0.14 to 0.37), (20.80±7.34)Pa (range: 15.23 to 31.60 Pa)),whereas no obvious disparities were observed between the latter two groups. In addition,the maximum FL WSS in the preoperative death MCAD group reached (125.76±26.57)Pa (range: 87.55 to 147.91 Pa),markedly exceeding that of the non-preoperative death MCAD group ((64.89±30.45)Pa (range: 28.62 to 102.40 Pa)) and the non-preoperative death DCAD group ((91.15±28.16)Pa (range: 61.51 to 126.41 Pa)).Elevated FL flow and abnormally high shear stress may correlate with poor outcomes in patients with MCAD,and these parameters could serve as potential biomechanical biomarkers. title: [Value of a CT angiography-based deep learning model for differentiating SVS grade Ⅱ and grade Ⅲ blunt thoracic aortic injury: a retrospective multicenter staged study].
abstract: Objectives: Methods: Results: Conclusions: CI To develop a segmentation-guided multitask deep learning model for Society for Vascular Surgery (SVS) grades Ⅰ to Ⅳ classification of blunt thoracic aortic injury (BTAI) and validate its clinical utility for differentiating SVS grades Ⅱ and Ⅲ.This is a retrospective case series study. Computed tomography angiography (CTA) data were collected from 317 patients with BTAI at 12 hospitals in China, including the First Medical Center of Chinese People's Liberation Army General Hospital, West China Hospital of Sichuan University, the First Affiliated Hospital of Zhengzhou University, the Affiliated Hospital of Southwest Medical University, and other local hospitals, between January 2006 and May 2026. The cohort included 258 male and 59 female patients, with an age of (54.8±15.3) years (range:16 to 92 years). The 253-patient development cohort was divided using a patient-level random split stratified by SVS injury grade and source center at an approximate ratio of 8∶2 into a training set of 202 patients and an internal validation set of 51 patients. The 64 BTAI cases from the Affiliated Hospital of Southwest Medical University were locked in advance as an independent external test set. The model consisted of a shared encoder, a lesion-segmentation branch, and a mask-guided classification branch. The primary outcomes were the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) and grade Ⅲ sensitivity for differentiating SVS grade Ⅱ (intramural hematoma) from grade Ⅲ (pseudoaneurysm) in the external test set. Secondary outcomes included segmentation, automated measurements, and offline reader-study results.The internal validation set covered SVS grades Ⅰ to Ⅳ, with an overall grading accuracy of 92.2% (47/51) and a macro-averaged F1 score of 0.919. The external test set included 31 SVS grade Ⅱ (intramural hematoma) cases and 33 SVS grade Ⅲ (pseudoaneurysm) cases. The model had an AUC of 0.968 (95%:0.924 to 0.996), an accuracy of 92.2% (59/64), grade Ⅲ sensitivity of 93.9% (31/33), and grade Ⅱ specificity of 90.3% (28/31); two grade Ⅲ cases were misclassified as grade Ⅱ. The automated segmentation success rate was 96.9% (62/64), the overall lesion Dice similarity coefficient was 0.872±0.072 (range:0.46 to 0.99), and model inference time per case was (15.4±2.4) s (range:10.8 to 22.6 s). In the fixed-sequence reader study, six junior physicians had higher grade Ⅱ/Ⅲ accuracy and grade Ⅲ sensitivity and shorter interpretation times during the artificial intelligence-assisted phase than during the unaided phase.The segmentation-guided CTA deep learning model developed in this study performed BTAI lesion segmentation, SVS grading, and measurement of key morphologic parameters, and maintained good discrimination between SVS grades Ⅱ and Ⅲ in the independent external test set. Model assistance may help reduce missed grade Ⅲ cases by junior physicians and shorten interpretation time, thereby supporting standardized imaging assessment of BTAI.

title: [Is there still a role for manual deployment techniques in the era of fenestrated/branched endovascular aortic repair? Normative boundaries and practical value in the management of hostile aortic landing zones].
abstract: Standard endovascular aortic repair has been widely used for the treatment of abdominal aortic aneurysms and selected complex aortic diseases because of its minimally invasive nature, rapid recovery, and favorable perioperative safety profile. However, in hostile aortic landing zones characterized by a short neck, severe angulation, conical neck configuration, mural thrombus, or circumferential calcification, standard endovascular repair remains associated with inadequate proximal apposition, type Ⅰ endoleak, endograft migration, and secondary intervention. Manual deployment techniques, including the push-up technique, reverse slider technique, Kabedon technique, and stepwise controlled deployment, may improve endograft axial alignment, proximal edge positioning, and local wall apposition to some extent; however, their role is mainly limited to optimization of the deployment process and cannot replace the principle of a durable sealing zone. This review summarizes the anatomical characteristics of hostile aortic landing zones, the mechanisms and clinical evidence of manual deployment techniques, the standardized value of fenestrated/branched endovascular aortic repair and physician-modified endografts, adjunctive fixation and intraoperative bailout techniques, and application scenarios in emergency repair of ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysms. The aim is to provide a practical reference for rational selection between optimized deployment of standard endografts and complex sealing-zone reconstruction in complex endovascular aortic repair.

title: [Technical considerations and advances in distal bypass for chronic limb-threatening ischemia of the lower extremities].
abstract: Chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) represents the end stage of lower extremity arterial disease and is associated with high rates of disability and mortality. With the rapid advancement of endovascular techniques, an "endovascular-first" strategy has become widely adopted. However, for patients with complex, long-segment, heavily calcified, diffuse, inflammatory lesions, or those with repeated endovascular failure, distal bypass surgery remains an indispensable option for limb salvage. The success of distal bypass depends not only on advanced surgical expertise but also on appropriate patient selection, accurate assessment of inflow and outflow tracts, optimal conduit choice, and meticulous perioperative management. Based on recent international guidelines and clinical evidence, this review focuses on key technical aspects of distal bypass, including inflow selection, target artery assessment, conduit selection, graft tunneling, distal anastomosis, intraoperative flow assessment, postoperative antithrombotic therapy and wound management. It also discusses the appropriate role of these techniques in the comprehensive treatment of CLTI based on recent evidence-based medical findings. In addition, emerging developments such as alternative conduits, and gene/cell therapy are discussed, aiming to provide insights into optimizing revascularization strategies for patients with CLTI.

title: [From critical evaluation based on the gold standard to precision full-process management: advances in the diagnosis and treatment framework for aortic arch artery pathologies].
abstract: Supra-aortic arch artery diseases, including lesions of the carotid,subclavian,and vertebral arteries,represent major causes of cerebral and upper extremity ischemia. The diagnostic and therapeutic strategies for these conditions are undergoing a profound transformation-from conventional open surgery toward minimally invasive endovascular treatment,and further to individualized precision medicine. Recent advances in imaging assessment have substantially improved lesion characterization and risk stratification. The iterative evolution of endovascular devices has enhanced procedural safety. Meanwhile,several topics have become research hotspots,the evidence-based comparison between transcarotid artery revascularization and transfemoral carotid stenting;the renewed pathophysiological understanding of subclavian steal syndrome and vertebral artery diseases;and the construction of individualized treatment decision-making frameworks. Nevertheless,current clinical practice still faces challenges such as controversies over optimal surgical approaches,insufficient prevention and management of complications,and a lack of robust long-term outcome data. From the perspective of vascular surgery,this article systematically reviews recent advances in endovascular devices,surgical techniques,and treatment concepts,aiming to provide front-line clinicians with up-to-date,practical,and actionable insights into the management of supra-aortic arch artery diseases.

title: [A brief discussion on the progress and development directions of clinical research in vascular surgery].
abstract: Vascular surgery has experienced rapid development over the past three decades. With the application of minimally invasive and interventional techniques in the diagnosis and treatment of vascular diseases, clinical research and technological innovation in vascular surgery have expanded significantly. As populations aging accelerates globally-including in China-and the number of patients with cardiovascular and cerebrovascular disease within the existing healthcare system becomes increasingly evident. The future of vascular surgery will center on three core principles: minimization, precision, and intelligence. By integrating breakthroughs in basic science, engineering, and artificial intelligence, clinical translation will be accelerated. The discipline will shift from "disease treatment" to "health management", and from a "surgery-centered" single model to a "patient-centered" integrated approach model. Future developments will further incorporate artificial intelligence, big data models, precision medicine, more advanced and comprehensive minimally invasive technologies, enhancing multidisciplinary collaboration and preventive care. These advancements are expected to significantly improve diagnostic accuracy, treatment outcomes, and quality of life for patients with vascular diseases.

title: Learning Manipulation Features for Quantitative Assessment and Skill-Level Classification in Robot-Assisted Intervention: In Vivo Rabbit Studies.
abstract: Robot-assisted vascular interventions demand precise manipulation within tortuous millimeter-scale vessels, where surgical outcomes remain critically dependent on surgeon skill. Conventional metrics such as completion time or navigation success are too coarse to capture the subtle, yet decisive control differences between experts and novices, while sensor-heavy external approaches obscure the surgeon's intrinsic dynamics. This article introduces a task-aware spectral modeling (TASM) framework that directly extracts skill signatures from joystick control signals, revealing how surgical expertise manifests in the time-frequency domain. In vivo rabbit experiments demonstrate that expert manipulation emerges as smooth, deliberate low-frequency rhythmic control, whereas novice performance degenerates into fragmented, high-frequency corrections. Spectral analysis indicates that approximately 96% of control energy lies below 5 Hz, suggesting that low-frequency components may serve as an indicative spectral characteristic associated with expert-novice differentiation under similar experimental and task conditions. By deriving interpretable spectral descriptors, the framework achieves an average ROC-AUC of 0.992 across nine classifiers. Clinically, the proposed framework may support quantitative assessment of surgical skill and control stability in robot-assisted endovascular procedures, with potential value for identifying inconsistent control behaviors and informing future training and evaluation pipelines.

title: Quantification of the flexural rigidity of endovascular surgical devices using three-point bending tests.
abstract: Endovascular surgical procedures require the navigation of catheters and wires through the vasculature to reach distal target sites. Quantitative frameworks for device selection have the potential to improve navigation success by optimizing device flexural rigidity for a given patient-specific anatomy. However, data are lacking to facilitate this technology, in part because typical endovascular devices have intricate spatial variations in mechanical properties that are challenging and tedious to quantify repeatably. We therefore developed a three-point bend test methodology using a custom rig and applied it to measure lengthwise flexural rigidity profiles of devices commonly used in neuroendovascular procedures. The methodology demonstrated high repeatability and was able to characterize transition zones in detail. We applied the methodology to generate the first comprehensive, quantitative library of device flexural rigidities, spanning guidewires, intermediate guides, and long sheaths. We observed that these three classes of device have properties that fall into distinct ranges. Additional plots examining relationships between flexural rigidity, device diameter, and length revealed application-specific trends in flexural properties. This methodology and resulting data allow for standardized characterization and comparisons to aid device selection, and have the potential to both enhance surgical planning and inform future endovascular innovation.

title: The trajectories of comprehensive capacity of bedridden older people based on latent growth mixture models: a longitudinal study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Bedridden older people generally have poor comprehensive capacity and are prone to multi-system complications including pressure injuries and lower limb venous thrombosis, imposing heavy caregiving and financial burdens and severely affecting their health. OBJECTIVE: To identify distinct trajectories of ability in bedridden older people and characteristics distinguishing the trajectories, while assessing the prognostic value of these trajectories for early risk identification of pressure injury and deep-vein thrombosis (DVT). PARTICIPANTS: Two hundred twenty six bedridden older people aged 65 years and above from two nursing homes in China. METHODS: Patients were required 5 assessments during 1-year follow-up period. Latent Growth Mixture Modelling identified distinct trajectories, multinomial logistic regression identified characteristics distinguishing the trajectories and generalised estimating equations evaluated associations between trajectories and pressure injury and DVT. RESULTS: There are three distinct trajectories of comprehensive capacity among bedridden older people, including severe impairment with stable type (63.5%); moderate impairment with slowly deteriorating type (16.3%); moderate-to-severe impairment with fluctuating type (20.2%). Characteristics distinguishing the trajectories were tooth loss, hypertension, indwelling gastric tube and dysphagia. Compared with the severe impairment stable type, the other two groups had higher pressure injury risk; the moderate impairment with slowly deteriorating type also had higher DVT risk. CONCLUSIONS: Capacity trajectories of bedridden older people are heterogeneous. Nurses may want to focus on those with tooth loss, hypertension, indwelling gastric tube and dysphagia to deliver targeted care. These trajectories are significantly associated with pressure injury and deep vein thrombosis risks. Their identification enables earlier risk stratification and more targeted prevention.

title: Bilateral Lateral Tarsal Artery Bypass and Free Flap Reconstruction of an Infected Gangrenous Heel in Chronic Limb-Threatening Ischemia: A Case Report of Three-Year Functional Limb Salvage.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Distal bypass for chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) is technically demanding when the conventional pedal arteries are unavailable, and revascularization alone seldom heals an extensive heel defect. CASE PRESENTATION: A man in his 60s receiving maintenance hemodialysis presented with bilateral CLTI and gangrene of the left heel after failed endovascular therapy, and bilateral major amputations had been considered before referral. Both limbs were classified as Wound, Ischemia, and foot Infection clinical stage 4. Diffuse calcification of the infrapopliteal and pedal arteries left the lateral tarsal artery (LTA) as the only suitable distal target, and bilateral superficial femoral artery-to-LTA bypasses were performed with in situ great saphenous vein grafts under nerve block anesthesia. Because repeated debridement left the calcaneus exposed, a free latissimus dorsi musculocutaneous flap anastomosed to the left bypass graft was transferred and covered with a split-thickness skin graft. The wounds healed after minor amputations, and the patient regained independent ambulation. An ulcer subsequently developed on the weight-bearing surface of the transferred flap and never healed despite pressure-relieving insoles and additional inflow angioplasty; nevertheless, the flap remained viable, both grafts remained patent, and ambulatory function was preserved until the patient died of an unrelated cause 3 years after revascularization. CONCLUSIONS: The LTA can serve as a distal bypass target when the conventional pedal arteries are unavailable, and, when combined with free flap reconstruction, it may achieve long-term functional limb salvage despite extensive heel gangrene. The reconstructed weight-bearing heel nevertheless remains prone to ulceration that may not heal, so preventive off-loading and long-term surveillance are essential.

title: Mechanical Thrombectomy of a Combined Persistent Primitive Trigeminal Artery and Basilar Artery Occlusion: A Case Report and Literature Review.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Persistent primitive trigeminal artery (PPTA) is a rare anastomosis between the internal carotid artery and the posterior circulation, most commonly with the basilar artery (BA). It has been associated with neurovascular diseases such as cerebral hemorrhage and ischemic stroke. Its occlusion in the case of ischemic stroke presents multiple challenges, both diagnostic and therapeutic, as the modified vascular anatomy may complicate the initial imaging diagnosis and endovascular treatment with mechanical thrombectomy (MT). CASE PRESENTATION: We report here the case of a 64-year-old woman presenting with an altered conscious status and bilateral mydriasis due to an occlusion of a PPTA and the distal part of the BA, which was treated with MT. Complete recanalization was obtained using combined contact aspiration and stent retriever thrombectomy through the PPTA. CONCLUSION: PPTA is a rare vascular anatomical variant whose knowledge is important in the setting of stroke. In this setting, MT appears to be a feasible, safe, and effective technique compared to other proximal sites of occlusion.

title: Catheter-related deep vein thrombosis complicated by iatrogenic pulmonary embolism after thrombectomy leading to hemodialysis failure and successful rescue by automated peritoneal dialysis: A case report.
abstract: RATIONALE: Catheter-related deep vein thrombosis (DVT) is a serious complication in hemodialysis (HD) patients and may lead to pulmonary embolism (PE). Interventional treatment of catheter-related DVT may be complicated by acute PE and other life-threatening events. When recurrent vascular access failure and cardiovascular intolerance make HD unsustainable, automated peritoneal dialysis (APD) may provide an alternative renal replacement strategy. We report a case of successful rescue with APD after severe complications following interventional treatment of catheter-related DVT. PATIENT CONCERNS: An 82-year-old woman with end-stage renal disease developed right femoral vein thrombosis shortly after initiating urgent-start HD via a femoral catheter. Following percutaneous mechanical thrombectomy and catheter-directed thrombolysis, she developed acute hypoxemia, pulmonary embolism, severe thrombocytopenia, heart failure, and gastrointestinal bleeding. Recurrent central venous catheter dysfunction and repeated hypotension and oxygen desaturation during HD made continued conventional HD increasingly difficult. DIAGNOSES: The patient was diagnosed with catheter-related DVT complicated by acute PE following interventional thrombectomy. INTERVENTIONS: The patient received intensive supportive care, including anticoagulation when clinically feasible, continuous renal replacement therapy, blood transfusions, and management of gastrointestinal bleeding and heart failure. Because of recurrent central venous catheter dysfunction and intolerance to conventional HD, a multidisciplinary team recommended peritoneal dialysis (PD). After clinical stabilization and PD catheter placement, she was transitioned to APD. OUTCOMES: After APD initiation, the patient's uremic symptoms and lower-extremity edema resolved, and her functional capacity improved from bedridden to independent walking. Hemoglobin increased from 65.7 to 118.2 g/L, cardiac function improved, and adequate dialysis was achieved with a total dialysis adequacy index of 2.58. During approximately 10 months of follow-up, she remained free from peritonitis and PD catheter dysfunction. LESSONS: This case highlights the risk of serious thromboembolic complications following interventional treatment of catheter-related DVT in HD patients. When recurrent vascular access failure and cardiovascular intolerance render conventional HD unsustainable, timely reassessment of dialysis modality is crucial; APD may offer an effective rescue strategy for selected elderly patients.
englishSummary: RATIONALE: Catheter-related deep vein thrombosis (DVT) is a serious complication in hemodialysis (HD) patients and may lead to pulmonary embolism (PE). Interventional treatment of catheter-related DVT may be complicated by acute PE and other life-threatening events. When recurrent vascular access failure and cardiovascular intolerance make HD unsustainable, automated peritoneal dialysis (APD) may provide an alternative renal replacement strategy.

title: Risk factors for perioperative venous thromboembolism in patients undergoing colorectal cancer surgery: A single-center retrospective study.
abstract: Venous thromboembolism (VTE), including deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism, is a serious perioperative complication after colorectal cancer surgery. Although guidelines recommend prophylaxis, bleeding risks complicate decision-making, and evidence regarding Japanese patients remains limited. Therefore, this study aimed to identify perioperative risk factors associated with VTE in colorectal cancer surgery to inform effective risk stratification and targeted prevention strategies. A retrospective analysis of 397 patients who underwent elective colorectal cancer resection at a single institution between June 2014 and May 2024 was conducted. Preoperative and postoperative D-dimer levels were measured, and lower extremity venous ultrasonography was performed when indicated. When deep vein thrombosis was detected by venous ultrasonography, contrast-enhanced computed tomography was subsequently performed to evaluate the presence of pulmonary embolism. Univariate analyses were used to determine factors significantly associated with VTE, and a P-value < .05 was considered statistically significant. Preoperative VTE was observed in nine of 397 patients (2.3%), and postoperative VTE was observed in nine of 388 patients (2.3%). The univariate analysis suggested that age ≥75 years, female gender, albumin levels < 3.5 g/dL, and hemoglobin levels < 10 g/dL were significantly associated with preoperative VTE, while operative time ≥ 240 minutes and intraoperative blood loss ≥ 50 mL were significantly associated with postoperative VTE. Advanced age, female gender, hypoalbuminemia, anemia, prolonged operative time, and increased intraoperative blood loss were significantly associated with perioperative VTE in univariate analysis. Effective perioperative risk stratification and targeted surveillance may contribute to the early detection and prevention of VTE in Japanese patients undergoing colorectal cancer surgery.

title: Major re-amputation after initial diabetic foot amputation: A retrospective cohort study.
abstract: Reamputation after initial diabetic foot amputation remains a major clinical challenge associated with substantial morbidity. Identifying factors related to major reamputation may improve patient management and limb preservation. This study evaluated the impact of clinical, metabolic, nutritional, and vascular parameters on the risk of major reamputation. This retrospective cohort study included 141 patients who underwent lower-extremity amputation for diabetic foot disease between 2020 and 2025. Demographic variables, body mass index (BMI), smoking status, peripheral arterial disease (PAD), infection history, glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) levels, and Prognostic Nutritional Index (PNI) were analyzed. Major reamputation was defined as a subsequent ipsilateral amputation progressing to a below-knee or above-knee level; contralateral amputations and more proximal minor amputations confined to the foot were not considered outcome events. The median follow-up was 3.0 years (range, 1-5). Continuous variables were compared using the Mann-Whitney U test and categorical variables using the Pearson chi-square test. Kaplan-Meier analysis was used to estimate major reamputation-free survival, and Cox proportional hazards regression was performed to evaluate factors associated with time to major reamputation. A Fine-Gray competing-risk analysis was additionally performed considering death before major reamputation as a competing event. Major reamputation occurred in 31 patients (22.0%). Patients with reamputation had significantly lower BMI and PNI values and higher HbA1c levels (all P < .001). Smoking and PAD were significantly more frequent in the reamputation group (both P < .001), whereas no significant between-group differences were observed for age, sex, serum albumin, or infection history. In multivariable Cox regression analysis, PAD (adjusted hazard ratio [HR] 6.25, 95% confidence interval [CI] 2.13-18.32, P < .001) and higher HbA1c (adjusted HR 1.40, 95% CI 1.19-1.65, P < .001) were independently associated with an increased hazard of major reamputation, whereas higher PNI was associated with a reduced hazard (adjusted HR 0.95, 95% CI 0.91-0.99, P = .009). Lower BMI, higher HbA1c, reduced PNI, smoking, and PAD were associated with major reamputation. In multivariable time-to-event analysis, PAD, HbA1c, and PNI remained independently associated with the outcome. These findings demonstrate associations between routinely available clinical parameters and major reamputation and warrant further evaluation in prospective studies.
englishSummary: Reamputation after initial diabetic foot amputation remains a major clinical challenge associated with substantial morbidity. Identifying factors related to major reamputation may improve patient management and limb preservation. This study evaluated the impact of clinical, metabolic, nutritional, and vascular parameters on the risk of major reamputation.

title: Beyond Anatomy in Uncomplicated Type B Aortic Dissection: Hypoxia, Physiological Reserve, and the Next Generation of Intelligent Endovascular Devices.
abstract: Type B aortic dissection (TBAD) represents a heterogeneous disease process that cannot be fully understood through anatomy alone. Although the majority of patients initially meet current criteria for uncomplicated TBAD (uTBAD), a substantial proportion later progresses despite appearing stable during early assessment and surveillance. The mechanisms underlying this deterioration remain incompletely understood and extends beyond our current understanding of traditional anatomic high-risk criteria. This article examines impaired oxygenation and physiological reserve as potential dimensions of clinical vulnerability in uTBAD, while distinguishing their possible relevance to acute deterioration from their unproven value in predicting aortic progression or selecting patients for intervention. As such, TBAD is not simply a focal vascular event, but a disease with broader systemic and physiological implications. It also discusses how future intelligent endovascular technologies could support a more personalised approach to management by integrating embedded sensors, wireless physiological monitoring, and artificial intelligence-assisted haemodynamic analysis. Moreover, a conceptual framework is discussed in which the stent graft evolves from a purely mechanical device into an active therapeutic platform capable of physiological sensing and real-time feedback.

title: The chloroplast CLPD chaperone: consequences of under- and overexpression, interaction with the CLP protease core, and candidate substrates.
abstract: Expression of the chloroplast AAA + chaperone CLPD gene increases during senescence and drought, but its function in chloroplast proteostasis is poorly understood. This study provides a comprehensive analysis of Arabidopsis CLPD protein accumulation across development from early seedlings to senescence and compares results to its homologs CLPC1,2, as well as CLPB3 and cpHSP90. The developmental consequences of complete loss of CLPD expression (clpd-1), as well as overexpression of functional CLPD or CLPD impaired in ATP hydrolysis (CLPD-TRAP), were determined in Arabidopsis. clpd-1 has accelerated seedling development while functional CLPD overexpression lines, but not CLPD-TRAP, have delayed development. To determine whether CLPD is a bona fide CLP chaperone associating with the CLPPRT protease and to identify in vivo candidate substrates, we employed the CLPD-TRAP line during vegetative and flowering (senescent) growth stages. Affinity purification of CLPD-TRAP followed by mass spectrometry showed high enrichment of all 9 subunits of the CLP protease, suggesting that CLPD plays a role in substrate delivery to the CLP protease. CLPC1 and CLPC2 were also highly enriched in the CLPD-TRAP interactome, suggesting, together with prior information, heterooligomerization of the 3 chaperones. Nine chloroplast candidate substrates were identified in the CLPD-interactomes, including FHY2 involved in riboflavin synthesis, THI1 and THIC involved in thiamin metabolism, and 4 proteins of unknown function. Several of these were previously identified as potential CLP substrates based on CLPC1 trapping and comparative proteomics of clp mutants. Together, this suggests that CLPD acts in substrate selection within a heteromeric CLPC-CLPD hexamer, likely with unique contributions.

title: Sex-based differences in fibrosis markers in human abdominal aortic aneurysms.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Abdominal aortic aneurysms (AAA) are a complex degenerative vascular disease. The role of fibrosis in AAA progression is unclear. Our study evaluated the impact of fibroblast activation protein (FAP), collagen, and vimentin on AAA fibrosis and progression. We hypothesized that FAP may influence fibrosis and disease severity in AAA, with potential sex-specific differences. STUDY DESIGN: Multi-centered transcriptomic analysis of aortic samples from 15 human AAA and 5 non-AAA was performed to evaluate cell-specific fibrosis gene expression profiles. Histopathological and molecular analysis of 26 male and female AAA samples (mAAA and fAAA) and 29 male and female normal abdominal aortas (mNAA and fNAA) was performed to assess whole-tissue fibrosis markers and signaling. RESULTS: FAP COL1A1 Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) analysis identified eight major cell clusters with distinct sex-based distributions. Although vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs) and fibroblast clusters had reduced counts in both male and female AAAs, they more highly expressedandgenes, particularly in females. Whole-tissue analysis demonstrated elevated extracellular matrix deposits with markedly increased collagen type 1 in both mAAA and fAAA. Alpha-smooth muscle actin (α-SMA)-positive VSMCs were also reduced in mAAA and fAAA, but FAP was notably elevated, and robustly in fAAA. FAP-positive fibroblasts in fAAA exhibited increased expression of fibrosis markers, suggesting a unique pro-fibrotic phenotype. CONCLUSION: Our study reveals a sex-based difference in AAA tissue, with elevated fibrosis markers and increased FAP levels in females, suggesting its significant role in disease progression. These findings underscore the potential of FAP as a unique tissue biomarker for AAAs and warrants further investigation into novel targeted therapies that aim to stabilize AAAs, particularly in female patients.

title: Prognostic Value of the Frailty Index in Patients with Severe Aortic Regurgitation Undergoing Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Frailty represents a multidimensional vulnerability that predicts poor outcomes in cardiovascular disease. Its prognostic value in patients with severe native aortic regurgitation (AR) undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) is not well defined. OBJECTIVE: To determine whether an abbreviated cumulative deficit frailty index predicts one-year all-cause mortality and to explore its interaction with N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide in this population. METHODS: In this post hoc analysis of the prospective China DVD2 multicenter cohort, 298 patients with isolated severe AR who underwent TAVR were included. Frailty was assessed preprocedurally using an abbreviated 8-9-item cumulative deficit frailty index (FI) encompassing functional, cognitive, nutritional, and clinical domains. The primary endpoint was one-year all-cause mortality. The cohort-derived FI threshold for mortality was derived using time-dependent receiver operating characteristic analysis. Cox proportional hazards models adjusted for age, sex, body mass index, atrial fibrillation, and NT-proBNP were applied. Subgroup and interaction analyses were performed. RESULTS: The cohort-derived FI threshold was 0.407, classifying 32 patients as high frailty. High-FI patients exhibited greater symptom burden, higher prevalence of atrial fibrillation, larger left atrial diameter, and elevated NT-proBNP. One-year mortality was significantly higher in the high-FI group compared with low-FI patients (15.6% vs 3.4%, P = 0.010). High FI was associated with higher one-year mortality in Model 3 (HR 4.00, 95% CI 1.18-13.50; P = 0.026). No significant multiplicative or additive interaction with NT-proBNP was observed. CONCLUSIONS: Among patients undergoing TAVR for severe native aortic regurgitation, a high FI was associated with higher one-year mortality. These findings extend prior evidence on the prognostic implications of frailty to this understudied population.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Frailty represents a multidimensional vulnerability that predicts poor outcomes in cardiovascular disease. Its prognostic value in patients with severe native aortic regurgitation (AR) undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) is not well defined. OBJECTIVE: To determine whether an abbreviated cumulative deficit frailty index predicts one-year all-cause mortality and to explore its interaction with N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide in this population.

title: Imaging in tarsal tunnel syndrome: A case series.
abstract: Tarsal tunnel syndrome is an under-recognized yet potentially debilitating entrapment neuropathy that is often misdiagnosed due to its non-specific clinical presentation. This case series presents four representative cases of space-occupying lesions within the tarsal tunnel - ganglion cysts, varicose veins, lipomas, and peripheral nerve sheath tumors - with emphasis on high-resolution magnetic resonance imaging and complementary radiographic and ultrasound findings. We demonstrate the characteristic imaging hallmarks of these lesions, including their mass effect on the tibial neurovascular bundle, signal intensities, and enhancement patterns, to aid clinicians and radiologists in timely recognition of this condition.

title: Dissecting cell-type-specific genetic associations between colorectal cancer liability and thrombotic risk in peripheral blood immune cells.
abstract: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is a major complication of colorectal cancer (CRC), but whether CRC-associated thrombotic susceptibility includes cell-specific inherited regulatory components in peripheral blood remains unclear. To investigate associations between CRC genetic liability and VTE-related outcomes within peripheral blood mononuclear cell (PBMC) regulatory contexts. We integrated CRC GWAS, FinnGen VTE-related outcomes, and TenK10K PBMC single-cell eQTL data across 28 immune cell types using cell-stratified Mendelian randomization (csMR). Prioritized signals were further examined in single-cell RNA-seq datasets and bulk transcriptomes. Conventional MR showed no clear evidence that CRC liability increased VTE, DVT, or PE risk, and LD Score regression detected no significant genome-wide genetic correlation. In contrast, csMR identified nominal, cell-context-dependent associations. B intermediate cells were prioritized across VTE (OR, 1.16; 95% CI, 1.03-1.32), DVT (OR, 1.30; 95% CI, 1.08-1.57), and PE (OR, 1.26; 95% CI, 1.07-1.49), while CD14 + monocytes and CD4 + central memory T cells received additional support from downstream single-cell analyses. Gene-level analyses prioritized LAMA5, LIMA1, and TRIM28 in these respective cell contexts. In bulk blood, RPS21 showed consistent disease-associated expression patterns and discriminated VTE patients from healthy controls in an external dataset (AUC, 0.865; 95% CI, 0.800-0.923). These findings suggest that genetic overlap between CRC liability and thrombotic phenotypes may be localized to selected PBMC regulatory contexts rather than broadly detectable genome-wide. Among the prioritized signals, B intermediate cells showed the most consistent csMR associations across VTE, DVT, and PE. The cell-gene pairs, together with RPS21, warrant independent genetic, functional, and prospective validation as candidates for studying peripheral immune regulation and blood-based markers of CRC-associated thrombosis.

title: L5 Corpectomy in a 12-Year-Old Owing to Rosai-Dorfman Disease: A Case Report.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Rosai-Dorfman disease (RDD) is a rare non-Langerhans cell histiocytosis typically presenting with massive, painless lymphadenopathy or subcutaneous masses. Extranodal involvement, particularly in the spine, is exceedingly rare and poses significant diagnostic and management challenges. Lumbar spinal RDD with vertebral collapse and neurological compromise is almost unheard of in the pediatric population, with no prior reports of surgical intervention requiring L5 corpectomy and circumferential fusion in an adolescent. CASE DESCRIPTION: We present a case of a 12-year-old girl with a 6-month history of worsening lower back pain unresponsive to conservative treatment. Imaging revealed collapse of the L5 vertebral body and a destructive, enhancing lesion encasing the neural elements, leading to severe canal and foraminal stenosis. Computed tomography-guided biopsy confirmed the diagnosis of RDD. A multidisciplinary surgical team implemented a 2-stage circumferential surgical plan. Stage 1 involved posterior decompression and posterior instrumentation from L3 to the pelvis using S2AI screws. A silastic barrier was placed to protect neural elements. Stage 2, performed via an anterior approach with vascular surgery assistance, involved complete corpectomy of L5 and reconstruction with an expandable cage spanning L4 to S1. Postoperative recovery was uneventful, and the patient remained neurologically intact. At 1-year follow-up, the patient demonstrated solid anterior and posterior fusion, maintained spinal alignment, and had returned to full activity. CONCLUSION: This is the first reported case of pediatric RDD requiring an L5 corpectomy with circumferential spinal fusion. The case underscores the importance of early tissue diagnosis, individualized surgical planning, and interdisciplinary collaboration. Recognition of RDD as a potential etiology for pediatric spinal lesions is critical, particularly when imaging mimics malignancy. Our successful outcome supports the use of staged, tailored surgical approaches in managing rare spinal pathologies in children.

title: Routine Chest CTA Reliably Quantifies Left Ventricular Myocardial Mass.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Routine chest computed tomography angiography (CTA) is the primary imaging modality for thoracic aortic disease, yet cardiac information within these examinations remains underutilized. We evaluated whether left ventricular myocardial mass (LVMM) can be reliably quantified from routine non-electrocardiographically (ECG)-gated chest CTA and its application in thoracic aortic pathology. METHODS: CTA scans were obtained from 257 patients without aortic disease and 181 patients with thoracic aortic aneurysm or dissection. LVMM was quantified using automated three-dimensional segmentation. In a separate 10-patient validation cohort, LVMM was compared across end-systolic, end-diastolic, and non-ECG-gated source reconstructions. CTA-derived LVMM was compared with published echocardiographic and cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) reference values using Cohen's d. RESULTS: d d d d p p LVMM remained stable across cardiac phases and non-ECG-gated images (mean coefficient of variation, 2.4%), whereas left ventricular volume varied substantially (36.9%). CTA-derived LVMM demonstrated small effect sizes with the Penn method (= 0.22) and moderate effect sizes with ASE linear (= 0.67), area-length (= 0.68), and CMR (= 0.63). LVMM increased through young adulthood, with minimal association with age beyond 30 years. LVMM was comparable between patients with thoracic aneurysms and normal adults (140 ± 43 g vs. 141 ± 40 g; adjusted= 1.0) but significantly greater in acute (199 ± 61 g) and chronic (191 ± 57 g) aortic dissection (both adjusted< 0.001). CONCLUSIONS: Routine non-ECG-gated chest CTA enables reliable automated LVMM quantification without additional imaging or radiation and may facilitate large-scale investigations of ventricular remodeling in thoracic aortic disease.
