METHODS: CTA scans were obtained from 257 patients without aortic disease and 181 patients with thoracic aortic aneurysm or dissection.

title: Association of circumferential dissection on computed tomography angiography with preoperative rupture in type A aortic dissection.
abstract: BACKGROUND: To investigate the association between circumferential dissection on computed tomography angiography (CTA) and preoperative rupture in patients with type A aortic dissection (TAAD). METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 597 consecutive patients diagnosed with TAAD at Beijing Anzhen Hospital between January 2021 and December 2024. Patients were classified into circumferential dissection (n = 130) and non-circumferential dissection (n = 467) groups based on preoperative CTA. Clinical, laboratory, and imaging characteristics were compared between groups. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed to examine factors independently associated with preoperative rupture, and between-group differences in preoperative rupture were compared. RESULTS: Circumferential dissection was strongly associated with DeBakey type I dissection, supra-aortic branch involvement, and greater false-lumen expansion with true-lumen compression. Preoperative rupture occurred more frequently in patients with circumferential dissection than in those without (33.8% vs 7.1%, P < 0.001). Multivariable logistic regression demonstrated that circumferential dissection was independently associated with preoperative rupture ascertained by bedside echocardiography following the admission CTA after adjustment for demographic, laboratory, and imaging factors (OR = 5.24, 95% CI: 1.86-14.76, P = 0.002). CONCLUSION: Circumferential dissection on CTA is independently associated with preoperative rupture and may support timely surgical decision-making in TAAD.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 597 consecutive patients diagnosed with TAAD at Beijing Anzhen Hospital between January 2021 and December 2024. title: Machine learning models for predicting futile recanalisation after endovascular treatment in patients with large core infarction.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Predicting futile recanalisation following endovascular treatment (EVT) in patients with large core infarctions is crucial for guiding clinical decisions, optimising perioperative management and improving healthcare resource allocation. This study aimed to compare four machine learning (ML) algorithms and identify the most effective model for preinterventional prediction of futile recanalisation. METHODS: Patients achieving successful reperfusion (expanded Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction Score≥2b) from the EVT in Acute Anterior Circulation Large Vessel Occlusive Patients With a Large Infarct Core trial were stratified into two groups: no-futile recanalisation (90-day modified Rankin Scale (mRS) 0–3) and futile recanalisation (mRS 4–6). The least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression method was used for feature selection, and four ML algorithms, including logistic regression, support vector machine (SVM), decision tree and random forest, were applied. Model performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic curves, calibration plots and decision curve analysis. Feature importance was ranked using SHapley Additive exPlanation (SHAP) values. RESULTS: Among 146 patients, 74 experienced futile recanalisation. Eight predictors were identified and ranked by SHAP analysis from highest to lowest importance: sex, age, National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale, glucose, systolic blood pressure, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, fibrinogen and occlusion site. Among the four models, the SVM model achieved the highest area under the curve of 0.891 (95% CI 0.837 to 0.945), along with good calibration (Hosmer-Lemeshow test, p=0.103) and clinical utility. CONCLUSION: The SVM model emerges as the optimal predictive tool for futile recanalisation following EVT in patients with large core infarction. Nevertheless, external validation is required to confirm its performance before clinical application. TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: NCT04551664.

title: Factors associated with infarct volume growth after mechanical thrombectomy in large core infarction: ANGEL-ASPECT insights.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Infarct volume growth (IVG) correlates with outcomes and may represent a prognostic imaging biomarker in acute ischaemic stroke due to anterior circulation large vessel occlusion (LVO). This study aims to identify factors associated with IVG after mechanical thrombectomy (MT) in patients with large core infarction. METHODS: This is a post hoc analysis of the Endovascular Therapy in Anterior Circulation Large Vessel Occlusion with a Large Infarct randomised trial. IVG was calculated as final infarct volume minus baseline infarct volume (BIV). The optimal IVG threshold for predicting 90-day favourable outcomes (modified Rankin Scale score 0–3) was determined using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis, maximising both sensitivity and specificity. Factors associated with IVG were identified using multivariate logistic regression analyses. RESULTS: Among 228 included patients, ROC analysis identified an optimal IVG threshold of 105 mL for predicting favourable 90-day outcomes (area under the curve=0.71; specificity=0.85, sensitivity=0.53). Patients were stratified into mild (IVG <105 mL, n=150) and severe (IVG ≥105 mL, n=78) groups. Multivariate logistic regression identified BIV (OR 1.02, 95% CI 1.00 to 1.03; p<0.01), admission blood glucose (OR 1.20, 95% CI 1.04 to 1.37; p=0.01), time from puncture to recanalisation (OR 1.01, 95% CI 1.00 to 1.02; p=0.049) and recanalisation at 36 hours (±12 hours) (OR 0.19, 95% CI 0.05 to 0.72; p=0.01) as independent factors associated with IVG. CONCLUSION: IVG after MT significantly correlates with clinical outcomes. Identification of modifiable IVG determinants after MT may inform periprocedural management strategies in patients with large infarct due to LVO. TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: NCT04551664.

METHODS: This is a post hoc analysis of the Endovascular Therapy in Anterior Circulation Large Vessel Occlusion with a Large Infarct randomised trial.

title: Early Staged STABILISE Technique Achieves Favorable Aortic Remodeling after Central Repair for Acute Type A Aortic Dissection.
abstract: Residual distal aortic dissection often persists after repair of acute type A aortic dissection, and may cause progressive aortic enlargement requiring secondary intervention. We describe a 43-year-old male who underwent an early staged stent-assisted balloon-induced intimal disruption and relamination in aortic dissection repair (STABILISE)-thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR) procedure after central repair for an acute type A aortic dissection. Early postoperative computed tomography angiography demonstrated persistent false lumen perfusion, progressive false lumen enlargement, and marked true lumen compression. Thirty-eight days postoperatively, staged STABILISE-TEVAR was performed. Early staged STABILISE-TEVAR was technically feasible and achieved favorable aortic remodeling at 12 months in this patient.

title: Personalised approach to venous thromboembolism prophylaxis in heavier critically ill patients (PROSPER): A randomised, parallel-group, electronic medical record (EMR)-embedded feasibility trial.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Data are limited regarding optimal low molecular weight heparin dosing for venous thromboembolism prophylaxis in heavier critically ill patients. This trial evaluated the feasibility of a weight-based dynamic dosing algorithm. DESIGN SETTING PARTICIPANTS: Open-label, electronic medical record-embedded randomised feasibility trial. Patients, weighing ≥100 kg who required thromboprophylaxis were eligible. Enoxaparin was commenced with weight-based dosing and anti-Xa level-guided adjustment (target peak anti-Xa level 0.2-0.4 IU/mL) or usual care (40 mg twice daily). MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES: The primary outcome was peak anti-Xa level at 'steady state' (after ≥3 enoxaparin doses). The feasibility threshold was set at 95% of steady state anti-Xa levels in the intervention group being less than the threshold for therapeutic anticoagulant effect (≤0.6 IU/mL). RESULTS: Fifty participants (intervention n = 17, control n = 33) received 331 doses of enoxaparin (median of 4 [interquartile range {IQR}: 3-7] doses per participant, and a dose of 50 [IQR: 50-60] mg (intervention) and 40 [IQR: 40-40] mg (control)). Thirty-two 'steady state' peak anti-Xa measurements were recorded from 24 patients (12 intervention and 12 control). The proportion of peak anti-Xa levels that were ≤0.6 IU/mL was: 15 of 17 (88%) vs. 15 of 15 (100%). There were fewer peak anti-Xa measurements below the prophylactic range (<0.2 IU/mL) in the intervention group compared with the control group (2 of 17 [12%] vs. 5 of 15 [33%]). Six patients developed venous thrombosis or pulmonary embolism (2 of 17 [12%] vs. 4 of 33 [12%]). Major bleeding occurred in one patient in the intervention group. CONCLUSIONS: A weight-based dynamic thromboprophylaxis algorithm was implemented via the electronic medical record but did not meet the predefined feasibility threshold.

This trial evaluated the feasibility of a weight-based dynamic dosing algorithm. DESIGN SETTING PARTICIPANTS: Open-label, electronic medical record-embedded randomised feasibility trial.

title: Multimodal integration of carotid plaque ultrasound radiomics and dynamic systemic immune-inflammation trajectories for subacute risk stratification after stroke thrombectomy: development and internal validation of an exploratory prognostic model.
abstract: BACKGROUND: We hypothesized that integrating macroscopic carotid plaque architecture, quantified via ultrasound radiomics, with downstream micro-cellular temporal dynamics, defined by longitudinal immune trajectories, would yield a highly accurate prognostic framework for 90-day functional outcomes in patients undergoing endovascular thrombectomy (EVT). METHODS: N N This single-center, retrospective cohort study consecutively included 316 AIS-LVO patients who underwent successful EVT (modified Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction score ≥2b) within 24 h of symptom onset. Patients were partitioned into a discovery ( = 221) and an internal validation cohort ( = 95) using stratified random sampling. To capture temporal inflammatory heterogeneity, the Systemic Immune-Inflammation Index (SII) was measured at days 0, 1, 3, and 7, and clustered using Latent Class Mixed Models (LCMM). Concurrently, high-dimensional radiomic features strictly adhering to the Image Biomarker Standardisation Initiative (IBSI) guidelines were extracted from baseline two-dimensional carotid ultrasound images. A radiomics score (Rad-score) was constructed utilizing Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO) regression. Four progressive predictive models were developed, culminating in an Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) multimodal architecture. The primary endpoint was an unfavorable 90-day functional outcome (modified Rankin Scale score 3 to 6). RESULTS: p p p An unfavorable outcome occurred in 166 of 316 patients (52.5%). The LCMM objectively identified three longitudinal SII phenotypes. The "persistent high-inflammation" trajectory (Class 3, 17.0% of patients) was independently associated with an increased risk of an unfavorable outcome compared to the "rapid resolution" trajectory (Class 1) [adjusted odds ratio (aOR), 4.85; 95% confidence interval [CI], 2.20 to 10.85; < 0.001]. The ultrasound Rad-score, comprising 9 core textural features, also demonstrated robust independent predictive value (aOR, 1.52; 95% CI, 1.21 to 1.92 per 0.1-point increase; < 0.001). In the strictly isolated internal validation cohort, the full multimodal XGBoost model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.92 (95% CI, 0.86 to 0.97), with an accuracy of 86.3%, sensitivity of 88.0%, and specificity of 84.4%. This performance was statistically superior to the standard clinical baseline model (AUC, 0.74; 95% CI, 0.63 to 0.84; < 0.001 via DeLong test). Furthermore, the multimodal paradigm demonstrated clinical reclassification utility, yielding a continuous net reclassification improvement of 0.985 (95% CI, 0.684 to 1.286) and an integrated discrimination improvement of 0.194 (95% CI, 0.128 to 0.260). CONCLUSION: An exploratory model integrating baseline carotid plaque ultrasound radiomics with Day-0-to-Day-7 systemic immune-inflammation trajectories was associated with 90-day functional outcome after EVT and, on internal validation, discriminated outcomes more strongly than a conventional clinical model. Because the immune-trajectory component is only complete at Day 7, the model is intended for subacute post-EVT risk stratification rather than acute treatment selection, and requires external, prospective validation before any clinical application.

METHODS: N N This single-center, retrospective cohort study consecutively included 316 AIS-LVO patients who underwent successful EVT (modified Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction score ≥2b) within 24 h of symptom onset. Patients were partitioned into a discovery ( = 221) and an internal validation cohort ( = 95) using stratified random sampling.

title: Distinct patterns of vascular failure in COL1A1-associated osteogenesis imperfecta and FBN1-associated Marfan syndrome.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Heritable connective tissue disorders are an important cause of aortic disease; however, the mechanisms of vascular failure in genetically defined aortopathies remain incompletely understood. METHODS: We analyzed the clinical course, imaging findings, and histopathologic features of two patients with clinically and genetically characterized connective tissue disorders: COL1A1-associated osteogenesis imperfecta and FBN1-associated Marfan syndrome. RESULTS: The COL1A1-associated patient developed multilevel arterial complications, including aortic regurgitation requiring aortic valve replacement at age 36, rupture of a dissected right common iliac artery in the same year, chronic type A aortic dissection requiring root, ascending, and arch replacement at age 54, and rupture of the infrarenal abdominal aorta at a diameter of only 30 mm. The FBN1-associated patient presented with type B aortic dissection at age 34 and subsequently developed progressive aneurysmal disease requiring staged thoracoabdominal replacement, total arch replacement for acute type A dissection, and aortic root replacement, followed by multiple peripheral vascular reconstructions. Histopathologic examination demonstrated valvular myxomatous degeneration in both cases. The aortic wall in both patients showed medial degeneration with fragmentation of elastic fibers. In addition, the COL1A1-associated patient demonstrated abdominal aortic wall thinning, with a minimum thickness of 1.25 mm. CONCLUSIONS: These two patients exhibited contrasting longitudinal vascular courses despite some overlapping histopathologic findings. The COL1A1-associated OI patient experienced rupture of a dissected infrarenal aortic segment, whereas the FBN1-associated Marfan patient experienced repeated dissections followed by progressive vascular dilatation and multiple surgical reconstructions. These observations are descriptive and do not establish genotype-specific patterns or mechanisms of vascular failure.

title: Inflammation-associated clinical prognostic factors and primary patency after drug-coated balloon angioplasty for recurrent autogenous arteriovenous fistula stenosis: a single-center retrospective cohort study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Recurrent autogenous arteriovenous fistula (AVF) stenosis occurs in a vascular environment in which injury, neointimal hyperplasia and inflammation may coexist. Whether routine inflammatory or hematological markers contribute to clinical prognosis after drug-coated balloon (DCB) angioplasty remains uncertain. This retrospective study examines clinical outcomes and inflammation-related prognostic associations without assuming that inflammatory pathways were measured or causally established. METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort comprised 357 patients treated between February 2023 and May 2026. The primary outcome was time from index DCB angioplasty to clinically driven target-lesion reintervention. Kaplan-Meier and Cox analyses used available follow-up; a separate clinical logistic model addressed failure within 12 months in 356 patients with complete model data. No non-DCB comparator or patient-level molecular measurements were available. RESULTS: 12 Mean brachial-artery flow increased from 288.98 ± 139.37 to 980.92 ± 174.66 mL/min and minimal luminal diameter from 1.52 ± 0.50 to 5.21 ± 0.63 mm (both P < 0.001). Kaplan-Meier primary patency was 95.24%, 84.03%, 68.90%, and 55.40% at 3, 6, 9, and 12 months. In the extended Cox model (338 patients; 191 events), previous PTA count (HR 1.129 per procedure, P = 0.003) and lesion length (HR 1.105 per cm, P = 0.001) were associated with greater hazard; postprocedural flow (HR 0.889 per 100 mL/min, P = 0.014) and red-blood-cell count (HR 0.804 per 10/L, P = 0.027) were associated with lower hazard. The five-fold cross-validated AUC of the clinical 12-month model was 0.706. CONCLUSION: In this selected single-center cohort, recurrent AVF stenosis after DCB angioplasty was associated with previous PTA burden, lesion length, postprocedural flow, and red-blood-cell count. Routine blood-cell measures provide an exploratory inflammation-related clinical context but do not establish inflammatory mechanisms or validate a specific inflammatory biomarker. Independent validation and patient-level inflammatory measurements are required.

title: Effects of prehospital blood pressure on 90-day functional outcomes in patients with acute ischemic stroke due to large vessel occlusion.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Prehospital blood pressure (BP) could influence cerebral circulation and outcomes in acute large vessel occlusion (LVO). We investigated the association between prehospital BP and 90-day functional outcomes and explored effect modification by endovascular thrombectomy (EVT). METHODS: We analyzed 1,106 patients with acute LVO transported by emergency medical services between 2018 and 2024. Prehospital systolic BP (SBP, mmHg) measured at the scene was categorized into four groups: <120, 120-149, 150-179, and ≥180 groups. The primary outcome was a 90-day modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score of 0-2. Secondary outcomes included mRS 0-3 and hemorrhagic complications. Subgroup analyses for the primary outcome were also conducted. RESULTS: Mean age was 79 years, and 51% were male; 60% underwent EVT. The SBP <120, 120-149, 150-179, and ≥180 groups included 120, 403, 403, and 180 patients, respectively. Cardioembolic stroke was most common and decreased with increasing SBP. Compared with SBP <120 mmHg, SBP ≥180 mmHg was associated with lower odds of mRS 0-2 (adjusted OR, 0.43; 95% CI, 0.22-0.84; p = 0.01), with similar trends for mRS 0-3. This association was significant in EVT-treated patients but not in non-EVT patients (interaction p = 0.007). Hemorrhagic complications were similar across groups. CONCLUSIONS: Elevated prehospital SBP (≥180 mmHg) was associated with worse 90-day functional outcomes in acute LVO, especially following EVT. These findings highlighted the potential clinical relevance of prehospital BP assessment in patients with LVO. Further investigation should be considered for prehospital BP status in addition to the in-hospital managements.

title: Tumor necrosis factor inhibitors and cardiovascular outcomes in adults with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis is associated with persistent systemic inflammation and increased cardiovascular risk. OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the association between anti-TNF therapy and clinical cardiovascular outcomes in adults with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis. METHODS: The authors conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis in accordance with PRISMA 2020 and prospectively registered the protocol in PROSPERO (CRD420251270784). Randomized controlled trials and comparative observational studies evaluating anti-TNF therapy versus placebo, no anti-TNF exposure, topical therapy and/or phototherapy, or non-biologic systemic therapy were eligible. Outcomes of interest were Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events (MACE), myocardial infarction, stroke, cardiovascular death, heart failure, atrial fibrillation, venous thromboembolism, and all-cause mortality. RESULTS: Fourteen studies were included. In randomized evidence, anti-TNF therapy was not associated with significant differences in the risk of MACE, myocardial infarction, stroke, or heart failure. In observational analyses stratified by comparator, anti-TNF therapy was associated with a lower pooled risk of reported cardiovascular events versus topical therapy, but not versus oral therapy or phototherapy. STUDY LIMITATIONS: The available evidence was limited by short follow-up in randomized trials, low cardiovascular event counts, wide confidence intervals, and indirect assessment of cardiovascular outcomes, as most trials were designed primarily for dermatologic efficacy and general safety rather than cardiovascular endpoints. CONCLUSIONS: Anti-TNF agents were not associated with a clear increase in major cardiovascular risk and appear to have an acceptable short-term cardiovascular safety profile. However, current evidence does not establish a conclusive cardioprotective effect, and larger prospective studies with longer follow-up are needed.

OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the association between anti-TNF therapy and clinical cardiovascular outcomes in adults with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis. METHODS: The authors conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis in accordance with PRISMA 2020 and prospectively registered the protocol in PROSPERO (CRD420251270784).

title: Efficacy and safety of topical versus intravenous tranexamic acid in primary total knee arthroplasty: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Total knee arthroplasty (TKA) often leads to substantial perioperative blood loss and postoperative hemoglobin decline, frequently requiring allogeneic transfusions. Tranexamic acid (TXA) effectively reduces bleeding, but debate persists regarding whether topical or intravenous (IV) administration provides superior clinical outcomes.This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the efficacy and safety of topical versus IV TXA in primary TKA using pooled data from randomized controlled trials (RCTs). METHODS: PubMed was searched for parallel-group RCTs comparing topical and IV TXA. Random-effects models analyzed continuous outcomes via standardized mean differences (SMDs) and dichotomous outcomes via relative risks (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). RESULTS: Eleven RCTs were included. Pooled analysis demonstrated no statistically significant differences between topical and IV TXA across all metrics. Postoperative hemoglobin drop (9 studies, 815 patients; SMD = -0.292, 95% CI: -0.748 to 0.163, P = 0.208), total blood loss (5 studies, 418 patients; SMD = 0.356, 95% CI: -0.297 to 1.009, P = 0.284), drainage volume (5 studies, 357 patients; SMD = 0.721, 95% CI: -0.394 to 1.836, P = 0.204), and transfusion rate (10 studies, 914 patients; RR = 0.644, 95% CI: 0.343 to 1.209, P = 0.171). Safety data were limited, as usable deep vein thrombosis (DVT) data were reported in only seven studies (with four studies not reporting or not stating thromboembolic/adverse event), and only a single DVT event was reported in the IV group. CONCLUSIONS: In primary TKA, no clear difference was detected between topical and IV TXA for blood conservation, drainage volumes, and transfusion rates, with substantial uncertainty, especially for safety and thromboembolic outcomes.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Total knee arthroplasty (TKA) often leads to substantial perioperative blood loss and postoperative hemoglobin decline, frequently requiring allogeneic transfusions. Tranexamic acid (TXA) effectively reduces bleeding, but debate persists regarding whether topical or intravenous (IV) administration provides superior clinical outcomes.This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the efficacy and safety of topical versus IV TXA in primary TKA using pooled data from randomized controlled trials (RCTs). METHODS: PubMed was searched for parallel-group RCTs comparing topical and IV TXA.

title: Spontaneous passage of an ingested full-size AAA battery through the pediatric gastrointestinal tract: a case report.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Cylindrical battery ingestion is far less common than button battery ingestion in children. While cylindrical batteries can cause gastrointestinal injury through pressure necrosis, corrosive leakage, or prolonged mucosal contact, most batteries that pass beyond the esophagus are managed conservatively. However, pediatric data on natural history and outcomes remain limited. CASE PRESENTATION: A six-year-old boy presented 6 hours after accidentally swallowing a full-size AAA cylindrical battery. He remained asymptomatic throughout. Initial radiography located the battery in the stomach; subsequent imaging confirmed gradual migration through the jejunum and distal small bowel. Serial abdominal radiographs and repeated clinical assessments demonstrated continuous transit without obstruction or perforation, with subsequent spontaneous passage of the intact cylindrical battery in the stool. DISCUSSION: This case demonstrates that a full-sized AAA cylindrical battery can traverse the pediatric gastrointestinal tract uneventfully after passing through the esophagus. The favorable outcome supports the existing literature advocating expectant management in carefully selected asymptomatic patients with documented radiographic progression. Nevertheless, close clinical observation and serial imaging remain essential to identify patients requiring intervention due to impaction, lack of progression, symptom development, or evidence of battery-related injury. CONCLUSION: An intact, cylindrical AAA battery can pass spontaneously through the entire pediatric gastrointestinal tract without endoscopic or surgical intervention. Conservative management with vigilant clinical and radiological monitoring appears to be safe and effective in asymptomatic children demonstrating progressive battery transit.

title: Cause-specific mortality after endovascular treatment for anterior vs. posterior circulation large vessel occlusion: a multicenter cohort study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Acute ischemic stroke due to large vessel occlusion (AIS-LVO) carries substantial mortality despite endovascular treatment (EVT). Whether causes of death differ between anterior (AVO) and posterior (PVO) circulation occlusions is poorly characterized. We compared cause-specific 90-day mortality between patients with AVO and PVO treated with EVT. METHODS: In this multicenter retrospective cohort, consecutive patients with AIS-LVO who underwent EVT at 111 hospitals in China (ANGEL-ACT registry [Endovascular Treatment Key Technique and Emergency Workflow Improvement of acute ischemic stroke]) were included, and adjudicated causes of death were grouped into prespecified categories. Cause-specific mortality was assessed in the complete analytic cohort using the Fine-Gray subdistribution hazard model, with survivors censored at 90 days and deaths from other causes treated as competing events. Cumulative incidence functions were estimated with the Aalen-Johansen estimator. RESULTS: p p p p p p Among 1,671 eligible patients (1,300 AVO, 371 PVO), 228 deaths (13.6%) occurred within 90 days. All-cause mortality was higher in PVO than AVO (19.4% vs. 12.0%). Cerebral edema-related death was significantly more frequent in PVO than AVO (90-day cumulative incidence 9.16% vs. 4.15%; adjusted subdistribution hazard ratio [sHR] 0.47, 95% CI 0.30-0.73,= 0.001; Gray's test< 0.001). Fatal hemorrhagic transformation was numerically more frequent in AVO but did not reach statistical significance in the complete cohort (3.77% vs. 1.89%; adjusted sHR 1.76, 95% CI 0.78-3.98,= 0.17; Gray's test= 0.076), consistent across all sensitivity analyses. Pneumonia-related (adjusted sHR 0.34, 95% CI 0.17-0.68,= 0.003) and recurrent stroke-related (adjusted sHR 0.29, 95% CI 0.10-0.86,= 0.026) deaths were also more frequent in PVO; the pneumonia association remained significant after Bonferroni correction, whereas the recurrent stroke association did not. CONCLUSION: Fatal complications after EVT differ by occlusion territory. Posterior circulation occlusion is independently associated with a higher risk of death from cerebral edema, pneumonia, and recurrent stroke, although the recurrent stroke association did not survive Bonferroni correction. Hemorrhagic transformation accounted for a larger share of anterior circulation deaths, but this did not correspond to a statistically significant increase in risk in the complete cohort.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Acute ischemic stroke due to large vessel occlusion (AIS-LVO) carries substantial mortality despite endovascular treatment (EVT). Whether causes of death differ between anterior (AVO) and posterior (PVO) circulation occlusions is poorly characterized. We compared cause-specific 90-day mortality between patients with AVO and PVO treated with EVT.

title: Computational Fluid Dynamics Analysis of Contrast Agent Distribution in Acute Large Artery Occlusive Stroke: A Preliminary Proof-of-Concept Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Acute ischemic stroke (AIS) resulting from carotid artery occlusion (CAO) represents a significant clinical challenge because conventional imaging modalities often lead to inaccuracies in occlusion length assessment, potentially compromising therapeutic decision-making. We aimed to analyze the distribution patterns of contrast agents using computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations in AIS caused by CAO and to mitigate errors in estimating occlusion length. METHODS: Data from four patients with AIS caused by CAO were analyzed. CFD simulations were conducted using postoperative computed tomography angiography (CTA) data to model contrast agent flow, and the results were compared with those of preoperative CTA and intraoperative digital subtraction angiography (DSA). RESULTS: CTA/DSA demonstrated a flame sign at the ICA origin in Patients 1-3. Patients 1 and 2 had carotid dissection, whereas Patient 3 had a C4-segment embolic occlusion. In Patient 3, DSA showed C1-origin vortices, a horizontal contrast-blood interface, and no distal C1 opacification, features distinct from those in Patients 1 and 2. CFD simulations using the post-recanalization CTA model replicated this contrast distribution, including the vortices and interface; proximal C1 vortex ranges, velocities, pressures, and wall shear stress were comparable, but the mass-weighted average velocity varied over time. CONCLUSIONS: CFD simulations recreated contrast agent distribution during C4 segment occlusion, revealing a high-pressure dead space in the distal C1 segment. This study generated preliminary evidence for understanding contrast agent distribution in CAOs, offering valuable insights for clinical imaging assessments.

METHODS: Data from four patients with AIS caused by CAO were analyzed.

title: Update of a living network meta-analysis comparing noncompounded 1% polidocanol endovenous microfoam (Varithena) ablation versus endovenous thermal ablation in chronic venous insufficiency.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: We previously published a network meta-analysis showing no statistically significant difference between commercially manufactured 1% polidocanol endovenous microfoam (PEM) and endovenous thermal ablation (ETA) for vein closure or deep vein thrombosis, when PEM was distinguished from physician-compounded foam. This living network meta-analysis updates the previous analysis comparing the effectiveness and safety of PEM ablation vs ETA for the primary treatment of adult patients with venous insufficiency caused by lower-extremity truncal vein incompetence. METHODS: Systematic review searches following the prespecified protocol were conducted quarterly through March 2026. No changes were made to selection criteria. Vein closure, deep venous thrombosis, and ulcer healing were summarized as odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). A composite outcome of disease-specific quality of life (QoL) or symptom improvement scales was summarized with Hedges' g standardized mean difference. RESULTS: The updated search yielded 507 new citations and 11 new eligible studies, for a total of 24 studies (235,413 patients). PEM was not statistically different from ETA for vein closure (OR, 0.71; 95% CI, 0.42-1.21). A sensitivity analysis at longest follow-up (mean, 28 months; range, 12-72 months) showed similar results (OR, 0.71; 95% CI, 0.45-1.11). There was no evidence of increased deep venous thrombosis risk with PEM vs ETA (OR, 0.83; 95% CI, 0.29-2.43). Post-treatment improvement in disease-specific QoL or venous insufficiency symptoms showed no statistically significant difference between PEM and ETA (Hedges' g standardized mean difference, 0.04; 95% CI, -0.16 to 0.25), though the network was not fully connected. Finally, ulcer healing data was limited, but an exploratory analysis found no evidence of a statistically significant difference. CONCLUSIONS: This living network meta-analysis update reinforced the original findings that 1% PEM is not statistically different from ETA for venous closure or deep venous thrombosis in the treatment of chronic venous insufficiency, and adds new preliminary information on outcomes relevant to the patient experience. There was no evidence of a statistically significant difference between PEM ablation and ETA for a composite of disease-specific QoL and symptom improvement, or for ulcer healing. The living approach maintains rigor and efficiently keeps evidence current as new studies emerge.

This living network meta-analysis updates the previous analysis comparing the effectiveness and safety of PEM ablation vs ETA for the primary treatment of adult patients with venous insufficiency caused by lower-extremity truncal vein incompetence. METHODS: Systematic review searches following the prespecified protocol were conducted quarterly through March 2026.

title: Timeless therapeutics: cardiac indications for vitamin K antagonists in clinical practice.
abstract: Anticoagulation is a critical component in the treatment of cardiovascular diseases. Large randomised controlled trials have demonstrated that direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) are effective and safe for stroke prevention in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) and treatment or prevention of venous thromboembolism. Nevertheless, for specific cardiac indications and patient characteristics, vitamin K antagonists (VKAs) rather than DOACs are either preferred, or the benefit of DOACs in comparison to VKAs remains uncertain. These include, among others, mechanical heart valves, AF associated with moderate-to-severe mitral stenosis, left ventricular or atrial thrombus, and older patients with frailty. As VKAs will continue to play a vital role in the management of patients with cardiovascular diseases in the foreseeable future, this review discusses cardiac indications and patient characteristics that necessitate the use of VKAs and general management principles of VKA therapy.

title: Variation and temporal trends in Medicare Severity Diagnosis Related Group billing for carotid endarterectomy across Vascular Quality Initiative centers.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Hospitals use Medicare Severity Diagnosis Related Group (MS-DRG) coding to bill for each admission, with higher payment provided for those with complications or comorbidities (CCs) or major CCs (MCCs). We analyzed variation in MS-DRG coding for carotid endarterectomy (CEA) across Vascular Quality Initiative (VQI) centers to identify opportunities for improvement. METHODS: We matched CEA cases in the VQI registry with Medicare claims data from 2013 through 2023. A multivariable stepwise logistic regression model was created to identify variables associated with CC or MCC billing (with odds ratios [ORs]). We examined variations in CC or MCC billing percentages among centers and applied a multivariable model to compare observed-to-expected (O:E) CC or MCC billing rates to adjust for patient differences. Billing trends over time were analyzed using linear regression. RESULTS: Among 75,064 primary CEA admissions for Medicare beneficiaries, 39.5% were billed with CCs or MCCs (31.1% CCs, 8.4% MCCs) and 60.5% without. Eleven VQI clinical variables that indicated CCs were significantly associated with CC or MCC billing: dialysis dependence (OR, 22.30), postoperative neurological events (OR, 5.25), length of stay >2 days (OR, 4.98), pre-existing heart failure (OR, 4.08), any postoperative complication (OR, 3.70), reoperation (OR, 3.65), preoperative neurological event (OR, 1.70), higher American Society of Anesthesiologists class (OR, 1.50), urgent/emergent procedure (OR, 1.28), postoperative intravenous blood pressure management (OR, 1.27), and institutional transfer (OR, 1.16). Across 371 VQI centers, CC or MCC billing rates varied 5.6-fold, ranging from 15% to 84% of admissions. After risk adjustment, observed-to-expected ratios still demonstrated 4.2-fold variation, from 0.45 to 1.90 across centers. The observed rate of CC or MCC billing increased over time, from 35.5% in 2015 to 46.1% in 2023 (P < .001). In contrast, the expected adjusted rates predicted by the model remained stable (P = .269). A discrete inflection point was identified between 2016 and 2017, after which higher billing rates persisted (P < .001). CONCLUSIONS: Substantial variation exists for MS-DRG billing for CEA across VQI centers. Billing rates for CCs or MCCs increased from 2013 through 2023. These findings suggest potential underbilling at some centers and overbilling at others. Leveraging Medicare-linked VQI registry data and the proposed model could help to improve coding and billing accuracy, optimize reimbursement, and reduce Medicare audit risk.

title: Predictors of in-hospital venous thromboembolism in patients undergoing primary total hip arthroplasty.
abstract: PURPOSE: This study evaluated the national inpatient incidence, patient characteristics, and independent predictors of VTE following primary THA. METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was performed using the National Inpatient Sample from 2016 to 2022. Adult patients undergoing primary THA were identified using ICD-10 procedure codes. The primary outcome was in-hospital VTE, defined as deep vein thrombosis or pulmonary embolism during the index admission. Survey-weighted analyses were used to generate national estimates, compare baseline characteristics, and identify independent predictors of VTE using multivariable logistic regression. Statistical significance was set at P < 0.05. RESULTS: Among 855,645 weighted inpatient primary THA admissions, 1660 patients developed in-hospital VTE, corresponding to an incidence of 0.19%. Patients with VTE were older (P < 0.001) and more frequently covered by Medicare (P < 0.001), treated at large hospitals (P = 0.009), and treated at urban teaching hospitals (P = 0.013). They also had a greater prevalence of comorbidities, including autoimmune disease, coagulopathy, congestive heart failure, deficiency anemia, peripheral vascular disease, pulmonary circulation disorders, and moderate renal failure (all P < 0.001), as well as chronic pulmonary disease (P = 0.001) and obesity (P = 0.003). On adjusted analysis, the strongest predictors of VTE were paralysis (OR 9.79, P < 0.001), lymphoma (OR 4.35, P = 0.001), other neurologic disorders (OR 4.30, P < 0.001), and pulmonary circulation disorders (OR 3.50, P < 0.001). Additional independent predictors included peripheral vascular disease (OR 2.19, P < 0.001), autoimmune disease (OR 2.01, P < 0.001), congestive heart failure (OR 1.83, P = 0.022), coagulopathy (OR 1.80, P = 0.035), deficiency anemia (OR 1.65, P = 0.002), hypothyroidism (OR 1.45, P = 0.007), and obesity (OR 1.35, P = 0.018). CONCLUSION: In-hospital VTE following primary THA was uncommon but concentrated among medically complex patients. Improved risk stratification may guide perioperative counseling, surveillance, and individualized thromboprophylaxis for higher-risk patients.

METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was performed using the National Inpatient Sample from 2016 to 2022. Adult patients undergoing primary THA were identified using ICD-10 procedure codes.

title: Patient-specific finite element modeling of image-derived shell morphoelastic growth: A general framework and application to stented aortic dissection.
abstract: Vascular pathology often manifests in complex shape evolution visualized by longitudinal computed tomography (CT) imaging. Growth and remodeling (G&R) frameworks have been integrated into finite element (FE) modeling to probe the mechanics underlying this progression, extending into patient-specific approaches. Their scalability and translatability, however, are limited by the computational burden associated with heterogeneous, anisotropic growth fields and through-thickness meshing. While existing shell growth formulations can mitigate this burden, they require nontrivial FE implementation especially in commercial softwares (e.g., Abaqus) and their efficacy in patient-specific geometries under complex loading is unclear. In this work, we present a general computational framework to implement shell morphoelastic growth computed directly from registered patient-specific CT images. This shell implementation is validated against solid 3D formulations, allows thickness tunability, and increases compatibility with CT surfaces. We demonstrate the robustness of this formulation through modeling post-operative growth in a patient-specific aortic dissection under stent-based loading. Results first show that complex stent-based loading can deform the shell dissection flap to reproduce post-operative geometry. The outer aortic wall is then given a growth field calculated from registration of 1-month and 5-year post-operative CT images, which is implemented along with stent-based loading and pressurization. Results from this model capture the trends in total and lumen morphological evolution observed at intermediate timepoints. These findings establish a general framework, validated with a patient-specific case study of aortic dissection, with the potential to expand to other complex systems, scale to larger patient populations, and apply G&R to clinical translation.

title: Integrated transcriptomic and metabolomic analyzes reveal hepatic regulatory mechanisms of residual feed intake during the late growth stage of slow-growing yellow-feathered broilers.
abstract: This study aimed to characterize hepatic molecular features associated with residual feed intake (RFI) during the late growth stage of slow-growing yellow-feathered broilers through integrated transcriptomic and metabolomic analyzes. RFI was measured in 478 individually caged male Langya chickens from 96 to 133 days of age. After the feeding trial, the chickens were ranked in ascending order of RFI and classified into low-RFI (LRFI) and high-RFI (HRFI) subpopulations using the population mean RFI as the cutoff. Eight healthy chickens were then randomly selected from each subpopulation to form the LRFI and HRFI groups (n = 8 per group). Following slaughter and tissue collection at 133 days of age, hepatic transcriptomic and LC-MS-based untargeted metabolomic analyzes were conducted. Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) and differentially abundant metabolites (DAMs) were subsequently subjected to enrichment and correlation analyzes. Compared with HRFI chickens, LRFI chickens had lower feed intake (FI) and higher eviscerated carcass yield and breast muscle yield. They also had lower abdominal fat percentage and muscle fat width, whereas BWG and metabolic body weight were similar between groups. Liver profiling identified 850 DEGs and 282 DAMs. Integrated KEGG analysis identified 15 pathways significantly enriched in both datasets. The amino acid metabolism-related pathways among these shared pathways collectively pointed to aromatic amino acid (AAA)-related metabolism, including biosynthesis of amino acids, phenylalanine metabolism, phenylalanine, tyrosine and tryptophan biosynthesis, and tryptophan metabolism. A total of 16 DEGs and 29 DAMs were mapped to these pathways and showed widespread significant correlations. Among them, IL4I1, AFMID, ASS1, PHGDH, MAOB, IDO2, HAAO, and PAH were identified as candidate genes associated with RFI. These results characterized hepatic molecular features associated with RFI during the late growth stage of slow-growing yellow-feathered broilers. These findings indicate that hepatic AAA-related metabolism may play a potential role in RFI divergence during the late growth stage in slow-growing yellow-feathered broilers. The identified AAA metabolism-related pathways provide a focused set of candidate genes, metabolites, and pathways for further investigation of their roles in RFI and feed efficiency, and provide a theoretical basis for molecular breeding and breed conservation of slow-growing broilers.

title: PASCAL Precision System Outcomes by Implant Location and Lesion Location in Degenerative Mitral Regurgitation Patients From the STS/ACC TVT Registry.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Mitral valve transcatheter edge-to-edge repair can be more challenging in noncentral regions of the valve and in anterior or bileaflet lesions. We assess effect of implant location and leaflet lesion location on safety and effectiveness of PASCAL Precision system in degenerative mitral regurgitation (MR). METHODS: Mitral valve transcatheter edge-to-edge repair outcomes in patients with degenerative MR treated with PASCAL Precision system (September 2022-October 2024), from the US STS/ACC TVT (Society of Thoracic Surgeons/American College of Cardiology Transcatheter Valve Therapy) Registry, were analyzed by implant location (A2P2/non-A2P2) and leaflet lesion location (anterior/posterior/bileaflet). Procedural, clinical, and echocardiographic outcomes to 30 days were assessed. RESULTS: P P P P P P P P At 30 days, both A2P2 (n=1526) and non-A2P2 (n=299) groups had low event rates (cardiovascular mortality: 1.1% versus 1.0%, mitral valve reintervention: 0.4% versus 0.0% and single leaflet device attachment: 0.5% versus 0.3%; all>0.05) and demonstrated significant MR reduction (<0.001 versus baseline) with no significant difference between groups (=0.750) (MR ≤2+: 93.4% versus 95.4%; MR ≤1+: 72.0% versus 73.3%). Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Overall Summary scores improved significantly in both groups (∆19.3, ∆17.7 points;=0.741). The anterior (n=250), posterior (n=902), and bileaflet (n=192) disease groups also had low event rates (cardiovascular mortality: 0.4%, 1.1%, 0.0%; mitral valve reintervention: 0.8%, 0.1%, 0.5%; and single leaflet device attachment: 0.8%, 0.2%, 0.5%; all>0.05), and demonstrated significant MR reduction (<0.001 versus baseline) with no significant difference across groups (=0.459) (MR ≤2+: 94.1%, 93.1%, and 94.5%; MR ≤1+: 79.0%, 69.2%, and 72.4%). All groups experienced significant improvement in Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Overall Summary scores (∆21.4, ∆18.8, ∆12.0 points;=0.087). CONCLUSION: In real-world patients with degenerative mitral regurgitation, treatment with the PASCAL Precision system was associated with favorable safety and effectiveness at 30 days, regardless of implant location or leaflet lesion location.

title: Surgical management of splenic artery aneurysms: a case series of three patients with diverse presentations.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Splenic artery aneurysm (SAA) is the most common visceral artery aneurysm and includes true aneurysms and pseudoaneurysms, which have different etiologies and clinical behavior. Presentation ranges from incidental detection to life-threatening rupture with hemoperitoneum. Management depends on aneurysm size, symptoms, morphology, anatomical relationships, comorbidities, and rupture status. METHODS: We retrospectively described three consecutive patients with SAA or pseudoaneurysm treated surgically at a tertiary surgical center, Loghman Hakim Hospital, Shahid Beheshti University of Medical Sciences, Tehran, Iran, between 2020 and 2025. Clinical records, imaging, operative findings, histopathology, postoperative course, and available follow-up were reviewed. The series was reported in accordance with the PROCESS 2025 reporting guideline. CASE PRESENTATIONS: Case 1 was a 66-year-old man with chronic liver disease and thrombocytopenia in whom a giant true SAA measuring approximately 72 × 68 × 76 mm was incidentally identified during trauma imaging. The aneurysm was adjacent to the pancreatic body without rupture. Elective open splenectomy with aneurysm resection and concurrent liver wedge biopsy was performed. Case 2 was a 63-year-old woman with a 7-month history of postprandial epigastric pain and a symptomatic true SAA of undocumented size. Elective open resection with splenectomy was performed; histopathology unexpectedly demonstrated necrotizing granulomatous splenitis. Case 3 was a 38-year-old woman with sickle cell disease who developed acute abdominal pain after a generalized seizure, with severe anemia and hemoperitoneum. A ruptured splenic artery pseudoaneurysm was identified at emergency laparotomy after a ruptured ectopic pregnancy had initially been suspected. RESULTS: All three patients underwent open splenectomy with aneurysm excision, which was elective in cases 1 and 2 and emergent in case 3. There were no intraoperative deaths or reoperations. All three patients had uneventful postoperative recoveries. 6-month follow-up was available for case 1; longer-term uniform follow-up was not available for all patients. CONCLUSION: SAAs encompass a broad clinical spectrum, from incidentally discovered giant aneurysms to symptomatic lesions and catastrophic rupture. These cases illustrate the importance of anatomy-directed treatment selection, early recognition of rupture, and consideration of vascular causes in patients with unexplained hemoperitoneum. Endovascular therapy is preferred for anatomically suitable elective lesions, whereas open surgery remains an important option for giant, complex, or ruptured aneurysms. The proposed algorithm is an educational synthesis of published evidence, current Society for Vascular Surgery guidelines recommendations, and the clinical experience represented by this institutional series rather than a prospectively validated decision tool.

title: Cortical Destruction due to a Postoperative Femoral Artery Pseudoaneurysm: A Case Report.
abstract: CASE: Periprosthetic cortical destruction due to vascular complications is exceptionally rare, with only a few cases reported. We present an 82-year-old man with progressive hip pain 2 years after γ-nail fixation. Imaging revealed a large cortical defect of the proximal medial femur. CT-angiography demonstrated a pseudoaneurysm of the profunda femoris artery. Endovascular stent grafting was performed. The patient's symptoms resolved, and cortical remodeling was observed at 4 months. CONCLUSION: This case highlights the importance of considering vascular injury in the differential diagnosis of late postoperative hip pain and illustrates that timely recognition can guide adequate treatment and ensure favorable outcomes.

title: 6 The emerging role of mA in aortic dissection: from molecular mechanisms to therapeutic potential.
abstract: 6 6 6 6 6 6 6 6 6 Aortic dissection (AD) is an emergent medical condition with a hidden onset and sudden rupture, which usually results in a high mortality rate. N6-methyladenosine (mA) is the most abundant modification in eukaryotic RNA molecules and plays a critical role in regulating RNA metabolism. Dysregulation of mA modification has been linked to a variety of diseases. Interestingly, aberrant expression of mA-associated factors is observed in AD. The mA methylation can promote or inhibit the development of AD by modulating cell death, oxidative stress, macrophage polarization and VSMC phenotype switching, depending on mA-modified transcripts, readers and downstream pathways. In addition, mA exerts a significant effect on the major risk factors for AD, including hypertension, atherosclerosis, obesity and aortic aneurysm. Thus, modulating mA modification by small-molecule inhibitors, natural products or miRNAs may represent a promising approach for developing new therapeutic interventions for AD. In this review, we first give a brief perspective on mA modification and its regulators. Subsequently, we summarize the recent research progress on the role of mA in AD and related-risk factors, with an emphasis on its diagnostic value and therapeutic potential.

title: Early antithrombotic therapy improves 90-day functional outcomes in patients with postinterventional cerebral hyperdensity after mechanical thrombectomy: a retrospective cohort study.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE: Postinterventional cerebral hyperdensity (PCHD) is a specific type of hyperdensity commonly observed on computed tomography (CT) scans of the head after mechanical thrombectomy (MT). This study aimed to investigate the association between early antithrombotic therapy (EAT) and 90-day functional outcomes in anterior circulation acute ischemic stroke (acAIS) patients with PCHD. METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted on 141 consecutive acAIS patients with PCHD after MT. EAT was defined as antithrombotic therapy administered within 24 h post-MT. The primary outcome was a favorable 90-day functional outcome (modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score of 0-2). The secondary outcomes included 90-day mortality, ΔmRS (defined as the mRS score before MT minus the 90-day mRS score), enlargement of cerebral hyperdensity, and persistent hyperdensity on the 24-h follow-up CT graded by the European Cooperative Acute Stroke Study (ECASS III) morphology. Baseline and outcome data were compared between the EAT and non-EAT groups. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses were performed to assess the association between EAT and favorable outcomes. Sensitivity and subgroup analyses were performed to evaluate the robustness and internal consistency of the results. RESULTS: p p p p Of the 129 patients with complete 90-day mRS data, 59 (45.7%) received EAT. The EAT group had a higher proportion of favorable outcomes (59.3% vs. 37.1%,= 0.019). A multivariate logistic regression analysis showed that EAT remained significantly associated with favorable outcomes (Model 1: odds ratio (OR) 2.469, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.195-5.104,= 0.015; Model 2: OR 2.72, 95% CI 1.02-7.20,= 0.045; Model 3: OR 3.68, 95% CI 1.32-10.30,= 0.013), and the results were consistent after imputation based on discharge data and multiple imputation. Sensitivity and subgroup analyses showed consistent results, with no significant interaction effects observed. CONCLUSION: EAT is associated with improved 90-day functional outcomes in acAIS patients with PCHD, warranting further investigation in larger prospective studies.

This study aimed to investigate the association between early antithrombotic therapy (EAT) and 90-day functional outcomes in anterior circulation acute ischemic stroke (acAIS) patients with PCHD. METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted on 141 consecutive acAIS patients with PCHD after MT.

title: Association of the triglyceride-glucose index with the severity of lower extremity arterial disease across glucose metabolic states: a single-center cross-sectional study of 656 patients with angiographically confirmed disease.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To examine the cross-sectional association between the triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index and the severity of lower extremity arterial disease (LEAD) in hospitalized patients with angiographically confirmed LEAD, to test whether this association differs across Glucose Metabolic States, and to quantify the ability of the TyG index to discriminate prevalent ischemic tissue loss (Rutherford grades 5-6). METHODS: This single-center, retrospective, cross-sectional study included 656 consecutive patients with angiographically confirmed LEAD who were hospitalized in the Department of Vascular Surgery at the General Hospital of Ningxia Medical University from January 2023 through December 2024. Diagnosis was confirmed by digital subtraction angiography (DSA). Patients were classified into four groups according to their Glucose Metabolic States: normal glucose tolerance (NGT, n = 150), impaired glucose regulation (IGR, n = 148), diabetes with a duration of <10 years (DM<10y, n = 174), and diabetes with a duration of ≥10 years (DM≥10y, n = 184). Glucose and lipid parameters and LEAD severity (Rutherford classification) were assessed during the same hospitalization. Spearman correlation, multinomial logistic regression (with grade 1 mild claudication as the reference), ordinal logistic regression with a TyG × Glucose Metabolic States interaction term, proportional-odds assessment by cumulative binary splits, ROC analysis with bootstrap internal validation (1,000 resamples), and decision-curve analysis were performed. Sensitivity analyses used continuous glycemic measures instead of the categorical groups, excluded implausibly low fasting glucose values, and added liver enzymes to the adjustment set. The primary outcome was ischemic tissue loss, defined as Rutherford grades 5-6 (n = 205, 31.2%). RESULTS: The TyG index increased progressively across Glucose Metabolic States categories (8.79 ± 0.51, 9.15 ± 0.48, 9.57 ± 0.56, and 9.67 ± 0.52 for NGT, IGR, DM < 10 years, and DM ≥ 10 years, respectively; P < 0.001) and was strongly correlated with Rutherford grade (Spearman r = 0.677, P < 0.001). In a multinomial logistic regression model adjusted for age, sex, smoking, hypertension, BMI, and fatty liver disease (all variance inflation factors < 1.5), the TyG index remained associated with each severity category above the reference, with adjusted odds ratios per 0.5-unit increment of 2.51 (grade 2), 2.83 (grade 3), 7.56 (grade 4), 9.62 (grade 5), and 20.45 (grade 6). The interaction between TyG and Glucose Metabolic States was statistically significant (likelihood-ratio χ² = 95.63, df = 3, P < 0.001); stratum-specific odds ratios per 0.5-unit increment were 1.51 (95% CI 1.07-2.13) in IGR, 2.50 (1.90-3.29) in DM < 10 years, and 8.14 (5.23-12.67) in DM ≥ 10 years, whereas the NGT-stratum estimate was unstable (quasi-complete separation) and could not be interpreted. When the categorical groups were replaced with a continuous glycemic measure, the interaction with fasting plasma glucose remained significant but was in the opposite direction (χ² = 9.36, df = 1, P = 0.002): the TyG-severity association was stronger at lower fasting glucose levels (OR per 0.5 unit 4.81 at 4.8 mmol/L) than at higher fasting glucose levels (3.46 at 8.3 mmol/L). For discriminating Rutherford grades 5-6, the AUC was 0.833 (95% CI 0.796-0.870); the Youden-optimal cutoff was 9.42 (sensitivity 85.9%, specificity 71.0%, positive predictive value 57.3%, negative predictive value 91.7%, LR + 2.96, LR- 0.199), and this cutoff was stable across bootstrap resamples. Decision-curve analysis showed a positive net benefit relative to treat-all or treat-none strategies across threshold probabilities of approximately 0.09-0.57. CONCLUSION: In this cohort of patients with angiographically confirmed LEAD, the TyG index was independently associated with LEAD severity. The strength of this association appeared to vary across Glucose Metabolic States, but the apparent gradient from normal glucose tolerance to long-standing diabetes was not reproduced when glucose was modelled continuously, suggesting that part of the categorical pattern is attributable to the grouping itself (i.e., mathematical coupling and range restriction). The TyG index showed moderate ability to discriminate prevalent ischemic tissue loss. Because exposure and outcome were assessed during the same hospitalization, these findings represent a cross-sectional association rather than a predictive one; the proposed cutoff values were derived from the same sample in which they were evaluated and require external validation before they can be considered for clinical use.

METHODS: This single-center, retrospective, cross-sectional study included 656 consecutive patients with angiographically confirmed LEAD who were hospitalized in the Department of Vascular Surgery at the General Hospital of Ningxia Medical University from January 2023 through December 2024. Diagnosis was confirmed by digital subtraction angiography (DSA).

title: Case Report: Fetal giant congenital hemangioma with arteriovenous malformation: to be or not to be.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: This study reports a rare and life-threatening case of a giant congenital hemangioma with arteriovenous fistula in a neonate and describes its clinical management and outcomes. METHOD: A female neonate with a giant right forearm hemangioma with arteriovenous fistula, detected prenatally at 23 weeks, was managed by a multidisciplinary team. Postnatally, the infant developed severe pulmonary hypertension and active bleeding from the mass. Diagnosis was confirmed via computed tomography angiography and arteriography. Emergency intervention with combined embolization coil and sclerotherapy was performed, followed by oral propranolol therapy. RESULTS: Following the combined intervention and pharmacotherapy, the condition of the infant improved significantly. The severe pulmonary hypertension resolved, and the tumor size progressively reduced. CONCLUSION: Congenital hemangioma combined with arteriovenous malformation can lead to severe, life-threatening complications. A prompt, multidisciplinary approach involving embolization, sclerotherapy, and pharmacotherapy can achieve favorable outcomes, underscoring the importance of early recognition and integrated perinatal management.

title: Added value of brain perfusion ultrasound to prehospital stroke scales-a secondary analysis of the SONAS trial.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Accurate prehospital identification of acute ischemic stroke due to large vessel occlusion (LVO) is critical to guide selection of an optimal target hospital for either intravenous thrombolysis (IVT) alone and/or mechanical thrombectomy (MT). The novel portable non-imaging brain perfusion ultrasound (BPU) device SONAS(TM) indicated similar sensitivity and specificity as prehospital stroke scales. In this study, we reanalyzed data from the original 20 patient cohort to evaluate whether combining BPU with prehospital stroke scales (ph-SS) can further improve LVO detection. METHODS: Clinical data and NIHSS scores of all patients suffering from acute ischemic stroke with and without proven LVO in the SONAS trial were collected and applied to 16 different phSS. As an exploratory analysis we also applied a prehospital score for intracerebral hemorrhage (ph-ICH) to this cohort. The positive and negative predictive values as well as sensitivity and specificity were analyzed retrospectively for both methods. RESULTS: The best performing phSS, CG-FAST, and RACE, showed comparable performances to BPU, but still misdiagnosed patients. However, in our specific cohort, the combination of both methods allowed for a reliable classification into three groups: (A) "highly probably LVO", (B) "highly probable non-LVO" and (C) "not assessable" (including all patients misdiagnosed by one method alone). The addition of BPU resulted in shifts towards higher sensitivity and NPV. When using the ph-ICH score three patients were classified as ICH (false positive), and all of them showed severe perfusion deficits in BPU indicating LVO. CONCLUSION: The combination of BPU with phSS may hold the potential to enhance prehospital triage of acute stroke patients selecting patients to (A) endovascular-capable centers, (B) the nearest stroke unit for, i.e., IVT or (C) either depending on other clinical factors and local circumstances. However, validation is critical in stroke-call patients in the prehospital setting including application by paramedics with/without emergency physicians or telemedical support, and compared to other prehospital point-of-care diagnostics both in respect to sensitivity/specificity, timeline and, ultimately, costs. In the future, the addition of serum biomarkers for ICH may open new opportunities for early ICH treatment or even enable prehospital IVT, and/or streamline direct to angio-suite approaches in confirmed LVO.

title: Spatial multi-omics implicates vascular adipocytes proximal to tertiary lymphoid structures in human aortic aneurysm and B-cell autoreactivity.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Perivascular Adipose Tissue (PVAT), tertiary lymphoid structures (TLS), and the B lymphocytes they harbor have been implicated in regulating vascular diseases, including abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA). Yet, the relationship of adipose tissue to TLS and B-cell responses is poorly understood. APPROACH AND RESULTS: Here, using multi-omics approaches, we characterized the potential interplay of vascular adipocytes and TLSs in shaping microenvironments conducive to pathogenic B-cell immunity in human AAA pathology. Single-nucleus RNA sequencing identified white adipocytes expressing transcripts for lipogenesis, lipolysis, and extracellular remodeling. Unexpectedly, these adipocytes expressed haptotactic and chemotactic factors such as thrombospondin 1 and autotaxin, and extracellular matrix proteins with potential to recruit CD44+ leukocytes within AAAs. Immunohistology revealed two anatomical compartments for the adipocytes within AAAs: PVAT and the medial-adventitial region. Medial-adventitial adipocytes were frequently associated with CD44+ TLSs and were largely absent from control non-aneurysmal abdominal aortas. Visium HD spatial transcriptomics revealed mature TLSs recapitulated the organization of functional secondary lymphoid structures, with multiple B-cell follicles clustered to form a nodular structure partly covered by a layer of smooth muscle cells. The TLSs harbored isotype-switched B cells expressing IgG1, IgG3, or IgA, with dominant kappa chain usage and IgG antibodies to the aortic wall. Myeloid cells in AAA were implicated in promoting B-cell effects, as they were the primary producers of B-cell activating factor (BAFF), a cytokine that promotes B-cell infiltration, survival, and function. CONCLUSION: Altogether, our results support a model in which new adipocytes in the medial-adventitial layer elicit inflammatory pathways that promote early TLS formation, and BAFF produced by myeloid cells promotes the survival and maturation of vascular wall-antigen-exposed B cells, leading to mature TLS formation, production of antibodies to AAA antigens, fueling inflammation and AAA growth. CLINICAL IMPLICATIONS: Despite multiple drugs showing efficacy in preclinical animal models, no non-surgical treatments are available for AAAs. Therefore, we re-evaluated human aortic aneurysm pathology using new technologies to better understand human aneurysm pathogenesis. The results revealed formation of novel adipocytes in the medial-adventitial region of human AAAs. These vascular adipocytes exacerbate inflammation by attracting an arsenal of immune cells to the medial-adventitial region. B-cell activating factor (BAFF) further exacerbates the B-cell immune response by supporting the formation of mature tertiary lymphoid structures (TLSs) and production of antibodies against AAA tissue. While more studies are needed to confirm these findings, this work opens new avenues of investigation for potential therapeutics for treating small AAAs. Particularly, repurposing anti-adipogenesis drugs and anti-BAFF therapeutics may attenuate B-cell immune responses, inflammation, and AAA growth.

title: Percutaneous device closure of a massive pseudoaneurysm of the descending aorta in a paediatric patient with Takayasu arteritis.
abstract: TM Takayasu arteritis (TA) is commonly known as a disease of young women, highly prevalent in Asia and Central America, and associated with multiple vascular complications. Although it is well described in the paediatric population, severe complications are rarely seen. A 6-year-old girl was referred to our institution with features suggestive of a tuberculosis infection, along with a suspected intrathoracic mass on preliminary imaging. Further investigations confirmed the mass to be a massive pseudoaneurysm originating from the descending aorta and extending into the left hemithorax. A multidisciplinary discussion concluded that this pseudoaneurysm carried a high mortality risk with a direct surgical approach. This case report describes the use of an Amplatzerseptal occluder as a bridge to surgical excision of the massive pseudoaneurysm in a paediatric patient with confirmed TA.

title: Ascending and hemi arch replacement during bilateral orthotopic lung transplant: a case report.
abstract: Lung transplant candidates increasingly have concomitant cardiac disease. Prior studies have demonstrated the safety of lung transplant with concurrent cardiac surgery in small case series. Here, we describe a case of ascending aorta replacement at the same time as bilateral lung transplant utilizing a clamshell incision. The patient recovered well. With this case report, we aim to contribute to the growing literature showing the safety of concomitant heart and aortic surgery during lung transplant.

title: Post-Transcriptional Silencing of PHD2 by CRISPR-Cas13d Enhances Pro-Angiogenic Signaling in Human Endothelial Cells.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Peripheral artery disease (PAD) reduces tissue perfusion and causes ischemia, conditions in which hypoxia-responsive pathways have an important adaptive role. Hypoxia- inducible factor 1-alpha (HIF-1α), a central regulator of this response, is tightly controlled by prolyl hydroxylase domain protein 2 (PHD2), encoded by EGLN1. Here, we used an RNA-targeting CRISPR-Cas13d system to downregulate EGLN1 in human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs) under normoxia and hypoxia. METHODS: A PHD2-knockdown (PHD2-KD) HUVEC line was generated by lentiviral delivery of an EGLN1-targeting RNA guide, alongside non-transduced (CTRL) and non-targeting gRNA (NTG) control lines. Molecular and functional assays assessed hypoxia-related signaling, metabolic activity, migration, and sprouting responses under normoxia and hypoxia. RESULTS: Western blotting confirmed a marked reduction in PHD2 protein abundance in PHD2-KD cells relative to both CTRL and NTG cells. PHD2-KD HUVECs exhibited increased VEGFA transcript levels (6.5-fold under normoxia and 5.3-fold under hypoxia) and secreted VEGF concentrations (6.6-fold and 9.4-fold, respectively), together with early increases in HIF1A transcript and HIF-1α protein levels and lower TNF-α concentrations. Functional assays showed higher metabolic activity, faster wound closure (2.0-fold under normoxia and 2.2-fold under hypoxia), and enhanced sprouting, with up to 7.2-fold more sprouts per bead and sprouts up to 2.7-fold longer than those formed by CTRL. DISCUSSION: CRISPR-Cas13d-mediated EGLN1 targeting reduced PHD2 protein abundance and was associated with higher endothelial metabolic activity, faster wound closure, enhanced sprouting behavior, and lower TNF-α secretion. CONCLUSION: CRISPR-Cas13d-mediated downregulation of EGLN1/PHD2 was associated with increased pro-angiogenic signaling and improved angiogenesis-related endothelial responses in vitro, supporting RNA-targeting strategies to modulate hypoxia-responsive pathways.

title: Factors associated with failures and outcomes of Peripherally Inserted Central Catheters in hospitalized COVID-19 patients.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: to analyze factors associated with catheter progression failure and outcomes of Peripherally Inserted Central Catheters inserted by nurses in hospitalized COVID-19 patients. METHOD: observational cohort study was conducted with hospitalized COVID-19 patients, following the STROBE guidelines. Categorical variables were described as absolute and relative frequencies; quantitative variables were expressed as median and interquartile range. Non-parametric tests were applied due to non-normal distribution. Associations were analyzed using Pearson's chi-squared or Fisher's exact tests. Logistic regression was performed for variables associated with outcomes. RESULTS: a total of 1061 Peripherally Inserted Central Catheters were analyzed. The main indications were for antibiotic therapy, and most catheters were removed after treatment completion. First-attempt failure and clinical patient profile were associated with catheter progression failure. Subcutaneous heparin was a protective factor. Among Peripherally Inserted Central Catheters successfully inserted, tip confirmation via chest X-ray and catheter-to-vessel ratio between 31%-40% were associated with thrombosis, whereas Sherlock™ confirmation was protective. CONCLUSION: catheter progression failure was associated with clinical conditions and first-attempt failure. Adverse outcomes were associated with X-ray tip confirmation and catheter-to-vessel ratio, whereas Sherlock™ use and subcutaneous heparin were protective factors.

title: Evaluation of morphometric characteristics and positional variations of the carotid sinus using computed tomography angiography.
abstract: PURPOSE: The aim of this study was to determine the morphometric characteristics and spatial variations of the carotid sinus (CS) using computed tomography angiography (CTA) images. METHODS: In the study, cervical CTA images of a total of 100 individuals (200 sides) comprising 55 men and 45 women were examined. The diameters of the proximal and distal segments of the common carotid artery (CCA) and the internal carotid artery (ICA), as well as the proximal diameter of the external carotid artery (ECA), were measured. In addition, measurements of the maximum transverse diameter and length of the CS were taken; the resulting data were compared according to the variables of age, gender and side. RESULTS: All artery diameters, CS length (mean 8.78 ± 1.33 mm), and maximum CS diameter (mean 8.27 ± 1.10 mm) were found to be significantly higher in men than in women (p < 0.001). It was determined that the diameters of the CCA and ICA on the left side were statistically significantly wider than those on the right side (p < 0.001). It was found that CS localization was asymmetric in 29% of cases and most commonly occurred in the proximal ICA (Type I) in 74.5% of cases. In addition, a positive and statistically significant correlation (r = 0.554; p < 0.001) was found between age and CS length. CONCLUSION: Understanding the morphological variations of the CS is of critical importance in preventing unintended CS stimulation and related complications during surgical procedures in this region, particularly carotid endarterectomy.

title: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Endovascular and Open Surgical Repair for Infective Native Aortic Aneurysms.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Infective native aortic aneurysms (mycotic) are rare but highly lethal, and the optimal treatment strategy between endovascular repair and open surgical repair (OSR) remains debated because of a persistent trade-off between early survival and durable infection control. We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis comparing early and long-term outcomes of endovascular repair and OSR, complemented by a single-arm meta-analysis characterizing outcomes after endovascular repair. METHODS: PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception to June 16, 2026. Comparative studies were pooled using inverse-variance random-effects models with restricted maximum likelihood estimation of between-study variance (odds ratios [ORs]); single-arm proportions were pooled using logit-transformed, inverse-variance-weighted random-effects models. Risk of bias was assessed with Risk of Bias In Non-randomized Studies of Interventions-I. Outcomes included 30-day and 1-year all-cause mortality, reinfection (a new or persistent infection requiring antimicrobial therapy or source control), sepsis recurrence (a new episode meeting sepsis criteria after initial clinical resolution), reintervention, and acute kidney injury (AKI). RESULTS: Thirty-five retrospective studies were included: 18 comparative studies (2,853 enrolled patients; 1,305 endovascular repair and 1,548 OSR; 17 of which, comprising 2,836 patients, reported 30-day mortality) and 17 single-arm studies (444 endovascular repair patients; 16 of which reported 30-day mortality). Endovascular repair was associated with significantly lower 30-day mortality than OSR (OR 0.72, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.55-0.93) but not with 1-year mortality (eight studies, 1,630 patients; OR 1.23, 95% CI 0.66-2.29), and with a higher risk of reinfection (14 studies, 1,448 patients; OR 2.56, 95% CI 1.71-3.82). No significant differences were found for sepsis recurrence, reintervention, or AKI, though these comparisons were imprecise and compatible with both clinically meaningful benefit and harm, and should not be interpreted as evidence of equivalence between strategies. In the single-arm analysis, pooled 30-day mortality after endovascular repair was 6.5%, 1-year mortality was 22.4%, and reinfection was 14.7%. CONCLUSION: In pooled analysis, endovascular repair was associated with lower early mortality compared with open surgical repair, although this finding was sensitive to the inclusion of a single large registry-based study and should be interpreted with caution. No significant difference in 1-year mortality was observed, but this comparison was imprecise and based on few studies and should not be interpreted as evidence that a survival advantage is absent. Endovascular repair carries a higher risk of reinfection. Careful patient selection, prolonged antimicrobial therapy, and structured postoperative surveillance remain essential regardless of the repair strategy chosen. Certainty of evidence for all comparative outcomes was very low (GRADE), reflecting the observational design, serious risk of confounding by indication, and imprecision of the pooled estimates.
