title: Lesion Water Content on CT Predicts 12-Month Outcome and Modifies Thrombectomy Effect in Large-Core Stroke-A Secondary Analysis of the TENSION Trial.
abstract: In large-core ischemic stroke, outcomes after thrombectomy remain heterogeneous, and imaging markers that capture treatment-modifiable injury beyond lesion extent are needed. We investigated whether lesion water content on noncontrast CT, quantified as net water uptake (NWU), predicts 12-month functional outcome and modifies the effect of endovascular thrombectomy (EVT). This secondary analysis of the randomized TENSION trial included 198 patients with admission CT suitable for NWU quantification and available 12-month modified Rankin Scale (mRS) scores; 168 had paired 24-h CT for follow-up NWU (NWUFU) assessment. The primary outcome was ordinal 12-month mRS. Multivariable ordinal and logistic regression tested associations and the NWU × EVT interaction, with discrimination assessed by area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Median baseline NWU was 16.4% and NWUFU 28.9%. At 12 months, 45 patients (23%) had mRS 0-3 and 111 (56%) had died. Higher baseline NWU independently predicted worse 12-month mRS (adjusted common odds ratio [acOR], 1.10 per percentage-point; 95% CI, 1.05-1.16; P < 0.001) and modified the EVT effect (interaction acOR, 1.17; 95% CI, 1.06-1.30; P = 0.002), with greater discrimination than ASPECTS. NWUFU was the strongest single imaging predictor (acOR, 1.10; 95% CI, 1.06-1.14; P < 0.001; AUC, 0.78 for mRS 0-3) and superseded baseline NWU when co-modeled. Among 97 90-day survivors, higher NWUFU independently predicted late mortality (adjusted odds ratio, 1.09; 95% CI, 1.02-1.18; P = 0.019). Lesion water content may therefore provide a clinically accessible CT biomarker linking treatment-modifiable injury at baseline with realized post-treatment injury and long-term outcome.

title: Contact Aspiration Versus Combined Thrombectomy in Basilar Artery Occlusion: Clinical Severity and First-pass Recanalization Are Associated with Outcome.
abstract: PURPOSE: Acute basilar artery occlusion (BAO) carries high rates of death and disability despite endovascular therapy, and the optimal technique remains unclear. We compared contact aspiration (CA) alone with combined CA plus stent retriever (CA + SR) and identified factors associated with first-pass reperfusion and 3‑month outcome. METHODS: In the prospective multicenter SARA-3 registry, the primary outcomes compared between CA and CA + SR were first-pass recanalization (modified Treatment in Cerebral Infarction [mTICI] 2b-3) and 3‑month functional independence. Secondary outcomes were final recanalization, procedural time, safety, 24‑h NIHSS, and mortality. Factors associated with unfavorable outcome (modified Rankin Scale [mRS] 3-6) were assessed by Firth penalized logistic regression, with first-line technique forced in as a sensitivity analysis. RESULTS: Among 68 patients (median admission National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale [NIHSS] 11), 50 (73.5%) received CA and 18 (26.5%) CA + SR. The two techniques showed no statistically significant differences in reperfusion, safety, or 3‑month unfavorable outcome (48% vs. 53%; underpowered), but CA was faster (21 vs. 38 min; P = 0.007). Admission NIHSS (odds ratio [OR] 1.08 per point; P = 0.004) and first-pass mTICI 2b-3 (OR 0.06; P < 0.001) were independently associated with outcome; their combination discriminated well (area under the curve 0.83). Forcing technique into the model did not change these associations (CA + SR adjusted OR 1.19; P = 0.81). No baseline characteristic was independently associated with first-pass reperfusion. CONCLUSIONS: CA and CA + SR showed no statistically significant difference in 3‑month outcomes, but CA was faster. First-line technique was not associated with functional outcome; instead, outcome reflected baseline stroke severity and first-pass reperfusion, which defined prognostic groups that may aid risk stratification if externally validated.

title: AI-enhanced intraoperative decision-making in robotic surgery: from augmented reality navigation to foundation models.
abstract: Robotic surgical platforms have improved instrument dexterity, tremor filtration, and ergonomic control, yet intraoperative decisions still depend on a surgeon interpreting a moving, partially observed field under time pressure. Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used to close parts of this loop by recognizing anatomy, tracking instruments, anticipating events, and-experimentally-planning or executing selected actions. This review maps the computational technologies that support intraoperative decision-making in robotic surgery and appraises the clinical evidence for them.Because the direct robotic evidence base is still uneven, we explicitly distinguish three kinds of material: (i) studies conducted on robotic systems during surgery; (ii) non-robotic surgical evidence from laparoscopic and thoracoscopic procedures that use the same vision and workflow methods; and (iii) preclinical, preoperative, and perioperative work that is conceptually relevant but not intraoperative. Robotic and non-robotic settings are labeled throughout the tables and text. We further separate non-AI image guidance-indocyanine green (ICG) fluorescence and registered overlays-from AI-based inference, and we include image-guided endovascular robotics as a complementary setting in which fluoroscopic perception, vascular-topology reasoning, and closed-loop instrument control are particularly advanced.We organize the field into four computational layers: perception, anatomical and procedural reasoning, action planning, and control and execution. Augmented-reality and fluorescence navigation can improve orientation and selected intermediate outcomes, and several randomized trials now exist. Computer-vision systems can recognize anatomy, phases, instruments, and adverse events, and in endovascular work they can track guidewires and reason over vascular topology. Foundation models broaden language and multimodal capabilities but remain, in surgery, largely preclinical. Autonomous subtasks have shown promise in phantoms, animals, and a small number of carefully bounded tissue tasks; no system has demonstrated safe, accountable patient-level autonomous decision-making.Navigation and AI-assisted systems have improved orientation, reduced ischemia, and accelerated recognition of critical events in some studies. Whether these intermediate gains improve patient outcomes, generalize across institutions, or justify their cost remains unknown. The question is not whether AI can interpret surgical scenes, but which decisions can be delegated, with what evidence, uncertainty limits, oversight, and outcome measures.

title: Mechanical and Hemodynamic Effects of Balloon-Expandable and Self-Expanding Stents in a Saccular Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Model: Fluid-Structure Interaction Analyses.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to compare the effects of balloon-expandable and self-expanding stents on vessel wall mechanics and hemodynamics in a patient-specific saccular abdominal aortic aneurysm model. METHODS: A patient-specific aneurysm model was constructed using computed tomography images, and balloon-expandable and self-expanding stent models were created. Aortic wall stress was evaluated by contact analysis. Fluid-structure interaction analyses were performed at 5 representative phases selected from the cardiac cycle. Mean intra-aneurysmal flow velocity, wall shear stress (WSS), pressure loss, and energy loss were compared. RESULTS: The balloon-expandable stent produced greater localized aortic wall stress than the self-expanding stent, whereas wall stress was more uniformly distributed with the self-expanding stent. Both stents reduced the mean intra-aneurysmal flow velocity, WSS, pressure loss, and energy loss compared with the no-stent model. However, greater reductions in WSS, pressure loss, and energy loss were noted with the balloon-expandable stent than with the self-expanding stent. CONCLUSIONS: Balloon-expandable and self-expanding stents exhibited different effects on vessel wall mechanics and hemodynamics. The findings indicate the importance of evaluating both hemodynamic and mechanical effects when assessing stent-vessel interactions.

METHODS: A patient-specific aneurysm model was constructed using computed tomography images, and balloon-expandable and self-expanding stent models were created. Aortic wall stress was evaluated by contact analysis.

title: Ortner's syndrome associated with a saccular aortic arch aneurysm presenting as isolated unilateral vocal cord paralysis: a case report.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Ortner's syndrome, or cardiovocal syndrome, is an uncommon cause of recurrent laryngeal nerve palsy due to cardiovascular pathology. Thoracic aortic aneurysm is a rare but important etiology that may present only with hoarseness. CASE PRESENTATION: An 85-year-old man with hypertension and a history of chronic smoking presented with progressive hoarseness for 1 month. Flexible laryngoscopy showed paralysis of the left vocal cord without laryngeal pathology. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) revealed a 22 × 17 mm saccular aneurysm arising from the distal aortic arch at the aortopulmonary window, with mural thrombus and in close proximity to the left recurrent laryngeal nerve. No cervical, mediastinal, pulmonary, or laryngeal malignancy was detected. Echocardiography showed preserved systolic function without significant valvular disease or pulmonary hypertension. Ortner's syndrome associated with the distal aortic arch aneurysm was considered the most likely diagnosis based on the clinical and radiological findings and the exclusion of other identifiable causes. Surgical repair was advised, but the patient declined and was managed conservatively. At the 11-month clinical follow-up, he remained stable with persistent hoarseness; no follow-up CT was performed. CLINICAL DISCUSSION: Aortic arch aneurysm is a rare cause of Ortner's syndrome and may mimic more common causes of unilateral vocal cord paralysis, particularly malignancy. Imaging along the recurrent laryngeal nerve pathway, including the thorax, is essential when laryngoscopy does not reveal a local cause. CONCLUSION: Unexplained left vocal cord paralysis should prompt an evaluation for cardiovascular causes. Early cross-sectional imaging can identify a thoracic aortic aneurysm and guide timely multidisciplinary management.

title: A VPS4A Microtubule-Interacting and Trafficking Domain Variant in a Child With Hypomyelination and Developmental Regression: A Case Report With Features of CIMDAG Syndrome.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Hypomyelinating leukodystrophy in infancy has a broad differential diagnosis. Heterozygous variants in VPS4A, an endosomal sorting complexes required for transport-associated AAA-ATPase, have been reported in CIMDAG (cerebellar hypoplasia-cataracts-impaired intellectual development-congenital microcephaly- dystonia-dyserythropoietic anemia-growth retardation) syndrome, a multisystem neurodevelopmental disorder with variable systemic involvement. METHODS: A 14-month-old girl presented with inability to crawl or walk and delayed milestones. Examination showed a head circumference of 43.5 cm, a depressed nasal bridge, bilateral 4th-5th toe clinodactyly, motor delay, and hypotonia. Metabolic screening and targeted genetic tests were nondiagnostic. Brain magnetic resonance imaging showed diffuse deficient myelination, a thin corpus callosum, optic nerve hypoplasia, and basal ganglia signal abnormalities. At 2 years 7 months, the child re-presented with loss of independent sitting and speech, tremor, and epileptiform electroencephalography abnormalities. Follow-up magnetic resonance imaging showed persistent deficient myelination despite mild interval progression of myelination. Echocardiography showed moderate mitral regurgitation and a patent foramen ovale. RESULTS: Whole-exome sequencing identified a heterozygous VPS4A variant, NM_013245.3:c.217T>G (p.Tyr73Asp), reported as absent from population databases and previously unreported at the time of testing. Maternal testing was negative; paternal testing was unavailable. The laboratory classified the variant as a variant of uncertain significance. CONCLUSIONS: The clinical and imaging findings overlap with the VPS4A-associated CIMDAG spectrum. This case describes a candidate heterozygous microtubule-interacting and trafficking domain variant in a child with hypomyelination and regression; its contribution to the phenotype remains unconfirmed.

title: From hypoxia to thrombosis: a hypothesis-driven framework for pulmonary embolism risk in deep underground environments.
abstract: Pulmonary embolism (PE) is one of the most severe manifestations of venous thromboembolism, yet current diagnostic and preventive frameworks have largely been developed in ground-based clinical settings. Deep underground environments represent complex occupational exposure systems characterized by relative hypoxia or oxygen fluctuation, normobaric to mildly hyperbaric pressure, high humidity and heat, airborne particulates, radon accumulation, restricted ventilation, limited mobility, circadian disruption, and enclosed psychosocial stress. These factors may interact dynamically with oxygen sensing, cardiopulmonary compensation, venous return, endothelial function, and coagulation-inflammation pathways. However, the relationship between deep underground exposure, thrombogenesis, PE recognition, and prevention remains insufficiently conceptualized. Direct epidemiological evidence linking deep-underground occupational exposure to incident venous thromboembolism or PE remains scarce, and existing PE prediction tools have not been specifically validated in deep-underground occupational populations. Therefore, this review does not assume that underground exposure independently increases PE incidence or that established clinical tools are inadequate. Instead, we develop a hypothesis-driven framework to examine whether exposure-related factors-including oxygen fluctuation, heat and dehydration, restricted mobility, altered hemodynamics, and inflammatory stress-could modify thrombotic susceptibility, symptom interpretation, or the operational performance of conventional PE pathways. We summarize the environmental and physiological stressors relevant to PE, examine how they may amplify Virchow's triad, and discuss research questions concerning symptom recognition, anticoagulation, reperfusion decision-making, preventive interventions, and the staged development of dynamic risk warning models. This review aims to provide a conceptual foundation for future surveillance, prevention, and clinical research on PE in deep underground occupational populations.

title: Anticoagulation management in a pediatric patient with protein S deficiency and acute pulmonary embolism undergoing ECMO-supported intervention: a case report.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Protein S deficiency is a predominant form of hereditary thrombophilia in Asian populations. Pediatric venous thromboembolism (VTE) is exceedingly rare, with an incidence of only 0.2%-0.6%, and acute massive pulmonary embolism (PE) requiring extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) support in children with thrombophilia presents exceptional clinical challenges. The core therapeutic dilemma lies in reconciling the hypercoagulable state inherent to protein S deficiency with the high bleeding risk following thrombolytic therapy, compounded by the obligatory anticoagulation requirement during ECMO. This case report describes the nursing management of a pediatric patient with protein S deficiency and acute PE who successfully underwent ECMO-supported interventional treatment under high bleeding risk. OUTCOME: The patient was successfully weaned from ECMO after 98 h of support, extubated on day 6, and discharged in stable condition after 30 days of hospitalization. At 6-month follow-up, no thrombus recurrence was observed, and the patient had fully resumed normal life and academic activities. CONCLUSION: This case demonstrates that an individualized low-dose heparin anticoagulation strategy, guided by the PEACE consensus and supported by meticulous monitoring, can effectively balance the competing risks of thrombosis and hemorrhage in pediatric ECMO patients with underlying thrombophilia and recent thrombolysis. Notably, as a single case report, this finding cannot be broadly generalized to all pediatric ECMO patients with thrombophilia. Instead, this case provides a potential framework for individualized anticoagulation and nursing management that requires further validation in larger pediatric cohorts. The nursing experience provides a practical reference for managing similar complex cases in pediatric critical care.

title: Dietary aromatic amino acids, their food sources, and incident hypertension in Chinese adults: a prospective cohort study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Prospective evidence linking dietary aromatic amino acids (AAAs), including phenylalanine (Phe), tyrosine (Tyr), and tryptophan (Trp), to incident hypertension currently remains limited, particularly regarding their individual components and food sources. Herein, we examined the association between dietary AAAs, their food sources, and incident hypertension among Chinese adults. METHODS: Using the China Health and Nutrition Survey database, this prospective cohort study collected data from 10,087 adults without hypertension at baseline. Baseline dietary intake was assessed using three consecutive 24-h dietary recalls, combined with household food weighing; the energy-adjusted AAA intake was expressed in g/1,000 kcal. Incident hypertension was defined as measured blood pressure, physician diagnosis, or use of antihypertensive medication. Mixed-effects Cox proportional hazards models with household identifiers as random intercepts were used to estimate hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Dose-response, food-source-specific, subgroup, and sensitivity analyses were performed. RESULTS: During the 95,153 person-years of follow-up, 3,531 participants developed hypertension. In fully adjusted models, the highest quartile of total AAA intake was associated with a modestly higher risk of incident hypertension compared with the lowest quartile (HR, 1.16; 95% CI, 1.03-1.31; P for trend = 0.006). Positive associations were more consistent for Phe (HR for Q4 vs. Q1, 1.26; 95% CI, 1.11-1.44) and Trp (HR, 1.29; 95% CI, 1.14-1.46) individually, while Tyr intake showed no significant association with hypertension. Dose-response analyses indicated approximately linear positive associations for total AAA, Phe, and Trp. The association for total AAA was attenuated following additional adjustment for baseline province (HR for Q4 vs. Q1, 1.10; 95% CI, 0.97-1.24), while the positive associations for Phe and Trp persisted. Cereals were the predominant contributors to AAA intake, and plant-derived Phe and Trp were positively associated with the risk of hypertension. CONCLUSION: Higher dietary intakes of Phe and Trp showed consistent positive associations with incident hypertension, while Tyr showed no clear association. The modest association for total AAA was attenuated after adjusting for baseline province and should therefore be interpreted cautiously in relation to potential regional confounding factors. These findings support the component-specific interpretation of dietary AAAs and consideration of their regional and food source contexts.

title: Artificial intelligence for vascular minimally invasive surgery: techniques, clinical integration, and challenges.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Minimally invasive surgery (MIS), including endovascular and robot-assisted procedures, is widely used for vascular pathologies but remains limited by technical complexity, cognitive workload, and postoperative complications. Artificial Intelligence (AI) may help address these challenges through predictive analysis, decision support, image analysis, and automation. METHODS: A structured Google Scholar search was conducted from February 21, 2025, to January 1, 2026, and updated through September 2026. Peer-reviewed studies applying AI to vascular MIS were included, with additional targeted searches addressing clinical translation, deployment, regulation, and ethical considerations. RESULTS: Thirty primary studies were analyzed, including eight on machine learning, nine on deep learning, four on natural language processing, and nine on robotics or reinforcement learning. Machine learning supported risk stratification and outcome prediction, deep learning enabled imaging and segmentation applications, natural language processing facilitated clinical information extraction, and robotic systems supported navigation and procedural assistance. DISCUSSION: AI demonstrates substantial potential across the vascular MIS pathway, but broader clinical adoption requires stronger validation, prospective multicenter studies, standardized reporting, health-economic evaluation, and careful consideration of regulatory, liability, and accessibility challenges.

title: From revascularization to multimodal integrated therapy for peripheral arterial disease: immunomodulation, metabolic correction, and tissue engineering.
abstract: Peripheral arterial disease (PAD), a critical manifestation of systemic atherosclerosis (AS), poses substantial therapeutic challenges. Despite pharmacological interventions and revascularization, efficacy remains constrained by high restenosis rates and suboptimal functional recovery. These limitations underscore a necessary transition from localized structural revascularization toward integrated systemic repair, with a particular focus on the underlying immunopathology. The progression of PAD is driven by a dysregulated immune response, characterized by an imbalance in macrophage polarization (M1/M2), overactivation of the NLRP3 inflammasome, and a vicious cycle of immune-metabolic coupling. Current research trajectories emphasize the synergistic orchestration of the vascular microenvironment through immunomodulation. Beyond modulating localized inflammatory responses, emerging strategies target metabolic homeostasis and advanced tissue engineering, including spatiotemporal growth factor delivery, extracellular vesicle-based therapies, and bioengineered scaffolding systems. These interdisciplinary developments point toward a multimodal integrated therapeutic strategy for PAD. Such a strategy would build on conventional revascularization and may address its limitations, including restenosis, through targeted immunomodulation and local tissue regeneration. Whether this approach can improve long-term outcomes compared with revascularization alone remains to be tested. If validated, it could shift the clinical standard beyond vessel patency toward comprehensive, long-term vascular health.

title: Staphylococcus aureus -associated infected subclavian artery pseudoaneurysm treated with dual bare-metal stent implantation: a case report.
abstract: Staphylococcus aureus Infected subclavian artery aneurysms are exceedingly rare, life-threatening vascular lesions associated with high risks of rupture and mortality. We report a 70-year-old male presenting with intermittent hemoptysis, who was diagnosed with a pseudoaneurysm of the left subclavian artery adjacent to the dominant vertebral artery. Blood cultures confirmed methicillin-sensitiveinfection. The patient underwent endovascular repair with dual bare-metal stents to preserve vertebral artery perfusion. Hemoptysis completely resolved post-intervention. Complete thrombosis and occlusion of the aneurysm sac were achieved at the 3-month follow-up, with remarkable sac shrinkage observed at 6 months. This case suggests that dual bare-metal stents may represent a feasible potential treatment alternative for highly selected patients with infected subclavian artery aneurysms. Long-term safety and efficacy remain to be further verified. Long-term antimicrobial therapy and close surveillance remain mandatory.

title: Quality and reliability of short videos about type A aortic dissection on Bilibili and TikTok: a cross-sectional study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Type A aortic dissection (TAAD) is a life-threatening cardiovascular emergency. Short-video platforms such as TikTok and Bilibili have become important channels for health information dissemination, but the quality and reliability of TAAD-related videos remain unclear. OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate the quality and reliability of TAAD-related short videos on TikTok and Bilibili, with particular attention to platform differences and uploader characteristics. METHODS: The top 250 videos ranked by comprehensive ranking on each platform were screened using the Chinese keyword "A." A total of 391 eligible videos were included. Uploaders were classified as medical practitioners, individual users, or institutions. Video quality and reliability were assessed using the Global Quality Score (GQS), modified DISCERN (mDISCERN), JAMA benchmarks, and Video Information Quality Instrument (VIQI). Multivariable regression analyses were performed to identify factors independently associated with video quality. RESULTS: TikTok videos showed higher engagement, whereas Bilibili videos were longer and provided broader coverage of epidemiology, etiology, and clinical presentation-related content. TikTok remained independently associated with higher VIQI scores after adjustment. Medical practitioners and institutions generally achieved higher VIQI and JAMA scores than individual users, and content coverage score was independently associated with higher video quality. However, mDISCERN scores did not differ significantly among uploader types. CONCLUSION: TAAD-related short videos demonstrated moderate overall quality but limited reliability. Platform characteristics, uploader type, and content coverage were associated with assessed information quality. Professional participation may improve some aspects of health communication, but uploader identity alone does not ensure higher reliability or transparency.

title: Yeast Mitochondrial Escape 1-Like as a Mitochondrial Gatekeeper in Aging-Related Cardiovascular Disease.
abstract: Mitochondrial dysfunction is a hallmark of aging and is closely linked to the progression of cardiovascular disease. Yeast mitochondrial escape 1-like (YME1L) is an adenosine triphosphate (ATP)-dependent i-AAA (intermembrane space AAA, AAA=ATPase associated with diverse cellular activities) protease embedded in the mitochondrial inner membrane that maintains mitochondrial homeostasis by regulating proteostasis, cristae architecture, and metabolic adaptation. Notably, YME1L influences mitochondrial fusion-fission dynamics, respiratory chain supercomplex organization, and oxidative phosphorylation efficiency through the regulated processing of optic atrophy protein 1 (OPA1). Accumulating evidence suggests that age-associated impairment of YME1L function contributes to mitochondrial fragmentation, energetic insufficiency, and reduced stress tolerance, particularly in long-lived, high-energy demand tissues. In the cardiovascular system, experimental models indicate that YME1L deficiency disrupts cristae organization, promotes maladaptive metabolic remodeling, and promotes heart failure-like phenotypes. Conversely, preservation of YME1L activity supports mitochondrial integrity and enhances cardiac resilience under hemodynamic stress. In addition to cardiomyocytes, YME1L also supports endothelial mitochondrial homeostasis, thereby linking mitochondrial proteostasis to vascular aging and diastolic dysfunction. Although YME1L has been extensively studied in cancer biology, its relevance to aging-related cardiovascular vulnerability is increasingly recognized, especially in cardio-oncology, where therapy-induced mitochondrial stress may be exacerbated by age-dependent decline in mitochondrial quality control. This review integrates current evidence supporting YME1L as a context-dependent regulator of mitochondrial stress adaptation, with particular emphasis on the roles of YME1L in cardiovascular aging, heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF), and stress tolerance. Rather than positioning YME1L as a universal therapeutic target, we discuss how modulating YME1L-associated pathways may help preserve mitochondrial resilience and mitigate age-related cardiovascular dysfunction.

title: Trends, outcomes and patient- and hospital-level factors associated with sepsis following cesarean delivery: a propensity-matched nationwide inpatient analysis (2016-2022).
abstract: BACKGROUND: Sepsis is a major global health concern and a serious complication of cesarean delivery. However, contemporary nationwide data describing both the temporal trend in post-cesarean sepsis and its downstream clinical and economic burden-particularly in propensity-matched comparisons-remain limited. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective, propensity-matched analysis of all adult inpatients undergoing cesarean delivery recorded in the U.S. Nationwide Inpatient Sample (NIS, 2016-2022). Sepsis and cesarean delivery were defined using International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision, Clinical Modification (ICD-10-CM) codes. After 1:5 propensity-score matching on demographics, comorbidity burden and hospital characteristics, we compared in-hospital mortality, length of stay (LOS), total hospitalization costs, and the incidence of perioperative complications between septic and non-septic patients. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify patient- and hospital-level factors independently associated with sepsis. RESULTS: n P P P Of 1,619,187 hospitalizations for cesarean delivery, 1,589,186 adults met the inclusion criteria. Annual sepsis prevalence rose from 0.058% in 2016 to 0.136% in 2022. In the 1:5 propensity-matched cohort ( = 10,050), septic patients had markedly higher in-hospital mortality (2.4% vs. 0.0%, < 0.001), longer median LOS (6 vs. 3 days, < 0.001), and approximately 2.6-fold higher median total hospitalization costs (USD 71,466 vs. USD 27,063, < 0.001). Non-elective admission, treatment in teaching hospitals, a higher comorbidity burden, Asian/Pacific Islander race, and hospital region were independently associated with sepsis. After propensity matching, septic patients also showed substantially elevated adjusted odds of pulmonary embolism (OR 61.7), postoperative shock (OR 28.7), deep-vein thrombosis (OR 24.6), urinary tract infection (OR 25.5), and chronic respiratory diseases (OR 13.2). CONCLUSIONS: In this large U.S. study, sepsis after cesarean section was linked to much higher death rates, twice the hospital stay, about 2.6 times higher costs, and more severe problems like blood clots, shock, infections, and heavy bleeding. These results show that post-cesarean section sepsis is a growing concern, remind us to spot at-risk mothers early, and offer a benchmark against which prevention and cost-effective care can be evaluated.

title: Endothelial glycocalyx dysfunction in the setting of mechanical thrombectomy: a conceptual link between cardiometabolic vulnerability and microvascular reperfusion failure.
abstract: Mechanical thrombectomy (MT) has made macrovessel reopening achievable in acute ischemic stroke, but angiographic success does not ensure effective tissue-level reperfusion or microvascular oxygen delivery. This narrative review examines endothelial glycocalyx dysfunction as a plausible blood-facing interface that may connect pre-existing cardiometabolic vulnerability with post-thrombectomy microvascular dysfunction. Targeted English-language literature from PubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science, Embase, and Google Scholar through 30 April 2026 was synthesized, with emphasis on MT, impaired microvascular reperfusion (IMR), no-reflow, blood-brain barrier (BBB) and neurovascular-unit (NVU) biology, glycocalyx-related biomarkers, cardiometabolic risk, perfusion imaging, and microcirculatory rescue. The evidence base is heterogeneous and is explicitly separated into direct human MT/LVO evidence, indirect human biomarker or imaging evidence, experimental cerebral evidence, non-cerebral/cross-disease vascular evidence, and hypothesis-generating mechanistic inference. Ischemic priming, abrupt reperfusion, oxidative and inflammatory stress, complement activation, metabolic stress, distal embolization, device-endothelial trauma, and host vulnerability may converge on the luminal endothelial surface. Glycocalyx dysfunction may amplify leukocyte adhesion and capillary plugging, platelet adhesion and microthrombosis, impaired mechanosensing and nitric-oxide signaling, BBB destabilization, and heterogeneous capillary flow; however, direct causal proof in human MT is lacking. Circulating syndecan-1, heparan sulfate, and hyaluronan are therefore best interpreted as time- and compartment-dependent systemic signals rather than direct readouts of the cerebral glycocalyx. Post-EVT microcirculatory rescue trials show that downstream perfusion may remain therapeutically actionable, but they do not demonstrate glycocalyx repair as the operative mechanism. A practical translational strategy is to combine serial, compartment-annotated biomarkers with prespecified early perfusion/barrier imaging and tissue endpoints, while explicitly modeling cardiometabolic vulnerability and competing microvascular mechanisms. The glycocalyx framework should therefore be considered a testable network hypothesis rather than an established primary cause of post-thrombectomy no-reflow or futile recanalization.

title: Perforated marginal ulcer after Roux-en-Y gastric bypass: a national analysis of operative approaches, outcomes, and practice variations, 2018-2022.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Perforated marginal (gastrojejunal) ulcer is an uncommon but life-threatening complication after Roux-en-Y gastric bypass. Evidence is limited to single-center series and one 2022 systematic review of approximately 600 patients; contemporary national International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision (ICD-10)-era data are lacking. METHODS: We queried the National Inpatient Sample (2018-2022) for adults with a perforated gastrojejunal ulcer and a code indicating prior bariatric surgery. Operative approach was classified as laparoscopic patch, open patch, revisional gastrojejunostomy/reversal, or non-operative management. Survey-weighted statistics, negative-binomial (length of stay), gamma (total charges), and logistic (predictors of operative repair) models were estimated with hospital cluster-robust standard errors. RESULTS: The cohort included 1,669 unweighted admissions (8,345 weighted). Operative repair was performed in 28.9% (laparoscopic patch 12.6%, open patch 7.2%, revisional/reversal 9.2%); 71.1% were managed non-operatively. Crude in-hospital mortality was 1.1% overall. Non-operative management rose from 64.1% (2018) to 72.0% (2022), while laparoscopic patch declined from 18.1% to 12.1%. Open patch was associated with longer length of stay than laparoscopic patch [incidence-rate ratio 1.41, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.13-1.77] and higher complication rates after correction for multiple comparisons of sepsis, acute kidney injury, respiratory failure, and venous thromboembolism. Elective admission strongly predicted operative repair (adjusted odds ratio 2.58, 95% CI 1.74-3.83), elective admissions were concentrated in the revisional group, but the reason for elective admission could not be determined from administrative data. Operative rates declined modestly each year (adjusted odds ratio 0.91, 95% CI 0.84-0.98). Case mix differed between laparoscopic-first and open-first centers. CONCLUSIONS: In the largest contemporary national cohort to date, non-operative management dominated and increased during 2018-2022. Among operatively managed patients, laparoscopic patch repair was associated with shorter length of stay and a more favorable complication profile than open repair. Because operative approach was not randomized and patients selected for open repair may have carried greater physiologic severity or technical complexity, these associations support-but do not establish-a laparoscopic-first approach where anatomy and physiology permit. Prospective evidence is needed to refine operative vs. non-operative triage.

METHODS: We queried the National Inpatient Sample (2018-2022) for adults with a perforated gastrojejunal ulcer and a code indicating prior bariatric surgery.

title: Aortic Dissection Incidentally Detected on PET/CT During Evaluation for Suspected Multiple Myeloma.
abstract: The identification and diagnosis of aortic dissection on PET/CT remain challenging without the use of contrast agents. Such cases are prone to misdiagnosis or being overlooked, particularly when the examination is focused on an unrelated primary clinical objective. We present a case of thoracic aortic dissection that was incidentally detected on initial PET/CT during the further evaluation of suspected multiple myeloma. The FDG-avid lesion was initially mistaken for an esophageal mass, with differential diagnoses including extramedullary plasmacytoma associated with multiple myeloma and primary esophageal neoplasm.

title: Risk factors and clinical outcomes of reocclusion after endovascular treatment for acute ischemic stroke: an updated systematic review, meta-analysis and meta-regression.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Early reocclusion after endovascular treatment (EVT) for acute ischemic stroke is underrecognized; its determinants and impact remain poorly defined. METHODS: Random-effects meta-analysis of early reocclusion after successful EVT (PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library through January 2026). Crude odds ratios (ORs) were pooled and certainty rated with GRADE. Post hoc sensitivity analyses included only same-site reocclusion definitions. RESULTS: Ten studies (3,381 patients) were included; 244 (7.2%) reoccluded. Reocclusion was associated with lower 90-day functional independence (OR 0.25, 95% CI 0.17-0.38) and higher mortality (OR 1.86, 1.29-2.68), both moderate certainty. Reocclusion was more frequent with large-artery atherosclerosis (OR 2.24, 1.41-3.55; same-site 3.04, 1.73-5.33) and less frequent with cardioembolism (OR 0.40, 0.28-0.57) and atrial fibrillation (OR 0.39, 0.26-0.59), mutually confounded associations reflecting one embolic-versus-atherothrombotic axis. Prestroke antiplatelet therapy (OR 0.43, 0.28-0.67) lost significance under the same-site definition (0.60, 0.31-1.16). Exploratory data (two cohorts) linked eTICI 2c-3 reperfusion with less reocclusion (OR 0.44, 0.28-0.69). No study reported when etiology was adjudicated; the atherosclerosis association may be partly outcome-induced. CONCLUSIONS: Early reocclusion is uncommon but carries a substantial prognostic penalty. Its determinants appear to lie in the vascular substrate rather than thrombectomy technique; prospective studies with uniform same-site definitions and systematic follow-up imaging are needed.

METHODS: Random-effects meta-analysis of early reocclusion after successful EVT (PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library through January 2026). Crude odds ratios (ORs) were pooled and certainty rated with GRADE.

title: Analysis of risk factors for venous thromboembolism in hospitalized patients with acute herpetic neuralgia and construction of a predictive nomogram model.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: To explore the risk factors for venous thromboembolism (VTE) in hospitalized patients with acute herpetic neuralgia (AHN) and to construct a VTE prediction model based on clinical indicators to help clinicians better identify high-risk patients and develop prevention and treatment strategies. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This study retrospectively included 327 patients diagnosed with AHN who were hospitalized in the Pain Department of Hengshui People's Hospital between December 2020 and December 2023, of whom 26 developed VTE during hospitalization. The basic clinical data of the patients were collected, and the independent risk factors for VTE were screened by LASSO regression and multifactorial Logistic regression analysis, and the VTE prediction model was constructed. Model performance was evaluated by ROC curves, calibration curves, and decision curves, and internal validation was performed using ten-fold cross-validation and bootstrap resampling. RESULTS: P P P P The incidence of VTE in AHN patients was 7.95%. LASSO regression screened for 10 relevant variables, and final multifactor logistic regression analysis identified FIB (fibrinogen), FDP (fibrin degradation products), NRS (Numerical Rating Scale) score, and thrombotic risk score as independent predictors. Among them, FIB was a protective factor for VTE (OR = 0.477,= 0.006), while FDP (OR = 1.48,< 0.001), NRS score (OR = 1.584,= 0.039), and thrombotic risk score (OR = 2.05,< 0.001) were risk factors. The AUC of the prediction model was 0.853 (95% CI: 0.764-0.941), and the bootstrap optimism-corrected C-index was 0.834. At the optimal cutoff, the sensitivity and specificity were 0.731 and 0.877, respectively, with good calibration and clinical applicability. CONCLUSIONS: In this study, a VTE prediction model was constructed for patients with AHN. The model can accurately predict the risk of VTE in patients with AHN and provide a reference for clinical prevention and intervention; however, external validation in larger, multicenter cohorts is warranted before clinical implementation.

title: Artificial intelligence-driven imaging-based prediction models for hemorrhagic transformation after mechanical thrombectomy in acute ischemic stroke: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Hemorrhagic transformation (HT) is a major complication after mechanical thrombectomy (MT) in acute ischemic stroke (AIS). Although artificial intelligence (AI)-driven imaging-based prediction models have shown promise for predicting HT, their overall predictive performance remains uncertain. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated their predictive performance. METHODS: PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, CNKI, Wanfang, VIP, and CBM/SinoMed were searched from inception to July 2, 2026. Studies developing or validating AI-driven imaging-based prediction models for predicting HT after MT in AIS, including both pre- and post-procedural imaging predictors, were included. A random-effects model was used to pool the area under the curve (AUC), while a bivariate random-effects model was used to jointly estimate pooled sensitivity and specificity and construct the SROC curve. Subgroup analyses explored potential sources of heterogeneity. RESULTS: N I p 2 Eleven studies (total = 3,541) were included, 10 studies contributed eligible AUC estimates, with evaluation cohorts ranging from 18 to 261 participants. The pooled AUC was 0.891 (95% CI: 0.853-0.928), with low between-study heterogeneity ( = 29.0%, = 0.238). The bivariate random-effects model yielded a pooled sensitivity of 0.666 (95% CI: 0.578-0.744) and a pooled specificity of 0.919 (95% CI: 0.842-0.960). Exploratory subgroup analyses did not provide robust evidence supporting the superiority of any specific subgroup, and their interpretation was limited by small subgroup sizes and methodological heterogeneity. However, these findings should be interpreted cautiously because of the limited number of studies within individual subgroups. CONCLUSION: AI-driven imaging-based prediction models showed generally favorable discrimination in predicting HT after MT in AIS. However, current evidence does not establish the superiority of any specific model type. The predominance of retrospective studies, limited external validation, and methodological heterogeneity limit the generalizability of current findings. Large, multicenter prospective studies with rigorous external validation are needed before clinical implementation. SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: The systematic review was registered with PROSPERO (CRD420261441463).

Although artificial intelligence (AI)-driven imaging-based prediction models have shown promise for predicting HT, their overall predictive performance remains uncertain. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated their predictive performance.

title: Hierarchies of vascular risk: gendered perceptions of arterial and venous disease.
abstract: This study explores how patients interpret vascular risk through the intersecting lenses of disease type and gender. Drawing on qualitative interviews with 28 patients in Italy diagnosed with peripheral arterial disease (PAD) or chronic venous disease (CVD), the analysis examines how individuals construct meanings around symptoms, risk, and care. Findings reveal a hierarchy of vascular risk in which arterial disease is perceived as life-threatening and generates vigilance, anxiety, and intensive self-monitoring, whereas venous disease is often normalized and trivialized within everyday life. Gender further shapes these perceptions: men tend to minimize symptoms and delay care, while women demonstrate greater bodily attentiveness and concern. Theoretically, the study advances the concept of a socially constructed hierarchy of vascular risk, showing how culturally differentiated meanings of disease severity intersect with gendered embodiment to shape risk perception, symptom interpretation, and healthcare engagement. By integrating sociological theories of risk, biographical disruption, and gendered embodiment within the study of vascular disease, the analysis extends risk scholarship to an underexplored clinical domain and demonstrates how biomedical risk is translated into socially differentiated lived experience.

title: Study protocol of a prospective, non-interventional cohort study evaluating the benefits of transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt in patients with hepatocellular carcinoma receiving first-line atezolizumab plus bevacizumab (NISTIPS TRITICC-4, IKF092).
abstract: BACKGROUND: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is a leading cause of cancer-related mortality, with most patients diagnosed at an advanced stage. Atezolizumab plus bevacizumab is a current standard first-line therapy; however, outcomes are strongly influenced by underlying cirrhosis and clinically significant portal hypertension (CSPH). Complications such as ascites and variceal bleeding may limit treatment continuation, particularly as bevacizumab increases bleeding risk. Transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPS) reduces portal pressure and may improve outcomes, but its role in patients receiving immunoncology-based systemic therapy remains unclear. METHODS: NISTIPS TRITICC-4 is a prospective, multicentre, non-interventional cohort study conducted at up to 25 centers in Germany. A total of 350 adult patients with cirrhosis and unresectable or metastatic HCC receiving first-line atezolizumab plus bevacizumab will be enrolled. Patients are allocated to two cohorts: TIPS in situ plus atezolizumab and bevacizumab or atezolizumab plus bevacizumab alone, according to routine clinical practice.The primary endpoint is time to deterioration of liver function (TTDL), defined as persistent worsening of liver parameters for >4 weeks. Secondary endpoints include overall survival, time on treatment, overall response rate, time to new extrahepatic lesions or death, and safety with focus on bleeding and TIPS-related complications.Time-to-event endpoints will be analyzed using Kaplan-Meier methods and Cox models. Propensity score matching will be applied to adjust for confounding. Analyses are exploratory. DISCUSSION: This study will provide real-world evidence on the impact of TIPS in HCC patients receiving atezolizumab plus bevacizumab and may support more individualized management strategies in this high-risk population. CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: www.clinicaltrials.gov identifier is NCT07365930.

title: Total hip arthroplasty in the presence of peri-articular pellets due to an old shotgun injury: case report and literature review.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Gunshot injuries to the hip can result in devastating outcomes, leading to post-traumatic arthritis and presenting a significant surgical challenge during total hip arthroplasty (THA) due to metallic fragments and damaged soft-tissue structures. However, there is a lack of studies in the literature specifically addressing gunshot or shotgun injuries to the hip joint. CASE PRESENTATION: A 29-year-old woman, 13 years after a shotgun injury, presented with severe pain, a limp, and a 5 cm limb-length discrepancy. Imaging revealed chronic dislocation and avascular necrosis, with multiple pellets around the hip. The infection workup (white blood cell count, C-reactive protein, erythrocyte sedimentation rate) was normal. She underwent lateral THA via the Hardinge approach, including trochanteric osteotomy, femoral shortening, and wire fixation. Early mobilization, 24 hours of antibiotics, and 14 days of deep vein thrombosis (DVT) prophylaxis were initiated. DISCUSSION: Complete extraction of all pellets was not feasible; infection was excluded pre-operatively. At 18-month follow-up, there were no infections, dislocations, or DVTs; limb-length discrepancy was less than 1 cm, and gait was pain-free, supporting the safety of single-stage THA when soft-tissue conditions are optimized and infection has been ruled out. CONCLUSION: When retained peri-articular shotgun pellets are present, carefully planned single-stage THA can restore function with a low risk of complications, provided infection is ruled out and limb length is corrected with femoral-shortening osteotomy.

title: Inflammatory bowel disease and the heart: how trained immunity shapes cardiovascular outcomes.
abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), comprising Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis, is a chronic relapsing intestinal inflammatory disorder. Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is a leading cause of death in patients with IBD, with elevated risks of myocardial infarction, heart failure, stroke, and venous thromboembolism that are independent of traditional risk factors. Disease activity and histological inflammation independently predict major adverse cardiovascular events, and Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis differ in cardiovascular risk profiles. This residual risk points to immune mechanisms that remain unclear. Trained immunity (TI), an innate immune memory induced by epigenetic and metabolic reprogramming, may link chronic intestinal inflammation to cardiovascular injury. This review integrates epidemiological and mechanistic evidence, outlines cardiovascular risk features in IBD, examines the molecular basis of TI and its roles in atherosclerosis, myocardial injury, and heart failure, and evaluates candidate biomarkers and targeted therapeutic strategies. We also discuss current limitations and challenges in clinical translation and propose future research directions, to inform mechanistic studies and clinical interventions for IBD-associated CVD.

title: Novel techniques in the prophylaxis and treatment of type II endoleaks: a narrative review.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Type II endoleaks (T2ELs) are a frequent complication after endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR), posing a risk of aneurysm expansion. This review evaluates modern techniques for T2ELs management, moving beyond traditional embolization methods. METHODS: Recent controlled trials and observational studies were analyzed to trace evidence on conventional and novel techniques employed in managing T2ELs. RESULTS: Novel techniques, such as transcaval embolization (TCE) and laser-assisted transgraft embolization (LATE), have demonstrated encouraging early technical and clinical outcomes, although the available evidence remains limited. In addition, shape memory polymer (SMP) embolization resulted in significant sac shrinkage in >85% of patients and prevented clinically significant T2ELs. CONCLUSIONS: TCE, LATE, and prophylactic SMP embolization are promising alternatives to conventional methods, offering high technical success and the potential to reduce reinterventions. Larger studies are needed to confirm long-term outcomes and define optimal use.

title: Tissue-specific moderate DNA methylation alterations featuring hypomethylation in microRNA regulatory regions associated with advanced carotid atherosclerosis.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: DNA methylation is an important epigenetic mechanism involved in the regulation of gene expression, but its contribution to the regulation of microRNA genes in atherosclerosis remains poorly understood. METHODS: MIR10B, MIR21, MIR100, MIR127, and MIR143 We profiled DNA methylation of regulatory elements and gene bodies of five microRNA genes () in vascular tissues and paired peripheral blood leukocytes from 92 patients with advanced carotid atherosclerosis along with peripheral blood leukocytes of 32 subclinical atherosclerosis controls, using targeted bisulfite sequencing. RESULTS: MIR10B, MIR127 MIR100 MIR100 MIR127 MIR100 MIR10B, MIR21 MIR127 MIR10B, MIR21 MIR100 MIR10B MIR143 MIR21 MIR10B MIR143HG CARMN We identified distinct tissue-specific DNA methylation patterns for all studied regions of microRNA genes. The regulatory regions of, andwere moderately hypomethylated in carotid atherosclerotic plaques compared with intact vascular tissues. We further integrated our findings with lab-internal and publicly available epigenome-wide methylation datasets and evaluated the contribution of vascular and blood cell composition using computational deconvolution. After adjustment for estimated vascular cell proportions, methylation at CpG sites within theandregions remained associated with atherosclerosis. Increased DNA methylation at a single CpG site (chr11:122025143, GRCh37/hg19) located in theE-box region was associated with metabolic syndrome, while DNA methylation levels of, andin atherosclerotic plaques were linked with indicators of histological instability and a history of acute cerebrovascular events. In peripheral blood cells, we observed moderate hypomethylation, predominantly at individual CpG sites within the regulatory regions of, and theE-box region in patients compared with controls. However, MIR10B methylation showed weak associations with estimated blood cell composition. In blood,andmethylation correlated with lipid metabolism and carotid stenosis, while theCpG island showed strong correspondence between blood and plaque methylation. Using miRNA-seq to analyze microRNA expression in vascular samples, we identified miR-143-3p, miR-21-5p, miR-100-5p, miR-145-5p, miR-145-3p, and miR-10b-5p as the most highly expressed microRNAs. Methylation of CpG sites withinand() promoters was inversely associated with the expression of the corresponding microRNAs. DISCUSSION: Advanced carotid atherosclerosis is characterized by specific moderate tissue-associated DNA methylation patterns of microRNA genes, predominantly involving hypomethylation of regulatory regions. These epigenetic shifts, driven both by changes in vascular cell composition and the functional state of the vessel wall, enable highly coordinated regulation of microRNA expression profiles. These findings highlight promising candidate loci and biomarkers for predicting the complicated course of atherosclerosis, which warrants further validation in larger independent cohorts.

title: De-escalated rivaroxaban in postoperative isolated distal deep vein thrombosis: a propensity score-matched study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: In postoperative isolated distal deep vein thrombosis (IDDVT), anticoagulation intensity is frequently constrained by bleeding risk, which may compromise treatment continuity and clinical effectiveness. OBJECTIVES: To compare the effectiveness and safety of a de-escalated (rivaroxaban 10 mg once daily) versus standard-maintenance rivaroxaban regimen for postoperative IDDVT in a real-world surgical cohort. METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included patients diagnosed with IDDVT following urological surgery between 2013 and 2025. Patients received rivaroxaban at either a low maintenance dose (10 mg once daily) or a standard maintenance dose (20 mg once daily) according to routine clinical practice. Propensity score matching (1:1) was applied to balance baseline characteristics, incorporating surgical approach (endoscopic vs. major structural procedures) as a surrogate for surgical trauma and bleeding risk. The primary outcome was thrombus progression to proximal deep vein thrombosis or pulmonary embolism. Secondary outcomes included IDDVT resolution and clinically relevant non-major bleeding (CRNMB). Competing-risk analyses were performed. RESULTS: P P P After matching, 152 patients were included (76 per group). Thrombus progression did not differ significantly between groups (subdistribution hazard ratio [SHR] 1.29; 95% CI 0.48-3.46; = 0.613). No statistically significant difference in IDDVT resolution was detected between the two groups (SHR 0.93; 95% CI, 0.64-1.36; = 0.721). The low-dose regimen was associated with a significantly lower risk of CRNMB (HR 0.31; 95% CI, 0.11-0.85; = 0.023) and fewer early bleeding-related treatment interruptions. Early postoperative hematuria was more frequent in the standard-dose group. CONCLUSIONS: In this single-center retrospective cohort of patients with isolated distal deep vein thrombosis after urological surgery, low-dose rivaroxaban (10 mg once daily) was associated with a lower incidence of clinically relevant non-major bleeding than 20 mg once daily. No statistically significant differences were detected between regimens in thrombus progression or complete thrombus resolution. However, these findings should not be interpreted as evidence of equivalent antithrombotic efficacy, given nonrandomized treatment allocation, residual confounding, limited sample size, and wide confidence intervals for thrombotic outcomes. The results are hypothesis-generating and support studies-preferably randomized non-inferiority trials-to determine whether dose de-escalation can provide an acceptable balance between thrombotic protection and bleeding risk in postoperative patients.

OBJECTIVES: To compare the effectiveness and safety of a de-escalated (rivaroxaban 10 mg once daily) versus standard-maintenance rivaroxaban regimen for postoperative IDDVT in a real-world surgical cohort. METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included patients diagnosed with IDDVT following urological surgery between 2013 and 2025.

title: Perioperative prothrombin time activity trajectories and subsequent mortality after surgical repair of acute type A aortic dissection.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Perioperative prothrombin time activity (PTA) changes rapidly during surgical repair of acute type A aortic dissection (ATAAD), but single measurements do not capture heterogeneous longitudinal patterns. We sought to identify recurring perioperative PTA trajectories, characterize their clinical context, and examine their association with subsequent all-cause mortality. METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort included 284 adults who underwent ATAAD repair from 2021 through 2023. Group-based trajectory modeling used the last preoperative and observed postoperative day (POD) 1-7 PTA measurements. Patients required at least three observed PTA measurements for trajectory modeling. Mortality analyses began immediately after POD7. The primary Cox model adjusted for age and sex; Firth regression addressed sparse events. Incremental information beyond last preoperative PTA was evaluated by a prespecified likelihood-ratio comparison. RESULTS: P P P P P The trajectory cohort comprised 268 patients with 1,895 observations and 27 deaths after POD7. Four perioperative PTA trajectory groups were identified: moderate-stable [87 (32.5%)], low-declining [50 (18.7%)], preserved-rapidly-declining [61 (22.8%)], and high-preserved [70 (26.1%)]. Cumulative mortality differed globally (log-rank = 0.00210), and trajectory group remained associated with subsequent mortality in the age- and sex-adjusted Cox model (global = 0.0322) and Firth sensitivity analysis (global = 0.0481). The prespecified direct low-declining-versus-preserved-rapidly-declining comparison did not demonstrate a clear difference. Adding trajectory group to age, sex, and last preoperative PTA did not show clear incremental information (likelihood-ratio = 0.304; Firth = 0.380). After exclusion of mechanical-valve recipients, the principal trajectory structure was largely preserved, although this sensitivity analysis did not exclude treatment-related effects on PTA. CONCLUSION: Four reproducible perioperative PTA trajectories characterized distinct longitudinal patterns and were associated with mortality after the POD7 landmark. These trajectories should be interpreted as composite perioperative patterns reflecting both disease and treatment context rather than as intrinsic coagulation states. They were not ordered mortality-risk tiers and did not show clear incremental prognostic information beyond last preoperative PTA. External validation is required.

We sought to identify recurring perioperative PTA trajectories, characterize their clinical context, and examine their association with subsequent all-cause mortality. METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort included 284 adults who underwent ATAAD repair from 2021 through 2023.

title: Comparison of ultrasound-guided oblique-axis versus short-axis approaches for right internal jugular vein cannulation in the left decubitus position: a prospective, randomized, single-center trial.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Central venous cannulation in the left decubitus position is more difficult than in the supine position and may be required when patients cannot safely return to supine. Whether the oblique-axis (OA) approach improves the success and safety of right internal jugular vein (RIJV) cannulation compared with the short-axis (SA) approach remains unknown. METHODS: Seventy-four patients (ASA I-III) scheduled for elective surgery in the left decubitus position under general anesthesia requiring RIJV cannulation were randomly assigned 1:1 to the OA or SA group (n = 37 each). Under real-time ultrasound guidance and a 20° Trendelenburg tilt, cannulation was performed by one of three experienced attending anesthesiologists, each with more than 15 years of experience in ultrasound-guided central venous cannulation. Venipuncture attempts and total procedure time were recorded by a separate investigator; patients were blinded by general anesthesia. The primary outcome was first-time puncture success; secondary outcomes were overall cannulation success, procedure time, venipuncture attempts, and mechanical complications. RESULTS: All 74 randomized patients completed the trial and were analyzed. The first-time puncture success rate was higher in the OA group (27/37 [73.0%] vs. 18/37 [48.6%]; risk difference 24.3%, 95% CI 2.8% to 45.9%; P = 0.032, Pearson chi-square test; Fisher exact test P = 0.056). Venipuncture attempts were fewer in the OA group (median 1 vs. 2; IQR 1-2; P = 0.037). Total procedure time did not differ significantly between groups (median 2.79 [IQR 2.46-3.19] vs. 3.01 [2.72-3.45] min; P = 0.060). Mechanical complications occurred in 6 of 37 patients (16.2%) in the SA group (one arterial puncture and five posterior wall penetrations) and in none in the OA group (P = 0.025); overall cannulation success was 100% in both groups. CONCLUSIONS: For RIJV cannulation in the left decubitus position, the oblique-axis approach was associated with a higher first-time puncture success rate than the short-axis approach and with fewer mechanical complications detected during or immediately after the procedure; however, the primary-endpoint evidence was borderline and the complication estimates were imprecise. TRIAL REGISTRATION: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR2400091385; registered 28 October 2024).

title: Noninvasive hemodynamics of nonthrombotic iliac vein lesions are disturbed in patients with a history of deep vein thrombosis.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Nonthrombotic iliac vein lesions (NIVLs) are thought to be associated with deep vein thrombosis (DVT), yet most individuals with NIVL never develop thrombotic complications. This study assessed whether ultrasound-derived hemodynamic measurements differ between NIVL patients with and without a history of DVT, and whether these hemodynamic measurements better discriminate DVT history than percent stenosis alone. METHODS: We performed a retrospective case control study of patients evaluated at a tertiary academic referral center between 2022 and 2025 who underwent pelvic venous duplex ultrasound imaging. Patients with left common iliac vein (LCIV) stenoses greater than 20% were included and categorized by history of left lower-extremity DVT. Exclusion criteria included concurrent DVT or previous venous stenting. Ultrasound images were digitized to obtain vessel diameters and spectral Doppler velocities in the iliac veins. Mean velocity, peak velocity, flow rate, shear rate, and ipsilateral and contralateral ratios were calculated. Continuous variables were compared using Welch t-tests, with statistical significance defined as P < .05. RESULTS: 2 2 2 2 Forty-five patients were included, comprising nine patients with previous DVT and 36 without. Among all metrics, velocity-based metrics at the compressed LCIV showed the strongest associations with a history of previous DVT, including ipsilateral velocity ratio [logfold change (FC), -1.539; P = .007], peak velocity (logFC, -0.999; P = .002), and mean velocity (logFC, -0.989; P = .002). Differences in percent stenosis were statistically significant but less discriminative than velocity-based metrics (logFC, 0.363; P = .033). Composite metrics such as flow rate and shear rate demonstrated weaker discrimination. Dimensionality reduction analysis revealed distinct clustering based on multivariate hemodynamic features between patients with and without a history of DVT. CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with NIVL, decreased velocity through the LCIV at the compression point was the strongest predictor of previous DVT, whereas percent stenosis was less discriminative. This study suggests that ultrasound-derived hemodynamic assessment can potentially provide a functional framework for risk stratification in patients with NIVL, but further prospective studies are needed to validate its clinical utility.

title: A pilot study of the InVera Infusion Device: Twelve-month outcomes in the treatment of incompetent saphenous veins.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: The InVera Infusion Device (IVID; InVera Medical) is a novel catheter designed for the delivery of sclerosant agents during nonthermal, nontumescent ablation of incompetent superficial truncal veins of the lower extremity. This device pilot study aimed to evaluate the technical success, safety, and 12-month clinical outcome. METHODS: A single-center, prospective pilot study enrolled 10 patients with primary symptomatic axial reflux who underwent chemical ablation procedures with sclerosant delivery using the IVID. Primary outcomes assessed were technical procedural success, adverse events, revised Venous Clinical Severity Score (rVCSS), patient-reported outcomes based on a Heaviness, Achiness, Swelling, Throbbing, and Itching (HASTI) symptom questionnaire, and anatomical success rates from duplex ultrasound examination at baseline, 1 and 8 weeks, 3, 6, and 12 months postprocedure. Baseline and 12-month postprocedures were compared for both the rVCSS and the HASTI results using a paired t-test and a Wilcoxon signed-rank test respectively. RESULTS: Technical procedural success was 100%. There were no device-related adverse events or serious adverse events including no deep vein thrombosis recorded throughout the follow-up period. Clinician assessed rVCSS and patient reported HASTI scores both showed statistically significant reductions from baseline to 12 months (adjusted P = .03 for both). Ultrasound-based anatomical assessment at 12 months demonstrated elimination of abnormal reflux and complete or partial occlusion in 90% of patients. CONCLUSIONS: The IVID provides a safe and effective technique for the delivery of sclerosant agents as part of the management of incompetent saphenous veins, demonstrating favorable 12-month anatomical, clinical and patient-reported outcomes in this pilot cohort.

title: Systematic review of devices, designs, and trials for the treatment of deep venous reflux.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Chronic venous insufficiency is driven primarily by venous reflux and affects nearly one-third of adults. Although superficial reflux is effectively treated with ablation, therapeutic options for deep venous reflux (DVR) remain limited. Despite decades of innovation, no prosthetic or bioprosthetic venous valve has achieved U.S. regulatory approval. We systematically reviewed device strategies, clinical and hemodynamic outcomes, complications, and barriers to translation for devices designed to treat DVR. METHODS: We conducted an International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (CRD420251101761) of six databases from inception through February 2026, including in vivo animal and human studies evaluating prosthetic or bioprosthetic devices for DVR. Studies of native valve repair or autotransplantation were excluded. The primary outcome for human studies was clinical improvement, and secondary outcomes included patency, procedural complications, valvular function, and thrombosis. RESULTS: Of 516 records identified, 15 met inclusion criteria: eight human and seven animal studies. Two principal strategies were identified: intraluminal valve restoration and external compression, with approximately 40% of devices delivered percutaneously or endovenously. In human studies, technical success ranged from 87.7% to 100%, patency from 67% to 100%, and perioperative complication rates from 0% to 44%, consisting primarily of bleeding, wound infection, and valve thrombosis. Valve occlusion occurred in up to 28% of animal implants and 18% to 22% of select human cohorts. Two perioperative deaths occurred in animal studies; none were reported in human studies. Among human studies, valve competency assessment methods varied substantially. Reported competency ranged from 0% to 92%, reflecting heterogeneity in imaging modalities and definitions. Discordance between anatomic patency, duplex-derived reflux reduction, and clinical improvement was frequently observed. In contemporary multicenter trial data, fewer than half of patients met predefined reflux-reduction end points despite high device patency and substantial clinical improvement, highlighting discordance between anatomic, hemodynamic, and patient-centered outcomes. By 1 year, pain had improved in 75% to 97% of patients; revised Venous Clinical Severity Scores decreased by 37% to 81%, with clinically meaningful (≥3-point) improvement in up to 84.6%; and ulcer healing ranged from 67% to 100%. Longer follow-up extended to 2 years in animal studies and up to 11 years in human series with various outcomes reported. CONCLUSIONS: Several devices developed for DVR have demonstrated technical feasibility and symptom improvement. However, the risk of thrombosis, the marginal impact on valvular function, and the lack of standardization and selection of adequate end points in the measurement of results remain major barriers to regulatory approval. Standardized composite end points integrating objective hemodynamic measures with patient-centered outcomes are essential to advance durable DVR device development and clinical translation.

title: Magnetic resonance imaging vs computed tomography for baseline imaging evaluation in acute basilar artery occlusion.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The optimal imaging modality, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) or computed tomography (CT), for identifying good treatment candidates among patients with acute basilar-artery occlusion (BAO) remains unclear. METHODS: This was a post hoc analysis of the ATTENTION trial. Patients were categorized into MRI or CT groups according to the baseline imaging modality. The primary outcome was mRS 0-3 at 90 days. The secondary outcomes included mRS score shift on an ordinal scale, early neurological deterioration, time from stroke onset to arterial puncture, and time from onset to randomization. The safety outcome was mortality within 90 days. Clinical outcomes and workflow times were compared between the two groups. RESULTS: Among 340 patients (CT: n = 277; MRI: n = 63), baseline imaging was not significantly associated with 90-day mRS 0-3 in the overall cohort (OR 0.99, 95% CI 0.50-1.95; P = 0.976). It remained highly consistent across both the endovascular treatment and best medical management subgroups. Baseline MRI assessment was not associated with significant workflow delays compared with CT, including time from stroke onset to randomization (mean difference [MD] 5.23 min; P = 0.843) and time to puncture (MD 13.16 min; P = 0.701). Furthermore, the association between imaging modality and outcomes was consistent across different time windows. DISCUSSION: In patients with acute BAO, we did not observe evidence supporting the preferential use of MRI over CT as the primary imaging strategy for patient selection. Conventional imaging appears sufficient as a first-line tool for selecting patients in clinical practice.

METHODS: This was a post hoc analysis of the ATTENTION trial. Patients were categorized into MRI or CT groups according to the baseline imaging modality.

title: Shotgun metagenomic and untargeted metabolomic analysis of gut microbiome associated with peripheral artery disease.
abstract: BACKGROUND: While the human gut microbiome is a potentially important and modifiable risk factor for cardiovascular diseases, the links between the gut microbiome and peripheral artery disease (PAD) and its clinical subgroups (claudication and chronic limb-threatening ischemia; CLTI) are not well understood. METHODS: We used shotgun metagenomics and untargeted metabolomics to analyze the fecal samples of people with PAD and age- and sex-matched non-PAD controls collected in a cross-sectional manner. We used functional prediction pathways, a network analysis, and weighted gene co-expression network analysis of metagenomic, metabolomics, and clinical data to better understand PAD-associated dysbiosis. RESULTS: Alpha and beta diversity were similar between the PAD (n=78) and non-PAD (n=20) groups. Differentially abundant species were dominated by those belonging to the Lachnospiraceae, Ruminococcaceae and Enterobacteriaceae families. Fecal butyrate levels were reduced between the non-PAD and PAD groups, but differences were not statistically significant. There was significantly reduced alpha diversity in the samples of the CLTI compared to claudication subgroup. Abundance of multiple butyrate producers were greater in the claudication group compared to CLTI. Network analysis revealed 5 meta-modules, each with specific associations to PAD presentation and metabolomic profiles, and species that are both top module hubs and differentially abundant between groups. Community interconnectedness appears to increase in claudication, followed by community disintegration in CLTI. CONCLUSIONS: This metagenomic-metabolomic analysis of the gut microbiome of individuals with PAD, highlights the importance of studying functional capacity, diversity, and connectivity between species. Microbial modules may allow an integrative view of the microbial ecology relevant to presence and progression of PAD.

title: Unintended shifts in high-priority adult heart transplant listings after the OPTN's September 2025 policy change.
abstract: The Organ Procurement and Transplantation Network amended Status 2 heart allocation criteria in September 2025, requiring documented failure of high-dose inotropes before candidates could qualify via intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP) or percutaneous endovascular ventricular assist device (PEVAD) support. Using OPTN data, we compared seasonally matched pre-policy (September 2024 to June 2025, n=4206) and post-policy (September 2025 to June 2026, n=4231) adult candidates. While standard Status 3 high-dose inotrope listings increased 2.0% to 4.1% and standard Status 2 IABP/PEVAD listings decreased 18.2% to 11.0%, Status 1 listings and Status 2 exceptions increased 7.7% to 10.6% and 17.5% to 21.5%, respectively (all p<0.001). Consequently, combined initial Status 1/2 listings were unchanged (44.5% vs 44.0%, p=0.71). Furthermore, overall transplant volume remained similar, but status at transplant shifted from standard Status 2 toward Status 2 exceptions and Status 1. Tightening standard Status 2 eligibility was associated with redistribution across high-priority pathways rather than reduced high-priority listings.

title: Plasma neutrophil gelatinase-associated lipocalin levels and risk of future incident venous thromboembolism.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Although neutrophils are suggested to play a role in the pathogenesis of venous thromboembolism (VTE), no study has investigated whether neutrophil gelatinase-associated lipocalin (NGAL), a marker of neutrophil activation, is associated with future VTE risk in the general population. OBJECTIVE: To investigate the association between plasma NGAL levels and the risk of future VTE. METHODS: Plasma NGAL levels were measured in 416 VTE cases and 848 age- and sex-matched controls in a nested case-control study derived from the Tromsø study cohort (1994-2007). Logistic regression models were used to estimate odds ratios (ORs) with 95% CIs for VTE according to quartiles of plasma NGAL, adjusted for age, sex, body mass index, arterial cardiovascular disease, cancer, and C-reactive protein. Separate analyses with follow-up restricted to the first 2 and 5 years after cohort inclusion were conducted to investigate potential short-term associations. RESULTS: We found no association between NGAL levels and risk of future VTE when analyzing the entire study period (OR for highest vs lowest quartile of NGAL: 1.02, 95% CI, 0.70-1.51). However, when follow-up was restricted to 2 years, higher NGAL levels were associated with increased risk of future VTE (OR, 3.87; 95% CI, 1.15-13.03). The association was attenuated when follow-up was extended to 5 years (OR, 1.51; 95% CI, 0.82-2.80). CONCLUSION: Higher plasma NGAL levels were associated with a transiently increased risk of future VTE.
