title: Incidence of thrombosis and bleeding in patients with JAK2-positive myeloproliferative neoplasms receiving low-dose aspirin: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Patients with Janus kinase 2 (JAK2) V617F-positive myeloproliferative neoplasms (MPNs) are at increased thrombotic risk and commonly receive low-dose aspirin, yet its net clinical benefit is uncertain. OBJECTIVES: We estimated the incidence of thrombotic and bleeding events in patients with JAK2-positive MPNs treated with low-dose aspirin. METHODS: A systematic review was performed for studies evaluating thrombotic and hemorrhagic events in patients with JAK2 V617F-positive MPNs while taking low-dose aspirin. Study-level incidence rates (IRs) per 100 person-years and incidence rate ratios (IRRs) comparing aspirin use with no aspirin were calculated and pooled using random-effects meta-analysis. The certainty of evidence was assessed using the Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) approach. RESULTS: 2 2 2 2 We included 3 randomized clinical trials and 7 observational studies (n = 1760 with aspirin, n = 367 without aspirin). The pooled IR of thrombotic events in patients with JAK2 V617F-positive MPNs receiving low-dose aspirin prophylaxis was 2.72 per 100 person-years (95% CI, 1.59-4.65; I= 93%), with pooled IRR receiving aspirin vs no aspirin of 0.59 (95% CI, 0.40-0.86; I= 16%). The pooled IR of major and nonmajor bleeding on low-dose aspirin prophylaxis was 1.97 (95% CI, 1.06-3.65; I= 90%) per 100 person-years, with a pooled IRR of 2.43 (95% CI, 1.15-5.11; I= 43%). The GRADE level of confidence for the investigated risks was low. CONCLUSION: Aspirin was associated with a 40% reduction in thrombosis but a 2.5-fold increase in bleeding risk with low certainty of evidence. More studies are needed to gain high-quality evidence to better define the role of aspirin in JAK2 V617F-positive MPNs.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Patients with Janus kinase 2 (JAK2) V617F-positive myeloproliferative neoplasms (MPNs) are at increased thrombotic risk and commonly receive low-dose aspirin, yet its net clinical benefit is uncertain. OBJECTIVES: We estimated the incidence of thrombotic and bleeding events in patients with JAK2-positive MPNs treated with low-dose aspirin. METHODS: A systematic review was performed for studies evaluating thrombotic and hemorrhagic events in patients with JAK2 V617F-positive MPNs while taking low-dose aspirin.

title: SGLT2 Inhibitors and Cardiovascular Outcomes in Patients With Moderate-to-Severe Psoriasis Receiving Biologic Therapy: A Propensity Score-Matched Cohort Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Patients with moderate-to-severe psoriasis have an increased risk of cardiovascular disease. Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors provide cardiovascular benefits, but their association with cardiovascular outcomes in patients with psoriasis remains insufficiently studied. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the global TriNetX research network. Patients older than 40 years with plaque psoriasis receiving biologic therapy were categorized according to SGLT2 inhibitor use. Propensity score matching was performed to balance demographic characteristics, cardiovascular risk factors, kidney disease, and concomitant antidiabetic medications. RESULTS: After matching, 2016 patients were included in each cohort. SGLT2 inhibitor use was associated with a significantly lower incidence of acute myocardial infarction (HR, 0.601; 95%CI, 0.426-0.849), stroke (HR, 0.553; 95%CI, 0.381-0.804), heart failure (HR, 0.751; 95%CI, 0.581-0.970), peripheral artery disease (HR, 0.648; 95%CI, 0.470-0.894), and angina pectoris (HR, 0.601; 95%CI, 0.404-0.894). No significant association was observed for transient ischemic attack. CONCLUSIONS: SGLT2 inhibitor use was associated with favorable cardiovascular outcomes in patients with moderate-to-severe psoriasis receiving biologic therapy. These findings support further prospective investigation of SGLT2 inhibitors as a potential strategy for cardiovascular risk reduction in this population.

title: Asymptomatic Versus Symptomatic Carotid Revascularization: A Single Institution Retrospective Review.
abstract: BACKGROUND: While carotid revascularization reduces stroke risk in both asymptomatic (AD) and symptomatic (SD) carotid diseases, its role continues to evolve with advances in medical therapy, surgical techniques, and cost considerations. METHODS: This retrospective study reviews outcomes of patients undergoing revascularization at a level 1 stroke center between 2019 and 2024. Primary endpoints were ipsilateral stroke, myocardial infarction (MI), and death at 30 days, 90 days, and 1 year. Secondary endpoints include restenosis rates. RESULTS: A total of 113 patients underwent 127 carotid endarterectomies. Sixty-four percent presented with SD, with a median time to intervention of 9 days (interquartile range 6-11). Patients with SD had a longer median length of stay (2 vs. 1 day, P = 0.076. Follow-up rates were higher in AD at 1 year (65% vs. 36%, P = 0.003). MI rates were 0% at 30 days and 90 days and 0.9% at 1 year. Stroke rates were 0.9%, 0.9%, and 1.8% at 30 days, 90 days, and 1 year, with no difference between AD versus SD. One-year mortality rates were 0.9% and 5.3% at 90 days and 1 year, without a difference by AD versus SD. Restenosis occurred in 4% of patients, with no difference between groups. CONCLUSION: Carotid endarterectomy was associated with low perioperative rates of ipsilateral stroke, MI, and death. Despite a longer length of stay, patients with SD did not have significantly different outcomes or restenosis rates. While males had improved follow-up rates, there was no significant difference in outcomes by gender or race. These findings support favorable outcomes following CEA in both AD and SD.

title: The emerging molecular landscape of abdominal aortic aneurysms: non-coding RNAs as diagnostic and therapeutic targets.
abstract: An abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) is a progressive, often asymptomatic condition whose rupture is associated with a high mortality rate. Ultrasonography and computed tomography are established diagnostic methods, while molecular biomarkers may provide additional information about disease activity. This review discusses the potential role of non-coding RNAs (ncRNAs) as diagnostic and therapeutic tools in AAAs. These molecules, including microRNAs (miRNAs), long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) and circular RNAs (circRNAs), are strongly involved in the regulation of gene expression. Through binding to their target mRNAs, miRNAs primarily suppress translation or promote mRNA degradation. Some lncRNAs and circRNAs act as miRNA sponges, affecting their availability. Here, these mechanisms are discussed by pathological function, distinguishing human tissue and circulating studies from animal, cellular and computational findings. Particular attention is given to miR-21, H19, GAS5, circCdyl and miR-26b-3p, which have functional experimental evidence or human biomarker data beyond expression profiling. Abnormal expression can be detected in peripheral blood or aortic tissue, but these findings do not necessarily predict aneurysm growth or rupture. Integration of ncRNA profiling with imaging and clinical parameters may improve the assessment of AAAs. However, prospective validation and further studies of delivery and safety are needed before these molecules can be used in clinical practice.

title: Lipid control in a cohort of patients with cardiorenal disease (LIPID-REN): a subanalysis of the CARDIOREN registry.
abstract: AIMS: Advanced chronic kidney disease (CKD) confers a very high cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk, requiring comprehensive risk factor assessment. However, real-world data on current practices in patients with cardiorenal disease remain limited. We aimed to evaluate the control of cardiovascular risk factors, with a focus on lipid management, in a contemporary cardiorenal cohort. METHODS: This cross-sectional analysis was conducted within the CARDIOREN Registry, which enrolled patients with chronic heart failure from 13 tertiary hospitals in Spain (2021-2022). Of 1107 patients, 885 with complete data on low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C), albuminuria, and atherosclerotic CVD (ASCVD) were eligible. The present analysis was restricted to the patients who met the definition of advanced CKD, defined as estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) <30 ml/min/1.73 m² or eGFR 30-45 ml/min/1.73 m² with albuminuria >30 mg/g. ASCVD was defined as prior ischemic heart disease, stroke, or peripheral arterial disease. The proportion of patients with LDL-C <55 mg/dl was assessed. Multivariable logistic regression models, including a parsimonious primary model and sensitivity analyses, were used to identify factors associated with lower LDL-C levels. RESULTS: P Advanced CKD was present in 221 patients (25%); median age was 79 years, 58.8% were male, and 52.9% had ASCVD. Median LDL-C was 73 mg/dl, and only 22.6% achieved an LDL-C <55 mg/dl. Achievement of LDL-C <55 mg/dl was significantly lower in patients without ASCVD compared with those with ASCVD (13.4% vs. 30.7%; = .002). In multivariable analysis, ASCVD was independently associated with a higher likelihood of achieving LDL-C <55 mg/dl, whereas female sex was independently associated with a lower likelihood of achieving this level. CONCLUSIONS: In patients with advanced CKD, lipid control was below cardiology guideline recommendations for patients at very high CVD risk, particularly among those without ASCVD and in women.

title: Apparent Diffusion Coefficient Composition and Tissue Heterogeneity as Predictors of Functional Outcomes After Endovascular Thrombectomy in Patients With Large Ischemic Core.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Recent trials established endovascular thrombectomy efficacy in large ischemic cores, yet outcomes remain heterogeneous despite similar infarct volumes, suggesting that current volumetric assessments may not fully capture tissue viability. We examined whether tissue composition quantified by apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) distribution and tissue heterogeneity within baseline diffusion-weighted imaging lesions are associated with functional outcomes in large-core patients after successful endovascular thrombectomy. METHODS: -6 2 We retrospectively analyzed patients with large vessel occlusion with large ischemic cores (diffusion-weighted imaging candidate volume ≥50 mL) achieving successful reperfusion after endovascular thrombectomy. We quantified ADC tissue composition as proportions within 3 ADC ranges relative to total diffusion-weighted imaging lesion volume: low (<540), mid (540-700), and high (>700 × 10mm/s). Separately, tissue heterogeneity was assessed using Shannon entropy, a metric quantifying ADC distribution heterogeneity. The primary outcome was 3-month good functional outcome (modified Rankin Scale score of 0-3), analyzed via adjusted logistic regression. RESULTS: P P Among 126 patients (age, 70.8±12.4 years; 60.3% men; diffusion-weighted imaging candidate volume, 93.7±41.2 mL), 39.7% achieved a good functional outcome. Both tissue heterogeneity (adjusted odds ratio, 1.45 per 0.1-unit increase, 1.09-1.93,=0.011, area under the curve, 0.671) and mid-ADC fraction (adjusted odds ratio, 1.78 per 5% increase, 1.20-2.63,=0.004, area under the curve, 0.688) were associated with good functional outcomes. Neither low-ADC nor high-ADC fractions showed significant associations with functional outcomes. CONCLUSIONS: -6 2 Higher mid-ADC (540-700 × 10mm/s) fraction and greater tissue heterogeneity predicted favorable outcomes in patients with large ischemic core, indicating that tissue composition within the ischemic core, beyond its volume, is associated with functional outcome after reperfusion. Among large-core patients who achieved successful reperfusion, ADC-based tissue characterization may help predict functional outcome.

title: The ECMO-PoCS Score: Derivation and Internal Validation of an Implantation-Time Model for In-Hospital Mortality in Postcardiotomy Venoarterial Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: To derive and internally validate a mortality score (ECMO-PoCS) for use at venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) implantation for postcardiotomy cardiogenic shock (PCS), hypothesizing that a few implantation-time variables would discriminate in-hospital mortality better than European System for Cardiac Operative Risk Evaluation II (EuroSCORE II), Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation II (APACHE II), or pre-ECMO lactate. DESIGN: Retrospective, single-center cohort study. SETTING: Tertiary cardiac surgical center. PARTICIPANTS: A total of 149 consecutive adults receiving VA-ECMO for PCS (2007-2024), excluding 7 bridged directly to transplantation. INTERVENTIONS: None. MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Hospital mortality was 65.8% and 1-year survival 33.4%. A 4-variable logistic model (age, pre-ECMO lactate, peripheral artery disease [PAD], and any preoperative right ventricular [RV] dysfunction) was fitted in 133 complete cases; PAD (adjusted odds ratio [OR] = 4.58; p = 0.022) and RV dysfunction (adjusted OR = 3.16; p = 0.020) were independently associated with mortality. In 130 patients with all comparators, ECMO-PoCS (area under the curve [AUC] = 0.715) discriminated better than European System for Cardiac Operative Risk Evaluation II (EuroSCORE II) (0.583; DeLong p = 0.043) and lactate alone (0.601; p = 0.030) but not significantly better than APACHE II (0.610; p = 0.13); adding these variables to APACHE II increased its AUC to 0.727 (likelihood ratio p = 0.002). Bootstrap optimism-corrected AUC was 0.687 and the shrinkage factor 0.82. A 0- to 5-point score defined low-, intermediate-, and high-risk groups (mortality 23.1%, 63.6%, and 86.0%, respectively; trend p < 0.001). CONCLUSIONS: ECMO-PoCS, based on 4 variables available at implantation, discriminated in-hospital mortality better than EuroSCORE II and lactate alone and added information to APACHE II. Internally validated only, it is intended for risk description, research stratification, and benchmarking, not for decisions to initiate or withdraw support, pending external validation.

DESIGN: Retrospective, single-center cohort study. SETTING: Tertiary cardiac surgical center.

title: Microsurgical Clipping of a Tumor-Like Bilobulated Ophthalmic Aneurysm: A 2-Dimensional Operative Video.
abstract: 1-3 4-6 2,4,7 8 Ophthalmic artery aneurysms are technically challenging lesions because of their complex paraclinoid anatomy and intimate relationship with the optic apparatus, internal carotid artery (ICA), and ophthalmic artery.Visual dysfunction is an important clinical presentation, particularly in large aneurysms causing optic nerve compression, and visual outcomes remain a major consideration when selecting among microsurgical and endovascular treatment strategies.Microsurgical clipping remains an important option in selected complex aneurysms because it provides definitive exclusion while allowing direct optic nerve decompression and parent vessel reconstruction.We present the operative video of a 59-year-old woman with progressive right-predominant visual deterioration over approximately 30 days. Imaging demonstrated a large, irregular, bilobulated ophthalmic artery aneurysm measuring 18 × 11 mm, with an 8-mm neck and postcontrast wall enhancement. Given the progressive visual deficit and optic nerve compression, microsurgical treatment was selected. Following proximal cervical ICA control and a pterional-transsylvian approach,the optic nerve was decompressed and the aneurysm exposed. Its broad neck and complex bilobulated morphology required tandem clip reconstruction of the ICA while preserving ophthalmic artery flow. Motor-evoked potentials and indocyanine green videoangiography guided clip adjustment. Atherosclerotic plaque at ophthalmic artery origin further influenced final clip positioning. Postoperative computed tomography angiography confirmed parent vessel patency, and visual field testing demonstrated improvement at 2 weeks. This video demonstrates optic nerve decompression, reconstructive clipping, and flow-preserving microsurgical strategies for a complex ophthalmic artery aneurysm.

title: Limb salvage is possible in select patients with arterial injuries and elevated mangled extremity severity scores.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Lower extremity trauma with vascular compromise is frequently associated with other injuries and requires emergent and complex decision-making. The Mangled Extremity Severity Score (MESS) is widely utilized to predict the need for amputation in these cases. As the tool was developed >30 years ago, its accuracy in the modern trauma setting remains a topic of investigation and discussion. This study investigated the correlation of an elevated MESS with the need for amputation in patients with traumatic lower extremity arterial injuries. METHODS: A retrospective chart review was performed for patients ≥18 years old with traumatic lower extremity arterial injuries at a level I trauma center from July 2012 to December 2023. Demographics, injury characteristics, interventions, and outcomes including amputation upon presentation, amputation during hospitalization, and amputation after discharge following limb salvage attempts were recorded. RESULTS: In our cohort of 238 limbs with lower extremity arterial injury, the median age was 33 years, and the majority of patients were male (84.1%). The predominant mechanism was penetrating (65.1%). Concomitant injuries were noted in 84 cases of lower extremity injures (35.3%). The median MESS was 5 (interquartile range, 3-6). Vascular repair was performed for 179 lower limbs (75.2%); 168 underwent open repair (93.9%), 9 endovascular (5.0%), and 2 hybrid (1.1%). Ninety-two limbs underwent concomitant orthopedic repair (38.7%). Six limbs underwent primary amputation (2.5%) after a multidisciplinary consensus, all of which had a MESS of ≥7. Of the 179 lower limbs that underwent vascular repair, 8.4% required amputation before discharge, and another 2.8% required amputation after discharge. Thirty-three lower extremities with a MESS of ≥7 underwent vascular repair. The majority did not require a subsequent amputation (22/33, 66.7%). In the entire cohort, a MESS of ≥7 was significantly associated with any amputation (P < .0001) when compared with MESS < 7. MESS ≥ 7 was associated with a significantly higher odds of amputation in both univariable (odds ratio, 10.6; 95% confidence interval, 4.65-24.1; P < .0001) and multivariable analyses after adjustment for age, ischemia time, mechanism of injury, concomitant injuries, arterial injury location, and fracture status (adjusted odds ratio, 5.40; 95% confidence interval, 1.79-16.3; P = .003). CONCLUSIONS: Lower extremity arterial injuries are frequently associated with complex orthopedic and soft tissue trauma. An elevated MESS, blunt mechanism, and the presence of multiple vascular injuries are significantly associated with the risk of limb loss. Although a MESS of 7 or greater is predictive of an increased risk of amputation, limb salvage can still be achieved in many patients with prompt vascular repair despite high MESS.

title: Outcomes of hepatic artery thrombosis after paediatric liver transplantation (HEPATIC): an international, multicentre, retrospective registry study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Hepatic artery thrombosis after paediatric liver transplantation is a severe complication that can lead to acute graft failure, often requiring urgent re-transplantation. We aimed to assess the 1-year incidence of graft loss and mortality and to evaluate outcomes according to the timing of hepatic artery thrombosis and the treatment approaches in patients with hepatic artery thrombosis after paediatric liver transplantation. METHODS: In this international, multicentre, retrospective study, the HEPATIC registry, which had 33 centres across 21 countries as of December, 2025, was used to identify patients who developed hepatic artery thrombosis at age younger than 18 years after paediatric liver transplantation between Jan 1, 2002, and Dec 31, 2021, and who either received a diagnosis of or received an intervention for hepatic artery thrombosis before Jan 1, 2023. Donor-related, recipient-related, and transplantation-related characteristics collected from local medical records were entered retrospectively into electronic case reports by participating centres, with centralised data quality control. Primary outcomes were 1-year graft loss and mortality after hepatic artery thrombosis diagnosis. The outcomes were examined based on when hepatic artery thrombosis occurred after paediatric liver transplantation (early [≤7 days] vs late [>7 days]), primary management strategy (conservative management, surgical revascularisation, endovascular therapy, or immediate listing for re-transplantation), and transplantation era (in 5-year intervals). The registry was registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT05818644. FINDINGS: Hepatic artery thrombosis occurred in 415 patients, of whom 216 (52%) were female and 199 (48%) were male, and median age was 1·7 years (IQR 0·8-6·5). Median follow-up was 50·9 months (IQR 17·0-112·6). Graft loss occurred in 180 patients by 1 month (cumulative incidence 43% [95% CI 38-48]) and 222 by 1 year (54% [49-58]); 51 patients died by 1 month (12% [9-15]) and 77 by 1 year (19% [15-22]). Surgical revascularisation was the first-line treatment approach in 195 (47%) patients. Other strategies included listing for re-transplantation in 99 (24%), conservative management in 79 (19%), and endovascular therapy in 42 (10%). Treatment approaches changed over time, with increased use of conservative management and endovascular therapy and reduced listing for re-transplantation (p<0·0001), with no accompanying change in 1-year mortality across eras (p=0·14). Early (≤7 days) hepatic artery thrombosis occurred in 282 (68%) patients and was associated with higher 1-year graft loss than late (>7 days) hepatic artery thrombosis (cumulative incidence 57% [95% CI 51-63] vs 47% [37-55], log-rank p=0·010). Surgical revascularisation was used in 167 (59%) patients and listing for re-transplantation in 66 (23%) patients with early hepatic artery thrombosis, whereas conservative management was used in 51 (38%) patients and endovascular therapy in 21 (16%) patients with late hepatic artery thrombosis; however, 1-year mortality did not differ between treatment strategies among patients with early versus late hepatic artery thrombosis. INTERPRETATION: Hepatic artery thrombosis after paediatric liver transplantation is associated with notably high 1-year graft loss and mortality, particularly if hepatic artery thrombosis occurs within 7 days after the procedure. The management strategies for hepatic artery thrombosis differ according to the post-transplantation timing of hepatic artery thrombosis occurrence. Despite changes in management over the past 20 years, outcomes have remained poor, underscoring the need to improve therapeutic strategies for this complication. FUNDING: None.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Hepatic artery thrombosis after paediatric liver transplantation is a severe complication that can lead to acute graft failure, often requiring urgent re-transplantation. We aimed to assess the 1-year incidence of graft loss and mortality and to evaluate outcomes according to the timing of hepatic artery thrombosis and the treatment approaches in patients with hepatic artery thrombosis after paediatric liver transplantation. METHODS: In this international, multicentre, retrospective study, the HEPATIC registry, which had 33 centres across 21 countries as of December, 2025, was used to identify patients who developed hepatic artery thrombosis at age younger than 18 years after paediatric liver transplantation between Jan 1, 2002, and Dec 31, 2021, and who either received a diagnosis of or received an intervention for hepatic artery thrombosis before Jan 1, 2023.

title: Transseptal Transcatheter Mitral Valve Replacement for Mitral Annular Calcification: ENCIRCLE MAC Registry 1-Year Outcomes.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Patients with symptomatic mitral valve dysfunction (MVD) and mitral annular calcification (MAC) represent one of the most challenging populations in structural heart disease. Advanced age, multiple comorbidities, extensive annular calcification, and unfavorable anatomy often preclude surgical mitral valve replacement or transcatheter repair, leaving many patients with limited treatment options. Whether fully percutaneous transseptal transcatheter mitral valve replacement (TMVR) can provide a meaningful treatment pathway for patients with MAC-related MVD remains uncertain. OBJECTIVES: The goal of this study was to evaluate 1-year clinical, echocardiographic, and patient-centered outcomes after transseptal TMVR with the SAPIEN M3 system in patients with symptomatic MAC-related MVD. METHODS: The ENCIRCLE (SAPIEN M3 System Transcatheter Mitral Valve Replacement Via Transseptal Access) trial MAC Registry is a prospective, multicenter, single-arm study that enrolled symptomatic patients with MAC-related MVD, including ≥ moderate to severe mitral regurgitation (MR), severe mitral stenosis, or combined moderate MR with at least moderate mitral stenosis, who were considered unsuitable for surgery or transcatheter repair. The primary endpoint was a nonhierarchical composite of all-cause mortality and heart failure hospitalization (HFH) at 1 year. RESULTS: Among 364 screened patients, TVMR was attempted in 100, and the valve was implanted in 93. Mean age was 76.1 ± 9.2 years, 51.0% were male, 73.0% were in NYHA functional class III/IV, and mean Society of Thoracic Surgeons Predicted Risk of Mortality score for mitral valve replacement was 8.4% ± 4.9%. At 1 year, the Kaplan-Meier estimate of all-cause mortality or HFH was 33.6% (95% CI: 25.0%-44.1%), with 21.1% all-cause mortality and 19.4% HFH. Disabling stroke occurred in 5.1%, clinically significant left ventricular outflow tract obstruction in 4.8%, valve thrombosis in 2.3%, hemolysis requiring transfusion or mitral valve reintervention in 9.2%, and mitral valve re-intervention in 11.4%. Among implanted patients, MR ≤1+ was achieved in 98.5% at 1 year. Improvements in NYHA functional class, Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Overall Summary score, and 6-minute walk distance were sustained through 1 year. CONCLUSIONS: In carefully selected patients with symptomatic MAC-related MVD unsuitable for surgery or transcatheter repair, transseptal TMVR with the SAPIEN M3 system was associated with sustained MR reduction and meaningful improvements in symptoms and quality of life through 1 year. These findings support consideration of transseptal TMVR as a treatment pathway for selected patients with MAC-related MVD.

Whether fully percutaneous transseptal transcatheter mitral valve replacement (TMVR) can provide a meaningful treatment pathway for patients with MAC-related MVD remains uncertain.

title: "Not so Minor" - Digital Amputation as a Precursor to Major Amputation and Mortality in an Irish Tertiary Vascular Center.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Minor (toe) amputations are a common consequence of peripheral arterial disease and/or diabetes. They can herald further forefoot and major amputations and are a poor prognostic indicator for 5-year survival. This study aimed to identify prognostic indicators for progression from minor amputation to major amputation and all-cause mortality. METHODS: Index digital amputations performed by vascular surgeons in a tertiary referral hospital between 2017 and 2022 were identified from Hospital In-Patient Enquiry data. Electronic records for each limb were followed up to October 2025 for further ipsilateral minor and major amputations and mortality. RESULTS: A total of 224 limbs in 209 patients underwent at least 1 minor amputation. The cohort was predominantly male (86%) with a mean age of 66.3 years (±12.7). 70% had peripheral arterial disease and 80% had diabetes. In total, 34% (n = 73/215) required further ipsilateral amputation, 78.3% of which occurred within 12 months of index surgery. Minor and major reamputation rates were 25.6% and 11%, respectively. Predictors of further amputation at any level included ischemic heart disease (IHD) (odds ratio [OR] 2.796, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.54-5.06), diabetes (OR 2.31, 95% CI 1.04-5.136), and dialysis (OR 2.20, 95% CI 1.021-4.915). Index hallux amputation, IHD, and revascularization at index admission were risk factors for further major ipsilateral amputation. All-cause mortality was 11.4%, 24.8%, and 48% at 1, 3, and 5 years, respectively. CONCLUSION: Consistent with international data, minor amputations are poor prognostic factor for limb loss and death. In this cohort, patients with IHD and dialysis were most at risk for further amputation.

title: Comparative Outcomes of Endovascular and Open Surgical Repair for Extracranial Carotid Artery Aneurysms: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Extracranial carotid artery aneurysms (ECAAs) are rare lesions managed by open surgical repair (OpR) or endovascular repair (ER). We compared the perioperative and long-term outcomes of both strategies. METHODS: A Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analysis (PRISMA)-compliant systematic review and meta-analysis, registered in International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (PROSPERO), was performed. Comparative studies were pooled using random-effects models, and separate single-arm meta-analyses were conducted for OpR and ER. RESULTS: Twenty-six retrospective studies involving 707 patients and 725 procedures were included (574 OpR and 151 ER). Six comparative studies (228 procedures) showed no significant differences between ER and OpR in 30-day mortality (odds ratio [OR], 2.58; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.53-12.52), 30-day stroke (OR, 1.08; 95% CI, 0.30-3.91), late stroke, reintervention, or primary patency. In the single-arm analyses, pooled 30-day mortality and stroke rates after OpR were 1.18% and 4.29%, respectively. No 30-day deaths and one stroke were reported after ER, yielding a pooled stroke rate of 1.25% (95% CI, 0.18-8.34). Primary patency was high after both OpR (98.44%) and ER (94.50%). CONCLUSION: Observational evidence suggests similar perioperative outcomes and similar observed late event rates for ER and OpR in ECAAs, although heterogeneous follow up and the absence of time-to-event analyses limit formal comparison of long-term durability. Both approaches were associated with low mortality, stroke, reintervention rates, and excellent primary patency. Open repair remains supported by a larger body of evidence and longer follow up, whereas evidence for ER remains comparatively limited. Because treatment allocation in the available studies was influenced by patient characteristics, anatomical complexity, and surgical risk, the observed similarity in outcomes should not be interpreted as evidence of therapeutic equivalence. Given the observational design and the predominantly moderate-to-serious risk of bias of the included studies, these findings should be interpreted with caution.

We compared the perioperative and long-term outcomes of both strategies. METHODS: A Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analysis (PRISMA)-compliant systematic review and meta-analysis, registered in International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (PROSPERO), was performed.

title: Spatial Organization of Disturbed Flow after Carotid Endarterectomy and Carotid Artery Stenting.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Carotid endarterectomy (CEA) and carotid artery stenting (CAS) create distinct postoperative geometries. Conventional wall shear stress (WSS)-derived biomarkers quantify disturbed-flow magnitude but not its spatial organization. We evaluated whether spatial organization provides complementary hemodynamic information after CEA and CAS. METHODS: In this retrospective, patient-specific computational fluid dynamics study, 9 carotid geometries (3 healthy, 3 post-CEA, and 3 post-CAS) were reconstructed from computed tomography angiography. Identical pulsatile boundary conditions were applied to isolate morphological effects. Time-averaged WSS (TAWSS), oscillatory shear index (OSI), relative residence time (RRT), and endothelial cell activation potential (ECAP) were computed. Regions of adverse flow were defined using percentile thresholds (P90, P95, and P99). Spatial organization was quantified by total area at risk, largest connected hotspot area, hotspot number, and the Spatial Dominance Index (SDI), defined as the largest hotspot area divided by total area at risk. RESULTS: ECAP, OSI, and RRT colocalized with low TAWSS, and spatial descriptors were consistent across biomarkers. Healthy carotids showed the most focal pattern (SDI approximately 0.22; 8-12 hotspots). CEA had the largest total area at risk and largest hotspot but retained relatively high dominance (SDI, 0.16-0.17; 48-75 hotspots). The Roadsaver-treated CAS geometries had the smallest total area at risk but the most fragmented pattern, with smaller hotspots and the lowest dominance (SDI, 0.09-0.12; 39-70 hotspots). These patterns persisted across P90-P99 thresholds. CONCLUSION: Spatial organization distinguished carotid revascularization strategies beyond biomarker magnitude. CEA largely preserved a focal, dominant pattern, whereas the Roadsaver-treated CAS geometries showed fragmented, distributed disturbed flow. The simple, dimensionless SDI may complement established WSS-derived biomarkers in patient-specific hemodynamic assessment.

Conventional wall shear stress (WSS)-derived biomarkers quantify disturbed-flow magnitude but not its spatial organization. We evaluated whether spatial organization provides complementary hemodynamic information after CEA and CAS.

title: Endovascular Iliac Stenting Versus Open Aortobifemoral Bypass for Aortoiliac Occlusive Disease: A Retrospective Multicentre Cohort Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Aortoiliac occlusive disease (AIOD) causing chronic or critical limb-threatening ischemia can be treated by open aortobifemoral bypass (ABF) or endovascular reconstruction. Comparative effectiveness data adjusted for treatment selection bias remain limited. This multicenter study compared mid-term outcomes of endovascular versus open reconstruction for AIOD. METHODS: Retrospective, nonrandomized cohort study of 171 patients with AIOD (Rutherford 3-6) treated at three centers (UK, Ireland, and Egypt) between January 2023 and February 2026. Outcomes were primary patency, freedom from reintervention (FFR), amputation-free survival (AFS), overall survival, and perioperative complications. Cox regression and inverse-probability-of-treatment weighting (IPTW) were used to adjust for confounding. RESULTS: 125 patients (73.1%) underwent endovascular treatment and 46 (26.9%) open bypass. Endovascular patients were older (66.8 vs 60.8 years, P < 0.001) and had a lower burden of TransAtlantic Inter-Society Consensus II (TASC II) C-D disease (53.6% vs 93.5%, P < 0.001). Primary patency at 24 months was 62.7% versus 91.8% (log-rank P < 0.001; IPTW-adjusted hazard ratio [HR] 5.67, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.75-18.37). FFR at 24 months was 63.1% versus 93.3% (P < 0.001). AFS (85.0% vs 87.4%, P = 0.992) and overall survival (93.3% vs 90.0%, P = 0.335) were comparable between groups. Wound infection was less frequent after endovascular treatment (0.8% vs 10.9%, P = 0.006). Major amputation was independently predicted by critical limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) presentation (odds ratio [OR] 4.0) and age, not treatment group. Progressive infrainguinal disease, rather than failure of proximal revascularization, accounted for most amputations in both groups. CONCLUSION: Open bypass confers a substantial mid-term patency and reintervention-free survival advantage over endovascular reconstruction for AIOD, most pronounced in TASC D and CLTI subgroups, without a corresponding difference in limb salvage or survival. These findings support risk-stratified rather than uniformly endovascular-first treatment selection, pending confirmation from the ongoing Endovascular Versus Open revascularisation in severe oCClusive aorto-iliac disease (EVOCC) randomized trial.

Comparative effectiveness data adjusted for treatment selection bias remain limited. This multicenter study compared mid-term outcomes of endovascular versus open reconstruction for AIOD.

title: Association between Increased Superficial Calcification Clusters in Carotid Atherosclerosis and Cardiovascular Events after Carotid Artery Stenting: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The role of calcification in carotid atherosclerosis before and after carotid artery stenting (CAS) remains controversial. This study assessed the association between the extent of calcification in target carotid plaques and outcomes after CAS. METHODS: A total of 292 subjects with carotid stenosis who underwent CAS were retrospectively enrolled. Follow-up for major adverse cardiovascular events (MACEs) was conducted via outpatient visits and telephone. Ultimately, 211 subjects completed 2-year follow-up. Superficial calcification clusters were counted on computed tomography angiography. Subjects with ≥4 superficial calcification clusters (n = 24) were matched in a 1:4 ratio to those with <4 superficial calcification clusters (n = 96). Sensitivity analysis was performed based on the matched cohort. RESULTS: Over a median follow-up of 1.92 years, 14 MACEs occurring more than 30 days after discharge were recorded. In univariate Cox analysis, symptom status (P = 0.0116), alcohol abuse (P = 0.0091), total number of calcification clusters (P = 0.0428), and number of superficial calcification clusters (P = 0.0022) were significantly associated with MACEs. In bivariate analyses, the number of superficial calcification clusters maintained a reasonably good association with MACEs. In sensitivity analysis, superficial calcification clusters remained significantly associated with MACE when loss to follow-up was classified as MACE (P = 0.0256, HR = 1.2548, 95% CI 1.0281-1.5315) or as no MACE (P = 0.0265, HR = 1.4948, 95% CI 1.0479-2.1323). CONCLUSION: The number of superficial calcification clusters may independently serve as a prognostic risk factor in patients with carotid atherosclerosis undergoing CAS.

This study assessed the association between the extent of calcification in target carotid plaques and outcomes after CAS. METHODS: A total of 292 subjects with carotid stenosis who underwent CAS were retrospectively enrolled.

title: Severity-Dependent Patterns of Hemodynamic Change in Symptomatic Carotid Stenosis during the Waiting Period Before Endarterectomy.
abstract: BACKGROUND: To determine whether the rate of hemodynamic change after a symptomatic carotid event differs between moderate and severe stenosis. METHODS: Serial duplex examinations in symptomatic patients awaiting carotid endarterectomy were analyzed with a linear mixed-effects model, using an extended, prospectively maintained database. Maximum internal carotid artery peak systolic velocity (ICA PSV) was modeled as a linear function of time from the index event interacting with baseline severity (moderate 125-229, severe ≥230 cm/s), with a random intercept per patient. The rate of change (cm/s per day) and the moderate-severe difference were the principal outcomes. Categorical interval comparisons and paired within-patient changes, including distal common carotid artery (CCA) PSV, were secondary analyses. RESULTS: The time course of maximum ICA PSV differed by baseline severity (interaction P = 0.006). The modeled rate of change was +1.20 cm/s per day (95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.28 to 2.12) in moderate and -0.21 cm/s per day (95% CI: -0.58 to 0.17) in severe stenosis (difference 1.41 cm/s per day, 95% CI: 0.42 to 2.40; P = 0.005). Secondary analyses were consistent: moderate stenosis accelerated with stable inflow, whereas severe stenosis showed no further ICA acceleration but a fall in distal CCA PSV (-3.0 cm/s; P < 0.001). CONCLUSION: The rate of hemodynamic change during the waiting period depends on baseline severity: moderate stenosis accelerates, whereas severe stenosis shows little further ICA acceleration, consistent with behavior near a velocity ceiling. Maximum ICA PSV and distal CCA PSV are best read as separate, time-sensitive variables rather than as a single ratio.

METHODS: Serial duplex examinations in symptomatic patients awaiting carotid endarterectomy were analyzed with a linear mixed-effects model, using an extended, prospectively maintained database. Maximum internal carotid artery peak systolic velocity (ICA PSV) was modeled as a linear function of time from the index event interacting with baseline severity (moderate 125-229, severe ≥230 cm/s), with a random intercept per patient.

title: Diagnostic Accuracy of the BlueDop Vascular Expert for Detecting Peripheral Arterial Disease in People with Suspected Intermittent Claudication Referred to Secondary Care: A Cross-Sectional Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Manual ankle-brachial pressure index (ABI) assessment reqiuires significant time and expertise, precluding its use in primary care. Automated vascular assessment tools may offer a simple and efficient alternative for detecting peripheral arterial disease (PAD). However, further evidence is needed before they can be recommended. This study considers the diagnostic accuracy of the BlueDop vascular expert (BVE) in people with suspected intermittent claudication. METHODS: We performed a cross-sectional cohort study including people referred to our nurse-led intermittent claudication clinic. BVE measurements were compared to the manual resting ABI/toe brachial index (TBI) method, using traditional cutoff values of <0.9 and < 0.7, respectively. RESULTS: 217 participants and 430 limbs were included, with an overall PAD prevalence of 46%. Sensitivity, specificity, positive predictor values (PPVs) and negative predictor values (NPVs) for the BVE were 88.5%, 80.7%, 81.3% and 88.1% respectively, when compared to the manual ABI. When compared to the manual TBI, the sensitivity, specificity, PPV and NPV for the BVE were 45.5%, 88%, 62.5%, and 78.6% respectively, though this analysis included only 38 limbs. No BVE diagnoses were based on ABI alone, 71% were based on waveform alone and 29% were based on a combination of ABI and waveform. The BVE assessment was significantly quicker to perform than the manual method (P < 0.01). CONCLUSION: The BVE demonstrated favorable sensitivity and specificity for detecting or excluding PAD compared to the manual ABI. Further work is needed comparing this device to others, across a range of clinical populations and settings before it can be considered in routine clinical practice.

title: Endoscopic versus open great saphenous vein harvesting for lower extremity arterial bypass: A systematic review, meta-analysis and meta-regression.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To compare postoperative outcomes of patients undergoing lower extremity arterial bypass (LEAB) for peripheral artery disease with endoscopic great saphenous vein harvest (EVH) vs open vein harvest (OVH), and to investigate the impact of publication year on bypass patency. METHODS: PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were systematically searched from inception through January 2025 for comparative studies of EVH vs OVH in LEAB. Individual patient data were reconstructed from Kaplan-Meier curves and analyzed using Cox proportional hazards models. Binary and continuous outcomes were pooled using random-effects models. Meta-regression and subgroup analyses by publication year (≤2015 vs >2015) were performed to explore temporal trends in patency. RESULTS: 2 Thirteen retrospective cohort studies comprising 12,401 patients were included. EVH was associated with higher risk of primary patency loss compared with OVH (hazard ratio [HR], 1.32; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.04-1.68; P = .030) and a borderline longer operative time (mean difference, 58.98 minutes; 95% CI, 0.63-117.32; P = .050; I= 96%), but significantly lower wound complications (risk ratio, 0.68; 95% CI, 0.57-0.80; P < .001). No differences were observed in primary-assisted patency, secondary patency, length of stay, major amputation, limb salvage, or mortality. Subgroup analysis showed that the primary patency disadvantage was driven by studies published up to 2015 (HR, 1.49; P = .010), with no significant difference in studies published after 2015 (HR, 0.97; P = .900), although the interaction test was not significant (P = .100). Meta-regression did not demonstrate an association between publication year and primary patency effect size (P = .890). CONCLUSIONS: EVH significantly reduces wound complications but is associated with lower primary patency and potentially longer operative times compared with OVH, disadvantages that do not translate into differences in secondary patency, limb salvage, major amputation, or mortality. Further prospective studies are needed to define the role of EVH to better inform LEAB operative planning.

title: Clinical outcomes of transperitoneal versus retroperitoneal approaches of open aortic repair for abdominal aortic aneurysm stratified by iliac bifurcation involvement.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Aortic aneurysm with iliac bifurcation involvement (AAAIB) is associated with higher rates of systemic comorbidities and increased complexity of open aortic repair (OAR), resulting in worse outcomes compared with OAR for isolated abdominal aortic aneurysm (IAAA). The Society for Vascular Surgery practice guidelines recommend the retroperitoneal approach (RPA) for OAR in certain patients with abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA). However, there is limited evidence to determine whether the relative advantages and disadvantages of RPA and the transperitoneal approach (TPA) change depending on whether the aneurysm distally involves the iliac bifurcation. This study compared the outcomes of TPA and RPA for AAA, stratified by iliac bifurcation involvement, in a multi-institutional, real-world setting. METHODS: The Society for Vascular Surgery Vascular Quality Initiative database was queried for patients who underwent OAR for AAA from January 2003 to September 2024. Patients were stratified as having AAAIB or IAAA based on whether the aneurysm involved the iliac bifurcation and required a distal anastomosis beyond the common iliac artery bifurcation, or not. Baseline characteristics and clinical outcomes, such as overall 30-day mortality, major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE: death, myocardial infarction, and stroke), and 1-year survival, were compared between the TPA and RPA groups in patients with IAAA and AAAIB. Univariable and multivariable analyses and a confirmatory analysis with inverse probability-weighted regression were performed. RESULTS: Of all the reviewed patients, 17,009 were included in the final analysis, of whom 15,218 (89.5%) had IAAA and 1791 (10.5%) had AAAIB. Among patients with IAAA, compared with RPA, TPA was associated with a higher odds of overall 30-day mortality (odds ratios [OR], 1.26; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.05-1.49; P = .011) and of MACE (OR, 1.26; 95% CI, 1.11-1.44; P = .001) and a lower 1-year survival rate (hazard ratio, 1.23; 95% CI, 1.09-1.39; P = .001). Among patients with AAAIB, TPA was associated with a lower odds of lower extremity ischemia (OR, 0.47; 95% CI, 0.25-0.91; P = .024), without significant differences in 30-day mortality (OR, 0.80; 95% CI, 0.42-1.51; P = .485), MACE (OR, 0.86; 95% CI, 0.52-1.42; P = .563), and 1-year survival (hazard ratio, 0.93; 95% CI, 0.59-1.47; P = .768). CONCLUSIONS: In this real-world study, iliac bifurcation involvement in AAA was an effect modifier for the outcomes of different OAR approaches. For patients with IAAA, compared with RPA, TPA was associated with worse 30-day mortality, MACE, and 1-year survival. In contrast, for patients with AAAIB, TPA was associated with a lower odds of lower extremity ischemia, without significant differences in 30-day mortality, MACE, or 1-year survival. This study suggests that RPA may be the procedure of choice for IAAA if it is otherwise feasible. However, TPA may be the procedure of choice for patients with AAAIB who are otherwise anatomically suitable. Larger prospective studies are warranted to validate these findings.

title: Blood Pressure and Heart Rate Stationarity in Predicting TEVAR Response.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Hypertension is a major risk factor for type B aortic dissections and rupture, with guidelines recommending systolic blood pressure (SBP) control below 130 mmHg to improve outcomes. While post-TEVAR blood pressure is often managed with a focus on mean SBP, little is known about temporal hemodynamic patterns and their association with surgical success. This study investigates blood pressure and heart rate (HR) time-series metrics within 24 hours post-TEVAR and their predictive potential for outcomes. METHODS: Blood pressure (n = 560) and HR (n = 680) time-series data from 31 patients were analyzed alongside preoperative aortic geometry metrics. Exploratory data analysis identified correlations between BP variability and outcomes. Stationarity tests were performed on time-series data to assess statistical properties. Logistic regression models incorporating hemodynamic metrics, along with CT-derived features, were used to predict TEVAR outcomes. RESULTS: Successful outcomes correlated with greater diastolic blood pressure variability and strictly stationary SBP. Logistic regression models combining these metrics along with heart rate standard deviation and preoperative aortic geometry achieved 96.67% 5-fold cross-validation accuracy in predicting outcomes. CONCLUSION: Post-TEVAR behaviors of hemodynamic variables are critical predictors of TEVAR success, with higher DBP standard deviation and strict stationarity of SBP significantly associated with favorable outcomes. These findings highlight the importance of hemodynamic variability and stationarity in optimizing post-TEVAR patient care.

title: The axillary vein and its tributaries: anatomical variations, morphometry, and surgical implications.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Precise morphometric data of the axillary vein (AV) network are essential for surgical and endovascular safety. This study aims to characterize main-trunk morphometry, formation patterns (Types A/B), tributary variations, and the lateral venous channel (LVC), providing an anatomical framework potentially relevant to surgical navigation and vascular access. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Forty formalin-fixed upper extremities from adult whole-body donors were dissected. Two independent investigators measured external venous diameters at standardized landmarks and the AV to coracoid apex distance; terminal drainage patterns were recorded during dissection. The LVC was operationally defined as a distinct longitudinal venous channel coursing along the lateral axillary wall, separate from the main AV and from the principal course of its distal communicating vein, while forming an additional distal-to-proximal venous connection within the axillary venous system. RESULTS: Mean proximal AV diameter was 10.42 ± 2.06 mm; distance from the coracoid apex to the AV was 44.01 ± 13.08 mm. Male donors showed significantly larger proximal AV (p = 0.016) and subscapular vein (p = 0.033) diameters. Brachial vein termination comprised Type A (independent, 75.0%) and Type B (common trunk, 25.0%). An LVC was identified in 62.5% of specimens, most frequently showing distal communication with the lateral brachial vein and proximal termination in the AV. Cephalic vein absence was 10.0%. CONCLUSIONS: The axillary venous network displays marked variability. The LVC represents a recurrent lateral axillary venous configuration with variable distal communications; in the present series, all identified channels joined the AV proximally. These findings provide a detailed anatomical framework that may assist procedural planning and recognition of venous variations during axillary interventions.

title: Imaging and Outcomes in the Treatment of Sacral Dural Arteriovenous Fistulas.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Spinal dural arteriovenous fistulas (DAVFs) in the sacral region are extremely rare, and their intradural retrograde draining system has not been investigated in detail. The aim of this study was to characterize the venous drainage patterns of sacral DAVFs based on our clinical experience in treating patients with this condition. METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed the clinical data of patients with sacral DAVFs treated at our institution from January 2016 to January 2024. Preoperative spinal angiography was used to evaluate the positional relationship between the shunt point of sacral DAVF and the vertebral midline. We proposed that if the location of the shunt point was located on the midline, the draining vein would be the filum terminale vein (FTV); if the shunt point was located off the midline, the draining vein would be the radiculomedullary vein (RMV). RESULTS: A total of 17 patients with sacral DAVFs treated with direct surgery were included in this study. All patients presented with lower extremity weakness and numbness. Sphincter dysfunction was present in 15 patients (88.2%). The mean interval from the symptom onset to diagnosis was 14.1 months (range, 1-96 months). Preoperative magnetic resonance imaging detected T2 hyperintensity at the level of the conus medullaris and intradural flow voids in all patients. Spinal angiography confirmed the diagnosis of sacral DAVFs in all cases, and complete fistula occlusion was achieved with surgical ligation in all patients. Intraoperatively, 4 patients with the midline location of the shunt point were confirmed to have the FTV as the draining vein, whereas the other 13 patients with off-midline shunt point were confirmed to have the RMV as the draining vein. The intraoperative findings were completely consistent with the preoperative assessment of the draining veins based on the location of the shunt point. CONCLUSIONS: The draining veins of sacral DAVFs are not always the FTVs; in fact, most sacral DAVFs drain via the RMV. With our simple imaging-based method, the 2 different types of draining veins in sacral DAVFs can be preliminarily identified before surgery.

METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed the clinical data of patients with sacral DAVFs treated at our institution from January 2016 to January 2024.

title: Anatomic Level as a Modifier of Racial/Ethnic Disparities in Chronic Limb-Threatening Ischemia: Outcomes after First-Time Endovascular Revascularization.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Racial and ethnic disparities in chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) outcomes are well documented, but whether these disparities vary by anatomic level of endovascular intervention remains unclear. We evaluated racial and ethnic differences in limb outcomes following endovascular revascularization for CLTI stratified by intervention level. METHODS: We performed a retrospective cohort study using the TriNetX US Collaborative Network, including adults undergoing first-time lower extremity endovascular revascularization for CLTI between 2015 and 2024. Patients were stratified by intervention level: iliac, femoropopliteal, tibioperoneal, or combined femoropopliteal and tibioperoneal (multilevel). Propensity score matching balanced demographics and comorbidities across racial/ethnic cohorts. The primary outcomes were rates of 1-year major amputation and amputation-free survival. Outcome comparisons were reported as risk ratios (RRs). RESULTS: Among 14,786 patients, there were 3,071 iliac, 5,178 femoropopliteal, 2,363 tibioperoneal, and 3,718 multilevel interventions. After matching, Black patients demonstrated increased major amputation risk following iliac intervention (RR: 1.80, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.13-2.88, P = 0.012) and femoropopliteal intervention (RR: 1.83, 95% CI 1.39-2.41, P < 0.001) compared with White patients. No significant differences in amputation were observed following tibioperoneal or multilevel interventions. Hispanic patients exhibited increased amputation risk only in the multilevel cohort (RR: 1.57, 95% CI: 1.02-2.40, P = 0.037). Despite differences in amputation, amputation-free survival remained similar across racial and ethnic groups. CONCLUSION: Racial and ethnic disparities in CLTI outcomes following endovascular revascularization varied by anatomic intervention level. Disparities were most pronounced after proximal interventions and attenuated in distal disease, suggesting anatomic disease pattern may modify inequities in limb outcomes after revascularization.

METHODS: We performed a retrospective cohort study using the TriNetX US Collaborative Network, including adults undergoing first-time lower extremity endovascular revascularization for CLTI between 2015 and 2024.

title: Ultrasound-guided central venous access in the NICU: indications, insertion and management.
abstract: UNLABELLED: Ultrasound-guided cannulation of deep veins has advanced in little more than a decade from the operating room to the neonatal bedside and from a rescue maneuver to a planned procedure. Centrally inserted central catheters (CICCs) and femorally inserted central catheters (FICCs) are quite different from epicutaneo-cava catheters: they are 3-4 Fr power-injectable polyurethane catheters that are easy to tunnel, secured by subcutaneous anchorage, and suitable for blood transfusion, high-flow infusions, repeated blood sampling, and hemodynamic monitoring. This narrative review examines the indications, materials, insertion bundles for CICCs and FICCs in newborns, as well as their management, complications, and the training gap that now limits their diffusion more than any technical obstacle. In published studies, procedural success is 97-100%, immediate complications are absent or rare (when an insertion bundle is used), and the bloodstream infection rate is severalfold lower in infants below 1,500 g and below 1,000 g compared with the epicutaneo-cava catheter. Since the evidence comes mainly from a few high-volume centers with high procedural expertise, the priority for future research is to define strategies - structured programs, simulation, proctoring - to build and maintain the same level of competence in lower-volume units. CONCLUSION: Though the supporting evidence is observational, Ultrasound-guided CICCs (or FICCs, if in selected cases) appear to be the most appropriate central venous access for the critically ill newborn. WHAT IS KNOWN: • Ultrasound-guided CICCs and FICCs can be placed at the bedside in neonates, including extremely low birth weight infants, and outperform epicutaneo-cava catheters in safety, flow, dwell time, and range of use. • The adoption of insertion bundles reduces immediate and late complications of central venous catheterization in neonates and children. WHAT IS NEW: • Multicenter and comparative neonatal data show reproducible procedural success across centers and several-fold lower bloodstream infection rates in the smallest infants, compared with epicutaneo-cava catheters. • The limiting factor is no longer technical feasibility but structured training; tunneling remains the most frequently omitted step in the insertion bundle and the least easily replaced.

title: Unilateral adrenal haemorrhage during bridging anticoagulation in primary antiphospholipid syndrome: a case-based review.
abstract: Antiphospholipid syndrome (APS) is a major cause of acquired thrombophilia and is frequently associated with recurrent venous thromboembolism requiring long-term anticoagulation. We report a 42-year-old man with primary APS and recurrent pulmonary embolism and deep vein thrombosis who developed acute right upper-quadrant abdominal pain during peri-procedural bridging anticoagulation with enoxaparin. Computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated acute-to-subacute unilateral right adrenal haemorrhage without evidence of abdominal trauma, malignancy or infection. The patient remained haemodynamically stable and did not develop adrenal insufficiency. This case highlights the complexity of anticoagulation management in high-risk APS patients and emphasises the importance of considering adrenal haemorrhage in APS patients presenting with abdominal pain during anticoagulation modification. A review of previously reported unilateral APS-associated adrenal haemorrhage cases is also presented. Key Points • Unilateral adrenal haemorrhage is a rare manifestation of primary antiphospholipid syndrome. • Bridging anticoagulation may represent a vulnerable period for adrenal haemorrhage in high-risk APS. • Early CT/MRI imaging and assessment of adrenal function are essential. • Conservative management with careful reintroduction of anticoagulation may lead to favourable outcomes.

title: Canadian Cardiovascular Society/Canadian Society of Cardiovascular Surgery/Canadian Association of Interventional Cardiology Clinical Practice Update on Transcatheter Mitral and Tricuspid Valve Intervention: Patient Evaluation and Management.
abstract: The management of mitral valve (MV) and tricuspid valve (TV) regurgitation has undergone significant transformation during the past decade. This change has been driven by a growing understanding of the adverse clinical consequences of these conditions, particularly their strong association with heart failure progression, reduced quality of life, and increased mortality-and by the emergence of effective transcatheter options for valve intervention. Among these, transcatheter MV edge-to-edge repair and replacement and transcatheter tricuspid edge-to-edge repair and replacement have become important therapeutic tools that provide a less invasive alternative to surgery in appropriately selected patients. In this clinical practice update we aim to provide contemporary, evidence-based guidance for clinicians in the evaluation and management of patients with severe, symptomatic MV or TV regurgitation who might benefit from transcatheter intervention. Key topics include the clinical presentation of these valve lesions, the diagnostic evaluation with emphasis on multimodality imaging and hemodynamics, criteria for patient selection, and current data on procedural and long-term clinical outcomes. A central theme is the role of timely referral and structured assessment to avoid missed opportunities for intervention. Optimal outcomes require active engagement from referring physicians and close collaboration within a multidisciplinary heart team, including cardiologists, cardiac surgeons, imaging specialists, heart failure specialists, and nursing partners-to ensure careful patient selection, procedural planning, and comprehensive post-intervention follow-up. By integrating clinical judgement with guideline-based recommendations and procedural expertise, transcatheter edge-to-edge repair or transcatheter valve replacement can offer substantial symptomatic relief and improved quality of life for selected patients, while minimizing procedural risk and enhancing overall cardiovascular outcomes.

title: The central coupler of ClpXP controls intersubunit communication and couples intrasubunit chemical energy with force generation.
abstract: ClpX is a clockwise hexameric helical arrangement that hydrolyzes ATP to unfold proteins and translocate them into the proteolytic chamber. We investigate the central coupler, a three α-helix module conserved among AAA+ ATPases, which is proposed to enable intersubunit communication and mechanochemical coupling. Although fundamental in AAA+ ATPases, the molecular mechanism underlying these processes remains elusive in ClpX. By combining single-molecule optical tweezers, biochemical assays and single-particle cryo-EM we demonstrate that the central coupler, of the second-highest subunit of the ClpX clockwise helical arrangement, positions its Arginine-finger, sensor-I and sensor-II to contact the ATP of the anticlockwise neighbor subunit to trigger its hydrolysis. Then, the central coupler of the highest subunit rapidly couples the ATP hydrolysis with the downward motion of its substrate-translocating loop, enabling fast force generation to swiftly unfold protein substrates while maximizing the thermodynamic efficiency of the motor.

We investigate the central coupler, a three α-helix module conserved among AAA+ ATPases, which is proposed to enable intersubunit communication and mechanochemical coupling. Although fundamental in AAA+ ATPases, the molecular mechanism underlying these processes remains elusive in ClpX.

title: One-Year Outcomes of Endovascular Repair of Zone 0/1 Aortic Arch Lesions With a Thoracic Branched Endoprosthesis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The GORE TAG thoracic branch endoprosthesis pivotal nonrandomized, multicenter, prospective trial evaluated 1-year outcomes in patients at high risk for open-surgical repair undergoing aortic arch and descending thoracic aorta endovascular repair (zone 0/1). METHODS: End points evaluated from endovascular procedure through 12 months included aortic-related death, disabling stroke, permanent paraplegia or paraparesis, new onset renal failure, and unanticipated reintervention. Core lab identified end points included aortic rupture or enlargement (≥5 mm), type I/III endoleak, device integrity, device migration, fistula, patency, and new dissection. RESULTS: The 77 patients enrolled had aneurysm (n = 50), dissection (n = 24), or other isolated lesion types (n = 3); 90.9% had a zone 0 proximal stent landing zone. Patients had a mean age of 70.8±10.8 years, 66.2% were men, and 57.1% were White. All had the aortic and side branch component implanted. Technical success was 94.8%. Early outcomes to 12 months included 8 aortic-related deaths (10.4%), 6 disabling strokes (7.8%, all in the aneurysm cohort), 4 unanticipated reintervention (5.2%), 2 aortic ruptures (2.6%), and 1 renal failure (1.3%). Type IA/IB or type III endoleaks occurred in 6 patients (7.8%). Loss of side branch patency occurred in 1 patient (1.3%). There was no permanent paraplegia or paraparesis or loss of device integrity or migration. A total of 5 patients had aortic enlargement; none required reintervention. CONCLUSIONS: Early data from this prospective investigation of the thoracic branch endoprosthesis device in zone 0/1 applications signal that the device is a reasonable therapeutic alternative in patients with appropriate anatomy deemed high risk for open arch surgery.

title: Emergency Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation for Decompensated Aortic Stenosis accompanied by Cardiogenic Shock.
abstract: Patients with severe aortic stenosis (AS) often present acutely with decompensated heart failure, cardiogenic shock or cardiac arrest requiring immediate intervention. Treatment options for these patients include palliative care, balloon aortic valvuloplasty (BAV), emergency transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI), or surgical aortic valve replacement. TAVI procedure is performed electively in majority of the patients. However, it can be considered a rescue therapy in patients with cardiogenic shock secondary to acutely decompensated valvular AS. Here, we report the successful use of emergent TAVI for a patient presenting with cardiogenic shock secondary to decompensated AS.

Treatment options for these patients include palliative care, balloon aortic valvuloplasty (BAV), emergency transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI), or surgical aortic valve replacement. TAVI procedure is performed electively in majority of the patients.

title: Comparison of a Novel Geometric Landmark Method Versus Conventional Palpation Technique for Central Venous Cannulation: A Comparative Observational Study of Two Techniques.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To compare the effectiveness and safety of a novel geometric landmark technique with the conventional palpation technique for central venous cannulation. STUDY DESIGN: Comparative observational study. PLACE AND DURATION OF THE STUDY: This study was conducted at National Medical Centre (NMC) from January 01, 2025 to June 30, 2025. METHODS: A total of 100 adult patients requiring central venous cannulation were enrolled and allocated into two groups based on the technique used. Group A (n = 50) underwent cannulation using the geometric landmark method, while Group B (n = 50) underwent cannulation using the conventional palpation technique. First-attempt success rate was the main outcome. Secondary outcomes were the number of attempts, arterial puncture, and change of technique. SPSS software was used for analysis. Chi-square test was used to compare categorical variables whereas the Mann-Whitney U test was applied to the non-normally distributed continuous variables. A P value of less than 0.05 was considered statistically significant. RESULTS: First-attempt success was significantly higher in the geometric landmark group compared to the palpation group (98% vs. 86%; P = 0.027). The geometric landmark technique was associated with fewer cannulation attempts (mean 1.00 ± 0.00 vs. 1.18 ± 0.57; P = 0.012). Arterial puncture occurred in one patient (2%) in each group, with no statistically significant difference (P = 1.000). Technique change was required in one patient (2%) in each group, with no statistically significant difference between the two techniques (P = 1.000). The two groups had similar baseline demographic and clinical characteristics. CONCLUSION: The geometric landmark technique significantly improves first-attempt success and reduces the number of cannulation attempts compared with the conventional palpation method while maintaining a comparable safety profile. This technique represents a practical and cost-effective alternative for central venous cannulation, particularly in resource-limited settings.
englishSummary: OBJECTIVE: To compare the effectiveness and safety of a novel geometric landmark technique with the conventional palpation technique for central venous cannulation. STUDY DESIGN: Comparative observational study. PLACE AND DURATION OF THE STUDY: This study was conducted at National Medical Centre (NMC) from January 01, 2025 to June 30, 2025.

title: Thoracic endovascular aortic repair in hyperacute type B aortic dissection: a mini review.
abstract: Thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR) is established as the preferred treatment for many patients with complicated acute type B aortic dissection (TBAD). However, its role during the hyperacute phase (within 24 hours of symptom onset) remains controversial, as the acutely dissected aortic wall may be vulnerable to device-related injury. Nevertheless, hyperacute timing should not be regarded as an absolute contraindication to TEVAR. In patients with rupture, malperfusion, impending aortic rupture, persistent pain, refractory hypertension, or progressive true-lumen collapse, prompt entry-tear coverage can restore perfusion and prevent irreversible organ injury. Similarly, in patients without initial complications, high-risk anatomical features may help identify those who could benefit from early intervention. However, evidence supporting routine TEVAR within the first 24 hours remains limited and is predominantly observational. To ensure safe hyperacute TEVAR, careful assessment of the landing zones, conservative device sizing, avoidance of aggressive balloon molding, preservation of branch-vessel and spinal cord perfusion, and prompt recognition of retrograde type A dissection, stroke, spinal cord ischemia, and stent-graft-induced new entry are required. Ultimately, hyperacute TEVAR may be a reasonable option for selected patients with complicated TBAD, with a potential role in high-risk uncomplicated TBAD. Future prospective randomized trials integrating multimodal imaging and dynamic biomarkers are warranted to establish definitive criteria for timing and candidate selection.

However, its role during the hyperacute phase (within 24 hours of symptom onset) remains controversial, as the acutely dissected aortic wall may be vulnerable to device-related injury. Nevertheless, hyperacute timing should not be regarded as an absolute contraindication to TEVAR.

title: Cerebral Air Embolism After Navigational Bronchoscopy Treated With Aspiration Thrombectomy: A Case Report.
abstract: Systemic arterial air embolism is a rare but potentially devastating complication of bronchoscopic lung biopsy. A 68-year-old man with severe emphysema developed abrupt bradycardia, hypotension, and failure to regain consciousness after navigational bronchoscopy under general anaesthesia. Computed tomography demonstrated air within the left middle cerebral artery, and angiography confirmed proximal large-vessel occlusion. Urgent aspiration thrombectomy achieved complete reperfusion after one pass, with retrieved material compatible with thrombus. Despite technically successful reperfusion, major neurological deficits persisted. This case highlights haemodynamic collapse and delayed emergence as warning signs and supports rapid neuroimaging with selective endovascular treatment when an accessible large-vessel occlusion is present.

A 68-year-old man with severe emphysema developed abrupt bradycardia, hypotension, and failure to regain consciousness after navigational bronchoscopy under general anaesthesia. Computed tomography demonstrated air within the left middle cerebral artery, and angiography confirmed proximal large-vessel occlusion.

title: Recognizing Pelvic Venous Disease in Chronic Pelvic Pain: A Primary Care Case Report.
abstract: Chronic pelvic pain is a common and challenging condition with a broad differential diagnosis and a substantial impact on quality of life. Pelvic congestion syndrome (PCS) is a clinical manifestation of pelvic venous disease that may involve venous reflux, obstruction, collateralization, and dilation across different pelvic venous territories. Its non-specific clinical presentation and overlap with gynecological, gastrointestinal, and musculoskeletal disorders may lead to significant diagnostic delay. A 42-year-old woman presented to a general and family medicine consultation with a six-year history of chronic pelvic pain, progressively worsening over the previous six months. She described persistent pressure-like pelvic pain, rated 7/10 in intensity, aggravated by prolonged standing and associated with severe deep dyspareunia, which prevented sexual intercourse, associated with low back pain radiating to the pelvis and both thighs, lower-limb heaviness, and significant sleep disturbance. She denied urinary symptoms or a relationship with the menstrual cycle. During the previous six years, she had undergone repeated medical assessments, with symptoms being attributed to recurrent gynecological infections, probable irritable bowel syndrome, and other non-specific causes. Previous investigations, including colonoscopy and emergency department assessments, had not identified a clear etiology for her symptoms. Physical examination revealed hypogastric tenderness and mild superficial lower-limb varicosities, without vulvar or perineal varices. Pelvic and lumbar computed tomography (CT) demonstrated bilateral dilated periuterine veins measuring up to 13 mm, raising suspicion for a symptomatic pelvic venous disorder. The patient was referred to vascular surgery for further assessment; however, specialist evaluation remained pending at the time of manuscript revision. Pelvic venous disease should be considered in women with persistent pelvic pain, particularly when symptoms worsen with prolonged standing or sexual intercourse and are accompanied by low back pain or lower-limb heaviness. The absence of vulvar varices or previous inconclusive investigations does not exclude a possible pelvic venous etiology. This case illustrates how the non-specific presentation of pelvic venous disease may result in years of fragmented investigation and delayed recognition. Continuity of care in general and family medicine facilitated a longitudinal review of the patient's symptoms and previous investigations, allowing recognition of a pattern suggestive of pelvic venous disease. Greater awareness of pelvic venous disease in primary care may facilitate earlier consideration and appropriate specialist referral in women with otherwise unexplained chronic pelvic pain.
englishSummary: Chronic pelvic pain is a common and challenging condition with a broad differential diagnosis and a substantial impact on quality of life. Pelvic congestion syndrome (PCS) is a clinical manifestation of pelvic venous disease that may involve venous reflux, obstruction, collateralization, and dilation across different pelvic venous territories. Its non-specific clinical presentation and overlap with gynecological, gastrointestinal, and musculoskeletal disorders may lead to significant diagnostic delay.
